```
E = Σ_i [ 500 × d_i + 5 × max(0, 120 − t_i) ]  +  1000 × L_remaining
    d_i = difficulty weight of i-th cleared level ∈ [1, 3] (from §3.8 difficulty function, scaled)
    t_i = clear time of level i (s); 120 s = speed bonus cap
    L_remaining ∈ {0,1,2,3} — the documented 3-life budget
```

**Worked example** — 10-level session, 1 life remaining, clear times 55/60/70/65/80/75/90/85/95/100 s, difficulty weights ramping 1.00 → 1.93 (saturating exponential, §3.8.4; Σd ≈ 14.51 — levels 1–2 clamp the raw 0.60/0.85 up to the d ≥ 1 floor):

- Difficulty points: 500 × 14.51 = 7,255
- Speed points: 5 × [(120−55)+(120−60)+(120−70)+(120−65)+(120−80)+(120−75)+(120−90)+(120−85)+(120−95)+(120−100)] = 5 × (65+60+50+55+40+45+30+35+25+20) = 5 × 425 = 2,125
- Lives: 1000 × 1 = 1,000
- **E = 10,380** → session leaderboard (§19) upload.

#### 3.7.4 Infinity score

```
I = 100 × H_max + 10 × N_placed
```

`H_max` = maximum stack height reached (block units) before the run-ending water contact; `N_placed` = pieces placed. Leaderboards sort primarily by `H_max` (the documented mode goal is height, [Switch sheet](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24), secondarily by `I`. Worked: H_max 23, N 58 → I = 2,300 + 580 = 2,880.

#### 3.7.5 Swift Stacker scoring

Match score **[DOCUMENTED]** structure: race wins rounds; match length selectable 5/7/9 rounds (documented for the WiiWare Versus ancestor, [NL WiiWare review](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24). Round-level tiebreaker/MVP points and the combo/chain mechanic **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

```
P_round   = 100 + clamp(0, 200, round(2 × (t_losingTeam − t_winningTeam)))
P_awarded = round(P_round × m(chainCount))
m(c)      = min(1 + SwiftChainStep × c, SwiftChainCap)     SwiftChainStep = 0.1, SwiftChainCap = 1.5
```

**Combo/chain mechanic** **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: each team carries a chain counter. A round won with `t_winningTeam` ≤ `T_fast` = `SwiftChainParRatio` × `T_par` (the round puzzle's `LevelDefinition` par time; `SwiftChainParRatio` = 0.75) is a *fast clear*: the winning team's chain counter increments. A slow win or a lost round resets the counter to 0. `chainCount` is the team's consecutive fast clears *including the current round*, so the multiplier starts at ×1.1 on the first fast clear and saturates at ×1.5 (5 consecutive fast clears). `T_par` is per-round and shared by both teams because Swift Stacker races the identical puzzle (§3.6), so one par drives both the chain threshold and the Time Challenge par math.

**Worked example** (match excerpt; `T_par` = 60 s per round → `T_fast` = 0.75 × 60 = 45 s; team A perspective):

| Round | A clears | B clears | P_round | Fast clear? | chainCount | m | P_awarded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 42.3 s | 51.0 s | 100 + round(2 × 8.7) = 117 | yes (42.3 ≤ 45) | 1 | ×1.1 | round(117 × 1.1) = 129 |
| 2 | 44.8 s | 55.0 s | 100 + round(2 × 10.2) = 120 | yes (44.8 ≤ 45) | 2 | ×1.2 | 144 |
| 3 | 47.6 s | 58.9 s | 100 + round(2 × 11.3) = 123 | no (47.6 > 45) | 0 (reset) | ×1.0 | 123 |

Team A's MVP-point total over the excerpt = 129 + 144 + 123 = 396. Round points — base and chain alike — never decide the match (rounds do); they feed only the post-match MVP screen and aggregate profile stats.

#### 3.7.6 Tower Tumble scoring

**[DOCUMENTED]**: turn-based placement; whoever topples loses the round; everyone else scores a point; pieces per round are randomly generated ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), [NWR](http://www.nintendoworldreport.com/review/38619/art-of-balance-wii-u-review), accessed 2026-09-24). Match target **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: first to 5 points wins (configurable 3/5/7 in `Lobby`). Round-random queues use a seeded RNG displayed as a shared seed code so rematches are reproducible.

#### 3.7.7 ScoreModel (pure math, testable)

`ScoreController` (§6) subscribes to §3.3.4 events and calls this allocation-free static model; every formula above is editmode-unit-testable (§14) because nothing here touches scene objects:

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoBClone.Gameplay
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Pure scoring math for all modes. All formulas are [ORIGINAL DESIGN]
    /// except where the member cites a documented skeleton (see §3.7).
    /// </summary>
    public static class ScoreModel
    {
        #region Consts

        public const int HeightPointsPerUnit = 25;
        public const int TimePointsPerSecond = 10;
        public const int PrecisionPointsPerUnit = 25;
        public const int ChallengeFlatBonus = 250;
        public const int StarThresholdStep = 50;
        public const float TwoStarRatio = 0.7f;
        public const int EnduranceDifficultyPointsPerLevel = 500;
        public const int EnduranceSpeedCapSeconds = 120;
        public const int EnduranceSpeedPointsPerSecond = 5;
        public const int EnduranceLivesPoints = 1000;
        public const int InfinityPointsPerHeightUnit = 100;
        public const int InfinityPointsPerPiece = 10;
        public const int SwiftRoundBasePoints = 100;
        public const int SwiftMarginWeight = 2;
        public const int SwiftMarginCap = 200;
        public const float SwiftChainParRatio = 0.75f;
        public const float SwiftChainStep = 0.1f;
        public const float SwiftChainCap = 1.5f;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>
        /// Arcade level total: placements + height + time + precision + challenge
        /// (see §3.7.1). Placement points are authored per PieceDefinition.
        /// </summary>
        public static int ComputeLevelScore(
            int placementPoints,
            int finalHeightUnits,
            int parTimeSeconds,
            int elapsedSeconds,
            int footprintWidthUnits,
            int parFootprintWidthUnits,
            bool challengeCompleted)
        {
            int height = finalHeightUnits * HeightPointsPerUnit;
            int time = Mathf.Max(0, parTimeSeconds - elapsedSeconds) * TimePointsPerSecond;
            int precision = Mathf.Max(0, parFootprintWidthUnits - footprintWidthUnits) * PrecisionPointsPerUnit;
            int challenge = challengeCompleted ? ChallengeFlatBonus : 0;
            return placementPoints + height + time + precision + challenge;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Star rating from a reference-par anchored threshold (see §3.7.2).
        /// </summary>
        public static int DeriveStars(int score, int threeStarThreshold)
        {
            if (score >= threeStarThreshold)
            {
                return 3;
            }
            int twoStarThreshold = RoundToStep(
                Mathf.RoundToInt(TwoStarRatio * threeStarThreshold), StarThresholdStep);
            return score >= twoStarThreshold ? 2 : 1;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Endurance session total: documented skeleton (speed + lives +
        /// difficulty) instantiated per §3.7.3.
        /// </summary>
        public static int ComputeEnduranceScore(int clearedCount, float difficultyWeightSum, int speedBonusSeconds, int livesRemaining)
        {
            int difficulty = Mathf.RoundToInt(EnduranceDifficultyPointsPerLevel * difficultyWeightSum);
            int speed = EnduranceSpeedPointsPerSecond * speedBonusSeconds;
            int lives = EnduranceLivesPoints * livesRemaining;
            return difficulty + speed + lives;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Infinity run total (see §3.7.4). Leaderboards sort by height first.
        /// </summary>
        public static int ComputeInfinityScore(int maxHeightUnits, int piecesPlaced)
        {
            return (maxHeightUnits * InfinityPointsPerHeightUnit)
                + (piecesPlaced * InfinityPointsPerPiece);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Swift Stacker round tiebreak points (see §3.7.5). Never decides the match.
        /// </summary>
        public static int ComputeSwiftRoundPoints(float winnerSeconds, float loserSeconds)
        {
            int margin = Mathf.Clamp(
                Mathf.RoundToInt(SwiftMarginWeight * (loserSeconds - winnerSeconds)),
                0, SwiftMarginCap);
            return SwiftRoundBasePoints + margin;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Swift Stacker round tiebreak points with the consecutive-fast-clear
        /// chain multiplier (see §3.7.5). chainCount = the winning team's
        /// consecutive fast clears including this round; a non-fast round ignores
        /// the counter (the caller resets it to 0). Never decides the match.
        /// </summary>
        public static int ComputeSwiftRoundPoints(
            float winnerSeconds,
            float loserSeconds,
            float parSeconds,
            int chainCount)
        {
            int basePoints = ComputeSwiftRoundPoints(winnerSeconds, loserSeconds);
            bool fastClear = winnerSeconds <= SwiftChainParRatio * parSeconds;
            float multiplier = fastClear
                ? Mathf.Min(1f + SwiftChainStep * chainCount, SwiftChainCap)
                : 1f;
            return Mathf.RoundToInt(basePoints * multiplier);
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private static int RoundToStep(int value, int step)
        {
            // Round half-DOWN to match the §3.7.2 derivation rule
            // (round50(1,675) = 1,650, not 1,700 — keeps 3★ reachable at half-steps).
            return Mathf.Max(step, ((value + step / 2 - 1) / step) * step);
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Leaderboard plumbing (per-platform backends, upload cadence, and anti-cheat signing of score payloads) is specified in §14 (DevSecOps) and §19 (Steam) — this section fixes only the numbers and the events that feed them.

### 3.8 Difficulty curves and pacing

#### 3.8.1 Difficulty levers

Content volume **[DOCUMENTED]**: 200 levels across 8 worlds with one distinct lounge environment each ([3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); shape inventory 16 base + 5 special shapes. The levers a `LevelDefinition` (§5) pulls, in order of player-perceived pressure:

| Lever | Low pressure | High pressure |
|---|---|---|
| Queue length | 4–6 pieces | 18–25 pieces |
| Special ratio | 0 | 40%+ |
| Platform usable width | 10+ units | 3–4 units |
| Water distance below platform | 6 units | 0–1 units (near-surface platform) |
| Base motion | Static | Swaying/floating base (documented mechanic, [Cubed3 3DS](https://www.cubed3.com/games/reviews/nintendo-3ds/art-of-balance-touch), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Par targets | Generous T_par/W_par | Tight T_par/W_par (score pressure only) |

Composite difficulty function (drives the §5 validation heuristic, Endurance/Infinity generation targets, and telemetry binning) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

```
D = 0.35·N̂ + 0.20·Ŝ + 0.20·P̂ + 0.15·Ŵ + 0.10·Ĉ   (each component normalized to 0–10)
  N̂ = min(queueCount, 30)/3            Ŝ = 10 × specialsRatio
  P̂ = 10·(1 − usableWidth/12)          Ŵ = 10·(1 − waterDistance/6)
  Ĉ = chaos points: swaying base +2, gravity-flip layout +3, dual basins +2 (cap 10)
```

Worked check: queue 18 (N̂=6), specials 4/18 (Ŝ=2.2), width 5 (P̂=5.83), water 2 units below (Ŵ=6.67), sway (+2): D = 2.10 + 0.44 + 1.17 + 1.00 + 0.20 = **4.9** — mid-game.

#### 3.8.2 Per-world schedule

World themes/names are undocumented in every fetched source (only "each with its own unique lounge style"), so this schedule is our pacing design on top of the documented 200-levels/8-worlds volume (the 25-per-world split is our convention, §5.6.1) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**. Special-block behavior references are documented (§8 owns mechanics):

| World | Introduces | Special focus | Target D range | New-skill verb |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Base shapes 1–8 | Wide static platforms; teach 45° diagonal resting | 1–2 | "place" |
| 2 | Base shapes 9–12; **breakable** blocks (hold ≤ ~3 regulars, [Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | Load management | 2–3 | "distribute" |
| 3 | Base shapes 13–16; **timer** blocks (start when stacked atop, [Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | Sequencing under expiry | 3–4 | "sequence" |
| 4 | **Swaying/floating bases** (documented 3DS+ mechanic) | Dynamic reference frame | 4–5 | "time the sway" |
| 5 | **Fire** shapes (explode on mutual contact, [3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) | Separation planning | 5–6 | "segregate" |
| 6 | **Gravity-inverter** (flips stack to platform at screen top; top+bottom platforms, [Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | Inverted planning | 6–7 | "build downward" |
| 7 | **Linked/seesaw pairs** — our extension (§8) | Coupled-torque reasoning | 7–8 | "counterbalance" |
| 8 | Nothing new; full vocabulary mixes | Gauntlet + super challenges | 8–10 | "master" |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: the 5th special shape's identity in the 2012+ originals is undocumented (the archived official sentence truncates after four). Per plan decision, "linked/seesaw" is implemented as an [ORIGINAL DESIGN] extension alongside the four documented specials; if the true identity is ever confirmed (in-game capture), re-slot world 7. -->

#### 3.8.3 Within-world pacing (25 levels)

Tension/rest curve per the game-designer pacing guidance (escalating tension with relief valves; teach → develop → twist → test → crown) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Levels | Beat | Pacing role |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | Teach the world's new verb on oversized platforms | Rest/learning; near-zero fail pressure |
| 4–10 | Develop: apply the verb with shrinking platforms/growing queues | Rising tension |
| 11–17 | Twist: combine with the previous world's verb (e.g., timer blocks *on* swaying bases) | Peak tension; fail-rate spike expected |
| 18–24 | Test: full-difficulty applications; one Breath level at 19 (D −1.5) as a deliberate rest valve | High plateau with one rest |
| 25 | Super-challenge: documented Time/Height/Balance challenge level ("for extra points", [Wii About](https://web.archive.org/web/20091116220135/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) | Climax; crown of the world |

World boundaries are rest beats: world N+1 level 1 always drops D by ≥ 2 and re-teaches in the new environment (documented environment switch is the natural reset, [3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24). Telemetry fail-rate targets **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: world-first quartile 10–20%, mid-world peaks 40–60%, level 25 up to 70% (skippable levels make gates soft, §3.9.1).

#### 3.8.4 Procedural ramp (Endurance, Infinity)

Session difficulty target follows a saturating exponential so early levels are warm-ups and pressure asymptotes rather than spiking **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

```
D_target(i) = D_min + (D_max − D_min) × (1 − e^(−0.15·(i−1)))
  Endurance: D_min = 2, D_max = 8      Infinity: D_min = 2, D_max = 10 (never saturates visually)
```

Level i of the session is drawn (Endurance) or the feed is biased (Infinity) toward `D_target(i)` using the seeded RNG (§3.9.4). Endurance difficulty weights for §3.7.3: `d_i = 3 × D_target(i) / 10` ∈ [0.6 → 2.4], clamped to [1, 3] — matching the worked example's 1.00 → 1.93 ramp (the first two levels' raw 0.60/0.85 clamp up to the 1.00 floor; Σd ≈ 14.51).

### 3.9 Level flow, unlocks, awards, and ghosts

#### 3.9.1 Progression and unlocks

**[DOCUMENTED]** structure: within a world the player chooses level order and may skip individual levels; the next world unlocks after enough successes ([Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24 — "In jeder Spielwelt hat man eine gewisse Entscheidungsfreiheit, in welcher Reihenfolge man spielt. Einzelne Abschnitte kann man auch auslassen, nach genügend Erfolgen wird die nächste Spielwelt freigeschaltet."). Instantiation **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: world 2 unlocks at 15 of 25 completions in world 1, escalating to 21 of 25 (84%) for the world-8 gate — per-world thresholds 15/17/18/19/20/20/21 per §5.6.1 (Σ = 130/175 = 74%) — stored per `WorldDefinition` so the gate is tunable per world; every level remains playable after unlock for star-chasing; no level is ever *required*.

#### 3.9.2 Medals and level stats

Per-level 3★ ratings per §3.7.2 **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; `SaveSystem` (§6) persists per-level: best score, stars, best time, attempts, challenge flag. Level-select pins render state (locked / open / 1–3★) via the §9 theme system.

#### 3.9.3 Awards / achievements

**[DOCUMENTED]** anchor: the 3DS edition shipped 13 awards, including "Complete 50/100 levels" and "finish a later puzzle in under 30 seconds" ([3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), [Cubed3 3DS](https://www.cubed3.com/games/reviews/nintendo-3ds/art-of-balance-touch), accessed 2026-09-24). Our award list mirrors that spirit with ~13–16 achievements mapped onto platform systems (Steam achievements §19; console equivalents §18/§19) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — milestone completions (50/100/200 levels), speed citations (sub-30 s late puzzle), challenge sweeps (all Time/Height/Balance medals), mode citations (Endurance score tiers, Infinity height tiers), and multiplayer citations (Tower Tumble shutout, Swift Stacker 5-0 sweep).

#### 3.9.4 Ghost replays

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** extension (no ghost feature is documented in any fetched source). Determinism constraints from T11 research bound the design: Unity's shipped physics engines are deterministic on the same device given identical inputs, but not guaranteed across devices ([Unity staff MelvMay, 2023-02-27](https://discussions.unity.com/t/fully-deterministic-physics/910507/10); cf. PhysX "limited deterministic simulation" — same scene, same actor insert order, same timestep, same release, same platform, [NVIDIA PhysX 5.8 docs](https://nvidia-omniverse.github.io/PhysX/physx/5.8.0/docs/Simulation.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Therefore:

- A ghost is a recorded **input log**: ordered `(stepIndex, inputEvent)` pairs quantized to fixed steps (the T11 recipe), plus the level seed and a build/physics-config hash.
- Playback re-simulates on-device. Personal ghosts (same device, same build) are exact by construction; shared ghosts (leaderboard tops, friends) carry a per-N-step checksum and are flagged `desync-corrected` (snap to recorded keyframe poses) rather than silently wrong.
- Keyframe poses (all piece transforms every 600 steps) are embedded to bound drift and to scrub the results-screen replay UI.
- Cross-device lockstep play remains out of scope for v1 (§2, §21); the upstream Box2D v3 determinism program ("designed to be deterministic across thread counts and platforms", [Box2D v3 manual](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html), accessed 2026-09-24) is tracked in §21 as the path that could later upgrade shared ghosts from correction-tolerant to exact.

#### 3.9.5 Attempt lifecycle summary

One attempt = `Loading` (deterministic scene build, fixed actor order per PhysX insert-order sensitivity) → `Idle`/intro → repeat §3.3 loop → `Cleared` (stars, score, save, optional ghost capture) or `Failed` (fail sting, retry per §3.3.3). Abandonment (quit mid-attempt) records attempts+1 and no score. Every attempt logs the telemetry tuple defined in §14 (level id, D-score, duration, fail phase, water-contact piece) so §3.8's fail-rate targets are measurable from day one.

## 4. Technical Architecture Overview

This section defines the Unity project skeleton that every other engineering section builds on: engine baseline and project creation (§4.1), the package manifest (§4.2), folder and assembly layout (§4.3), the runtime system map (§4.4), the event architecture (§4.5), IDE and External Tools configuration (§4.6), per-scene Editor organization (§4.7), the ProjectSettings inventory (§4.8), build profiles and scripting defines (§4.9), and the configuration-file strategy (§4.10). The architectural decomposition itself — system names, boundaries, and wiring — is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (the original's internals are undocumented; see §1); every external engine fact carries its source inline.

Three layering rules govern everything below, chosen to serve the pillars in §2 (determinism-friendly physics, data-driven content, every-input-device parity, small-team pipeline):

1. **Simulation / presentation / platform separation.** Gameplay state changes flow one way through events; UI, audio, camera, and VFX are pure consumers. Platform code (Steam, mobile, Xbox) sits behind interfaces in `Aob.Platform` and never leaks upward.
2. **Data-driven content.** Levels, pieces, worlds, and modes are ScriptableObject assets (§5) loaded via Addressables; no level logic is hardcoded in scenes.
3. **One fat contract, thin managers.** No god-`GameManager`. `GameStateMachine` owns flow; each system in §4.4 owns one job and communicates via the §4.5 channels.

### 4.1 Engine baseline and project creation

#### 4.1.1 Unity version pin

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Editor line | Unity 6.6 (internal 6000.6), "Supported"/Update release — Unity dropped the "Tech Stream" name for this tier | ([Unity support page](https://unity.com/releases/unity-6/support), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Initial release | 6000.6.0f1, released 2026-08-31 | ([6000.6.0f1 release notes](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Latest patch at research time | 6000.6.2f1, 2026-09-18 | ([eosl.date](https://eosl.date/eol/product/unity/), accessed 2026-09-24 — tertiary cross-check) |
| Family position | Final Supported release of the Unity 6 family; 6.7 (in beta) becomes the next LTS — multi-source: the Sep 1 2026 staff announcement, the 6000.6.0f1 release notes ("no longer be available after Unity 6.7 LTS"), and the CoreCLR article's "Unity 6.7LTS Alpha" naming | ([announcement thread](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-6-6-is-now-available/1735357), [release notes](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), [CoreCLR article](https://discussions.unity.com/t/path-to-coreclr-2026-upgrade-guide/1714279), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Support horizon | Same support/stability/critical-updates level as LTS "until the next release — in this case 6.7 — arrives" (official wording) | ([announcement thread](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-6-6-is-now-available/1735357), accessed 2026-09-24) |

We pin **6000.6.xf1 (latest patch)** for this greenfield project, matching official staff guidance on the 6.6 thread: use 6.3 LTS for projects about to ship, 6.6 Supported for new projects ([announcement thread](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-6-6-is-now-available/1735357), accessed 2026-09-24). 6.3 LTS (supported until December 2027) is the pre-planned downgrade path if 6.6 churn blocks us ([Unity support page](https://unity.com/releases/unity-6/support), accessed 2026-09-24); the upgrade-to-6.7-LTS decision point is tracked as a risk in §21. `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` is committed and CI (§16) builds with exactly that revision.

#### 4.1.2 Project template and scripting baseline

- **Template:** Universal 3D (URP). The 6.x line ships URP major 17 ([URP What's New](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/urp/whats-new/urp-whats-new.html), accessed 2026-09-24); dynamic batching is removed in this generation, so all shaders are authored SRP-Batcher-compatible from day one ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Full URP asset/tier configuration lives in §9.
- **Scripting runtime:** C# 9 / .NET Standard 2.1 on Mono in-editor, IL2CPP for all shipping players. Api Compatibility Level = **.NET Standard 2.1**, and every precompiled/third-party assembly we vendor is kept on netstandard2.1 so the announced CoreCLR migration (Unity 6.8 removes Mono; .NET 10 becomes the only TFM) stays mechanical rather than surgical ([CoreCLR article](https://discussions.unity.com/t/path-to-coreclr-2026-upgrade-guide/1714279), accessed 2026-09-24 — schedule-sensitive, slippage precedent documented there).
- **CoreCLR-prep discipline (6.6 defaults):** new projects default Enter Play Mode to "Reload Scene only" (domain reload off); we keep it that way per official recommendation, which forces explicit static-state hygiene — statics reset via `AutoStaticsCleanup`/`NoAutoStaticsCleanup` attributes and a Project Auditor analyzer pass ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24). `UNITY_64`/`DEVELOPMENT_BUILD` defines are deprecated in 6.6 and must not appear in our code; the new Managed Code Variant setting stays at its default ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24).
- **Serialization headroom:** 6.6 adds native `Dictionary<TKey,TValue>` serialization with Inspector support ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — used for config maps in §4.10 and content metadata in §5 instead of custom drawer workarounds.
- **Color space:** **Linear** (Player Settings → Other Settings → Rendering). Long-standing URP guidance; the dedicated docs page was unreachable during research, so treat the requirement as high-confidence guidance rather than a quoted rule ([URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

#### 4.1.3 Version control bootstrap

Git + Git LFS, initialized before first Editor launch (so `Library/` is never committed):

```bash
git init
git lfs install
# Binary asset classes only; force-text .asset files stay in plain git for reviewability
git lfs track "*.psd" "*.png" "*.tga" "*.exr" "*.fbx" "*.obj" "*.mp3" "*.wav" "*.ogg" "*.ttf" "*.otf" "*.blend" "*.unitypackage"
```

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** refinement of the standard track list (from the unity-game-dev-expert skill): we deliberately do **not** LFS-track `*.asset` wholesale — with Force Text serialization (§4.8) most ScriptableObjects are reviewable YAML, and keeping them in plain git preserves diff-based code review for the 200+ level definitions (§5); only genuinely binary assets (textures, meshes, audio, fonts, `.blend` sources) go to LFS. `.gitignore` excludes `Library/`, `Temp/`, `Obj/`, `Build(s)/`, `Logs/`, `UserSettings/`, `*.csproj`, `*.sln`, IDE directories.

Smart merge is wired per Unity docs: UnityYAMLMerge ships with the Editor (`C:\Program Files\Unity\Editor\Data\Tools\UnityYAMLMerge.exe` on Windows), and `mergespecfile.txt` lets it act as the git merge driver for Unity YAML ([Smart Merge docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/SmartMerge.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Serialized-asset merge policy (scene vs. prefab vs. SO) and the `.gitattributes` lines that route each class to UnityYAMLMerge are defined with the full VCS recipe in §4.8 and §16.

#### 4.1.4 Creation command

The repo is stood up by the Unity CLI (not the Hub GUI) so a clean clone reaches editor-ready state deterministically (full bootstrap script in §15):

```bash
unity projects create AoBClone --no-cloud   # cloud-project creation is the DEFAULT and exits 3 unsigned-in; --no-cloud keeps it local
```

([Unity CLI docs — Use](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24: cloud-by-default behavior and exit code 3; CLI is experimental, current 1.0.0-beta.11 as of 2026-09-22 per the [release notes](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/release-notes), accessed 2026-09-24.) The Hub itself auto-installs the CLI since Hub 3.21.0 (announced 2026-08-18, bundling CLI 1.0.0-beta.6) ([Hub 3.21 thread](https://discussions.unity.com/t/now-available-unity-hub-3-21-1/1734183), accessed 2026-09-24).

### 4.3 Folder structure and assembly definitions

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** layout, adapting the unity-game-dev-expert `_Project/` convention (project assets bucketed ahead of package assets; never mixed with third-party code):

```text
Assets/
├── _Project/
│   ├── Art/            # Models/, Textures/, Materials/, Shaders/, Fonts/, Animations/
│   ├── Audio/          # Music/, SFX/, Mixers/
│   ├── Prefabs/        # Pieces/, Environment/, VFX/, UI/
│   ├── Scenes/         # Boot/, Menu/, LevelSelect/, Gameplay/, TestScenes/
│   ├── Scripts/
│   │   ├── Core/       # GameStateMachine, events, pooling, config, services
│   │   ├── Gameplay/   # LevelManager, PieceSpawner, StabilityMonitor, ScoreController, BlockBehaviours
│   │   ├── UI/         # HUD, menus, safe area, glyph system
│   │   ├── Input/      # InputRouter + IPieceInputProvider implementations (§7)
│   │   ├── Platform/   # Steam, mobile, Xbox adapters behind interfaces
│   │   └── Data/       # PieceDefinition, LevelDefinition, WorldDefinition, GameModeDefinition SOs
│   ├── Settings/       # GameConfig, platform overrides, quality URP assets, presets
│   ├── Addressables/   # group assets
│   └── Editor/         # LevelEditor window, validators, import presets
├── Plugins/            # Steamworks.NET native plugins etc.
├── StreamingAssets/    # steam_appid.txt (dev only), versioned manifests
└── ThirdParty/         # vendored precompiled assemblies (netstandard2.1)
```

Assembly definitions enforce the boundaries (mechanics per Unity docs; best-practice constraints from the unity-game-dev-expert skill and T10: per-module asmdefs, player-code loop depth ≤ 1 to avoid compile-order workarounds):

```text
Aob.Core      (no refs)
Aob.Gameplay  → Aob.Core
Aob.Input     → Aob.Core
Aob.UI        → Aob.Core, Aob.Gameplay        (read-models + event listeners only)
Aob.Platform  → Aob.Core                       (per-platform Include Platforms where applicable)
Aob.Editor    → all runtime assemblies         (Include Platforms: Editor only)
Aob.Tests.EditMode  → Aob.Core, Aob.Gameplay   (Include Platforms: Editor only)
Aob.Tests.PlayMode  → all runtime assemblies
```

Rules **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: `Aob.Core` contains zero `UnityEngine` scene dependencies beyond what events/config need, so the physics rules and scoring math are edit-mode-testable without Play Mode (§14); `Aob.Gameplay` never references `Aob.UI`/`Aob.Platform` (dependency arrows point one way); platform-specific code inside `Aob.Gameplay` is forbidden — it goes through interfaces realized in `Aob.Platform` with `#if` directives confined there (full platform `#if` table in §19); `Aob.Editor` ships nothing.

### 4.4 Runtime system map

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** decomposition; class names follow the shared vocabulary defined across sections (`LevelManager`, `StabilityMonitor`, `PieceDefinition`, `IPieceInputProvider`, `IBlockBehaviour`, `GameStateMachine`, `ScoreController`).

| System | Responsibility | Owns | Listens to (key channels) | Tick |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GameStateMachine` | Top-level flow (Bootstrap → MainMenu → LevelSelect → Playing → Paused → Results); owns scene transitions; thin — no gameplay rules (states detailed in §3) | current/previous `GameState`, transition log | `Ev_GameStateChanged` requests, `Ev_PauseRequested` | Update (transition evaluation) |
| `LevelManager` | Level lifecycle Load → Intro → Play → Evaluate → Results; queue advancement; retry/undo orchestration (skeleton in §6) | runtime level state, piece queue, level timer | `Ev_PieceReleased`, `Ev_StabilityWindowCompleted`, `Ev_LevelFailed` | event-driven |
| `PieceSpawner` | Instantiate pieces from the queue via `PoolManager`; attach views + `IBlockBehaviour` components (§8) | active piece registry | `Ev_PieceOffered` | event-driven |
| `StabilityMonitor` | Settling detection, the 3-second stability window, water-contact checks, stack integrity (full skeleton §6) | per-piece velocity/height history, window state | `Ev_PieceSettled`, `Ev_WaterContact` | fixed cadence inside `PhysicsStepper` (240 Hz target, §6) |
| `ScoreController` | Applies the §3 scoring formula, star thresholds, Endurance lives (formula is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** beyond the documented speed+lives+difficulty factors) | score, multiplier, Swift Stacker fast-clear chain state (`chainCount` per team, §3.7.5 — updated from `Ev_LevelCompleted` round results; resets on a slow win or loss) | `Ev_PieceSettled`, `Ev_BlockBehaviourTriggered` (risk multipliers), `Ev_LevelCompleted` | event-driven |
| `InputRouter` | Binds the active `IPieceInputProvider` (§7) to carrying-piece commands; device hot-swap; input buffering per §7 | provider registry, buffered intents | Input System callbacks | Update (consume at sim boundary) |
| `BlockBehaviourDriver` | Drives `IBlockBehaviour` lifecycle hooks for the four documented specials + the linked/seesaw **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** extension (§8) | behaviour instances per piece | `Ev_PieceSettled`, timer ticks | fixed cadence + events |
| `SaveSystem` | `ISaveable` aggregation, versioned JSON at `persistentDataPath`, cloud sync hooks (§6/§14/§19) | save schema version, dirty flag | `Ev_LevelCompleted`, `Ev_SaveRequested` | event-driven |
| `PoolManager` | Generic pooling (skill pattern) for pieces, VFX, splash particles | pools per prefab | — | lazy |
| `AudioDirector` | AudioMixer snapshots, adaptive music layers tied to stack tension (§6/§9) | AudioSource pools, layer weights | `Ev_StabilityWindowStarted`, `Ev_StackCollapsed`, `Ev_WaterContact` | event-driven |
| `CameraDirector` | Framing from `LevelDefinition` camera hints; subtle dynamic FOV/shake on collapse (juice list §6/§9) | virtual cameras, impulse listeners | `Ev_StackCollapsed`, `Ev_LevelLoaded` | LateUpdate |
| `VFXDirector` | Splash, settle dust, shatter, gravity-flip triggers (§9) | particle pools | `Ev_WaterContact`, `Ev_BlockBehaviourTriggered` | event-driven |
| `HapticsDirector` | Gamepad rumble for game events per the canonical §13.4 haptic event map; pause/resume/stop gating with the pause menu (§7.4.5) | active gamepad handle, motor-stop deadline | `Ev_PieceSettled`, `Ev_StabilityWindowProgress`, `Ev_WaterContact`, `Ev_StackCollapsed` | Update (time-based motor stop) |
| `ContentLibrary` | Addressables load/unload of worlds, levels, piece definitions; validation at load (§5) | catalogs, ref counts | load requests | async |
| `ConfigService` | Merges `GameConfig` + platform overrides at Boot (§4.10); publishes the immutable runtime snapshot | `RuntimeConfig` snapshot | — | Boot once |
| `PlatformService` | Steam / mobile / Xbox adapters behind one interface: init, achievements, leaderboards (§18/§19) | platform handles | `Ev_LevelCompleted`, `Ev_ScoreChanged` | event-driven |

Scalability check (ultra-master skill: architecture must survive 10x content): none of these systems loop over "all levels"; content volume (§5's 8 worlds × 25 levels) touches only `ContentLibrary` and Addressables groups.

### 4.5 Event architecture

**Choice: typed ScriptableObject event channels as the cross-system backbone, plain C# events for intra-system hot paths. [ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Justification against plain C# `event`s: SO channels (the skill's event-bus pattern) decouple raisers from listeners at the asset level, so `Aob.Gameplay` raises events that `Aob.UI`/`Aob.Platform` consume without any assembly back-reference (matching the §4.3 dependency arrows); channels are inspectable, lockable, and testable in the Editor (a listener component can be attached in a debug scene to observe production traffic); and channel lookup happens at bind time, not per raise, so the per-raise cost is a delegate invocation with zero allocations. Plain C# events remain the rule *inside* a system for per-frame, per-piece notifications (e.g., `StabilityMonitor`'s internal per-piece updates), where an SO hop would add indirection for no decoupling value. `UnityEvent`/`SendMessage` are banned (skill anti-patterns: reflection cost, no compile-time safety).

Channel base (skill conventions; no hot-path allocations — the listener list is pre-allocated and iterated in reverse):

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>Typed ScriptableObject event channel; the game's cross-system bus.</summary>
[CreateAssetMenu(fileName = "Ev_New", menuName = "AoB/Events/Typed Event")]
public class GameEventChannel<TPayload> : ScriptableObject
{
    #region Private Fields

    private readonly List<IGameEventListener<TPayload>> _listeners = new List<IGameEventListener<TPayload>>(32);

    #endregion

    #region Public Methods

    /// <summary>Raises the channel. Reverse iteration so listeners may unsubscribe during raise.</summary>
    public void Raise(in TPayload payload)
    {
        for (int i = _listeners.Count - 1; i >= 0; i--)
        {
            _listeners[i].OnEventRaised(in payload);
        }
    }

    public void Register(IGameEventListener<TPayload> listener) => _listeners.Add(listener);

    public void Unregister(IGameEventListener<TPayload> listener) => _listeners.Remove(listener);

    #endregion
}
```

The named channel set (**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; payloads in parentheses; emitters → consumers):

| # | Channel | Payload | Raised by | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Ev_LevelLoaded` | `LevelContext` | `LevelManager` | CameraDirector, AudioDirector, UI, StabilityMonitor |
| 2 | `Ev_LevelIntroFinished` | — | UI intro sequence | `LevelManager`, InputRouter (enable carry) |
| 3 | `Ev_PieceOffered` | `PieceDefinition`, queue index | `LevelManager` | PieceSpawner, UI (queue preview) |
| 4 | `Ev_PieceGrabbed` | `PieceHandle` | InputRouter | AudioDirector, VFXDirector |
| 5 | `Ev_PieceRotated` | `PieceHandle`, delta degrees | InputRouter | AudioDirector, CameraDirector (micro-punch) |
| 6 | `Ev_PieceReleased` | `PieceHandle`, pose | InputRouter | `LevelManager`, StabilityMonitor |
| 7 | `Ev_PieceSettled` | `PieceHandle` | StabilityMonitor | ScoreController, BlockBehaviourDriver, HapticsDirector |
| 8 | `Ev_StackCollapsed` | `CollapseReport` | StabilityMonitor | CameraDirector (shake), AudioDirector, VFXDirector, HapticsDirector |
| 9 | `Ev_WaterContact` | `PieceHandle`, contact point | StabilityMonitor | `LevelManager` (fail rule, §3), VFXDirector (splash), AudioDirector, HapticsDirector |
| 10 | `Ev_StabilityWindowStarted` | duration | StabilityMonitor | AudioDirector (tension layer), UI (countdown) |
| 11 | `Ev_StabilityWindowProgress` | lights lit (1–3) | StabilityMonitor | UI — drives the three sequential green lights documented for the original ([T01 digest]; sources in §1); HapticsDirector (per-light pulse, §13.4) |
| 12 | `Ev_StabilityWindowCompleted` | — | StabilityMonitor | `LevelManager` → `Ev_LevelCompleted` |
| 13 | `Ev_LevelCompleted` | `LevelResult` (score, stars, time) | `LevelManager` | SaveSystem, ScoreController (finalize), PlatformService (leaderboard/achievements) |
| 14 | `Ev_LevelFailed` | `FailureCause` | `LevelManager` | UI, AudioDirector, PlatformService |
| 15 | `Ev_ScoreChanged` | `ScoreDelta` | ScoreController | UI, PlatformService |
| 16 | `Ev_BlockBehaviourTriggered` | `BlockBehaviourType`, `PieceHandle` | BlockBehaviourDriver | ScoreController (multipliers), VFXDirector, AudioDirector |
| 17 | `Ev_GameStateChanged` | from/to `GameState` | `GameStateMachine` | all directors (pause/resume), SaveSystem (autosave on exit) |
| 18 | `Ev_LifeLost` | lives remaining | `LevelManager` (Endurance mode, §3.3.4) | HUD (lives counter), Endurance session-end check |
| 19 | `Ev_PauseRequested` | — | InputRouter (pause intent, §7) / UI | `GameStateMachine` (Playing ⇄ Paused, §3.2) |
| 20 | `Ev_SaveRequested` | — | `GameStateMachine` (autosave on state exit), UI (explicit save) | `SaveSystem` |

This registry is the canonical channel set: §3.3.4's loop-event table mirrors it (queue advance is carried by `Ev_PieceOffered`'s queue-index payload — there is no separate queue-advanced channel; §6's internal `LevelManager` notification stays a plain C# event per the intra-system rule above).

**Unity External Tools** (Edit → Preferences → External Tools):

- **Script editor:** per-host choice above; "External Script Editor Args" left default (`$(Project)`/`$(File)` line-jump form).
- **Android toolchain — accept the "Installed with Unity" checkboxes** so the whole team and CI (§16) share one toolchain instead of divergent local installs. Unity 6.6 (6000.2–6000.4+ row) ships: SDK Build-tools 36.0.0, SDK Command-line tools 16, SDK Platform-tools 36.0.0, NDK r27c (27.2.12479018), JDK 17 (OpenJDK), CMake 3.22.1 ([Android dependency versions](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-supported-dependency-versions.html), accessed 2026-09-24); Gradle 9.3.1 with Android Gradle Plugin 9.1.1 from 6000.6.3f1+ (docs-built 2026-09-21, T07 track). Android min graphics is OpenGL ES 3.1 (ES 3.0 support removed in 6.6) — we are Vulkan-first anyway ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24).
- **Xcode (macOS host):** Unity's iOS page "recommends Xcode 16 or later", but Apple's hard upload floor is stricter — since 2026-04-28 App Store Connect requires Xcode 26+ with the iOS 26 SDK ([Apple upcoming requirements](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/), accessed 2026-09-24); Apple's rule wins, and Unity 6.6's supported iOS floor is iOS 15 ([iOS requirements](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/ios-requirements-and-compatibility.html), accessed 2026-09-24). iOS Player Settings detail lives in §18.

### 4.7 Editor and Inspector settings; per-scene organization

**Scene list [ORIGINAL DESIGN]:**

| Scene | Purpose | From template | Lighting window |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Boot` | ConfigService merge, Addressables init, PlatformService init, scene flow hand-off | BootTemplate | None (ambient only) |
| `MainMenu` | Front-end, mode select (Arcade/Endurance/Infinity/Swift Stacker/Tower Tumble — §3) | MenuTemplate | Baked (static geometry) |
| `LevelSelect` | World map, unlocks, medals (§3/§5) | MenuTemplate | Baked |
| `Gameplay` | The one gameplay scene — every level is data (§5), not a scene | GameplayTemplate | Mixed: basin/environment baked; pieces lit by probes + main light realtime (full strategy §9) |
| `TestScenes/PhysicsLab`, `InputLab`, `PerfGym`, `RenderTest` | §14 test harnesses and §9 render matrix | LabTemplate | Per-test |

Templates are captured with the scene-template package (canonical scaffolds registered as templates, so new test scenes inherit wiring); import **presets** in `_Project/Editor/Presets` default mesh/texture import settings for the §9 pipeline — including the 6.6 gotcha that meshes used by `MeshCollider` must now explicitly enable Read/Write or the build fails, so the piece-mesh preset sets it deliberately ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Baked lighting uses the new Unity Compute Light Baker (the Progressive CPU baker is deprecated in 6.6) ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

**Per-scene Editor organization [ORIGINAL DESIGN]:** Scene view lighting toggled off for graybox passes; grid snap set to the piece-module size (0.25 move / 15° rotate — must divide the 45° rotation step from §3); two locked Inspectors pinned on `StabilityMonitor` (debug mode) and the active piece during tuning; Preset Manager defaults bound to the import presets; saved Editor layout shipped in repo (`UserSettings/` ignored, layout exported to `_Project/Editor/Layouts`).

**Tag/Layer table [ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (layers 0–5 keep Unity defaults; 4 keeps its built-in name "Water"):

| Bit | Layer | Used by | Collision notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | `Piece` | stackable pieces | collides with Piece, Platform |
| 7 | `Platform` | basin/platform geometry | collides with Piece only |
| 8 | `WaterSensor` | water trigger volume | trigger vs Piece; never physical |
| 9 | `Debris` | shatter residue (non-colliding visual) | matrix row cleared — no physics interaction (§8) |
| 10 | `Environment` | static dressing | collides with nothing dynamic |
| 11 | `PieceGhost` | carried-piece preview | matrix row cleared — no physics during carry (§3/§7) |

The Layer Collision Matrix is pruned to exactly these pairs ([Physics Manager reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-PhysicsManager.html), accessed 2026-09-24); UI does not get a physics layer (uGUI canvases, §9). Tags: only `PieceRoot` and `WaterVolume` (debug/telemetry filters) — tag use is deliberately minimal.
