Every `ProjectSettings/*.asset` we touch, and why. (The on-disk file list below follows the standard convention; verify against the actual 6000.6 project on creation — cheap self-check.)

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: ProjectSettings folder inventory is convention-level knowledge (T10 medium confidence); confirm the exact asset filenames on first project creation and correct this table in-repo. -->

| Asset | What we change | Why / value |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectSettings.asset` (Player) | Company/product name, version; **Color Space = Linear** (§4.1); **Active Input Handling = Both**; icon defaults | Active Input Handling: the Input System is the default solution since Unity 6 and ships as a built-in module from 6.6, while the legacy `DefaultEventSystem.LegacyInputProcessor` was removed in 6.6 ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), accessed 2026-09-24; [Input System article](https://discussions.unity.com/t/get-up-and-running-with-the-input-system/1620267), accessed 2026-09-24). All first-party code uses the Input System exclusively via §7; **Both** is kept as transitional safety so third-party/editor tooling that still polls legacy axes (`ENABLE_LEGACY_INPUT_MANAGER`) keeps working at zero measurable cost for this workload — flip to Input-System-only after the §14 supply-chain audit confirms no legacy Input usage. Editor restart required on change (T09). |
| `EditorSettings.asset` | Asset Serialization = **Force Text** (the default) + **Reduce version control noise** on | One-line reference serialization for clean diffs ([Editor settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-EditorManager.html), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| `VersionControlSettings.asset` | Mode + Smart Merge enabled; `mergespecfile.txt` routes git merges to UnityYAMLMerge | Scene/prefab YAML merges ([Smart Merge docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/SmartMerge.html), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| `QualitySettings.asset` | Quality levels (`PC_High`, `PC_Base`, `Mobile_High`, `Mobile_Base` **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** names), each assigning its URP Asset; one default per platform in the level×platform matrix | Per-level Render Pipeline assignment and per-platform defaults are Quality-settings mechanics ([Quality settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24); tier contents in §9 |
| `TimeManager.asset` | Fixed Timestep **0.0041667 (1/240)** per §6.2 (default is 0.02, not printed on the docs page — set explicitly, per T11); Maximum Allowed Timestep kept at **0.3333** (not lowered); Time Scale 1 | Chosen contract is §6.3 Option A — Fixed Update @ 1/240: the Fixed Timestep IS the 240 Hz simulation cadence (Physics 2D Simulation Mode = Fixed Update; the engine steps physics immediately after FixedUpdate; only physics-adjacent systems may subscribe to FixedUpdate, §6.3). `PhysicsStepper.Awake()` pins `Time.fixedDeltaTime` = 1/240 and `Time.maximumDeltaTime` = 0.3333f in code so every build and CI runner shares the contract; the asset values match §6.2's "Ours" column (belt-and-suspenders — the pin is enforcement, not a substitute). Maximum Allowed 0.3333 caps worst-case catch-up so one slow frame cannot queue dozens of 240 Hz steps; fixed-dt `Physics2D.Simulate` is fallback Option B only, not the shipped mechanism ([Time Manager reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-TimeManager.html), accessed 2026-09-24; T11). |
| `DynamicsManager.asset` (Physics 3D) | Solver iterations/velocity iterations, Sleep Threshold, Default Contact Offset, gravity; multithreaded-vs-single-threaded simulation dropdown (new in 6.6) | Full tuning table with values and rationale is §6's deliverable; the 6.6 threading dropdown is documented in the release notes ([6000.6.0f1 notes](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), accessed 2026-09-24). Layer matrix pruning per §4.7. |
| `Physics2DSettings.asset` | 2D solver iterations + 2D layer matrix (only if §6 selects the 2D engine) | Settings live in `ProjectSettings/Physics2DSettings.asset` (T10, medium confidence — same verify note as above) |
| `GraphicsSettings.asset` | Default Render Pipeline Asset (fallback only — real assignment is per Quality level); shader stripping: Lightmap/Fog Modes Automatic, **Instancing Variants Strip Unused** | Automatic stripping interacts with Addressables-loaded shaders — the known trap when variants live outside built scenes ([Graphics settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-GraphicsSettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24); mitigation in §5/§9 |
| `TagManager.asset` | Layers/tags per §4.7 | — |
| `AudioManager.asset` | DSP buffer size per platform (§6 audio subsystem owns values) | — |
| `InputManager.asset` (legacy) | **Untouched** | Superseded by the Input System module (§7); file remains because Active Input Handling = Both keeps the legacy axis definitions resident |
| `EditorBuildSettings.asset` | Scene list for Editor play-entry | Build scene lists now live in Build Profile assets (§4.9); this file only feeds the Editor's play-from-top workflow |
| `NavMeshAreas.asset` | **Untouched — no navigation in this game** | NavMesh unused; keep defaults, ship no NavMesh components (size + cert surface) |
| `VFXManager.asset` | Defaults until §9 fixes the VFX Graph vs particle split | §9 |
| `UnityConnectSettings.asset`, `ClusterInputManager.asset`, `PresetManager.asset` | Untouched | — |

**Managed stripping** (Player → Optimization): IL2CPP for every shipping target (§4.9); stripping level raised stepwise (Minimal → Low) only with a full build+Addressables test pass at each step, preserving reflection-touched code via `[Preserve]`/`link.xml` ([managed code stripping docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/managed-code-stripping.html), accessed 2026-09-24). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact stripping level names per backend (Minimal/Low/Medium/High) are knowledge-level, not page-verified — confirm in the 6.6 Player Settings UI. -->

### 4.9 Build profiles and scripting defines

Unity 6 replaces Build Settings with **File → Build Profiles**. Semantics that shape our setup ([build profiles docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/build-profiles.html), accessed 2026-09-24): *platform* profiles share settings (a Development Build toggle propagates across platform profiles) and "Platforms also share the same scene data across each platform profile" (quoted); *build* profiles are unlimited, custom-named, version-controllable Assets with independent settings **and their own scene lists**.

**Profile set [ORIGINAL DESIGN]:**

| Build profile | Target / host | Backend · arch | Scene list | Defines | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PC-Windows-Release` | Win64 / any host | IL2CPP · x64 | Boot, MainMenu, LevelSelect, Gameplay | `AOB_STEAM` | Graphics API order + signing in §19 |
| `PC-Windows-Dev` | Win64 / any host | IL2CPP · x64, Development + Script Debugging | + TestScenes | `AOB_STEAM;AOB_DEV` | Development flags propagate across platform profiles (docs, above) |
| `PC-macOS-Release` | osxuniversal / **macOS host** | IL2CPP · Universal (Apple Silicon + x64) | shared four | `AOB_STEAM` | IL2CPP same-host rule: "to build a macOS Player with IL2CPP, you must build on macOS" ([IL2CPP intro, 6.3](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Never Intel-only: x86_64 macOS players are deprecated upstream ([6.7 Beta mac requirements](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.7/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html), accessed 2026-09-24); Metal-only in practice |
| `Android-Release` | Android / any host | IL2CPP · ARM64, AAB | shared four | `AOB_MOBILE` | Play requires API 36 targeting for new apps/updates from 2026-08-31 ([Play target API policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878), accessed 2026-09-24); Gradle/AGP per §4.6 |
| `Android-Dev` | Android / any host | as above + Development | + TestScenes | `AOB_MOBILE;AOB_DEV` | Device profilers §18 |
| `iOS-Release` | iOS / **macOS host** | IL2CPP · ARM64 | shared four | `AOB_MOBILE` | Xcode project export + post-processing skeleton in §18 |
| `Xbox-Dev` | Xbox / Windows host | IL2CPP | shared four | `AOB_XBOX` | Gated on ID@Xbox (§19); profile created but not exercised until access lands |

Scene-list discipline falls out of the profile model: the four shipping scenes are identical everywhere (levels are data, §5), and TestScenes exist only in Dev profiles' own lists. Build-profile assets are committed; the Unity CLI can create/inspect profiles (`--create-profile`, requires Unity 6000.0+) and per-project defaults live in `ProjectSettings/UnityCliConfig.json` ([Unity CLI reference](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference), accessed 2026-09-24) — that file carries build/test defaults only, never credentials (DevSecOps: secrets ride env vars in §16).

**Scripting defines [ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (besides built-ins `UNITY_STANDALONE_WIN`/`UNITY_STANDALONE_OSX`/`UNITY_ANDROID`/`UNITY_IOS`): `AOB_STEAM`, `AOB_MOBILE`, `AOB_XBOX`, `AOB_DEV` (asserts, debug draw, cheat keys), `AOB_PHYSICS_DIAG` (on-screen physics telemetry, §6). They gate code, never content; the full platform `#if` directive table (including where each is allowed to appear — §4.3's `Aob.Platform`-only rule) is §19's cross-platform deliverable.

### 4.10 Config file strategy

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — a three-layer config merge, because tuning constants (the 3-second stability window, 45° rotation step) are documented game rules that must stay adjustable for feel iteration (§3) while platform values (frame pacing, render scale) must vary per target (§9/§18/§19):

1. **`GameConfig` SO** — base tuning: `StabilityWindowSeconds = 3` (documented core rule, §1/§3), `RotationStepDegrees = 45`, queue-preview count, water-failure policy, audio ducking curves, camera juice intensities.
2. **Platform override SOs** — `WindowsOverrides`, `macOSOverrides`, `AndroidOverrides`, `iOSOverrides`, `XboxOverrides`: frame pacing (`vSyncCount` vs `targetFrameRate` — the two are mutually exclusive and docs recommend vSyncCount where smooth pacing matters and the platform has it ([targetFrameRate reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24; mobile policy lands in §18), quality-level default, texture-streaming budget overrides, save slot roots, feature flags (leaderboards on/off per platform).
3. **Device-class overrides** (optional, mobile only): low-RAM shader/quality floor — applied from the §18 device matrix.

Merge order is fixed — base ← platform ← device-class — executed once in `Boot` before the first gameplay scene, producing an immutable snapshot; runtime code reads the snapshot, never the SOs (avoids accidental mid-level tuning drift and keeps hot-path reads allocation-free). User-facing settings (volume, rebinding, language) are *not* config — they are player data through `SaveSystem` (§6/§14). Config SOs are content: reviewed in PRs like code, never remote-loaded in v1, and never contain secrets.

```csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core
{
    /// <summary>Immutable, merged view of GameConfig + platform overrides; read-only at runtime.</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public sealed class RuntimeConfig
    {
        #region Public Fields

        public float StabilityWindowSeconds = 3f;      // documented core rule (§1)
        public float RotationStepDegrees = 45f;        // documented core rule (§1)
        public int TargetFrameRate = 60;
        public int VSyncCount = 0;

        #endregion
    }

    /// <summary>Boot-time merge of base GameConfig with the active platform override asset.</summary>
    public sealed class ConfigService
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private const string OverrideResourceError = nameof(PlatformConfigOverrides) + " asset missing for platform ";

        private readonly RuntimeConfig _snapshot = new RuntimeConfig();

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        /// <summary>The frozen runtime configuration; null until <see cref="Merge"/> runs in Boot.</summary>
        public RuntimeConfig Snapshot => _snapshot;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Applies base values, then platform overrides. Runs exactly once, in Boot.</summary>
        public void Merge(GameConfig baseConfig, PlatformConfigOverrides platformOverride)
        {
            if (baseConfig == null)
            {
                throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(baseConfig));
            }
            if (platformOverride == null)
            {
                throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(platformOverride), OverrideResourceError + Application.platform);
            }

            _snapshot.StabilityWindowSeconds = baseConfig.StabilityWindowSeconds;
            _snapshot.RotationStepDegrees = baseConfig.RotationStepDegrees;
            _snapshot.TargetFrameRate = baseConfig.TargetFrameRate;
            _snapshot.VSyncCount = baseConfig.VSyncCount;

            platformOverride.Apply(_snapshot); // override fields only where overridden; JSON-diffable in tests
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

`GameConfig` and `PlatformConfigOverrides` are plain serialized SOs in `_Project/Settings/` (field lists above; full skeletons with 6.6-native dictionary serialization for per-mode tuning live with §5's data model, where per-mode `GameModeDefinition` deltas consume them). The merge is covered by an edit-mode test asserting platform override precedence (§14) — config regressions fail CI, not playtests.

Frame pacing and quality policy consuming this config: desktop profiles use `QualitySettings.vSyncCount = 1` (hardware sync; docs-recommended where available), mobile/TV-class targets use `vSyncCount = 0` + `Application.targetFrameRate = 60` with the documented battery fallback (−1 → fixed 30 fps on mobile) and non-divisor rates rounding down (25 → 20 on 60 Hz) ([targetFrameRate reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24); iOS 120 Hz stays off unless ProMotion is deliberately enabled later (default off for new projects, same source). Resolution scaling (`Render Scale` scales the render target, not device resolution — URP asset semantics) is owned by the §9 quality tiers.

## 5. Core Systems A — Data & Content Model

Everything the game treats as content — piece shapes, block behaviours, levels, worlds, game modes, localization — is authored as version-controlled ScriptableObject (SO) assets, never as scene junk or code constants. This section specifies each content type as a full C# data contract, the authoring tooling that produces the 200-level campaign, the validation math that gates it, and the localization envelope. Runtime consumers (LevelManager, StabilityMonitor, ScoreController, GameStateMachine — system map in §4, implementations in §6) only ever read these assets; the data layer performs zero per-frame work and never mutates SO state at runtime.

### 5.1 Data-layer inventory and ground rules

| Asset type | File prefix | Folder (per §4 `_Project/` layout) | Primary runtime consumer | Specified in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PieceDefinition` | `Piece_*.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Pieces` | PieceSpawner / LevelManager (§6); tray UI | §5.2 |
| `BlockBehaviourParams` (nested) | — | — | BlockBehaviourDriver (§8) | §5.3 |
| `LevelDefinition` | `Level_W{n}_L{nn}.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Levels/World{n}` | LevelManager (§6) | §5.4 |
| `WorldDefinition` | `World_{n}.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Worlds` | Progression / menu flow (§3, §6) | §5.5 |
| `GameModeDefinition` | `Mode_*.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Modes` | GameStateMachine (§6) | §5.5 |
| `EnvironmentThemeDefinition` | `Theme_*.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Themes` | CameraDirector, AudioDirector (§6, §9) | §5.4 |
| `PiecePaletteEntry` | `Palette_*.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Palettes` | Material resolution; accessibility palettes (§14) | §5.2 |
| `ScoringProfile` | `Scoring_*.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/Modes` | ScoreController (§6) | §5.5.2 (values), math in §3 |
| `ContentLibrary` | `ContentLibrary.asset` | `ScriptableObjects/` | Boot-time integrity check (§4) | §5.6 |

Ground rules (enforced by code review checklist in §14 and by `OnValidate` clamps):

1. **Immutability.** SOs are read-only after `OnEnable`. Any value that changes during play (score, timer, queue cursor, behaviour state) lives on runtime components (§6, §8), never on the definition assets. This is what lets one `LevelDefinition` be retried, replayed, and ghosted (§3) without asset pollution.
2. **Deterministic serialization.** Content ships as ordered lists with parallel key/value arrays — no dictionaries, no hash-ordered structures. Unity 6.6 does add serialized `Dictionary` support (per the T02 release-note sweep), but we deliberately keep the parallel-list encoding so the content schema survives the planned migration onto Unity 6.7 LTS (§4, §21) without a re-serialization pass.
3. **Referential integrity.** Cross-references are direct asset references (GUID-backed). Human-readable ids (`pieceId`, `levelNameKey`) are kept redundant for save files, telemetry, and Addressables debugging, and are validated for uniqueness at boot by `ContentLibrary` and at authoring time by the validator (§5.6).
4. **Behaviour is data, not components.** The data layer encodes special-block rules as `BlockBehaviourType` + `BlockBehaviourParams`. `IBlockBehaviour` runtime components (§8) are attached by the spawner from this data; no interface-typed serialized fields exist anywhere in the data layer (Unity cannot serialize them portably).
5. **Two-sided validation.** Cheap clamps run in `OnValidate` while authoring; the full rule set (mass budget, tipping heuristic, feasibility) runs in `LevelValidator` on save, on demand in the Level Editor, and over all 200 levels in CI (§16).

### 5.2 `PieceDefinition` — the piece data contract

The original's shape inventory is officially documented: the Wii edition shipped "14 Shapes + 2 Special Shapes" ([official Wii About, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20091116220135/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**, and every edition from the 2012 3DS release onward ships "16 Shapes + 5 Special Shapes" ([official 3DS About, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**. Our clone matches the best-documented configuration: 16 base shapes + 5 specials = 21 master `PieceDefinition` assets; palette entries (§5.2.3) multiply the visual variants without touching physics.

```csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Immutable data definition for one placeable piece shape. Authored once in the editor;
    /// read-only at runtime. All mutable state (transform, body, behaviour timers) lives on the
    /// spawned piece component owned by LevelManager (see §6).
    /// </summary>
    [CreateAssetMenu(fileName = "Piece_New", menuName = "AoB/Content/Piece Definition")]
    public class PieceDefinition : ScriptableObject
    {
        #region Constants

        /// <summary>Number of discrete orientation steps in a full turn.</summary>
        public const int RotationStepCount = 8;

        /// <summary>Degrees per orientation step; the 45-degree rotation model is specified in §3.</summary>
        public const float RotationStepDegrees = 45f;

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Identity")]
        [Tooltip("Stable authoring id, e.g. 'base_rect2x1'. Never rename after ship; used by save files and telemetry.")]
        [SerializeField] private string pieceId = "piece_new";
        [Tooltip("Localization key for the display name, e.g. 'piece.rect2x1.name'.")]
        [SerializeField] private string displayNameKey = "piece.new.name";

        [Header("Visuals")]
        [SerializeField] private Mesh mesh;
        [Tooltip("Icon shown in the upcoming-pieces tray and the pause encyclopedia.")]
        [SerializeField] private Sprite iconSprite;
        [Tooltip("Palette entry resolving material variant plus accessibility color mapping (see §14).")]
        [SerializeField] private PiecePaletteEntry paletteEntry;

        [Header("Physics — authored defaults; live tuning tables live in §6")]
        [Tooltip("Mass in Regular Mass Units (RMU). One 'regular' block = 1.0 RMU by convention.")]
        [SerializeField] private float mass = 1f;
        [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f)] private float friction = 0.4f;
        [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f)] private float bounciness = 0.05f;
        [Tooltip("Optional explicit local center of mass; unchecked = computed from collider geometry.")]
        [SerializeField] private bool hasCenterOfMassOverride;
        [SerializeField] private Vector2 centerOfMassOverride = Vector2.zero;

        [Header("Collider")]
        [SerializeField] private PieceColliderProfile colliderProfile;

        [Header("Rotation")]
        [Tooltip("Bit i set = orientation (i * 45 degrees) is legal for this piece. 0xFF = all eight.")]
        [SerializeField] private int allowedRotationMask = 0xFF;

        [Header("Special Behaviour — runtime driver specified in §8")]
        [SerializeField] private BlockBehaviourType behaviourType = BlockBehaviourType.Base;
        [SerializeField] private BlockBehaviourParams behaviourParams = new BlockBehaviourParams();

        [Header("Scoring — baked by the §5.6 authoring tool via ScoreController.PlacementPointsFor (§6)")]
        [Tooltip("Points awarded when this piece is placed. Baked at authoring time as round(100 × C × R) (§3.7.1) so the runtime reads the authored value and never re-derives it.")]
        [SerializeField] private int placementPoints = 100;

        [Header("Authoring Metadata — editor validation only (see §5.6)")]
        [Tooltip("Conservative local-space extents (width, height) used by LevelValidator heuristics.")]
        [SerializeField] private Vector2 authoringFootprint = Vector2.one;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public string PieceId => pieceId;
        public string DisplayNameKey => displayNameKey;
        public Mesh Mesh => mesh;
        public Sprite IconSprite => iconSprite;
        public PiecePaletteEntry PaletteEntry => paletteEntry;
        public float Mass => mass;
        public float Friction => friction;
        public float Bounciness => bounciness;
        public BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType => behaviourType;
        public BlockBehaviourParams BehaviourParams => behaviourParams;
        public int PlacementPoints => placementPoints;
        public Vector2 AuthoringFootprint => authoringFootprint;
        public bool HasCenterOfMassOverride => hasCenterOfMassOverride;
        public Vector2 CenterOfMassOverride => centerOfMassOverride;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Returns true when the given 45-degree step index is a legal orientation.</summary>
        public bool IsRotationAllowed(int stepIndex)
        {
            int normalized = ((stepIndex % RotationStepCount) + RotationStepCount) % RotationStepCount;
            return (allowedRotationMask & (1 << normalized)) != 0;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Snaps an arbitrary step index to the nearest legal orientation, searching forward then
        /// backward. Returns -1 when no orientation is legal (authoring error caught in §5.6).
        /// </summary>
        public int ClampToNearestAllowedRotation(int stepIndex)
        {
            if (allowedRotationMask == 0)
            {
                return -1;
            }

            for (int offset = 0; offset < RotationStepCount; offset++)
            {
                int forward = ((stepIndex + offset) % RotationStepCount + RotationStepCount) % RotationStepCount;
                if ((allowedRotationMask & (1 << forward)) != 0)
                {
                    return forward;
                }

                int backward = ((stepIndex - offset) % RotationStepCount + RotationStepCount) % RotationStepCount;
                if ((allowedRotationMask & (1 << backward)) != 0)
                {
                    return backward;
                }
            }

            return -1;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Validation

        private void OnValidate()
        {
            if (mass <= 0f)
            {
                mass = 1f;
                Debug.LogWarning($"[{nameof(PieceDefinition)}] {pieceId}: mass must be positive; reset to 1 RMU.", this);
            }

            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(pieceId))
            {
                Debug.LogWarning($"[{nameof(PieceDefinition)}] missing {nameof(pieceId)} on {name}.", this);
            }

            if (allowedRotationMask == 0)
            {
                Debug.LogWarning($"[{nameof(PieceDefinition)}] {pieceId}: no legal orientations; reset to all.", this);
                allowedRotationMask = 0xFF;
            }

            if (behaviourType == BlockBehaviourType.Base && behaviourParams.HasNonDefaultValues)
            {
                Debug.LogWarning($"[{nameof(PieceDefinition)}] {pieceId}: params set on Base type are ignored.", this);
            }
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

#### 5.2.1 Field provenance and defaults

All numeric defaults in the skeleton are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — the original's internal physics configuration is not documented in any fetched source (T01 gap list), so mass, friction, bounciness, and centre-of-mass values are ours, tuned against the §6 physics tables. One anchor exists: the breakable's load limit is documented behaviorally as "no more than three other regulars" ([Cubed3 Wii U review](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**, which fixes the Regular Mass Unit convention: 1 RMU = the mass of one regular block, and the breakable's default `maxSupportedMassRmu = 3.0` is a direct transcription of that fact.

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pieceId` / `displayNameKey` | string | Stable identity; localization lookup | `"piece_new"` | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `mesh` / `iconSprite` | refs | 3D mesh; 2D tray icon | — | pipeline §9, §16 |
| `paletteEntry` | SO ref | Material variant + accessibility color slot | — | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `mass` | float (RMU) | Physics mass; also drives validation math (§5.6) | 1.0 | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `friction` / `bounciness` | float 0–1 | Physics material (2D/3D per §6 decision) | 0.4 / 0.05 | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `centerOfMassOverride` | Vector2 | Asymmetric pieces (L-shapes, wedges) | off | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `colliderProfile` | nested class | Collider geometry for either engine backend (§6) | box 1×1 | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `allowedRotationMask` | 8-bit int | Legal resting orientations | `0xFF` | mechanism **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; 45° step documented below |
| `behaviourType` + `behaviourParams` | enum + class | Special rules (§5.3) | `Base` | mixed, see §5.3 |
| `placementPoints` | int | Placement score consumed at runtime by ScoreController (§6); baked by the §5.6 authoring tool via `ScoreController.PlacementPointsFor` as §3.7.1's `round(100 × C × R)` | 100 | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `authoringFootprint` | Vector2 | Validator-only conservative extents | (1, 1) | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |

#### 5.2.2 Rotation model in data

Rotation in 45-degree increments is documented only at tertiary level — Wikipedia's gameplay section states "The blocks can be rotated at 45° angles" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_of_Balance), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**, with no primary source among the fetched official pages. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: locate a primary/official source (manual, eShop copy, or captured footage measurement) confirming the 45-degree increment; the entire rotation mask scheme below is built on it. --> The mask design follows the §3 rotation model: bit *i* set means orientation *i* × 45° can be offered and released. Symmetric pieces simply carry sparse masks, which the input layer (§7) and the validator (§5.6) both consume through `IsRotationAllowed`:

| Shape class | Mask | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Circle | `0x01` | One orientation (rotation is a no-op) |
| Square | `0x55` | Bits 0/2/4/6 — 90° symmetry |
| 2×1 rectangle | `0x11` | Bits 0/4 — 180° symmetry |
| Scalene triangle | `0x0F` | Bits 0–3 — right-triangle grid orientations |
| Irregular (L, arc) | `0xFF` | All eight orientations meaningful |

#### 5.2.3 Supporting types: collider profile and palette entry

The collider profile intentionally describes geometry, not an engine collider type, so the 2D-versus-3D physics decision (§6) does not bifurcate the content format — a `Polygon` profile becomes a `PolygonCollider2D` under Physics2D or a convex `MeshCollider` under PhysX.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>Engine-agnostic collider geometry for one piece (consumed by the §6 spawner).</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class PieceColliderProfile
    {
        public enum ShapeKind { Box, Polygon, Circle, Capsule }

        [SerializeField] private ShapeKind kind = ShapeKind.Box;
        [SerializeField] private Vector2 size = Vector2.one;          // Box / Capsule
        [SerializeField] private float radius = 0.5f;                 // Circle
        [SerializeField] private List<Vector2> polygonPoints;         // Polygon, local space, convex, CW

        public ShapeKind Kind => kind;
        public Vector2 Size => size;
        public float Radius => radius;
        public IReadOnlyList<Vector2> PolygonPoints => polygonPoints;
    }
}
```

`PiecePaletteEntry` is a small SO binding: base material reference, tint gradient slot per world theme (§9), and a colorblind-safe remap slot consumed by the accessibility layer (§14) — the original's block colors are undocumented internals, so the palette system is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

### 5.3 `BlockBehaviourType` and behaviour parameters

The enum covers the base block plus every special documented from T01, and the one extension mandated by the chief-architect decision:

```csharp
namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Catalogue of block behaviours: the base block, the four specials documented in official
    /// and review sources, and the linked/seesaw extension designed for this clone.
    /// Runtime drivers implement IBlockBehaviour (§8) and are attached from this data.
    /// </summary>
    public enum BlockBehaviourType
    {
        /// <summary>Plain piece, no special rules.</summary>
        Base = 0,

        /// <summary>Shatters when stacked load exceeds its limit (documented).</summary>
        Breakable = 1,

        /// <summary>Counts down once loaded, then breaks/vanishes (documented).</summary>
        Timed = 2,

        /// <summary>Explodes on contact with another fire piece (documented).</summary>
        Fire = 3,

        /// <summary>Inverts gravity; levels carry a top platform (documented).</summary>
        GravityInverter = 4,

        /// <summary>Original extension: linked pair sharing a virtual pivot.</summary>
        LinkedSeesaw = 5
    }
}
```

One serialized parameter block serves all types (unused fields ignored per type) — a flat class beats per-type subclasses here because the inspector surface stays uniform and the §8 driver reads a single contract:

```csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Serialized parameter block consumed by the §8 BlockBehaviourDriver. One flat class keeps
    /// inspector authoring uniform; fields not used by the active BlockBehaviourType are ignored.
    /// </summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class BlockBehaviourParams
    {
        #region Serialized Fields — Breakable

        [Tooltip("Maximum supported mass above this piece, in RMU. Documented: 'no more than three other regulars'.")]
        [SerializeField] private float maxSupportedMassRmu = 3f;
        [Tooltip("Fraction of max load at which stress telegraphing begins.")]
        [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f)] private float warnLoadFraction = 0.7f;
        [Tooltip("Delay between load-exceeded and shatter, for readability.")]
        [SerializeField] private float shatterDelaySeconds = 0.15f;

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields — Timed

        [Tooltip("Lifetime in seconds once armed. Documented trigger: armed when a piece is placed on top.")]
        [SerializeField] private float timerSeconds = 6f;
        [Tooltip("Remaining time at which the warning phase (flash + tick audio) starts.")]
        [SerializeField] private float warnRemainingSeconds = 2f;
        [Tooltip("If true, arms on placement even unloaded (level-design escape hatch).")]
        [SerializeField] private bool armImmediately;

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields — Fire

        [Tooltip("Contact-to-explosion delay; 0 = instant (documented behavior).")]
        [SerializeField] private float fuseSecondsOnContact;
        [Tooltip("Explosion impulse radius, world units.")]
        [SerializeField] private float explosionRadius = 2.5f;
        [Tooltip("Impulse magnitude applied to dynamic pieces in radius (§6 physics).")]
        [SerializeField] private float explosionImpulse = 8f;

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields — GravityInverter

        [Tooltip("Inversion duration in seconds; 0 = until the piece is destroyed or the level ends.")]
        [SerializeField] private float inversionDurationSeconds;
        [Tooltip("Levels with a gravity piece carry a top platform (documented); reserved for §8 use.")]
        [SerializeField] private bool usesTopPlatformAnchor = true;

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields — LinkedSeesaw ([ORIGINAL DESIGN])

        [Tooltip("Group id: two pieces sharing an id are linked; several pairs may coexist per level.")]
        [SerializeField] private int linkGroupId;
        [Tooltip("Virtual pivot offset from the pair midpoint, local units.")]
        [SerializeField] private Vector2 pivotOffset;
        [Tooltip("Coupling stiffness for the joint/torque coupling driving the pair (see §8).")]
        [SerializeField] private float couplingStiffness = 900f;
        [Tooltip("Maximum pivot rotation in degrees before the link snaps.")]
        [SerializeField] private float maxPivotAngleDegrees = 35f;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public float MaxSupportedMassRmu => maxSupportedMassRmu;
        public float WarnLoadFraction => warnLoadFraction;
        public float ShatterDelaySeconds => shatterDelaySeconds;
        public float TimerSeconds => timerSeconds;
        public float WarnRemainingSeconds => warnRemainingSeconds;
        public bool ArmImmediately => armImmediately;
        public float FuseSecondsOnContact => fuseSecondsOnContact;
        public float ExplosionRadius => explosionRadius;
        public float ExplosionImpulse => explosionImpulse;
        public float InversionDurationSeconds => inversionDurationSeconds;
        public bool UsesTopPlatformAnchor => usesTopPlatformAnchor;
        public int LinkGroupId => linkGroupId;
        public Vector2 PivotOffset => pivotOffset;
        public float CouplingStiffness => couplingStiffness;
        public float MaxPivotAngleDegrees => maxPivotAngleDegrees;

        /// <summary>True when any field differs from fresh defaults; used by OnValidate warnings.</summary>
        public bool HasNonDefaultValues => maxSupportedMassRmu != 3f || warnLoadFraction != 0.7f
                                           || shatterDelaySeconds != 0.15f || timerSeconds != 6f
                                           || warnRemainingSeconds != 2f || armImmediately
                                           || fuseSecondsOnContact != 0f || explosionRadius != 2.5f
                                           || explosionImpulse != 8f || inversionDurationSeconds != 0f
                                           || linkGroupId != 0;

        #endregion
    }
}
```

#### 5.3.1 Behaviour parameter table

| Type | Documented behavior (source) | Data parameters (defaults) | Provenance split |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Base** | Ordinary stacking piece | none | behavior **[DOCUMENTED]**, no params |
| **Breakable** | "one that break[s] once you put too much load on top" ([official 3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); holds "no more than three other regulars before smashing" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | `maxSupportedMassRmu = 3.0` (documented anchor), `warnLoadFraction = 0.7`, `shatterDelaySeconds = 0.15` | limit **[DOCUMENTED]**; telegraphy and delay **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| **Timed** | "or a timer runs out" (official 3DS About, above); blocks "countdown and disappear when a new piece is placed atop them" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | `timerSeconds = 6`, `warnRemainingSeconds = 2`, `armImmediately = false` | trigger semantics **[DOCUMENTED]**; durations **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (exact lifetimes undocumented) |
| **Fire** | "the fire shape explodes on contact with another fire shape" (official 3DS About, above); "flaming shapes explode when two touch" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | `fuseSecondsOnContact = 0` (instant), `explosionRadius = 2.5`, `explosionImpulse = 8` | pair-contact trigger **[DOCUMENTED]**; blast numbers **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| **GravityInverter** | "the gravity shape inverts gravity" (official 3DS About, above); gravity levels "have platforms at top AND bottom of screen and flip the stack" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | `inversionDurationSeconds = 0` (latched), `usesTopPlatformAnchor = true` | inversion + top platform **[DOCUMENTED]**; duration semantics **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| **LinkedSeesaw** | Fifth special exists from 2012 on but its identity is unverified — the archived official sentence truncates after the fourth special (T01 gap) | `linkGroupId`, `pivotOffset`, `couplingStiffness = 900`, `maxPivotAngleDegrees = 35` | entire behaviour **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** per chief-architect decision |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: identity of the original's fifth special shape (post-2012 editions). The archived official sentence cuts off at four; if a manual or eShop copy surfaces, reconcile the LinkedSeesaw extension with the real block or add the real one alongside. -->

Nintendo World Report offers an alternate reading of the specials — "shatter or disappear at contact with a similar type of block" ([NWR Wii U review](http://www.nintendoworldreport.com/review/38619/art-of-balance-wii-u-review), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]** — which suggests pair-contact semantics for breakable/timer blocks too. The data model accommodates both readings: `BlockBehaviourParams` carries per-type trigger fields, and the §8 driver selects trigger mode per piece, so a level could field either interpretation without schema change.

### 5.4 `LevelDefinition` — one playable puzzle

`LevelDefinition` is the workhorse asset: 200 of these carry the campaign. It binds the basin layout, the ordered piece queue, the optional challenge, the par/star targets, and presentation hints.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Complete authored description of one Arcade level. LevelManager (§6) instantiates basin,
    /// platforms, queue, and challenge from this asset; nothing here mutates at runtime.
    /// </summary>
    [CreateAssetMenu(fileName = "Level_W0_L00", menuName = "AoB/Content/Level Definition")]
    public class LevelDefinition : ScriptableObject
    {
        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Placement")]
        [SerializeField] private WorldDefinition world;
        [Tooltip("1-based index within the world; unique inside the world (validated, §5.6).")]
        [SerializeField] private int levelIndex = 1;
        [SerializeField] private string levelNameKey = "level.w0.l1.name";

        [Header("Basin Layout")]
        [SerializeField] private List<PlatformSpec> platforms = new List<PlatformSpec>();
        [Tooltip("Optional top platform present only in gravity-inversion levels (documented).")]
        [SerializeField] private PlatformSpec topPlatform;
        [Tooltip("World-space Y of the water surface. Water contact fails the attempt (§6 StabilityMonitor).")]
        [SerializeField] private float waterLevelY = -3.5f;
        [SerializeField] private float basinMinX = -8f;
        [SerializeField] private float basinMaxX = 8f;

        [Header("Piece Queue — ordered; index 0 is offered first")]
        [SerializeField] private List<QueueEntry> pieceQueue = new List<QueueEntry>();

        [Header("Challenge and Par")]
        [SerializeField] private ChallengeSpec challenge = new ChallengeSpec();
        [Tooltip("Target completion time in seconds for par scoring.")]
        [SerializeField] private float parTimeSeconds = 90f;
        [Tooltip("Par resting footprint width in block units (W_par, the §3.7.1 PrecisionBonus term); consumed at runtime by ScoreController via LevelManager (§6).")]
        [SerializeField] private int parFootprintWidthUnits = 9;
        [Tooltip("Retry count at or under which full star credit is kept.")]
        [SerializeField] private int parRetries;
        [Tooltip("[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Score cut-offs for the 1-3 star rating; derivation in §3.")]
        [SerializeField] private StarThresholds starThresholds = new StarThresholds();

        [Header("Presentation")]
        [SerializeField] private CameraFramingHint cameraFraming = new CameraFramingHint();
        [Tooltip("Optional per-level theme override; falls back to the owning world's theme.")]
        [SerializeField] private EnvironmentThemeDefinition themeOverride;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public WorldDefinition World => world;
        public int LevelIndex => levelIndex;
        public string LevelNameKey => levelNameKey;
        public IReadOnlyList<PlatformSpec> Platforms => platforms;
        public PlatformSpec TopPlatform => topPlatform;
        public float WaterLevelY => waterLevelY;
        public float BasinMinX => basinMinX;
        public float BasinMaxX => basinMaxX;
        public IReadOnlyList<QueueEntry> PieceQueue => pieceQueue;
        public ChallengeSpec Challenge => challenge;
        public float ParTimeSeconds => parTimeSeconds;
        public int ParFootprintWidthUnits => parFootprintWidthUnits;
        public int ParRetries => parRetries;
        public StarThresholds StarThresholds => starThresholds;
        public CameraFramingHint CameraFraming => cameraFraming;
        public EnvironmentThemeDefinition ThemeOverride => themeOverride;
        public int PieceCount => pieceQueue.Count;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Returns the queue entry offered at the given zero-based queue position.</summary>
        public QueueEntry GetQueueEntry(int index)
        {
            return pieceQueue[index];
        }

        /// <summary>Total queued mass in RMU; consumed by validator rule V3 (§5.6). Cold path only.</summary>
        public float ComputeTotalQueueMassRmu()
        {
            float total = 0f;
            for (int i = 0; i < pieceQueue.Count; i++)
            {
                total += pieceQueue[i].Piece != null ? pieceQueue[i].Piece.Mass : 0f;
            }

            return total;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Validation

        private void OnValidate()
        {
            if (parTimeSeconds <= 0f)
            {
                parTimeSeconds = 90f;
                Debug.LogWarning($"[{nameof(LevelDefinition)}] {name}: par time must be positive.", this);
            }

            for (int i = 0; i < platforms.Count; i++)
            {
                if (platforms[i] != null && platforms[i].Anchor.y - platforms[i].Thickness * 0.5f <= waterLevelY)
                {
                    Debug.LogWarning($"[{nameof(LevelDefinition)}] {name}: platform {i} top is at/below the waterline.", this);
                }
            }
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

#### 5.4.1 Nested layout types

```csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>One base platform in the basin. Floating/swaying bases are documented on the
    /// 3DS edition and later: a "floating foundation that sways on water" (Cubed3 3DS review,
    /// https://www.cubed3.com/games/reviews/nintendo-3ds/art-of-balance-touch, accessed 2026-09-24).</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class PlatformSpec
    {
        public enum BaseKind { Static, FloatingSway }

        [SerializeField] private BaseKind kind = BaseKind.Static;
        [Tooltip("Center of the platform's top surface, world space.")]
        [SerializeField] private Vector2 anchor = Vector2.zero;
        [SerializeField] private float width = 6.4f;
        [SerializeField] private float thickness = 0.6f;

        [Header("Floating Sway — kind must be FloatingSway")]
        [Tooltip("Horizontal sway amplitude, world units.")]
        [SerializeField] private float swayAmplitude = 0.35f;
        [SerializeField] private float swayPeriodSeconds = 5.2f;
        [SerializeField] private float swayPhase;

        public BaseKind Kind => kind;
        public Vector2 Anchor => anchor;
        public float Width => width;
        public float Thickness => thickness;
        public float SwayAmplitude => swayAmplitude;
        public float SwayPeriodSeconds => swayPeriodSeconds;
        public float SwayPhase => swayPhase;
    }

    /// <summary>One entry in the ordered piece queue. The tray/queue itself is documented:
    /// upcoming pieces are shown alongside play (3DS shows the selection on the lower screen —
    /// Der Spiegel, 2026-09-24 access of the 2012 review).</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class QueueEntry
    {
        [Flags]
        public enum Modifier { None = 0, HiddenUntilOffered = 1, MirrorHorizontally = 2 }

        [SerializeField] private PieceDefinition piece;
        [Tooltip("Initial 45-degree orientation step offered to the player (must satisfy the piece mask).")]
        [SerializeField] private int initialRotationStep;
        [SerializeField] private Modifier modifiers = Modifier.None;

        public PieceDefinition Piece => piece;
        public int InitialRotationStep => initialRotationStep;
        public Modifier Modifiers => modifiers;
    }

    /// <summary>Optional in-level bonus objective. The Time/Height/Balance challenge trio is
    /// documented; limit semantics and bonus values are ours (see §5.4.2).</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class ChallengeSpec
    {
        public enum Kind { None, TimeLimit, HeightTarget, Balance }

        [SerializeField] private Kind kind = Kind.None;
        [Tooltip("Seconds for TimeLimit; world units for HeightTarget; RMU tolerance for Balance.")]
        [SerializeField] private float limitValue;
        [Tooltip("Bonus points awarded on success; scoring math in §3.")]
        [SerializeField] private int bonusPoints;
        [Tooltip("True = expiry fails the level; false = only the bonus is forfeited.")]
        [SerializeField] private bool failOnExpiry;

        public Kind ChallengeKind => kind;
        public float LimitValue => limitValue;
        public int BonusPoints => bonusPoints;
        public bool FailOnExpiry => failOnExpiry;
    }

    /// <summary>[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Score cut-offs for the three stars; derivation method in §3.</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class StarThresholds
    {
        [SerializeField] private int bronze = 500;
        [SerializeField] private int silver = 1200;
        [SerializeField] private int gold = 2200;

        public int Bronze => bronze;
        public int Silver => silver;
        public int Gold => gold;
        public bool IsMonotonic => bronze <= silver && silver <= gold;
    }

    /// <summary>Camera framing request consumed by CameraDirector (§6); per-resolution execution in §9.</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public class CameraFramingHint
    {
        public enum FramingMode { FitBasin, FitStackHeight, Custom }

        [SerializeField] private FramingMode mode = FramingMode.FitBasin;
        [SerializeField] private Rect customRect = new Rect(-8f, -4f, 16f, 10f);
        [Tooltip("Padding added around the computed frame, world units.")]
        [SerializeField] private float padding = 1f;

        public FramingMode Mode => mode;
        public Rect CustomRect => customRect;
        public float Padding => padding;
    }
}
```

#### 5.4.2 Field semantics and provenance

| Field group | Design | Provenance |
|---|---|---|
| Basin + water line | 2D single-plane play over a water basin; any piece touching water fails the attempt — the core documented fail rule ([official Wii U About, archived 2016](https://web.archive.org/web/20160903223835/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/wiiu/about.php): "Watch out: Don't let any shape fall into the water!", accessed 2026-09-24) | layout concept **[DOCUMENTED]**; coordinate values **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Platform kinds | Static islands plus floating/swaying bases ("floating foundation that sways on water" — [Der Spiegel, 2012](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24; [Cubed3 3DS](https://www.cubed3.com/games/reviews/nintendo-3ds/art-of-balance-touch), accessed 2026-09-24) | sway existence **[DOCUMENTED]**; amplitude/period defaults **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `topPlatform` | Present only in gravity-inversion levels — platforms at top and bottom of the screen are documented ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | **[DOCUMENTED]** trigger, original geometry |
| Queue | Ordered fixed list per level; the upcoming-piece tray is documented on 3DS (selection on lower screen — [Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24) and referenced by reviews generally | fixed-order queue **[DOCUMENTED]**; `Modifier` flags (paced reveal, mirrored spawn) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Challenge | "Time Challenges, Height Challenges, Balance Challenges" for extra points ([official 3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); "use all pieces in a set time, build a tower as high as possible" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24); "some levels will also set a time or height limit" ([Nintendo Life WiiWare](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24) | trio **[DOCUMENTED]**; whether time expiry fails or only forfeits bonus is not pinned by sources — `failOnExpiry` defaults to `false` as **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Par targets | "Pieces" par is structurally fixed: the documented win condition requires placing ALL given pieces ("Once you place the last block in place, the structure must stay above water for three seconds" — [Nintendo Life WiiWare](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24), so queue length is the piece par. Our par vector is therefore `parTimeSeconds` + `parFootprintWidthUnits` (W_par for §3.7.1's PrecisionBonus) + `parRetries` | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Star thresholds | Three-tier per-level rating; original award systems beyond the 3DS's 13 achievements and the Endurance leaderboard inputs are undocumented | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** per chief-architect decision; derivation in §3 |
| Camera framing | Portrait/landscape basin framing differs per level shape; execution details in §6/§9 | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Env theme override | Per-world "unique lounge style" is documented ([Switch press sheet, live](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24); per-level override is ours | themes **[DOCUMENTED]** concept, override **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |

`EnvironmentThemeDefinition` (specified with §9, summarized here): sky gradient, water tint + surface material, lighting preset, ambient bed, and the world's music set — the "relaxing lounge soundtrack... 8 beautiful environments" wording is official ([Switch press sheet, live](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**; every concrete theme value is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** because the original's eight environment names/themes were never published (T01 gap).

### 5.5 `WorldDefinition` and `GameModeDefinition`

#### 5.5.1 WorldDefinition

The documented campaign shape is "Play 200 levels spread across 8 worlds, each with its own unique lounge style" ([official 3DS About, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**. Progression inside a world is free-order with skippable levels and world unlock after enough successes: "In jeder Spielwelt hat man eine gewisse Entscheidungsfreiheit, in welcher Reihenfolge man spielt. Einzelne Abschnitte kann man auch auslassen, nach genügend Erfolgen wird die nächste Spielwelt freigeschaltet." ([Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**. The threshold numbers are ours.

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace AoB.Data
{
    /// <summary>One of the eight campaign worlds: theme, level list, and unlock rule.</summary>
    [CreateAssetMenu(fileName = "World_1", menuName = "AoB/Content/World Definition")]
    public class WorldDefinition : ScriptableObject
    {
        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Identity")]
        [SerializeField] private int worldIndex = 1;                 // 1..8
        [Tooltip("World names are undocumented upstream; ours are original (see §5.7).")]
        [SerializeField] private string worldNameKey = "world.1.name";
        [SerializeField] private EnvironmentThemeDefinition theme;

        [Header("Levels")]
        [SerializeField] private List<LevelDefinition> levels = new List<LevelDefinition>();

        [Header("Progression")]
        [Tooltip("Completions in THIS world required to unlock the next. Rule documented qualitatively; number is ours. Default 18 is the editor-time fallback for newly created/unauthored assets; shipped values follow the §5.6.1 escalating schedule (15/17/18/19/20/20/21).")]
        [SerializeField] private int completionsToUnlockNextWorld = 18;

        [Header("Content Focus — editor metadata feeding the §5.6 content plan")]
        [SerializeField] private BlockBehaviourType introducedBehaviour = BlockBehaviourType.Base;
        [SerializeField, TextArea] private string designBrief;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public int WorldIndex => worldIndex;
        public string WorldNameKey => worldNameKey;
        public EnvironmentThemeDefinition Theme => theme;
        public IReadOnlyList<LevelDefinition> Levels => levels;
        public int CompletionsToUnlockNextWorld => completionsToUnlockNextWorld;
        public BlockBehaviourType IntroducedBehaviour => introducedBehaviour;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Returns the level with the given 1-based index, or null. Cold path (menu).</summary>
        public LevelDefinition GetLevel(int oneBasedIndex)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < levels.Count; i++)
            {
                if (levels[i] != null && levels[i].LevelIndex == oneBasedIndex)
                {
                    return levels[i];
                }
            }

            return null;
        }

        /// <summary>True when the player's completion count in this world unlocks the next world.</summary>
        public bool MeetsUnlockThreshold(int completionsInThisWorld)
        {
            return completionsInThisWorld >= completionsToUnlockNextWorld;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

#### 5.5.2 GameModeDefinition

The five modes are officially named and described on the PS4/Switch press sheets (live 2026-09-24): Arcade, Endurance ("Play a never ending string of puzzles to go for the best scores"), Infinity ("The blocks don't stop. Build the highest possible stack."), Swift Stacker ("Who can solve the puzzles faster?"), Tower Tumble ("Who will topple the tower first?") ([Switch press sheet](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**.

**`ScoringProfile` — the per-mode scoring value surface.** The `Scoring_*.asset` from §5.1's table, referenced by `GameModeDefinition.scoringProfile` above, carries every tunable constant of §3.7's scoring math as a serialized field whose default is value-identical to the matching const in §3.7.7's canonical static `ScoreModel`. §3.7.7 remains the single source of truth for the formulas; this asset exists so balance passes tune values without touching code, and any deviation from §3.7.7's defaults is a visible, reviewable asset diff.

```csharp

        public int SwiftMarginWeight => swiftMarginWeight;
        public int SwiftMarginCap => swiftMarginCap;
        public float SwiftChainParRatio => swiftChainParRatio;
        public float SwiftChainStep => swiftChainStep;
        public float SwiftChainCap => swiftChainCap;

        #endregion
    }
}
```

#### 5.5.3 Mode parameter delta table

| Parameter | Arcade | Endurance | Infinity | Swift Stacker | Tower Tumble |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Queue source | `FixedLevelQueue` (level asset) | `SeededShuffle` over campaign levels | `ProceduralEndless` | `FixedLevelQueue` (same level both sides) | per-round random draw |
| Lives / attempts | unlimited retries | **3 per session** **[DOCUMENTED]** — "three lives... spread out over your entire session" ([Nintendo Life Wii U](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24), triple-sourced | run ends on topple/water contact | unlimited (race format) | unlimited rounds |
| Win condition | all pieces placed + stability window | survive the level string until lives run out | maximum stack height | first team to solve wins the round; match = best of 5/7/9 | last player causing the topple loses; others +1 point |
| Scoring inputs | §3 formula + challenge bonuses | speed + lives kept + puzzle difficulty **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Nintendo Life Wii U](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24); weighting **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | height (world units) at topple | rounds won; tie-break by solve time **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | points from opponent topples |
| Leaderboard | per-level score (star-based, §3) | yes where online exists; 3DS was offline-only ([Cubed3 3DS](https://www.cubed3.com/games/reviews/nintendo-3ds/art-of-balance-touch), accessed 2026-09-24) | height leaderboard | per-round times **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | match points **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Randomness policy | none (fixed queue) | seeded level shuffle; seed policy per `fixedSeed` | seeded generator (§5.6 content plan) | identical seed mirrored to both teams **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | seeded piece draw — random pieces documented: "pieces per round are RANDOMLY GENERATED" ([Nintendo Life Wii U](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24) |

Mode-heritage notes: Swift Stacker is the documented evolution of the WiiWare 2-player Versus mode — "The Wii's multiplayer mode, now known as Swift Stacker" ([NWR Wii U](http://www.nintendoworldreport.com/review/38619/art-of-balance-wii-u-review), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]** — and the WiiWare Versus match length was selectable over 5/7/9 rounds ([Nintendo Life WiiWare](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**, which is why `versusRoundOptions = {5, 7, 9}` is a documented default rather than an invention. Endurance's string of random levels is documented as "Play random levels in succession" ([official 3DS microsite, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20201019172749/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**. Infinity's "endless feed for maximum height" reading is the documented press-sheet line ([Switch press sheet](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24); its generator parameters are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** and tie into the level-generation seam described in §12. Player-count matrices per edition are historical facts owned by §1/§11–§13; our v1 shipping matrix is decided in §2.

The `stabilityWindowSeconds` default of 3.0 s transcribes the documented Wii behavior — three seconds, shown as three sequential green lights ([Nintendo Life WiiWare](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**. Later editions "significantly shortened" the countdown ([Nintendo Life Wii U](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]** — but the exact post-Wii duration appears in no fetched source. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact post-Wii stability-countdown duration (only "significantly shorter" is documented). Our default stays 3.0 s pending a measured value from capture analysis; tune per edition-feel targets in §3. -->

### 5.6 Content volume plan, authoring workflow, validation, distribution

#### 5.6.1 Volume and pacing plan

The documented content volume is 200 levels across 8 worlds ([official 3DS About, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]**. The equal 25-per-world split is our convention **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (sources state only 200/8). Special-block introduction schedule and unlock thresholds are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**, paced against the §3 difficulty curves:

| World | Levels | Introduced content | Unlock threshold (completions in world) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 25 | Base shapes only; static platforms | open from start |
| 2 | 25 | Breakable blocks | 15 |
| 3 | 25 | Timed blocks | 17 |
| 4 | 25 | Floating/swaying platforms | 18 |
| 5 | 25 | Fire blocks | 19 |
| 6 | 25 | Gravity inversion + top platforms | 20 |
| 7 | 25 | Linked/seesaw pairs | 20 |
| 8 | 25 | All behaviours combined; hardest challenge variants | 21 |

Threshold rationale (math shown per the design-skill rule): a world has 25 levels; requiring 15/25 = 60% completion early and 21/25 = 84% late means a stuck player can always skip forward — matching the documented skippability ([Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — while total campaign gate is Σ thresholds = 15+17+18+19+20+20+21 = 130 of 175 pre-final-world levels (74%), leaving 45 optional completions of margin before world 8.

Production math for §10's roadmap: with the Level Editor + validator loop below, the sustainable single-designer rate is estimated at 6–10 finished levels/day once worlds 1–2 establish the vocabulary **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; 200 levels therefore budget as roughly 25–35 working days of pure authoring, before playtest iteration (§10 phases P4–P5 carry the full plan).

#### 5.6.2 Authoring workflow

1. **Create** — Level Editor's `CreateLevelInActiveWorld` duplicates the world's template asset, assigns the next free `levelIndex`, and registers it in `WorldDefinition.levels` (single-click; no manual asset wrangling).
2. **Block out the basin** — place platform specs (static or floating-sway), set the water line with the live scene overlay, add `topPlatform` only for gravity levels.
3. **Build the queue** — pick pieces from the ContentLibrary-filtered palette; set each entry's initial rotation (auto-clamped to the piece's mask); apply modifiers if pacing needs them.
4. **Set challenge and pars** — optional Time/Height/Balance objective, `parTimeSeconds` from a reference solve, `parFootprintWidthUnits` from the reference solve's resting footprint (W_par for §3.7.1's PrecisionBonus), star thresholds from the §3 derivation spreadsheet.
5. **Validate** — one click runs `LevelValidator`; fix errors (red), review warnings (amber).
6. **Play from level** — the editor opens the Gameplay scene with a boot payload referencing the asset (test hook specified in §6), so no menu navigation is needed per iteration.
7. **Review** — committed levels get an automated CI pass (§16: batch validation over all 200) and, optionally, an MCP-assisted design review where the agent reads the level's serialized form and flags pacing outliers (recipe in §17).

#### 5.6.4 Validation rules and the mass-budget math

`LevelValidator` is a static rule set run at save, on demand, and in CI. It cannot prove solvability — only the physics can (headless solve-smoke tests in §14/§16 cover that); what it rejects are the authoring errors that waste playtest cycles:

| ID | Rule | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| V0 | Footprint fit: widest queued piece must fit the primary platform: `max(w_i) ≤ W_p − 2·A_s` | error |
| V1 | Adversarial tipping margin (math below) | error |
| V2 | Breakable load: worst-case mass above any breakable ≤ `maxSupportedMassRmu` | warning (chain reactions may be intended) |
| V3 | Buoyant support: total queue mass ≤ floating-base capacity (default 12 RMU **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**) | error |
| V4 | Height-challenge feasibility: `Σ h_i ≥ 1.25 · H_target` (25% interlock-loss allowance) | error |
| V5 | Water clearance: platform top ≥ water line + 0.5 u | error |
| V6 | Rotation legality: every `initialRotationStep` satisfies its piece mask | error |
| V7 | Referential integrity: no null queue entries, unique `levelIndex`, bidirectional world↔level links, gravity pieces require `topPlatform` | error |

**V1 — adversarial tipping margin (the queue mass budget vs platform stability heuristic).** The validator simulates the *worst admissible* stack: every piece placed as far to one side as it can rest on the piece below (flush-right cascade). With piece widths `w_i`, each successive center offsets by `(w_{i−1} − w_i)/2`; cumulative positions `x_i` then give the combined center of mass:

`X = Σ(m_i · x_i) / Σ(m_i)`, with `x_i = x_{i−1} + (w_{i−1} − w_i)/2`, `x_0 = 0` (platform center).

Pass condition: `W_eff/2 − s − |X| ≥ 0`, where `W_eff = W_p − 2·A_s` (sway-reduced effective width), `s = 0.25 u` safety margin **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

Worked example — queue of 10 pieces, all 1 RMU, widths (u): 2.0, 2.0, 1.6, 1.6, 1.2, 1.2, 0.8, 0.8, 0.6, 0.6. Cascade offsets: 0, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.1, 0 → cumulative positions 0, 0, 0.2, 0.2, 0.4, 0.4, 0.6, 0.6, 0.7, 0.7 → `X = (0+0+0.2+0.2+0.4+0.4+0.6+0.6+0.7+0.7)/10 = 3.8/10 = 0.38 u`.

- Static platform `W_p = 6.4, A_s = 0`: margin = 3.2 − 0.25 − 0.38 = **2.57 u → PASS**.
- Floating platform `A_s = 0.35`: `W_eff/2 = (6.4 − 0.7)/2 = 2.85`; margin = 2.85 − 0.25 − 0.38 = **2.22 u → PASS**.
- Narrow floating platform `W_p = 1.6, A_s = 0.35`: `W_eff/2 = 0.45`; margin = 0.45 − 0.25 − 0.38 = **−0.18 u → ERROR** (and V0 already fails: first piece w = 2.0 > 1.6 − 0.7 = 0.9).

**V2 — breakable load.** Documented anchor: 3 regulars max above a breakable ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Worst case assumes every piece queued *after* the breakable stacks above it: `M_after = Σ_{j>i} m_j ≤ maxSupportedMassRmu`. Example: breakable at queue position 5 of the 10-piece queue above → `M_after = 5 RMU > 3` → warning; the author either reorders the queue, splits the load across two breakables, or sets the level's validator-override flag when the shatter is the intended teach.

**V3 — buoyant capacity.** Floating bases sink under excess load in our model: `M_queue ≤ M_buoyant_max` (default 12 RMU **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**). The example queue totals 10 RMU ≤ 12 → PASS.

**V4 — height feasibility.** HeightTarget `H = 5.0 u` with the example queue's vertical extents summing `Σ h_i = 6.4 u`: requirement `Σ h_i ≥ 1.25 · H = 6.25` → 6.4 ≥ 6.25 → PASS (barely; flagged as "tight" in the report).

```csharp
#if UNITY_EDITOR
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace AoB.Data.Editor
{
    /// <summary>Static rule set gating every LevelDefinition at authoring time and in CI (§16).</summary>
    public static class LevelValidator
    {
        public static LevelValidationReport Validate(LevelDefinition level)
        {
            var report = new LevelValidationReport(level);
            if (level == null)
            {
                return report;
            }

            CheckReferences(level, report);        // V7
            CheckRotationLegality(level, report);  // V6
            CheckWaterClearance(level, report);    // V5
            CheckFootprintFit(level, report);      // V0
            CheckMassBudget(level, report);        // V1 + V3
            CheckBreakableLoad(level, report);     // V2
            CheckHeightFeasibility(level, report); // V4
            return report;
        }

        /// <summary>V1: adversarial flush-right cascade CoM vs sway-reduced platform margin.</summary>
        private static void CheckMassBudget(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report)
        {
            // Simulate the cascade: x_i = x_{i-1} + (w_{i-1} - w_i)/2 over the queue in order;
            // X = sum(m_i * x_i) / sum(m_i); error when (Wp - 2*As)/2 - SafetyMargin - |X| < 0.
            // Also V3: sum(m_i) <= BuoyantCapacityRmu for every FloatingSway platform.
        }

        private static void CheckReferences(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report) { /* … */ }
        private static void CheckRotationLegality(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report) { /* … */ }
        private static void CheckWaterClearance(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report) { /* … */ }
        private static void CheckFootprintFit(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report) { /* … */ }
        private static void CheckBreakableLoad(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report) { /* … */ }
        private static void CheckHeightFeasibility(LevelDefinition level, LevelValidationReport report) { /* … */ }
    }
}
#endif
```

`LevelValidationReport` is a plain serializable list of `(ruleId, severity, message)` rows — the same shape the CI batch job (§16) emits as artifacts and the §17 MCP review recipe reads.

#### 5.6.5 Addressables groups for content

All content is local in v1; remote groups are reserved for post-launch worlds (§10 P8). Whole-game download anchor: the original Switch edition was a ~200 MB download ([Switch microsite, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20201015074209/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/switch/), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]** — our equivalent budget is 250 MB **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**, with levels themselves trivially small (serialized SOs; tens of KB per world) and art/audio owning the mass (§9).

| Group | Contents | Labels | Load policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core_bootstrap` | GameConfig, ContentLibrary, all GameModeDefinitions, ScoringProfiles | `bootstrap` | preload at Boot scene (§4) |
| `pieces_shared` | all 21 PieceDefinitions + meshes + materials + tray icons | `pieces` | preload with Gameplay scene; always resident |
| `themes` | EnvironmentThemeDefinitions + water/sky variants + world music sets | `themes`, `world{n}` | loaded per world entry, released on world change |
| `levels_world_1` … `levels_world_8` | 25 LevelDefinitions each | `levels`, `world{n}` | single-level load on selection; previous level released (§6 memory rules) |
| `ui_shared` | TMP font assets, glyph sets (§7), common UI art | `ui` | preload at Boot |
| `remote_reserved` | empty in v1 | `remote` | post-launch expansion worlds |

Group sizing budgets **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: ≤ 8 MB per world group (level data + any per-world art), themes ≤ 40 MB total, pieces ≤ 10 MB; per-platform texture compression choices that actually drive these numbers are owned by §9/§18/§19. Bulk SO authoring by agent (CoplayDev's `manage_scriptable_object` MCP tool, §17) versus editor C# scripts is a §17 decision — the data contracts in this section are the interface either path writes to.

### 5.7 Localization

The documented language envelope is the Switch edition's list: Japanese, American English, British English, French, Canadian French, German, Spanish, Latin American Spanish ([Switch press sheet, live](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24; [Nintendo.com store page, live](https://www.nintendo.com/store/products/art-of-balance-switch/), accessed 2026-09-24) **[DOCUMENTED]** — eight locale variants over five written languages. The PS4 edition's oft-quoted "four languages" figure could not be confirmed in any fetched source (T01 gap). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: PS4 supported-language list (per-region PS Store pages were not captured). If v1 ships before verification, the documented Switch set is the superset and safely covers it. -->

| Locale | Written language | Table strategy |
|---|---|---|
| `en-US` | English (US) | base table |
| `en-GB` | English (UK) | derived from `en-US` with spelling overrides (colour/centre, etc.) |
| `fr-FR` / `fr-CA` | French | `fr-CA` derived from `fr-FR` with lexical overrides |
| `de` | German | base table |
| `es-ES` / `es-419` | Spanish | `es-419` derived from `es-ES` with lexical overrides |
| `ja` | Japanese | full table; CJK font asset required |

String-table categories (Unity Localization package; selected in §4's manifest):

| Key namespace | Example key | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|
| `piece.{pieceId}.name` | `piece.base_rect2x1.name` | tray tooltips, encyclopedia |
| `world.{n}.name` / `.desc` | `world.3.name` | world map, menus — names are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (the original's world names were never published; official copy says only "8 worlds each with its own unique lounge style") |
| `level.{world}.{index}.name` | `level.w3.l07.name` | level select — generated names **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `mode.{kind}.name` / `.desc` | `mode.endurance.desc` | mode select; mode descriptions paraphrase the documented press-sheet lines |
