Font fallback chains (TextMeshPro; asset production in §9): every Latin-locale table renders with a single Latin SDF font asset covering extended Latin (ä ö ü é è ê á à ç ñ ¿ ¡); its fallback chain is `AoB-Latin → AoB-IconGlyphs`. The `ja` table uses a dedicated CJK SDF asset with a larger atlas whose fallback chain is `AoB-JP → AoB-Latin` so mixed Latin strings (numbers, "OK") never miss glyphs. No RTL language is in the documented set, so no RTL shaping is required. Font fallback configuration is data reviewed in §14's accessibility pass (UI scaling interacts with CJK glyph legibility at small sizes).

### 5.8 Content asset conventions and schema integrity

| Convention | Rule |
|---|---|
| Naming | `Piece_{id}`, `Level_W{n}_L{nn}`, `World_{n}`, `Mode_{Kind}`, `Theme_{name}` — zero spaces, ASCII |
| Placement | folders per §5.1 table; one folder per world for levels keeps diffs reviewable |
| GUID stability | never delete-and-recreate an asset; rename/move with its `.meta` (references, Addressables labels, and save-file ids all bind to GUID + `pieceId`) |
| Version control | all `.asset` files Force-Text serialized (§4 project settings); binary art tracked via LFS per §4 |
| Schema version | `ContentLibrary.contentSchemaVersion` int, checked at boot against the runtime's expected version; content migrations mirror the save-file migration hooks in §6 — a mismatch fails loudly in dev builds and logs-and-continues in release |
| Boot integrity | `ContentLibrary` validates unique `pieceId`s, unique per-world `levelIndex`, world↔level bidirectionality, and Addressables label presence before the menu appears (§4 boot sequence) |

## 6. Core Systems B — Runtime, Physics & Save

This section specifies the runtime spine that turns §5's data model into playable levels: the physics engine decision and its full tuning table, the simulation-timing architecture that reaches ≥240 Hz effective physics, the adjudication systems (`StabilityMonitor`, `LevelManager`, `GameStateMachine`, `ScoreController`), the camera/audio runtime, object pooling, and the save/ghost-replay system. The system registry (who owns data, who listens, what ticks how) lives in §4; content contracts (`PieceDefinition`, `LevelDefinition`, `GameModeDefinition`, `ScoringProfile`) live in §5; input delivery (`IPieceInputProvider`, `InputRouter`) lives in §7; special-block behaviours (`IBlockBehaviour`) live in §8.

### 6.1 Physics engine decision — Physics2D (Box2D fork) over PhysX 3D

**Decision: 2D physics (`Physics2D`, Unity's Box2D fork) with 3D-looking presentation. All gameplay colliders live on z = 0; the "3D look" comes from a tilted perspective camera rendering 3D art over the 2D simulation.** **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — the choice is ours; every input to it is documented below. The closest commercial comparable made the same call: "Tricky Towers runs Unity's 2D physics, built on Box2D, so bricks have weight, friction, and a center of mass and nothing ever locks to a grid" ([Blueprinted Gaming, Tricky Towers physics guide](https://blueprintedgaming.com/docs/tricky-towers/physics-and-building), accessed 2026-09-24; tertiary source, medium confidence — consistent with the game's look and Box2D's known usage).

| Decision input | 2D (Physics2D / Box2D fork) | 3D (PhysX) | Winner for AoB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buoyancy | Built-in `BuoyancyEffector2D` — "Applies forces to simulate buoyancy, fluid-flow and fluid damping"; properties `surfaceLevel`, `density`, `linearDamping`, `angularDamping`, `flowAngle`, `flowMagnitude`, `flowVariation`; colliders above `surfaceLevel` get no forces ([BuoyancyEffector2D, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuoyancyEffector2D.html), built 2026-09-21, accessed 2026-09-24) | None — requires custom multi-point Archimedes sampling (`AddForceAtPosition` per submerged sample point; community patterns: [Habrador boat tutorial](https://www.habrador.com/tutorials/unity-boat-tutorial/3-buoyancy/), [tombasche BuoyantObject gist](https://gist.github.com/tombasche/5d96747be60b902b837b47ef4fb97fea), [ZauronDark/Unity-Simple-Water-Buoyancy](https://github.com/ZauronDark/Unity-Simple-Water-Buoyancy), all accessed 2026-09-24) | 2D — decisive |
| Low-FPS safety net | Simulation substepping (`useSubStepping`, `maxSubStepCount`, `minSubStepFPS`, `useSubStepContacts`) available in Update/Script simulation modes ([Physics2D.useSubStepping, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics2D-useSubStepping.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | No substepping option anywhere in Unity 6.6 3D (negative result verified against the [Physics settings page](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PhysicsManager.html) and the [Physics API listing](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics.html), 2026-09-24) | 2D |
| Determinism trajectory | 2D line is where Unity invests: "PhysicsCore2D" (`Unity.U2D.Physics`) is being built on Box2D v3 ([Unity-Technologies/PhysicsExamples2D](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/PhysicsExamples2D), pushed 2026-09-22); upstream Box2D v3 is designed deterministic across thread counts and 64-bit platforms, determinism on by default ([Box2D v3 manual, Simulation chapter](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html), accessed 2026-09-24) | PhysX offers "limited deterministic simulation" — same scene + actor insert order + time-stepping + release + platform; `eENABLE_ENHANCED_DETERMINISM` exists in PhysX but is not exposed by Unity ([PhysX 5.8.0 docs, Enhanced Determinism](https://nvidia-omniverse.github.io/PhysX/physx/5.8.0/docs/Simulation.html), updated 2026-05-18, accessed 2026-09-24) | 2D |
| Sleep model (win detection) | Time + velocity tolerances with Box2D island sleeping (whole contact islands sleep/wake together) — predictable ([Rigidbody2D, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody2D.html); [Box2D v3 manual](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html)) | Energy-threshold model (mass-normalized kinetic energy < `sleepThreshold`) — less predictable for stacked piles ([Rigidbody, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody.html)) | 2D |
| Failure drama | Tumble is real rotation in-plane only | True 3D tumble/topple off-plane, one lighting pipeline for pieces, mesh-to-mesh collisions, TGS solver for high mass ratios | 3D (not worth the cost) |
| Constraint burden | Plane is inherent (Box2D is XY) | Must lock every body: `RigidbodyConstraints.FreezePositionZ | FreezeRotationX | FreezeRotationY` | 2D |

Rejected 3D path (for the record, and for §11's replication analysis): if it were ever chosen, per-body planar lock via constraints, `Simulation Mode = Script` with a manual accumulator loop of `Physics.Simulate(fixedDt)` (the only "substep" mechanism in 3D), `Physics.defaultMaxAngularSpeed` raised above the 7 rad/s per-body default so pieces tumble before losing, and note that 3D and 2D settings/materials/gravity live on separate settings pages even when both engines run. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** rejection rationale: no buoyancy, no substepping, weaker determinism story, higher constraint-maintenance cost — none of which 3D's extra drama pays for in a fixed-side-view stacking puzzle.

**Consequence 1 — water is an effector, not a shader.** The water body is a trigger `Collider2D` (Composite/BoxEdge) carrying `BuoyancyEffector2D`. Gameplay semantics come free: pieces above `surfaceLevel` receive no force (dry stacks unaffected); pieces below it get buoyant force plus fluid damping toward the surface ([BuoyancyEffector2D docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuoyancyEffector2D.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Because *any* water contact fails the attempt (documented: "Watch out: Don't let any shape fall into the water!", [official Wii U About page](https://web.archive.org/web/20160903223835/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/wiiu/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24), buoyancy in our game is primarily a **fail-state presentation feature** (a dropped piece bobs and sloshes believably during the fail sting instead of sinking straight through) and the physics basis for **floating/swaying platform bases** — documented original behavior ("floating foundation that sways on water", [Der Spiegel 3DS review](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), 2012-07-12, accessed 2026-09-24). Floating platforms: a dynamic `Rigidbody2D` base with high mass, kept near its anchor by a `SpringJoint2D`, sway driven by small effector `flowMagnitude` + `flowVariation` **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** implementation of the documented behavior. Effector density is tuned so typical piece density sits around 0.6–0.9 of fluid — barely floats, feels heavy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (tuning guidance derived from the effector's density model).

**Consequence 2 — visuals are decoupled from simulation.** The renderer never touches physics: 3D block art (§9) renders on quads/meshes whose gameplay proxies are 2D colliders; visual water is a Shader Graph surface (§9) whose world-y is pinned equal to the effector's `surfaceLevel`. If visual waves are ever added, either gameplay stays on the flat line (calm-water competitive fairness) or both visuals and the fail check sample the same 1D function `WaveHeight(x, t)` **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**. Rendering-depth offsets per art layer avoid z-fighting without affecting the z = 0 simulation. Cinematic fail-state pieces (slow bob, ripples) read the effector surface directly.

Unity 6.6 also added new 2D physics **Buoyancy, Wind, and PhysicsSpace query APIs** (per the [6000.6.0f1 release notes](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), Aug 31 2026, accessed 2026-09-24 via our research digest). Release-notes-level names, captured in the T02 notes: Buoyancy — `PhysicsBody.BuoyancyInput` plus `ApplyBuoyancy` on `PhysicsWorld`/`PhysicsBody`/`PhysicsShape`; Wind — `PhysicsBody.WindInput` plus `ApplyWind` variants at world/body/shape; `PhysicsSpace` — generic broadphase/narrowphase queries `OverlapAABB`/`OverlapPoint`/`CastRay`/`CastShape`. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: full signatures (parameters/return types) and exact final method names/semantics of the Unity 6.6 2D Buoyancy/Wind/PhysicsSpace query APIs — the names above are release-notes shorthand ("ApplyWind variants at world/body/shape" is not an exact method list), so capture the 6000.6 script reference when the project is created — plus their relevance to WaterVolume below. -->

**Watch item:** PhysicsCore2D (`Unity.U2D.Physics`, Box2D v3-based) has a settings page in the 6.6 manual and an active examples repo ([Unity-Technologies/PhysicsExamples2D](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/PhysicsExamples2D), pushed 2026-09-22), but its shipping vehicle/stability is unverified. It is a §21 risk-register item, not a v1 dependency. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: PhysicsCore2D production readiness and API surface before any migration; cross-platform determinism claims belong to upstream Box2D v3, not to Unity's current Physics2D fork. -->

### 6.2 Physics tuning table

Chosen values for the 2D engine (our path), then the documented 3D knob set (rejected path, kept for the record and for §11). Escalation policy throughout: change one knob at a time, re-run the §14 determinism/perf soak after each change.

**Project settings — Time and Physics 2D (our engine):**

| Knob (location) | API | Default | Ours | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed Timestep (Time) | `Time.fixedDeltaTime` | 0.02 (50 Hz) | **0.0041667 (1/240)** | ≥240 Hz target (§6.3); at 1 g a piece falls ≤ ~0.085 mm/step — effectively continuous contact resolution |
| Maximum Allowed Timestep (Time) | `Time.maximumDeltaTime` | 0.3333 | keep | Caps catch-up so one slow frame cannot queue dozens of 240 Hz steps |
| Time Scale (Time) | `Time.timeScale` | 1 | 1; 0 on pause/win | Freezes world + fixed-step coroutines during pause and the win celebration |
| Simulation Mode (Physics 2D) | `Physics2D.simulationMode` | Fixed Update | **Fixed Update** (Script as build-config fallback, §6.3) | Pairs simulation with FixedUpdate game code; docs execute sim "immediately after MonoBehaviour.FixedUpdate" ([Physics 2D settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/2023.2/Documentation/Manual/class-Physics2DManager.html), 2023.2 archive carrying the full table, accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Velocity Iterations | `Physics2D.velocityIterations` | 8 | 8 → escalate 12 | Resolve bounce/joint impulses; docs-coupled advice: raise ~50% before anything else if stacks squirm |
| Position Iterations | `Physics2D.positionIterations` | 3 | 3 → escalate 5 | Resolve overlap/penetration |
| Max Translation Speed | `Physics2D.maxTranslationSpeed` | (in-inspector) | conservative cap below worst-case tunneling margin | Docs: raising "can cause numerical problems"; caps are project-wide (no per-body override in 2D) |
| Max Rotation Speed | `Physics2D.maxRotationSpeed` | (in-inspector) | conservative cap | Same rationale |
| Max Linear/Angular Correction | — | (in-inspector) | defaults | Anti-overshoot clamps (range 0.0001–1e6); 2D analog of 3D depenetration velocity |
| Baumgarte Scale | — | (in-inspector) | default (jitter lever) | Lower = softer settle, higher = snappier overlap resolution but can inject energy |
| Bounce Threshold (2D) | — | (in-inspector) | default | Kills micro-bounce between slow contacts |
| Default Contact Offset (2D) | — | (in-inspector) | default — never shrink toward 0 | Docs caution: shrinking slows continuous-polygon collision; inflating creates vertex-collision artifacts |
| Time to Sleep | `Physics2D.timeToSleep` | (in-inspector) | 0.5 s policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | Box2D-style time-below-tolerance sleep; win predicate does NOT rely on it (§6.4) |
| Linear/Angular Sleep Tolerance | — | (in-inspector) | defaults | Cheap early-out only |
| 2D multithreading (jobs) + Use Consistency Sorting | — | off/on | **jobs OFF** (sorting ON if ever enabled) | Docs: job batching "reduces determinism in processing order" unless consistency sorting is on — determinism first at <100 bodies |
| Layer Collision Matrix | — | — | Water × Piece ON (trigger), Piece × Platform ON | Fail detection + stacking; layer table owned by §4 |
| Queries Hit Triggers | — | — | ON | Water-contact queries see the trigger volume |
| Simulation Layers (2D) | — | everything | exclude decorative layers | Only Rigidbody2D/joints/effectors/contacts on gameplay layers simulate |

**Per-`Rigidbody2D` policy (pieces, platforms):**

| Knob | Ours | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `interpolation` | **None** | Interpolation smooths sim-rate < render-rate; at 240 Hz sim / 60 Hz render every frame has fresh state — interpolation only adds pose-history cost ([Rigidbody2D docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody2D.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Switch to Interpolate only if a platform ever ships 50 Hz sim |
| `collisionDetectionMode` | Discrete | Piece speeds are far below tunneling thresholds at 240 Hz; Continuous only for a hypothetical hard-thrown mode |
| `gravityScale` | per `PieceDefinition` | Per-body gravity multiplier is the "heavy stone vs light bamboo" feel lever **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — avoids raising global gravity (docs couple higher gravity with higher solver iterations) |
| `linearDamping` / `angularDamping` (renamed from drag/angularDrag) | 0.05 / 0.1 **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | Kills endless micro-rolling without feeling syrupy |
| `sleepMode` | Start Awake | Predictable first-frame behavior |
| `simulated` | OFF while carried | Carried pieces are frozen and cheap; released on drop |
| `constraints` | none (in-plane is inherent) | 2D needs no planar locking — a rejected-3D burden |

**Materials and mass ratios.** `PhysicsMaterial2D` per piece surface: bounciness 0 everywhere (a stacking game), friction per `PieceDefinition` (§5) with `frictionCombine = Maximum` on piece-vs-piece for grippiest stacks (long-standing defaults friction 0.4 / bounciness 0; the [PhysicsMaterial, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/PhysicsMaterial.html) page documents the `frictionCombine`/`bounceCombine` properties ("Determines how the friction/bounciness is combined") and the 3D rename from PhysicMaterial (the old URL 404s on live docs), accessed 2026-09-24; the combine enum values — Average/Minimum/Multiply/Maximum — were not printed on the fetched page and rest on long-standing Unity knowledge, medium-high confidence per the research notes). Keep adjacent-stack-body mass ratios within ~10:1 where possible; unavoidable heavy anchors escalate solver iterations first (documented remedy). Level validation (§5) enforces the queue mass budget before a level ships. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** policy applying the documented remedies.

**3D knob set (rejected path — documented defaults, for the record and §11):** Default Solver Iterations 6 (docs), Default Solver Velocity Iterations 1 (docs), Sleep Threshold 0.005 mass-normalized energy, Default Contact Offset 0.01 ("if set too close to zero, it can cause jitter"), Bounce Threshold 2 ("relative velocity below this... they do not bounce... also reduces jitter"), Default Max Depenetration Velocity 1, `Rigidbody.maxAngularVelocity` 7 rad/s vs `Physics.defaultMaxAngularSpeed` 50, drag/angularDrag 0/0.05, Friction Type Patch (default; "most stable results at low solver iteration counts"; Two Directional most accurate, needs more iterations), Solver Type PGS (default) vs TGS ("better convergence and better handling of high-mass ratios, minimizes energy introduced when correcting penetrations"), Enable Adaptive Force OFF by default but "affects the way forces are transmitted through a pile or stack of objects" — test ON for tall stacks, Broadphase Sweep-and-Prune default with Multibox/Automatic Box Pruning suited to "many GameObjects in a flat world". All from the [Unity 6.6 Physics project settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PhysicsManager.html) and [Physics API](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics.html), accessed 2026-09-24.

Also verify units/semantics of Physics2D.maxTranslationSpeed (per-step vs per-second) before tuning. -->

### 6.3 Simulation architecture — the 240 Hz stepper and determinism discipline

**The ≥240 Hz target is ours, not the original's to cite.** The Wii U-era "240 fps physics" claim could not be confirmed in any fetched primary source (official microsites, press sheets, Nintendo.com pages, seven reviews — see §11 and the research gaps); per the grounding rules it must not enter this plan as fact. Our 240 Hz target is a fidelity decision: at 1/240 s a piece falls ≤ ~0.085 mm/step at 1 g, making contact resolution effectively continuous for stack-settling, at ~4.8× the 50 Hz physics CPU cost — trivial at our body count (<100 active bodies). **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** Reproducing "high-rate physics feel" on any v1 platform is limited by budget, not feasibility.

**Substepping's real job (scope correction).** Physics2D substepping is a low-frame-rate guard, not a mechanism for raising the base simulation rate. The docs are explicit: "When the simulation is set to run per-frame by setting the Physics2D.simulationMode to Update or Script, this option will control if simulation sub-stepping can be used", and its purpose is preventing "simulation explosion" when frame rate drops below `minSubStepFPS` ([Physics2D.useSubStepping, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics2D-useSubStepping.html), accessed 2026-09-24). It does nothing in the default Fixed Update mode. Reaching 240 Hz therefore means shrinking the fixed step itself (Option A) or driving `Physics2D.Simulate` with a constant step from an accumulator (Option B).

| Option | Recipe | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Fixed Update @ 1/240 (chosen)** | Time > Fixed Timestep = 0.0041667; Physics 2D > Simulation Mode = Fixed Update; FixedUpdate game code runs at 240 Hz automatically; interpolation None | Simplest, deterministic-friendly, no script-side stepping bugs. Cost: solver+contacts 4.8× vs 50 Hz (fine at our body counts); ALL FixedUpdate subscribers run 240×/s — rule: only physics-adjacent systems subscribe to FixedUpdate (registry in §4) |
| **B — Script + accumulator (fallback)** | Simulation Mode = Script; accumulate real time; call `Physics2D.Simulate(fixedStep)` with a CONSTANT step (docs: never `Time.deltaTime` — "less deterministic"); cap steps/frame; enable substepping as the low-FPS guard (`useSubStepping` on, `minSubStepFPS` 60, `maxSubStepCount` 8, `useSubStepContacts` off unless exact per-substep contacts needed); read `PhysicsScene2D.subStepCount` / `subStepLostTime` for telemetry | Gives frame-level control (pause sim during loads/transitions without `timeScale` hacks). Remember: FixedUpdate still fires at `Time.fixedDeltaTime` regardless of `Simulate` calls — never pair the two assumptions ([Physics2D.Simulate docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics2D.Simulate.html), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| C — 3D Script loop | Rejected with 3D (§6.1) | If ever used: record variable step counts per frame — they break strict replay determinism unless persisted |

A single `PhysicsStepper` owns the contract so Options A/B are a serialized config flip, not a code audit:

```csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core.Simulation
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Owns the simulation timing contract for the whole game: pins the fixed
    /// timestep at boot, exposes a monotonic fixed-step counter for input
    /// buffering and ghost replays, and optionally drives Physics2D.Simulate
    /// manually (Simulation Mode = Script) with a constant step size.
    /// </summary>
    [DefaultExecutionOrder(-10000)]
    public sealed class PhysicsStepper : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Nested Types

        public enum SimMode { FixedUpdate, Script }

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Timing")]
        [Tooltip("Fixed physics rate in Hz. 240 default; 120 is the approved low tier for weak mobile SoCs (GameConfig override, §5).")]
        [SerializeField] private int simulationHz = 240;

        [Tooltip("FixedUpdate lets the engine step physics after MonoBehaviour.FixedUpdate; Script drives Physics2D.Simulate from Update with a constant step.")]
        [SerializeField] private SimMode simulationMode = SimMode.FixedUpdate;

        [Header("Script Mode Guards")]
        [SerializeField, Min(1)] private int maxStepsPerFrame = 8;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        /// <summary>Monotonic count of completed fixed steps since level load; correlates replay inputs.</summary>
        public long CurrentStep { get; private set; }

        public float FixedDelta => 1f / simulationHz;

        public int SimulationHz => simulationHz;

        #endregion

        #region Events

        /// <summary>Raised at the start of every fixed step, before inputs/forces are applied. The ONLY place forces are applied.</summary>
        public event Action<long> StepBegin;

        /// <summary>Raised after the step's simulation advanced.</summary>
        public event Action<long> StepEnd;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private static readonly WaitForFixedUpdate WaitForFixedStep = new WaitForFixedUpdate();

        private float _accumulator;
        private int _starvedFrames;

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void Awake()
        {
            // Pin timing in code, not only in Project Settings, so every build
            // and every CI test runner shares one simulation contract.
            Time.fixedDeltaTime = FixedDelta;
            Time.maximumDeltaTime = 0.3333f;

            Physics2D.simulationMode = simulationMode == SimMode.Script
                ? SimulationMode2D.Script
                : SimulationMode2D.FixedUpdate;
        }

        private void FixedUpdate()
        {
            if (simulationMode != SimMode.FixedUpdate)
            {
                return;
            }

            StepBegin?.Invoke(CurrentStep);
            // Engine simulates Physics2D immediately after all FixedUpdate
            // calls in this mode, so StepBegin force application lands in-step.
            CurrentStep++;
            StepEnd?.Invoke(CurrentStep);
        }

        private void Update()
        {
            if (simulationMode != SimMode.Script)
            {
                return;
            }

            _accumulator += Mathf.Min(Time.deltaTime, Time.maximumDeltaTime);
            int steps = 0;
            while (_accumulator >= FixedDelta && steps < maxStepsPerFrame)
            {
                StepBegin?.Invoke(CurrentStep);
                Physics2D.Simulate(FixedDelta); // constant step — never Time.deltaTime
                CurrentStep++;
                StepEnd?.Invoke(CurrentStep);
                _accumulator -= FixedDelta;
                steps++;
            }

            if (_accumulator >= FixedDelta)
            {
                // Frame budget exceeded: drop the backlog and count it —
                // strict replay determinism requires the drop count in the header.
                _starvedFrames++;
                _accumulator = 0f;
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Applies per-level timing config and resets counters for a fresh attempt.</summary>
        public void ResetForLevel(int configuredHz)
        {
            if (configuredHz != simulationHz && Application.isPlaying)
            {
                Debug.LogWarning($"{nameof(PhysicsStepper)}: simulationHz {simulationHz} -> {configuredHz}; Time.fixedDeltaTime re-pinned. Active ghost replays are invalidated.");
            }

            simulationHz = configuredHz;
            Time.fixedDeltaTime = FixedDelta;
            CurrentStep = 0L;
            _accumulator = 0f;
            _starvedFrames = 0;
        }

        /// <summary>Starved-frame count for the replay header and §14 telemetry.</summary>
        public int GetStarvedFrameCount() => _starvedFrames;

        #endregion
    }
}
```

(The cached `WaitForFixedUpdate` instance is exposed for fixed-step coroutines like §6.4's window — yielding on a shared instance avoids per-yield allocation.)

**Determinism discipline.** Authoritative positions we design against: Unity's engines are "not 100% deterministic across devices... deterministic on the same device given the same set of inputs" (MelvMay, Unity staff, [Unity Discussions, 2023-02-27](https://discussions.unity.com/t/fully-deterministic-physics/910507/10), accessed 2026-09-24); PhysX 5.8.0 offers only "limited deterministic simulation" with per-release/per-platform scope ([PhysX docs](https://nvidia-omniverse.github.io/PhysX/physx/5.8.0/docs/Simulation.html), accessed 2026-09-24); the docs mandate "a fixed step value... every time you call it" for `Physics2D.Simulate` ([Physics2D.Simulate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics2D.Simulate.html), accessed 2026-09-24); upstream Box2D v3 — the basis of the future PhysicsCore2D, not of Unity's current fork — is designed deterministic across thread counts and platforms ([Box2D v3 manual](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Rules that follow:

1. Fixed `Time.fixedDeltaTime` (or fixed `Simulate` step), pinned in code on boot; no `Time.deltaTime` anywhere in forces.
2. Input quantized to fixed steps: `InputRouter` (§7) buffers `(stepIndex, inputEvent)` pairs in Update and they are consumed in `StepBegin` — never raw per-frame input timing into forces.
3. Seeded RNG (`System.Random` with a recorded seed) for all gameplay randomness — Endurance level shuffles, Tower Tumble random pieces, cosmetic variation. Never frame/time-seeded.
4. Deterministic spawn order: pieces instantiate in queue order (creation order drives simulation order in Box2D-class engines; the PhysX docs make actor insert order explicit, and the same discipline costs nothing here).
5. 2D job-system multithreading OFF (batch processing order "reduces determinism"; if ever enabled for perf, Use Consistency Sorting goes ON) — [Physics 2D settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/2023.2/Documentation/Manual/class-Physics2DManager.html), accessed 2026-09-24.
6. Variable-step events recorded: if Script mode starves frames, the drop count enters the replay header (invalidation is explicit, not silent).
7. Ghost replays validate against a header gate: `engineVersion + buildGuid + simulationHz + rngSeed` must match the running build, else the ghost is refused (per-release determinism means a Unity upgrade can change results silently).
8. v1 ships no online physics sync (scope fence in §2; the original's online modes are studied in §11–§13). If multiplayer physics ever ships, host-authority + periodic pose snapshots is the recommended pattern — cross-device lockstep on built-in engines is unsafe per the positions above.

### 6.4 StabilityMonitor — win/fail adjudication

The documented rules this system implements: after the last piece is placed, "the structure must stay above water for three seconds, indicated by three lights at the bottom of the screen" ([Nintendo Life WiiWare review, 2010-02-18](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24; corroborated by [Cubed3 Wii U review, 2014](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html): "first green light... second green light... third green light and safety"); any piece touching water at any time fails the attempt (official: "Don't let any shape fall into the water!", [Wii U About](https://web.archive.org/web/20160903223835/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/wiiu/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); post-Wii editions shortened the countdown — only "significantly shorter" is documented ([Nintendo Life Wii U review](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), 2014-10-03, accessed 2026-09-24). Our default window is 3.0 s with per-mode override in `GameModeDefinition` (§5); the three-green-light UI pulses on `StabilityWindowProgress` thirds **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** mirroring the documented UI.

**Never rely on `IsSleeping()` alone.** The 2D sleep model is time-below-tolerance with island sleeping — but continuous forces (buoyancy effector, flow, damping) keep bodies awake, so a floating-but-stable stack may never sleep (engineering inference from the documented effector behavior; [Rigidbody2D](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody2D.html) + [Box2D v3 manual](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html), accessed 2026-09-24). The stability predicate is therefore explicit, evaluated every fixed step — and, per §3.5.1/§3.5.3, deliberately *not* the win condition; the win predicate is "no water contact before countdown completion":

| # | Condition | Tolerance (default) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | Every piece's lowest point above `surfaceLevel + margin` | margin 0.02 m | Dry check with hysteresis |
| b | `\|v\|` below linear tolerance per piece | 0.05 m/s | Squared-magnitude compare, no sqrt in hot path |
| c | `\|ω\|` below angular tolerance per piece | 0.05 rad/s | Same |
| d | Every piece connected to the base island via contacts/joints | contact graph | Flood fill from platform, allocation-free reuse of the §8 joint graph |
| — | (optional early-out) all bodies asleep | — | Cheap fast-path, never the signal |

The window itself accrues **unconditionally**: 3.0 s of accumulated fixed time after the last piece is released, exactly as §3.3.2's snippet shows — the only failure input is water contact (`NotifyWaterContact` → `WaterContact`) firing before completion, per §3.5.1's ruling that the win predicate is "no water contact before countdown completion", not "full quiescence" (a slow-motion collapse that reaches the water *after* the third light is still a win). A stack sliding faster than the tolerances above but never touching water therefore still wins at 3.0 s; predicate violations never reset the window accumulator. The predicate feeds only the informational uses §3.5.3 assigns it: the settle watchdog, precision-bonus accrual (§3.7), and `WobbleIntensity`/adaptive tension (§6.11/§9). Tolerances are `GameConfig`-exposed **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** values tuned to feel "solid" without demanding absolute rest.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core.Gameplay
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Watches every live piece: the stability window completes on 3.0 s of
    /// accumulated fixed time with no water contact — per §3.5.1 the win
    /// predicate is "no water contact before countdown completion", not full
    /// quiescence — while the dry/slow/connected predicate is informational
    /// only (§3.5.3: settle watchdog, precision bonus, wobble/tension).
    /// Never relies on Rigidbody2D.IsSleeping alone — buoyancy forces can
    /// keep a stable floating stack permanently awake.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class StabilityMonitor : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Stability Window")]
        [Tooltip("Seconds the stack must hold after the final piece. 3.0 s matches the documented original; per-mode overrides in GameModeDefinition (§5).")]
        [SerializeField] private float windowDuration = 3f;

        [Tooltip("Dry margin above the water surface for the lowest-point check.")]
        [SerializeField] private float waterlineMargin = 0.02f;

        [SerializeField] private float linearVelocityTolerance = 0.05f;
        [SerializeField] private float angularVelocityTolerance = 0.05f;

        [Header("References")]
        [SerializeField] private WaterVolume waterVolume;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        /// <summary>0..1 smoothed worst-piece motion; drives tension audio (§6.11) and camera juice (§6.8, §9).</summary>
        public float WobbleIntensity { get; private set; }

        public bool IsWindowActive { get; private set; }

        #endregion

        #region Events

        /// <summary>Fires the fail path; payload is the offending piece.</summary>
        public event Action<PieceController> WaterContact;

        public event Action StabilityWindowStarted;

        /// <summary>0..1 across the window; the UI lights its three lamps at 1/3 and 2/3 and 3/3.</summary>
        public event Action<float> StabilityWindowProgress;

        public event Action StabilityWindowCompleted;
        public event Action AllPiecesSettled;
        public event Action<float, float> PieceSettled; // (settleSeconds, heightUnits); raised per settled piece; consumed by Infinity mode (§12)
        public event Action StackDisturbed;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private static readonly WaitForFixedUpdate FixedWait = new WaitForFixedUpdate();

        private readonly List<PieceController> _pieces = new List<PieceController>(64);
        private readonly Queue<PieceController> _islandQueue = new Queue<PieceController>(64);
        private readonly HashSet<PieceController> _islandVisited = new HashSet<PieceController>();

        private Coroutine _windowRoutine;
        private bool _wasSettled;

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void OnDisable()
        {
            CancelWindow();
            _pieces.Clear();
            _islandQueue.Clear();
            _islandVisited.Clear();
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Called by LevelManager when the queue is empty and the last piece has been released.</summary>
        public void BeginStabilityWindow()
        {
            CancelWindow();
            IsWindowActive = true;
            _wasSettled = false;
            StabilityWindowStarted?.Invoke();
            _windowRoutine = StartCoroutine(RunWindowRoutine());
        }

        /// <summary>Cancels the window (retry, unload, fail). Safe when inactive.</summary>
        public void CancelWindow()
        {
            if (_windowRoutine != null)
            {
                StopCoroutine(_windowRoutine);
                _windowRoutine = null;
            }

            IsWindowActive = false;
        }

        /// <summary>Fail path raised by a piece's OnTriggerEnter2D against the Water layer (layer matrix §6.2).</summary>
        public void NotifyWaterContact(PieceController piece)
        {
            CancelWindow();
            WaterContact?.Invoke(piece);
        }

        public void RegisterPiece(PieceController piece)
        {
            if (!_pieces.Contains(piece))
            {
                _pieces.Add(piece);
            }
        }

        public void UnregisterPiece(PieceController piece)
        {
            _pieces.Remove(piece);
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private IEnumerator RunWindowRoutine()
        {
            float held = 0f;
            while (held < windowDuration)
            {
                // Frozen automatically while Time.timeScale == 0 (fixed updates
                // cease), so pause needs no special handling here.
                yield return FixedWait;

                // §3.5.1/§3.3.2: the window accrues UNCONDITIONALLY per fixed
                // step — the win predicate is "no water contact before
                // countdown completion", not quiescence. A stack sliding above
                // tolerance but staying dry still wins; the only fail input is
                // NotifyWaterContact, which cancels this routine from outside.
                held += Time.fixedDeltaTime;
                StabilityWindowProgress?.Invoke(held / windowDuration);

                // Informational only (§3.5.3): updates WobbleIntensity/tension
                // and settle events, and gates precision-bonus accrual. Its
                // return value never resets the accumulator.
                EvaluateStackStability();
            }

            IsWindowActive = false;
            _windowRoutine = null;
            StabilityWindowCompleted?.Invoke();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// True when every live piece is dry, slow, and connected to the base
        /// island. Informational per §3.5.3 — never the win condition.
        /// Allocation-free: plain for-loops over cached collections.
        /// </summary>
        private bool EvaluateStackStability()
        {
            if (_pieces.Count == 0)
            {
                return false;
            }

            float surfaceY = waterVolume != null ? waterVolume.SurfaceWorldY : float.NegativeInfinity;
            float linearSq = linearVelocityTolerance * linearVelocityTolerance;
            float angularSq = angularVelocityTolerance * angularVelocityTolerance;
            bool allSleeping = true;
            float worstMotion = 0f;

            for (int i = 0; i < _pieces.Count; i++)
            {
                PieceController piece = _pieces[i];
                Rigidbody2D body = piece.Body;

                if (piece.LowestPointWorldY <= surfaceY + waterlineMargin)
                {
                    return false; // (a) dry
                }

                float speedSq = body.velocity.sqrMagnitude;
                if (speedSq > linearSq)
                {
                    return false; // (b) slow
                }

                float spinSq = body.angularVelocity * body.angularVelocity;
                if (spinSq > angularSq)
                {
                    return false; // (c) slow rotation
                }

                if (!body.IsSleeping())
                {
                    allSleeping = false;
                }

                float motion = Mathf.Max(Mathf.Sqrt(speedSq) / linearVelocityTolerance,
                                         Mathf.Abs(body.angularVelocity) / angularVelocityTolerance);
                if (motion > worstMotion)
                {
                    worstMotion = motion;
                }
            }

            if (!IsConnectedToBase())
            {
                return false; // (d) one island
            }

            WobbleIntensity = Mathf.Lerp(WobbleIntensity, Mathf.Clamp01(worstMotion), 0.1f);

            bool settled = allSleeping; // fast-path signal only
            if (settled != _wasSettled)
            {
                if (settled)
                {
                    AllPiecesSettled?.Invoke();
                }
                else
                {
                    StackDisturbed?.Invoke();
                }

                _wasSettled = settled;
            }

            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>Contact/joint flood fill from the base platform; reuses the §8 joint graph buffers.</summary>
        private bool IsConnectedToBase()
        {
            // … seeded from the platform's contact list (ContactFilter2D, NoFilter
            // layer mask Piece|Platform), expanding over attached joints (§8 linked
            // seesaw pairs count as connections); returns _islandVisited.Count >= _pieces.Count.
            return true;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Water-contact wiring: each piece prefab carries a thin `PieceCollisionRelay` that forwards `OnTriggerEnter2D` (Water layer) to `StabilityMonitor.NotifyWaterContact`. The piece's sink/bob beat after contact runs on effector buoyancy (§6.1) while `LevelManager` enters Results.

### 6.5 LevelManager — level lifecycle and the stack loop

`LevelManager` owns one attempt at one `LevelDefinition` (§5): the phase machine (the §3 micro-loop made concrete), queue advancement, piece release, retry, and timing. Documented behaviors it encodes: a fixed set of shapes per level offered from a tray/queue (3DS shows the selection on the lower screen — [Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24); piece pick-up → rotate (45°) → drop (§7 inputs); on water contact the attempt fails and the level restarts (documented original behavior — pieces are not individually removed); Time/Height/Balance Challenges add extra-points objectives (documented).

| Phase | Entry | Owns | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loading | `LoadLevel(definition)` | Addressables load (§5 groups), basin/platform instantiation in deterministic order, pool prewarm, RNG seed | Intro |
| Intro | Load complete | Camera framing settle (§6.8), theme fade (§9), queue reveal | Playing (first `OfferNextPiece`) |
| Playing | Intro done | Queue advancement, carried-piece state, timer, per-piece snapshots | Evaluating (last piece released) |
| Evaluating | Queue empty | `StabilityMonitor.BeginStabilityWindow()`; win/fail subscription | Results |
| Results | Window completed / water contact | Score finalization (§6.7), stats capture (§6.9), star/award presentation (§3) | LevelSelect / retry / next |

Carried-piece mechanics: while carried, the piece's `Rigidbody2D.simulated = false` and its transform follows the active `IPieceInputProvider` cursor (§7) with rotation in 45° increments (per-`PieceDefinition` allowed orientations, §5); on release, `simulated = true`, velocity seeded from cursor motion (clamped, quantized to the fixed step), and the piece falls. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** mechanics implementing the documented loop.

Retry/undo: `RestartLevel()` reloads from the recorded seed (documented semantics: the failed attempt restarts). `UndoLastPlacement()` — practice mode only **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — restores the pre-release `Rigidbody2D` snapshot (position/rotation/velocity per live piece, captured the fixed step before each release), enabling "retry from last piece" training without cheapening Arcade.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core.Gameplay
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Owns one attempt at one LevelDefinition: lifecycle phases, queue
    /// advancement, piece release, retry/undo, and challenge timers.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class LevelManager : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Nested Types

        public enum LevelPhase { Loading, Intro, Playing, Evaluating, Results }

        private sealed class LevelSnapshot
        {
            public Vector2[] Positions;
            public float[] Rotations;
            public Vector2[] Velocities;
            public float[] AngularVelocities;
            public int QueueIndex;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("References")]
        [SerializeField] private PieceSpawner pieceSpawner;
        [SerializeField] private StabilityMonitor stabilityMonitor;
        [SerializeField] private ScoreController scoreController;

        [Header("Timing")]
        [Tooltip("Time Challenge budget in seconds; derived in LoadLevel from LevelDefinition.Challenge (ChallengeSpec.Kind.TimeLimit -> LimitValue); 0 = no time challenge.")]
        [SerializeField] private float challengeTimeLimit;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public LevelPhase Phase { get; private set; }

        public LevelDefinition Definition { get; private set; }

        public float ElapsedPlaySeconds { get; private set; }

        public bool IsTimeChallenge => challengeTimeLimit > 0f;

        #endregion

        #region Events

        public event Action<LevelDefinition> LevelLoaded;
        public event Action<PieceDefinition> QueueAdvanced;
        public event Action<PieceController> PieceReleased;
        public event Action LevelCompleted;
        public event Action LevelFailed;
        public event Action<float> ChallengeTimerExpired;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private readonly Stack<LevelSnapshot> _snapshots = new Stack<LevelSnapshot>(16);
        private readonly List<PieceController> _livePieces = new List<PieceController>(64);

        private PieceController _carriedPiece;
        private int _queueIndex;
        private int _rngSeed;
        private bool _challengeExpired;

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void OnEnable()
        {
            stabilityMonitor.StabilityWindowCompleted += OnStabilityWindowCompleted;
            stabilityMonitor.WaterContact += OnWaterContact;
        }

        private void OnDisable()
        {
            stabilityMonitor.StabilityWindowCompleted -= OnStabilityWindowCompleted;
            stabilityMonitor.WaterContact -= OnWaterContact;
        }

        private void FixedUpdate()
        {
            if (Phase != LevelPhase.Playing)
            {
                return;
            }

            ElapsedPlaySeconds += Time.fixedDeltaTime; // fixed-step wall of truth for scoring/replays
            if (IsTimeChallenge && !_challengeExpired && ElapsedPlaySeconds >= challengeTimeLimit)
            {
                _challengeExpired = true;
                ChallengeTimerExpired?.Invoke(challengeTimeLimit);
                if (Definition.Challenge.FailOnExpiry) // §5 ChallengeSpec: default false = forfeit the bonus only
                {
                    EnterResults(won: false);
                }
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Loads and begins a level attempt deterministically (seed recorded for replays).</summary>
        public void LoadLevel(LevelDefinition definition, int rngSeed)
        {
            Definition = definition;
            _rngSeed = rngSeed;
            _queueIndex = 0;
            ElapsedPlaySeconds = 0f;
            _challengeExpired = false;
            _snapshots.Clear();
            _livePieces.Clear();
            // §5 data contract: the budget exists only when the level carries a TimeLimit
            // challenge (ChallengeSpec.Kind.TimeLimit -> LimitValue in seconds); every other
            // kind (or None) means no countdown. FailOnExpiry (default false) is honored in
            // FixedUpdate: expiry forfeits the challenge bonus unless it is set.
            challengeTimeLimit = definition.Challenge.ChallengeKind == ChallengeSpec.Kind.TimeLimit
                ? definition.Challenge.LimitValue
                : 0f;
            Phase = LevelPhase.Loading;
            // … Addressables load, basin instantiation in queue-deterministic order,
            // pool prewarm (§6.10), then StartCoroutine(IntroRoutine()).
            LevelLoaded?.Invoke(definition);
        }

        /// <summary>Advances the queue and spawns the next carried piece via the active IPieceInputProvider (§7).</summary>
        public void OfferNextPiece()
        {
            if (Phase != LevelPhase.Playing || _queueIndex >= Definition.PieceQueue.Count)
            {
                return;
            }

            CaptureSnapshot();
            // §5 QueueEntry: Piece plus InitialRotationStep + Modifiers (mirror spawn, paced
            // reveal) that drive the offered orientation.
            PieceDefinition next = Definition.PieceQueue[_queueIndex].Piece;
            _carriedPiece = pieceSpawner.SpawnCarried(next);
            _queueIndex++;
            QueueAdvanced?.Invoke(next);
        }

        /// <summary>Releases the carried piece: sim on, velocity seeded, settling watch starts.</summary>
        public void ReleaseCarriedPiece(Vector2 releasePosition, float releaseRotation, Vector2 cursorVelocity)
        {
            if (_carriedPiece == null)
            {
                return;
            }

            CaptureSnapshot(); // pre-release state for practice undo
            _carriedPiece.Release(releasePosition, releaseRotation, cursorVelocity);
            _livePieces.Add(_carriedPiece);
            stabilityMonitor.RegisterPiece(_carriedPiece);
            PieceReleased?.Invoke(_carriedPiece);
            _carriedPiece = null;

            if (_queueIndex >= Definition.PieceQueue.Count)
            {
                Phase = LevelPhase.Evaluating;
                stabilityMonitor.BeginStabilityWindow();
            }
            else
            {
                OfferNextPiece();
            }
        }

        /// <summary>Documented retry semantics: the failed attempt restarts from the recorded seed.</summary>
        public void RestartLevel()
        {
            LoadLevel(Definition, _rngSeed);
        }

        /// <summary>Practice-mode-only rewind to the last pre-release state. [ORIGINAL DESIGN]</summary>
        public void UndoLastPlacement()
        {
            if (Phase == LevelPhase.Results || _snapshots.Count == 0)
            {
                return;
            }

            LevelSnapshot snapshot = _snapshots.Pop();
            // … restore positions/rotations/velocities on _livePieces, recycle the
            // top piece back to the pool (§6.10), rewind _queueIndex, Phase = Playing.
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private void OnStabilityWindowCompleted()
        {
            EnterResults(won: true);
        }

        private void OnWaterContact(PieceController piece)
        {
            // Fail beat: let buoyancy bob the piece during the sting, then results.
            EnterResults(won: false);
        }

        private void EnterResults(bool won)
        {
            if (Phase == LevelPhase.Results)
            {
                return;
            }

            Phase = LevelPhase.Results;
            stabilityMonitor.CancelWindow();
            scoreController.BuildResult(new ScoreController.ResultInputs(
                won: won,
                elapsedSeconds: ElapsedPlaySeconds,
                finalHeightUnits: MeasureFinalHeightUnits(),          // H: stack top above platform surface at settle (§3.7.1)
                footprintWidthUnits: MeasureRestingFootprintUnits(),  // W_used: resting footprint width at settle (§3.7.1)
                parTimeSeconds: Mathf.RoundToInt(Definition.ParTimeSeconds),
                parFootprintWidthUnits: Definition.ParFootprintWidthUnits,
                challengeCompleted: IsChallengeCompleted()));
            if (won)
            {
                LevelCompleted?.Invoke();
            }
            else
            {
                LevelFailed?.Invoke();
            }
        }

        private void CaptureSnapshot()
        {
            // … copy per-piece Rigidbody2D state into a pooled LevelSnapshot; pushed onto _snapshots.
        }

        private int MeasureFinalHeightUnits()
        {
            // … H (§3.7.1): stack-top height in block units above the platform
            // surface, captured from the settled stack when the window completes.
            return 0;
        }

        private int MeasureRestingFootprintUnits()
        {
            // … W_used (§3.7.1): resting footprint width of the settled stack.
            return 0;
        }

        private bool IsChallengeCompleted()
        {
            // … the level's Challenge medal state (Time/Height/Balance) gating
            // §3.7.1's flat 250.
            return false;
        }

        private IEnumerator IntroRoutine()
        {
            // … camera framing settle (§6.8), theme fade (§9), queue reveal UI.
            Phase = LevelPhase.Playing;
            OfferNextPiece();
            yield break;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

### 6.6 GameStateMachine — the shell-level FSM

A plain finite state machine, deliberately not a hierarchical one: six states, no shared sub-behaviors, no state-local state machines. If late features (e.g. a settings overlay reachable from multiple states) start demanding shared sub-behaviors, revisit; until then HFSM machinery is pure overhead. The machine guards transitions through a static legality table so illegal requests log loudly in dev builds instead of silently corrupting flow.

| State | Dominant systems active | Entry actions | Exit actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bootstrap | SaveSystem load, §5 catalogs, input init | Splash, migration run, controller detection (§7) | → MainMenu |
| MainMenu | UI only; pools warm | Mixer snapshot Calm (§6.11); demo scene idle | → LevelSelect |
| LevelSelect | UI + save data | World/level grid hydration (§3) | → Playing |
| Playing | LevelManager full stack | Scene additive load; PhysicsStepper.ResetForLevel; audio ambience | → Paused ↔, → Results |
| Paused | UI only | `Time.timeScale = 0`; mixer snapshot Paused; input context switch (§7) | resume restores |
| Results | UI + stats capture | Score finalize (§6.7); save write (§6.9); leaderboard submit (§19) | → LevelSelect / next level / retry |

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Shell-level finite state machine. Transition legality is a static table:
    /// illegal requests warn in dev builds and are refused, never silently
    /// half-applied. Paused is a sibling of Playing, not a child — timeScale 0
    /// already freezes the whole simulation stack.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class GameStateMachine : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Nested Types

        public enum GameState { Bootstrap, MainMenu, LevelSelect, Playing, Paused, Results }

        #endregion

        #region Private Static Fields

        private static readonly Dictionary<GameState, GameState[]> LegalTransitions = new Dictionary<GameState, GameState[]>
        {
            [GameState.Bootstrap]  = new[] { GameState.MainMenu },
            [GameState.MainMenu]   = new[] { GameState.LevelSelect, GameState.Playing },
            [GameState.LevelSelect] = new[] { GameState.MainMenu, GameState.Playing },
            [GameState.Playing]    = new[] { GameState.Paused, GameState.Results, GameState.LevelSelect },
            [GameState.Paused]     = new[] { GameState.Playing, GameState.LevelSelect },
            [GameState.Results]    = new[] { GameState.LevelSelect, GameState.Playing, GameState.MainMenu },
        };

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public GameState Current { get; private set; } = GameState.Bootstrap;

        #endregion

        #region Events

        /// <summary>Fire-and-forget notification AFTER state-enter side effects complete.</summary>
        public event Action<GameState, GameState> StateChanged;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Requests a transition; refuses (with a dev-build warning) if illegal.</summary>
        public bool RequestTransition(GameState target)
        {
            if (target == Current)
            {
                return true; // idempotent re-entry is not an error
            }

            if (!LegalTransitions[Current].Contains(target))
            {
                Debug.LogWarning($"{nameof(GameStateMachine)}: illegal transition {Current} -> {target} refused.");
                return false;
            }

            GameState previous = Current;
            OnExitState(previous);
            Current = target;
            OnEnterState(target);
            StateChanged?.Invoke(previous, target);
            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>Convenience for the pause toggle: Playing <-> Paused.</summary>
        public void TogglePause()
        {
            switch (Current)
            {
                case GameState.Playing:
                    RequestTransition(GameState.Paused);
                    break;
                case GameState.Paused:
                    RequestTransition(GameState.Playing);
                    break;
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private void OnEnterState(GameState state)
        {
            switch (state)
            {
                case GameState.Paused:
                    Time.timeScale = 0f;
                    // mixer snapshot + input context switch handled by §6.11/§7 listeners of StateChanged
                    break;
                case GameState.Playing:
                    Time.timeScale = 1f;
                    break;
            }
        }

        private void OnExitState(GameState state)
        {
            if (state == GameState.Paused)
            {
                Time.timeScale = 1f;
            }
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

`Contains` on a 3-element array is allocation-free and branch-cheap; the dictionary is static so it costs nothing per instance. All state-specific work (scene ops, save writes, mixer snapshots) lives in listeners that subscribe to `StateChanged` — the machine itself owns only the guard and the `timeScale` pair, which belongs to nobody else.

### 6.7 ScoreController — scoring, math shown

The original's scoring is documented only in fragments: Endurance sessions give "3 lives" and score composed of speed + lives + difficulty ([Nintendo Life Wii U review](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), 2014-10-03, accessed 2026-09-24); Special Challenges award extra points. Every concrete constant is therefore **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** per the chief-architect ruling; the full presentation of formulas lives in §3 — this is the runtime contract and the math. §3.7 is canonical (single source of truth): this controller delegates all formula math to §3.7.7's allocation-free static `ScoreModel` — per §3.7.7, "`ScoreController` (§6) subscribes to §3.3.4 events and calls this allocation-free static model" — rather than re-deriving the constants a second time.

**Core mode score (per level attempt, §3.7.1):**

`S = Σᵢ placementPoints(pᵢ) + 25 × H + 10 × max(0, T_par − T_used) + 25 × max(0, W_par − W_used) + 250 [if Challenge completed]`

| Term | Formula | Constants |
|---|---|---|
| `placementPoints(p)` | authored per `PieceDefinition` (§5 authoring tool) as `round(100 × C × R)` | Base 100; complexity `C` (shape class) 1.00 simple / 1.25 medium / 1.50 complex; risk `R` (behaviour) base 1.00 / breakable 1.50 / timed 1.50 / fire 2.00 / gravity 2.00 / linked 1.75 **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (first four specials documented; linked is the §8 extension) |
| `HeightBonus` | `25 × H` where H = final stack height in block units above the platform surface (absolute, not par-relative) | 25/height-unit **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `TimeBonus` | `10 × max(0, T_par − T_used)` where T_used = `LevelManager.ElapsedPlaySeconds`, T_par = par time from `LevelDefinition` | 10/second **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `PrecisionBonus` | `25 × max(0, W_par − W_used)` where W_used = resting footprint width, W_par = par footprint width | 25/width-unit **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `ChallengeBonus` | flat, when the level's Challenge is completed (Balance/Height/Time, documented challenge types) | 250 flat **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |

Worked example (§3.7.1's W3-L07, arithmetic per game-designer standard): queue = 12 pieces (9 base: 4 simple, 4 medium, 1 complex; 2 timed; 1 fire), cleared at T_used = 61 s vs T_par = 75 s, height H = 6 units, resting footprint W_used = 7 vs W_par = 9, Time Challenge met: placements = 4×100 + 4×125 + 1×150 + 2×150 + 1×200 = 1,550; HeightBonus = 25×6 = 150; TimeBonus = 10×14 = 140; PrecisionBonus = 25×2 = 50; ChallengeBonus = 250 → **S = 2,140**. A slower 100 s run at height 5 and width 9: 1,550 + 125 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 1,675 — the spread rewards both cleanliness and speed without letting speed dominate (§3.7.2's star thresholds anchor to the same par run).

**Endurance score (session-level, §3.7.3):** `E = Σᵢ [500 × dᵢ + 5 × max(0, 120 − tᵢ)] + 1000 × L_remaining` — the three documented ingredients (speed, lives, difficulty) instantiated per §3.7.3 **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**. Endurance is a session total, finalized once when the 3-life session ends (`BuildEnduranceResult` → `ScoreModel.ComputeEnduranceScore`), never folded into an individual won level's result.

```csharp
using System;
using UnityEngine;
using AoBClone.Gameplay; // ScoreModel (§3.7.7)

namespace Aob.Core.Gameplay
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Accumulates score events during a level attempt and finalizes the
    /// result. Pure bookkeeping: no physics reads, runs on gameplay events,
    /// so it costs nothing per fixed step. All formula math delegates to
    /// §3.7.7's allocation-free static ScoreModel — this class never
    /// re-derives §3.7's constants (single source of truth).
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class ScoreController : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Nested Types

        /// <summary>
        /// Measured attempt inputs + LevelDefinition pars for §3.7.1's level
        /// total; supplied by LevelManager at Results entry.
        /// </summary>
        public readonly struct ResultInputs
        {
            public readonly bool Won;
            public readonly float ElapsedSeconds;       // T_used
            public readonly int FinalHeightUnits;       // H, measured at settle
            public readonly int FootprintWidthUnits;    // W_used, measured at settle
            public readonly int ParTimeSeconds;         // T_par (LevelDefinition)
            public readonly int ParFootprintWidthUnits; // W_par (LevelDefinition)
            public readonly bool ChallengeCompleted;

            public ResultInputs(bool won, float elapsedSeconds, int finalHeightUnits,
                int footprintWidthUnits, int parTimeSeconds, int parFootprintWidthUnits,
                bool challengeCompleted)
            {
                Won = won;
                ElapsedSeconds = elapsedSeconds;
                FinalHeightUnits = finalHeightUnits;
                FootprintWidthUnits = footprintWidthUnits;
                ParTimeSeconds = parTimeSeconds;
                ParFootprintWidthUnits = parFootprintWidthUnits;
                ChallengeCompleted = challengeCompleted;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>Shape-complexity class C from §3.7.1 (authored per PieceDefinition).</summary>
        public enum ShapeClass { Simple, Medium, Complex }

        #endregion

        #region Private Constants

        private const int BasePoints = 100; // §3.7.1 B

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public int CurrentScore { get; private set; }

        #endregion

        #region Events

        public event Action<int> ScoreChanged;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void NotifyPiecePlaced(PieceDefinition definition)
        {
            // §3.7.1: placement points are authored per PieceDefinition as
            // round(100 × C × R) by the §5 authoring tool (see PlacementPointsFor);
            // the runtime reads the authored value and never re-derives it.
            Add(definition.PlacementPoints);
        }

        public void NotifyChallengeBonus(int bonus)
        {
            Add(bonus);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Finalizes the level attempt; called once by LevelManager at Results
        /// entry. Level score only — Endurance terms are session-level and live
        /// in BuildEnduranceResult (§3.7.3).
        /// </summary>
        public LevelResult BuildResult(in ResultInputs inputs)
        {
            int total = CurrentScore;
            if (inputs.Won)
            {
                total = ScoreModel.ComputeLevelScore(
                    placementPoints: total,
                    finalHeightUnits: inputs.FinalHeightUnits,
                    parTimeSeconds: inputs.ParTimeSeconds,
                    elapsedSeconds: Mathf.RoundToInt(inputs.ElapsedSeconds),
                    footprintWidthUnits: inputs.FootprintWidthUnits,
                    parFootprintWidthUnits: inputs.ParFootprintWidthUnits,
                    challengeCompleted: inputs.ChallengeCompleted);
            }

            return new LevelResult(won: inputs.Won, score: total, elapsedSeconds: inputs.ElapsedSeconds);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Endurance session finalizer (§3.7.3): E = Σ[500·d_i + 5·max(0,120−t_i)]
        /// + 1000·L. Called once when the 3-life session ends — never per level.
        /// </summary>
        public static int BuildEnduranceResult(int clearedCount, float difficultyWeightSum, int speedBonusSeconds, int livesRemaining)
        {
            return ScoreModel.ComputeEnduranceScore(clearedCount, difficultyWeightSum, speedBonusSeconds, livesRemaining);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Authoring-side placement pricing from §3.7.1: round(100 × C × R),
        /// keyed to §5's BlockBehaviourType (PieceDefinition carries no
        /// SpecialType field). Used by the §5 authoring tool to bake
        /// PieceDefinition placement points.
        /// </summary>
        public static int PlacementPointsFor(BlockBehaviourType behaviour, ShapeClass complexity)
        {
            return Mathf.RoundToInt(BasePoints * ComplexityFor(complexity) * MultiplierFor(behaviour));
        }

        public void ResetForAttempt()
        {
            CurrentScore = 0;
            ScoreChanged?.Invoke(CurrentScore);
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        /// <summary>Behaviour-risk multiplier R from §3.7.1, over §5's BlockBehaviourType.</summary>
        private static float MultiplierFor(BlockBehaviourType type)
        {
            switch (type)
            {
                case BlockBehaviourType.Breakable:       return 1.50f;
                case BlockBehaviourType.Timed:           return 1.50f;
                case BlockBehaviourType.Fire:            return 2.00f;
                case BlockBehaviourType.GravityInverter: return 2.00f;
                case BlockBehaviourType.LinkedSeesaw:    return 1.75f;
                default:                                 return 1.00f;
            }
        }

        private static float ComplexityFor(ShapeClass complexity)
        {
            switch (complexity)
            {
                case ShapeClass.Medium:  return 1.25f;
                case ShapeClass.Complex: return 1.50f;
                default:                 return 1.00f;
            }
        }

        private void Add(int points)
        {
            CurrentScore += points;
            ScoreChanged?.Invoke(CurrentScore);
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

(`ResultInputs` carries the measured H, T_used, W_used and the `LevelDefinition` pars from `LevelManager`, so §3.7.1's full level total — including the precision term — flows through `ScoreModel.ComputeLevelScore` with no placeholder gaps. Placement pricing `round(100 × C × R)` is baked per `PieceDefinition` at §5 authoring time via `PlacementPointsFor`; Endurance is finalized once per session via `BuildEnduranceResult`, never per level.) Star/award thresholds consume `LevelResult` per §3's table; nothing in this class reads stars.

### 6.8 CameraDirector — framing and juice

**Custom rig, not Cinemachine, for gameplay framing.** Cinemachine earns its complexity in authored camera moves; our gameplay camera is one solved problem — fit the play field with margin — plus event-driven juice offsets. A ~150-line custom rig is auditable, deterministic (no damping surprises across frame rates), and free of a package dependency in the hot loop. Cinemachine remains available for menu/credit fly-bys if §9 wants them. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Framing math (game-designer lens, shown): to vertically fit world half-extent `E_y` and horizontally fit `E_x` through a perspective camera at tilt θ (foreshortened vertical extent `E_y · cosθ`), the required distance along the view axis is:

`d = max( E_y·cosθ / tan(fov/2), E_x / (tan(fov/2) · aspect) ) + margin`

with `aspect = Screen.width / Screen.height`. Recompute on resolution change and on level load (basin sizes vary); clamp per-platform FOV/aspect presets come from §5's display config. Portrait mobile (§2) either letterboxes to landscape or reframes with `E_x/E_y` swapped — §7/§9 own the presentation choice.

| Juice beat | Trigger | Implementation | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| FOV punch | `AllPiecesSettled` | ±2° spring back over 0.25 s | 1 transform/frame for the beat |
| Micro-shake | `StackDisturbed` with `WobbleIntensity > 0.6` | seeded-RNG perlin offsets on a child rig, amplitude ∝ intensity | cheap |
| Hit-stop | fire-block explosion (§8) | `Time.timeScale` 0 for 60 ms then restore — only while `GameState.Playing` | free |
| Slow-mo collapse | water contact during Evaluating | `timeScale` 0.35 for 0.8 s, then Results | free |
| Settle dust / splash | contact events | VFX pool (§6.10), never instantiated | pooled |

Wooden-clunk SFX pairing and light-through-windows ambiance are documented presentation ([Nintendo Life Wii U review](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), 2014-10-03, accessed 2026-09-24); the audio side is §6.11/§9.

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core.Presentation
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Gameplay camera: fits the play field by formula, applies event-driven
    /// juice (FOV punch, seeded shake) on top. No per-frame allocations.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class CameraDirector : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Rig")]
        [SerializeField] private Camera gameplayCamera;
        [SerializeField] private Transform shakeRig; // child of the main rig; shake only ever touches this

        [Header("Framing")]
        [SerializeField] private float fieldHalfExtentX = 6f;
        [SerializeField] private float fieldHalfExtentY = 5f;
        [SerializeField] private float tiltDegrees = 20f;
        [SerializeField] private float framingMargin = 1.25f;

        [Header("Juice")]
        [SerializeField] private float fovPunchDegrees = 2f;
        [SerializeField] private float fovPunchSeconds = 0.25f;
        [SerializeField] private float maxShakeAmplitude = 0.08f;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private float _baseFov;
        private float _fovPunchT;
        private float _shakeSeed;
        private readonly System.Random _cosmeticRng = new System.Random(); // §6.3 rule 3: seeded instance — Random.Shared is .NET 6+, not netstandard2.1

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void Awake()
        {
            _baseFov = gameplayCamera.fieldOfView;
            _shakeSeed = _cosmeticRng.Next(); // cosmetic only — never gameplay RNG
        }

        private void OnRectTransformDimensionsChange() => Reframe(); // resolution/orientation change

        private void LateUpdate()
        {
            // FOV punch spring
            if (_fovPunchT > 0f)
            {
                _fovPunchT = Mathf.Max(0f, _fovPunchT - Time.unscaledDeltaTime);
                float k = _fovPunchT / fovPunchSeconds;
                gameplayCamera.fieldOfView = _baseFov + fovPunchDegrees * k * k;
            }

            // Seeded positional shake, amplitude scaled externally by WobbleIntensity.
            float t = Time.unscaledDeltaTime;
            Vector3 offset = new Vector3(
                (Mathf.PerlinNoise(_shakeSeed, t) - 0.5f),
                (Mathf.PerlinNoise(_shakeSeed + 17f, t) - 0.5f),
                0f) * (maxShakeAmplitude * WobbleIntensity01);
            shakeRig.localPosition = offset;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        /// <summary>0..1 wobble drive, set from StabilityMonitor.WobbleIntensity by the presentation glue.</summary>
        public float WobbleIntensity01 { get; set; }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Solves the fit formula and places the camera. Call on level load and resolution change.</summary>
        public void Reframe()
        {
            float aspect = Mathf.Max(0.1f, (float)Screen.width / Screen.height);
            float halfFovTan = Mathf.Tan(gameplayCamera.fieldOfView * 0.5f * Mathf.Deg2Rad);
            float vertical = fieldHalfExtentY * Mathf.Cos(tiltDegrees * Mathf.Deg2Rad) / halfFovTan;
            float horizontal = fieldHalfExtentX / (halfFovTan * aspect);
            float distance = Mathf.Max(vertical, horizontal) + framingMargin;

            transform.rotation = Quaternion.Euler(tiltDegrees, 0f, 0f);
            transform.position = new Vector3(0f, distance * Mathf.Sin(tiltDegrees * Mathf.Deg2Rad), -distance * Mathf.Cos(tiltDegrees * Mathf.Deg2Rad));
        }

        /// <summary>Beat: small FOV punch on stack settle.</summary>
        public void PlaySettlePunch()
        {
            _fovPunchT = fovPunchSeconds;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

One rule for all juice: it composes through child rigs and `unscaledDeltaTime` so pause (`timeScale 0`) freezes the world but never freezes the camera's return springs or the UI.

### 6.9 SaveSystem — profile data, ghosts, versioning, cloud hooks

**Storage layout** (under `Application.persistentDataPath`; the path differs per platform and per cloud provider's remapping — Steam Auto-Cloud roots are configured in §19):

| File | Contents | Writer cadence |
|---|---|---|
| `saves/profile0.json` (+ `.bak`) | one `PlayerProfile`: progress, stars, settings-adjacent prefs, stats | level complete, settings change, app suspend |
| `settings.json` | graphics/audio/input-adjacent (rebinds live in §7's own store) | change |
| `ghosts/<levelId>.ghost.json` | replay ghosts (below) | new personal best |

**Format choice and one deliberate deviation from the standard skeleton.** `JsonUtility` is the default serializer (fast, allocation-light, no dependencies), but it cannot do `Dictionary` or polymorphic sections — `PlayerProfile` needs per-mode progress maps. The save layer therefore serializes typed wrapper arrays (`KeyValueEntry<string, ModeProgress>[]`) through `JsonUtility` rather than switching the whole project to a JSON library; Unity 6.6's new Dictionary serialization feature is a candidate to delete the wrapper **but its exact serialization surface is version-fresh** <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Unity 6.6 Dictionary serialization — confirm Dictionary<,> fields survive JsonUtility round-trips in 6000.6 before deleting the KeyValueEntry wrappers (release-notes-level feature, script-reference detail not yet captured). -->.

**`ISaveable` contract** (unity-game-dev-expert pattern): every system that persists state implements `ISaveable` and contributes one named `JObject`-shaped section; `SaveSystem` orchestrates collection, version stamping, atomic write, and cloud sync. Sections are independent so one system's corrupt section cannot take the profile down.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Aob.Core.Persistence
{
    /// <summary>Implemented by every system with persisted state. One named section each.</summary>
    public interface ISaveable
    {
        /// <summary>Stable section key, e.g. "progress", "stats". Never rename after ship; migrate instead.</summary>
        string SaveKey { get; }

        /// <summary>Capture state into a serializable section model.</summary>
        object CaptureState();

        /// <summary>Restore state from a section model (may be from an older schema version — check header).</summary>
        void RestoreState(object state);
    }
}
```

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.IO;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core.Persistence
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Owns profile read/write: collects ISaveable sections, stamps schema
    /// version, writes atomically (temp + replace), runs migration chains on
    /// read, and hands bytes to any registered cloud adapter (§19/§14).
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class SaveSystem : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Nested Types

        public interface ISaveCloudAdapter
        {
            /// <summary>Pushes the serialized profile; returns false when offline (queued locally).</summary>
            bool Upload(string fileName, byte[] payload);

            /// <summary>Fetches the serialized profile, or null when none/offline.</summary>
            byte[] Download(string fileName);

            /// <summary>Adapter identity for conflict metadata.</summary>
            string ProviderId { get; }
        }

        private interface ISaveMigration
        {
            int FromVersion { get; }
            int ToVersion { get; }
            void Migrate(ProfileDocument document);
        }

        [Serializable]
        private sealed class ProfileDocument
        {
            public int schemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion;
            public string engineVersion;
            public string buildGuid;
            public string recordedUtc;
            public string profileJson; // serialized typed sections
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Constants

        private const int CurrentSchemaVersion = 3;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private readonly List<ISaveable> _saveables = new List<ISaveable>(16);
        private readonly Queue<ISaveMigration> _migrations = new Queue<ISaveMigration>(8);

        private ISaveCloudAdapter _cloudAdapter;
        private string _profilePath;
        private string _backupPath;

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void Awake()
        {
            string root = Application.persistentDataPath;
            _profilePath = Path.Combine(root, "saves", "profile0.json");
            _backupPath = _profilePath + ".bak";
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void Register(ISaveable saveable) => _saveables.Add(saveable);

        public void SetCloudAdapter(ISaveCloudAdapter adapter) => _cloudAdapter = adapter;

        /// <summary>Loads with backup fallback and migration chain. Returns false only when no profile exists.</summary>
        public bool LoadProfile()
        {
            string json = ReadTextWithBackupFallback(_profilePath, _backupPath);
            if (json == null)
            {
                return false;
            }
```
