| B1 | Breakable (load-limit) | shatters when stacked load exceeds limit (~3 regulars) | Wii, 2010 (1 of 2 specials) | **[DOCUMENTED]** trigger/effect; all numbers **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| B2 | Timed (disappearing) | arms when a piece is placed on top; breaks/vanishes at zero, dropping everything above | Wii, 2010 (1 of 2 specials) | **[DOCUMENTED]** trigger/effect; all numbers **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| B3 | Fire (contact-pair detonation) | explodes on contact with another fire shape | 3DS, 2012 | **[DOCUMENTED]** trigger/effect; all numbers **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| B4 | Gravity-inverting | inverts gravity; levels carry platforms at top and bottom | 3DS, 2012 | **[DOCUMENTED]** trigger/effect; trigger timing **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| B5 | Linked seesaw pair | none — the official sentence truncates before the 5th special; identity unconfirmed | — | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (chief-architect decision) |

Two source-wording caveats, applied per the verification precedence rules: (1) Nintendo World Report summarizes the specials as blocks that "shatter or disappear at contact with a similar type of block" ([NWR Wii U review](http://www.nintendoworldreport.com/review/38619/art-of-balance-wii-u-review), accessed 2026-09-24) — this phrasing fits the fire pair and does not contradict the official per-type wording, but it is not used as a parameter source. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: if gameplay footage of the original becomes available, confirm the load-break block breaks on sustained weight only (official wording) and not on hard impact contact (NWR's loose phrasing). --> (2) The "no more than three regulars" limit is single-sourced to Cubed3. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: confirm the exact breakable load limit from original gameplay footage; our default is tuned to "holds 3, smashes on the 4th" per that review. --> Moving/swaying platform bases are also documented for 3DS+ ([Cubed3 3DS review](http://www.cubed3.com/games/reviews/nintendo-3ds/art-of-balance-touch), [Der Spiegel, 2012-07-12](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24) but they are level/platform vocabulary, not block behaviours — they are specified in §5 and §6 and excluded from this section's scope.

### 8.1 Behaviour component architecture

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (the original's internals are undocumented; this architecture is our design). Behaviours are strategy objects, not MonoBehaviours: one `BlockBehaviourDriver` MonoBehaviour per piece owns the Unity-facing surface (collision callbacks, fixed tick, gizmos) and drives zero or one `IBlockBehaviour` implementation created from the piece's `PieceDefinition` data (§5). Rationale: (a) composition over inheritance — the driver is the only component with a Unity lifecycle, so pieces never hide behaviour in scattered components (unity-game-dev-expert architecture rules); (b) plain-C# behaviours are unit-testable in Edit Mode without scene instantiation (§14 test strategy); (c) pooled pieces (§6) cache their behaviour instance and re-bind parameters per spawn, so a behaviour is allocated at most once per pool slot, never per placement (no hot-path allocations); (d) determinism — every behaviour receives its delta time and random state through the driver, never from `Time.deltaTime` or `UnityEngine.Random` directly (§6 replay discipline).

#### 8.1.1 Lifecycle hooks

| Hook | Fired when | Caller | Notes |
|------|-----------|--------|-------|
| `OnPlaced` | the piece transitions Carrying → Released (player drop, §3) | `LevelManager` → driver | Carried pieces are kinematic and behaviour-dormant (see §8.5 for why fire needs this). |
| `OnNeighborContact` | each physics step that has contacts (new or persistent) with Piece/Platform layers | driver (`OnCollisionStay2D` non-alloc path) | Delivered as `in` struct; includes contact age and impulse. |
| `OnTimerTick` | every fixed step while the piece is Released or settled | driver (`FixedUpdate`) | Delta is always the §6 fixed step; frozen when `GameStateMachine` pauses. |
| `OnStress` | every fixed step, after the shared stress estimator fills the sample | driver | See §8.2; behaviours only read. |
| `OnDestroyed` | immediately before this piece is destroyed/removed for any reason; also delivered to linked partners | driver | Reasons: `Shattered`, `Expired`, `Detonated`, `LinkBroken`, `WaterContact`, `LevelReset`. |
| `Teardown` | pool return and level unload | driver | Releases links and pooled buffers; must be idempotent. |

Events emitted upward (added to the §4 event table): `PiecePlaced`, `PieceDestroyed(reason, metadata)`, `BlockBehaviourTriggered(type, pieceId, payload)`, `GravityInverted(sourcePieceId)`. `ScoreController` consumes `PieceDestroyed` metadata for block-type multipliers (§3); `StabilityMonitor` consumes all of them because any destruction or flip invalidates the settle window (§6).

#### 8.1.2 `IBlockBehaviour` and supporting data

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Lifecycle contract for every special-block behaviour. Implementations are
    /// plain-C# strategy objects created and driven exclusively by
    /// <see cref="BlockBehaviourDriver"/>; they never implement Unity lifecycle
    /// methods, keeping them unit-testable in Edit Mode.
    /// </summary>
    public interface IBlockBehaviour
    {
        /// <summary>Behaviour kind; mirrors the <see cref="BlockBehaviourType"/> enum owned by §5.</summary>
        BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType { get; }

        /// <summary>One-time bind to piece context and designer parameters. Called on spawn and re-bind.</summary>
        void Initialize(BlockContext context, BlockBehaviourParams parameters);

        /// <summary>Called when the owning piece is released by the player and becomes dynamic.</summary>
        void OnPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt);

        /// <summary>Called for contacts with pieces or platforms, new or persistent.</summary>
        void OnNeighborContact(in BlockContactEvent evt);

        /// <summary>Fixed-step tick; delta is always the §6 fixed timestep.</summary>
        void OnTimerTick(float deltaTime);

        /// <summary>Per-step stress sample; see §8.2. Read-only for behaviours.</summary>
        void OnStress(ref BlockStressSample sample);

        /// <summary>Called immediately before this piece is removed, and to linked partners.</summary>
        void OnDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt);

        /// <summary>Severs links and returns pooled buffers; idempotent.</summary>
        void Teardown();
    }

    /// <summary>Immutable per-piece service and data facade handed to behaviours.</summary>
    public readonly struct BlockContext
    {
        public readonly Rigidbody2D Body;
        public readonly BlockBehaviourDriver Driver;
        public readonly PieceDefinition Definition;
        public readonly IBlockGameplayServices Services;
        public readonly int PieceId;

        public BlockContext(Rigidbody2D body, BlockBehaviourDriver driver,
            PieceDefinition definition, IBlockGameplayServices services, int pieceId)
        {
            Body = body;
            Driver = driver;
            Definition = definition;
            Services = services;
            PieceId = pieceId;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Narrow service facade so behaviours never reference managers directly (§4 decoupling).</summary>
    public interface IBlockGameplayServices
    {
        void RequestDestruction(int pieceId, BlockDestructionReason reason, in Vector2 impulse);
        void RequestGravityFlip(int sourcePieceId);
        BlockStressSample GetStress(int pieceId);
        bool TryGetPartner(int linkGroupId, out Rigidbody2D partnerBody);
        void RaiseBehaviourTriggered(BlockBehaviourType type, int pieceId, float payload);
        void PlayAudiocue(int audioCueId, in Vector2 position);
        void SpawnVfx(int vfxId, in Vector2 position, in Vector2 normal);

        /// <summary>Behaviour type of any live piece by id; used for fire↔fire pair detection.
        /// Backed by LevelManager's piece registry.</summary>
        BlockBehaviourType GetBehaviourType(int pieceId);

        /// <summary>Nearest static anchor body at/nearest the given position; used by seesaw pivots.
        /// Backed by LevelManager (static platform rigidbodies).</summary>
        Rigidbody2D GetStaticAnchor(Vector2 position);
    }
}
```

Payload structs (`BlockPlacementEvent`, `BlockContactEvent`, `BlockDestructionEvent`, `BlockStressSample`) are `readonly struct`s in the same namespace — field lists appear in §8.2 and the per-behaviour tables; all are passed by `in` so no per-contact garbage is produced.

#### 8.1.3 `BlockBehaviourDriver` skeleton

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Sole Unity-facing component on a piece. Routes physics callbacks and the
    /// fixed tick into the piece's <see cref="IBlockBehaviour"/> (§8.1) and
    /// publishes behaviour events to the §4 event channels.
    /// </summary>
    [RequireComponent(typeof(Rigidbody2D))]
    public class BlockBehaviourDriver : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Debug (Editor only)")]
        [SerializeField] private bool drawStressGizmo;
        [SerializeField] private bool drawTimerGizmo;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private Rigidbody2D _body;
        private IBlockBehaviour _behaviour;
        private BlockStressEstimator _stressEstimator;   // shared per-level instance, §8.2
        private IBlockGameplayServices _services;
        private PieceDefinition _definition;
        private int _pieceId;
        private float _behaviourTime;
        private static readonly List<ContactPoint2D> ContactBuffer = new(16); // reused, non-alloc

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void Awake()
        {
            _body = GetComponent<Rigidbody2D>();
        }

        private void FixedUpdate()
        {
            if (_behaviour == null)
            {
                return;
            }

            float delta = Time.fixedDeltaTime; // fixed by contract; never Time.deltaTime (§6 determinism)
            _behaviourTime += delta;
            _behaviour.OnTimerTick(delta);

            BlockStressSample sample = _stressEstimator.Evaluate(_pieceId, _body);
            _behaviour.OnStress(ref sample);
        }

        private void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D collision) => RouteContacts(collision, isNew: true);

        private void OnCollisionStay2D(Collision2D collision) => RouteContacts(collision, isNew: false);

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        /// <summary>Live piece id assigned at Bind; -1 while unbound. Read by other drivers
        /// when routing contacts (GetComponent lookup, §8.1.3 RouteContacts).</summary>
        public int PieceId => _pieceId;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Binds (or re-binds, for pooled pieces) definition data and creates the behaviour.</summary>
        public void Bind(PieceDefinition definition, IBlockGameplayServices services,
            BlockStressEstimator stressEstimator, int pieceId)
        {
            _definition = definition;
            _services = services;
            _stressEstimator = stressEstimator;
            _pieceId = pieceId;
            _behaviourTime = 0f;

            _behaviour = BlockBehaviourFactory.Create(definition.BehaviourType);
            var context = new BlockContext(_body, this, definition, services, pieceId);
            _behaviour.Initialize(context, definition.BehaviourParams);
        }

        /// <summary>Called by LevelManager on the Carrying → Released transition (§3).</summary>
        public void NotifyPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt) => _behaviour?.OnPlaced(evt);

        /// <summary>Called by LevelManager/pool before despawn or level reset; forwards to linked partners.</summary>
        public void NotifyDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt) => _behaviour?.OnDestroyed(evt);

        /// <summary>Resets transient state when the piece returns to the pool (§6).</summary>
        public void ResetForPool()
        {
            _behaviour?.Teardown();
            _behaviour = null;
            _behaviourTime = 0f;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private void RouteContacts(Collision2D collision, bool isNew)
        {
            if (_behaviour == null || collision.contactCount == 0)
            {
                return;
            }

            ContactBuffer.Clear();
            collision.GetContacts(ContactBuffer); // non-alloc overload
            for (int i = 0; i < ContactBuffer.Count; i++)
            {
                ContactPoint2D point = ContactBuffer[i];
                var evt = new BlockContactEvent(
                    otherPieceId: collision.collider.GetComponent<BlockBehaviourDriver>()?.PieceId ?? -1,
                    otherLayer: collision.collider.gameObject.layer,
                    normal: point.normal,
                    normalImpulse: point.normalImpulse,
                    relativeVelocity: collision.relativeVelocity,
                    isNew: isNew,
                    contactAgeSteps: _stressEstimator.GetContactAge(in point));
                _behaviour.OnNeighborContact(in evt);
            }
        }

        #endregion

#if UNITY_EDITOR
        private void OnDrawGizmos()
        {
            if (!drawStressGizmo || _behaviour == null)
            {
                return;
            }
            // Load bar above the piece; timer ring for B2 — see §8.9 debug hooks.
        }
#endif
    }
}
```

Factory is a static switch over `BlockBehaviourType` returning `new BreakableBehaviour()` etc. — called once per pool-slot bind, so the switch allocation is amortized to zero in steady state.

#### 8.1.4 Inspector presentation (shared)

`BlockBehaviourParams` is the single flat `[Serializable]` class on `PieceDefinition` (§5.3) — one serialized field group per behaviour type behind one enum, not per-type subclasses; §5.3 argues the flat-class trade and this section consumes that contract as-is. A custom `PropertyDrawer` draws only the field group matching the enum value (enum `Breakable` → the Breakable field group: `maxSupportedMassRmu`, `warnLoadFraction`, `shatterDelaySeconds`, plus the §8-only slam fields below, etc.) and greys out the rest, so designers cannot author dead fields. The driver itself gets a runtime debug inspector (toggle gizmos above, live readouts of `_behaviourTime`, current stress, and armed/disarmed state) — Editor-only, compiled behind `#if UNITY_EDITOR` so it never ships. Per-behaviour fields are documented in each table below; fields §5.3 does not define (`marginUnits`, `slamFactor`, `crackStages`, `debrisChunkCount`, `falloffExponent`, `flipOn`, `flipCount`, `cameraDipDegrees`, and the seesaw set `coupledPeriodSeconds`/`dampingRatio`/`targetSumDegrees`/`anchored`/`breakOnPartnerLoss`) are homed in the same flat class as additional per-type field groups so §8 and §5 share one schema. `LevelEditor` (§5) additionally validates cross-piece rules: seesaw `linkGroupId` values must appear exactly twice per level; gravity-flip levels must contain a ceiling platform (see §8.8 grammar).

### 8.2 Shared services: stress estimation and contact bookkeeping

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (the original's internal physics is undocumented). Two load estimators run per fixed step per piece; behaviours consume whichever they need.

**Sustained load (designer-legible, "how many blocks sit on me").** Define the reference mass `m_ref` = mass of the smallest regular block (`PieceDefinition.Block_Small`, §5). A *support contact* is a piece-piece or piece-platform contact whose normal `n` satisfies `dot(n, ĝ_up) > cos 45°`, persisted ≥ 4 fixed steps, with both bodies under the §6 settle velocity. Piece A *supports* piece B when a support contact exists and B lies on the gravity-opposite side of A. The load on A is the transitive closure of that relation:

```
L_s(A) = Σ_{i ∈ supports(A)*} m_i / m_ref        [load units; 1 unit = one regular block]
```

Traversal is a BFS over the level's contact book using a reused `int[]` queue and a stamp-array visited marker — no per-step allocations. Using mass ratios rather than raw counts futureproofs heavy specials: at our defaults regular = 1.00, timed = 0.80, fire = 0.60, gravity = 1.20, seesaw = 1.00 RMU. These per-type masses are per-`PieceDefinition` `mass` values (the §5.2.1 field), not `BlockBehaviourParams` fields — they are enumerated as the per-asset mass defaults in §5.2.1's provenance table **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**, and the load math here plus §8.3's worked example depend on them.

**Dynamic slam load (impact spikes).** `ContactPoint2D.normalImpulse` is the solver's normal impulse for the step; converting to force units and normalizing by one reference block's weight over a *constant reference window* `h_ref = 0.05 s` (a fixed normalization constant, deliberately **not** the simulation timestep):

```
J_step(A) = Σ support-contact normalImpulses      [kg·m/s]
L_d(A)    = J_step(A) / (m_ref · g · h_ref)       [load units; h_ref = 0.05 s constant, g = |gravity|]
```

`h_ref` must not be `Time.fixedDeltaTime`, for two reasons. (1) Magnitude: normalizing by the live step makes `L_d` scale with simulation rate — at the §6 default 1/240 s the same expression yields `√(2·Δy/g)/h ≈ 77–108` units for `Δy` = 0.5–1 m, so *every* landing impact would clear the slam threshold below (`3.0 × 2.5 = 7.5`) and any drop taller than ≈ 4.8 mm would shatter a breakable, destroying the "mild drops safe, hard slams break" design. (2) Parity: §6 allows `simulationHz = 120` on weak mobile SoCs, so dividing by the live fixed timestep would double `L_d` on the 240 Hz tier relative to the 120 Hz tier and make slam behaviour platform-dependent, violating §6 determinism/parity. A constant window keeps `L_d` simulation-rate independent on both tiers.

World-scale pin **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (no upstream source defines the original's block scale; no other section pins it): the smallest regular block, `Block_Small`, is 0.5 m tall — this is the `Δy` of a one-block-height drop. A regular block dropped one block-height onto A produces `L_d = J_step/(m_ref·g·h_ref) = √(2·Δy/g)/h_ref ≈ 6.4` units at `Δy = 0.5 m` and `≈ 9.0` at `Δy = 1 m` (a two-block-height drop) — i.e. `≈ 6–9` units, straddling the slam threshold below, so one-block-height drops stay safe while taller slams break: spikes are intentionally loud, so slam uses its own threshold multiplier.

**Break predicate (consumed by B1):** break when `L_s > maxSupportedMassRmu + marginUnits` (§5.3 `maxSupportedMassRmu = 3.0`; §8-only `marginUnits = 0.25`, homed in the flat class) **or** `L_d > maxSupportedMassRmu × slamFactor` (§8-only `slamFactor = 2.5`, homed in the flat class). With `maxSupportedMassRmu = 3.0` this reproduces the documented feel — three resting regulars (`L_s = 3.0`) hold; the fourth (`L_s = 4.0 > 3.25`) smashes ([Cubed3 Wii U review](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Worked example: a regular + a gravity special stacked on a breakable give `L_s = 1.0 + 1.2 = 2.2` → safe; add two regulars → `L_s = 4.2 > 3.25` → shatter.

Both estimators read the *current* gravity vector, not world-down, so they stay correct after B4 flips gravity. The contact book is rebuilt each fixed step from driver reports (age tracking) and is also what `StabilityMonitor` uses for its support-integrity check (§6), so the two systems can never disagree about what rests on what.

### 8.3 B1 — Breakable (load-limit)

Documented: breaks "once you put too much load on top" ([official Wii About](https://web.archive.org/web/20091116220135/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/about.php), [official 3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); holds "no more than three other regulars before smashing" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

| Aspect | Specification |
|--------|---------------|
| Trigger | `L_s > maxSupportedMassRmu + marginUnits` or `L_d > maxSupportedMassRmu × slamFactor` (§8.2; `maxSupportedMassRmu` from §5.3, slam fields homed per §8.1.4) |
| Effect | Block shatters after `shatterDelaySeconds` (§5.3, 0.15 s readability delay): collider disabled, rigidbody removed from sim, debris spawned (non-colliding, VFX layer), `PieceDestroyed(Shattered, {loadUnits, chainDepth})` emitted; supported pieces re-fall |
| Visual | Crack decal progressive states at `≥ warnLoadFraction` (70% default) and `≥ warnLoadFraction + 0.15` (85% default) of threshold (telegraph, §9); shatter burst of 8–12 chunks on the VFX layer; brief 50 ms presentation-only hit-stop (interpolation freeze, physics untouched — determinism per §6) |
| Audio | Creak cue at 60% state, crack cue at 85%, shatter burst at break; cues themed per world (§9) |
| Counter-play | Distribute load with long bridging pieces; place breakables last, on top; keep heavy specials off them; accept a planned shatter as a "controlled demolition" that drops a sub-stack onto a wider base |

| Parameter | Default | Range | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
| `maxSupportedMassRmu` | 3.0 | 1.0–10.0 | §5.3; tuned to documented "3 regulars" |
| `warnLoadFraction` | 0.7 | 0–1 | §5.3; first crack-stage threshold |
| `shatterDelaySeconds` | 0.15 | 0–0.5 | §5.3; load-exceeded → shatter delay |
| `marginUnits` | 0.25 | 0.1–1.0 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); hysteresis against oscillating loads |
| `slamFactor` | 2.5 | 1.5–5.0 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); impact sensitivity |
| `crackStages` | 2 | 0–3 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); at `warnLoadFraction` / `warnLoadFraction + 0.15` |
| `debrisChunkCount` | 10 | 4–16 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); VFX budget §9 |

All parameter values **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>B1: shatters when sustained or slam load exceeds the designer limit (§8.3).</summary>
    public sealed class BreakableBehaviour : IBlockBehaviour
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private BlockContext _context;
        private BlockBehaviourParams _p;
        private float _peakSustainedLoad;
        private float _time;
        private float _shatterAt = -1f;
        private BlockStressSample _pendingSample;
        private int _crackStage;
        private bool _shattered;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType => BlockBehaviourType.Breakable;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void Initialize(BlockContext context, BlockBehaviourParams parameters)
        {
            _context = context;
            _p = parameters; // flat §5.3 class; PropertyDrawer shows only the Breakable group
            _peakSustainedLoad = 0f;
            _time = 0f;
            _shatterAt = -1f;
            _crackStage = 0;
            _shattered = false;
        }

        public void OnPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt) { }

        public void OnNeighborContact(in BlockContactEvent evt) { }

        public void OnTimerTick(float deltaTime)
        {
            _time += deltaTime;
            if (_shatterAt >= 0f && !_shattered && _time >= _shatterAt)
            {
                Shatter(in _pendingSample); // fires after §5.3 shatterDelaySeconds
            }
        }

        public void OnStress(ref BlockStressSample sample)
        {
            if (_shattered)
            {
                return;
            }

            _peakSustainedLoad = Mathf.Max(_peakSustainedLoad * 0.98f, sample.SustainedLoadUnits); // decayed peak
            float limit = _p.MaxSupportedMassRmu;
            UpdateCrackStage(limit);

            bool sustainedBreak = sample.SustainedLoadUnits > limit + _p.MarginUnits;
            bool slamBreak = sample.SlamLoadUnits > limit * _p.SlamFactor;
            if (sustainedBreak || slamBreak)
            {
                if (_shatterAt < 0f)
                {
                    _pendingSample = sample;
                    _shatterAt = _time + _p.ShatterDelaySeconds; // one-shot; fires in OnTimerTick
                }
            }
        }

        public void OnDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt)
        {
            if (evt.Reason == BlockDestructionReason.LevelReset || evt.Reason == BlockDestructionReason.WaterContact)
            {
                return; // level already failing; no cascade, no score event
            }
        }

        public void Teardown()
        {
            _context = default;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private void UpdateCrackStage(float limit)
        {
            float stage1 = _p.WarnLoadFraction;           // §5.3 default 0.7
            float stage2 = Mathf.Min(stage1 + 0.15f, 1f); // 0.85 at default
            int stage = _peakSustainedLoad >= stage2 * limit ? 2
                      : _peakSustainedLoad >= stage1 * limit ? 1 : 0;
            if (stage != _crackStage)
            {
                _crackStage = stage;
                _context.Services.PlayAudiocue(stage == 2 ? AudioCue.Crack85 : AudioCue.Creak60,
                    _context.Body.position);
                _context.Driver.SetCrackStage(stage); // swaps decal material, §9
            }
        }

        private void Shatter(in BlockStressSample sample)
        {
            _shattered = true;
            _context.Services.SpawnVfx(VfxId.Shatter, _context.Body.position, Vector2.up);
            _context.Services.PlayAudiocue(AudioCue.Shatter, _context.Body.position);
            _context.Services.RequestDestruction(_context.PieceId, BlockDestructionReason.Shattered,
                impulse: Vector2.zero);
            _context.Services.RaiseBehaviourTriggered(BlockBehaviourType.Breakable, _context.PieceId,
                sample.SustainedLoadUnits); // ScoreController metadata, §3
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

**Physics interactions & edge cases.** (1) *Removal semantics:* destruction disables the collider and marks the rigidbody kinematic in the same fixed step, so the solver never sees a zero-mass body; pieces above lose their support contact next step and re-fall — `StabilityMonitor` invalidates any in-progress settle window (§6). (2) *Cascades:* breakable-under-breakable is legal; the contact book rebuild naturally propagates load increases one step at a time, producing the readable domino shatter the original shows; `chainDepth` in the destruction metadata counts consecutive shatters within 0.5 s for §3 combo scoring. (3) *Debris:* chunks are non-colliding — they live on the VFX layer, excluded from the Layer Collision Matrix (§4) and from the Water kill trigger, so shatter debris over water splashes visually (particle raycast against the water surface, §9) but never fails the level — the *pieces* that fall in do. (4) *Carried/queue states:* dormant — no stress evaluation while kinematic. (5) *Gravity-flipped:* stress axis follows current gravity (§8.2), so a breakable on the ceiling platform works identically. (6) *Win window:* a shatter mid-window resets the 3-second countdown exactly like any other instability (§6); the documented win rule (all pieces placed, then the structure stands three seconds) is untouched — pieces destroyed after placement still count as placed, see §8.5.

### 8.4 B2 — Timed (disappearing)

Documented: "a timer runs out" → breaks/vanishes ([official Wii About](https://web.archive.org/web/20091116220135/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); countdown starts "when a new piece is placed atop them" and at zero the block disappears, "dropping everything above" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

| Aspect | Specification |
|--------|---------------|
| Trigger | First piece placed on top (support contact from a *released* piece) arms a one-shot countdown of `timerSeconds` (§5.3; `armImmediately` is the level-design escape hatch that arms on placement even unloaded); at zero the block vanishes |
| Effect | Instant removal (no corpse): collider off, everything supported re-falls; `PieceDestroyed(Expired)` |
| Visual | Hourglass/ring icon fills over lifetime; warning phase (final `warnRemainingSeconds`, 2 s default) pulses the block emissive, accelerating — capped at 3 Hz for photosensitivity (§14); last 1 s shrinks 5% scale per pulse as pre-collapse squash (§9 game feel) |
| Audio | Soft tick each second; tick rate doubles in warning phase; final 0.5 s rising tone then hollow "pop" on vanish (§9) |
| Counter-play | Stack timer blocks last and high; place light pieces above them; stagger multiple timers so cascades land separately; use the drop deliberately (shed a leaning side); race the 3-second win window — documented original behaviour the player must respect ([Nintendo Life WiiWare review](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), accessed 2026-09-24, for the window itself) |

| Parameter | Default | Range | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
| `timerSeconds` | 6 | 2–15 | §5.3; **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** <!-- TODO-VERIFY: original's exact timer length unknown; recover from gameplay footage if available. --> |
| `warnRemainingSeconds` | 2 | 0.5–4 | §5.3; warning phase length (absolute, not a fraction) |
| `armImmediately` | false | bool | §5.3; arms on placement even unloaded (level-design escape hatch) |
| `armOnContactFromAbove` | true | fixed | Documented arming rule |
| `resetOnNewContact` | false | fixed | Placing more pieces on an armed timer does *not* refresh it **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — reading of "a new piece is placed atop them" as the arming event |
| `disarmWhenUnloaded` | false | fixed | Knocking the load off does not stop the clock **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — keeps tension, simplest consistent rule |

**Physics interactions & edge cases.** (1) *Removal mid-stack:* identical semantics to B1 shatter (§8.3 case 1) — one-step support loss, settle-window invalidation. (2) *Never stacked:* an un-armed timer block behaves as a slightly lighter regular block forever (documented arming implies it). (3) *Water:* water contact fails the level before any expiry processing (§3 fail rule); a vanishing block's supported pieces that then touch water fail the attempt normally. (4) *Pause:* `OnTimerTick` stops when `GameStateMachine` pauses (timeScale 0 freezes the fixed loop, §6) — timers freeze with the game **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (original pause behaviour undocumented). (5) *Win window:* timers keep running during the 3-second window — the documented "drop everything above" happens whenever zero hits, so a level is only won if the remaining structure stands; this is the core tension of timer levels. (6) *Gravity flip:* arming direction follows current gravity (a piece landing on a timer now resting against the ceiling platform still arms it).

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>B2: arms when a released piece is placed on top; vanishes at zero (§8.4).</summary>
    public sealed class TimedBehaviour : IBlockBehaviour
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private BlockContext _context;
        private BlockBehaviourParams _p;
        private bool _armed;
        private float _remaining;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType => BlockBehaviourType.Timed;
        public float RemainingSeconds => _armed ? _remaining : float.NaN; // test hook, §8.9

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void Initialize(BlockContext context, BlockBehaviourParams parameters)
        {
            _context = context;
            _p = parameters; // flat §5.3 class; PropertyDrawer shows only the Timed group
            _armed = false;
            _remaining = _p.TimerSeconds;
        }

        public void OnPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt)
        {
            if (_p.ArmImmediately)
            {
                _armed = true; // §5.3 escape hatch: arms on placement even unloaded
            }
        }

        public void OnNeighborContact(in BlockContactEvent evt)
        {
            if (_armed || !IsContactFromAbove(in evt))
            {
                return;
            }

            _armed = true; // one-shot; no refresh on later contacts (design rule, §8.4)
        }

        public void OnTimerTick(float deltaTime)
        {
            if (!_armed)
            {
                return;
            }

            _remaining -= deltaTime;
            if (_remaining <= 0f)
            {
                _context.Services.SpawnVfx(VfxId.TimerVanish, _context.Body.position, Vector2.up);
                _context.Services.PlayAudiocue(AudioCue.TimerPop, _context.Body.position);
                _context.Services.RequestDestruction(_context.PieceId,
                    BlockDestructionReason.Expired, impulse: Vector2.zero);
            }
        }

        public void OnStress(ref BlockStressSample sample) { }

        public void OnDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt) { }

        public void Teardown()
        {
            _context = default;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private bool IsContactFromAbove(in BlockContactEvent evt)
        {
            // Contact normal points from this body toward the other; "above" means
            // against current gravity so ceiling stacks work after a B4 flip.
            return evt.IsNew && evt.OtherLayer == LayerMask.NameToLayer("Piece")
                && Vector2.Dot(evt.Normal, -Physics2D.gravity.normalized) > 0.707f;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Telegraph math: at default `timerSeconds = 6` (§5.3), warning occupies the final `warnRemainingSeconds = 2 s`; pulse frequency ramps `f(t) = lerp(1.5, 3.0, warningProgress)` Hz — the 3 Hz cap is the photosensitivity ceiling from §14. Tick cadence: 1 Hz nominal, 2 Hz in warning.

### 8.5 B3 — Fire (contact-pair detonation)

Documented: "the fire shape explodes on contact with another fire shape" ([official 3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); "flaming shapes explode when two touch" ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Not in the Wii original (its 2 specials were load-break and timer) — fire enters the vocabulary with the 2012 3DS edition.

| Aspect | Specification |
|--------|---------------|
| Trigger | Contact between two *fire* pieces — and only fire↔fire; contact with regular/special blocks or platforms is inert (official wording) |
| Effect | Both fire pieces detonate: removed instantly; radial impulse applied to dynamic bodies within `explosionRadius`; impulse can push stacks and can trip B1 slam thresholds (natural combo); `PieceDestroyed(Detonated)` ×2 |
| Visual | Constant ember shimmer (idle); ignition flare + expanding shockwave ring + ember burst on detonation; camera micro-shake per §6 camera juice rules (§9) |
| Audio | Low crackle loop while idle (ducked under music, §9); sharp double-crack detonation with sub-bass thump |
| Counter-play | Keep the pair separated in the final structure (long bridges, opposite ends); or detonate deliberately — both pieces count as *placed* (see accounting rule below), and the blast can tension-settle a wobbly neighbour stack or shed unwanted height |

| Parameter | Default | Range | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
| `fuseSecondsOnContact` | 0 | 0–0.2 | §5.3; 0 = instant (documented). Same-fixed-step pairing of both members is driver ordering (both destruction requests issue in one step), not a serialized delay |
| `explosionRadius` | 2.5 | 1.0–5.0 | §5.3; world units (m) |
| `explosionImpulse` | 8 | 2–16 | §5.3; impulse magnitude (kg·m/s) applied to affected bodies, scaled by falloff (not per-unit-mass) |
| `falloffExponent` | 2.0 | 1–3 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); `I(r) = I₀·(1 − r/R)·(1/r^falloffExponent)` |

All values **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (original gives no numbers).

**Placement accounting (interpretation, [ORIGINAL DESIGN]).** The documented win rule requires all pieces placed and the structure to stand three seconds ([Nintendo Life WiiWare](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), [Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), [Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Since timer blocks demonstrably vanish after placement while their levels remain winnable, destruction after placement cannot un-place a piece; the same accounting applies to detonated fire pairs and B1 shatters: `placed` is a one-way flag set on release, and the three-second stability check applies to whatever structure remains. Without this rule, any level containing two fire pieces would be unwinnable.

**Physics interactions & edge cases.** (1) *Carried pieces are kinematic* (§3 Carrying state) and generate no solver contacts, so hovering a carried fire piece over a settled one cannot detonate — detonation only occurs between released/settled fire pieces. This is also why `OnPlaced` exists as the behaviour activation point. (2) *Impulse application:* in one fixed step, `foreach` affected body → `AddForce(dir * I, ForceMode2D.Impulse)`; the body list comes from a non-alloc `Physics2D.OverlapCircleNonAlloc` against the Piece layer with a reused buffer; determinism preserved because ordering follows collider instance ids sorted once per detonation (§6). (3) *Fire + water:* a fire piece touching water fails the level first (documented fail rule outranks everything, §3); detonation near the surface spawns a splash VFX but the kill trigger only ever sees real pieces. (4) *Fire + breakable:* blast impulse counts as slam load next step — deliberate overload chains. (5) *Fire + timer:* detonation removing a timer's load does not disarm it (§8.4 rule). (6) *Win window:* detonation during the window resets the settle window like any instability; detonation before the final placement is pure level dynamics.

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>B3: detonates when two fire pieces touch; radial blast (§8.5).</summary>
    public sealed class FireBehaviour : IBlockBehaviour
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private BlockContext _context;
        private BlockBehaviourParams _p;
        private bool _detonated;
        private static readonly Collider2D[] BlastBuffer = new Collider2D[32]; // reused, non-alloc

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType => BlockBehaviourType.Fire;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void Initialize(BlockContext context, BlockBehaviourParams parameters)
        {
            _context = context;
            _p = parameters; // flat §5.3 class; PropertyDrawer shows only the Fire group
            _detonated = false;
        }

        public void OnPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt)
        {
            _context.Services.PlayAudiocue(AudioCue.FireCrackleLoop, _context.Body.position);
        }

        public void OnNeighborContact(in BlockContactEvent evt)
        {
            if (_detonated || evt.OtherLayer != LayerMask.NameToLayer("Piece")
                || !IsFirePiece(evt.OtherPieceId))
            {
                return; // fire↔fire only, per official wording
            }

            DetonatePair(evt.OtherPieceId);
        }

        public void OnTimerTick(float deltaTime) { }
        public void OnStress(ref BlockStressSample sample) { }
        public void OnDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt) { }
        public void Teardown() => _context = default;

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private bool IsFirePiece(int pieceId)
        {
            return _context.Services.GetBehaviourType(pieceId) == BlockBehaviourType.Fire;
        }

        private void DetonatePair(int otherPieceId)
        {
            _detonated = true;
            _context.Services.RequestDestruction(otherPieceId, BlockDestructionReason.Detonated,
                impulse: Vector2.zero);
            _context.Services.RequestDestruction(_context.PieceId, BlockDestructionReason.Detonated,
                impulse: Vector2.zero);
            ApplyBlast();
            _context.Services.SpawnVfx(VfxId.FireBlast, _context.Body.position, Vector2.up);
            _context.Services.PlayAudiocue(AudioCue.FireBlast, _context.Body.position);
            _context.Services.RaiseBehaviourTriggered(BlockBehaviourType.Fire, _context.PieceId, 0f);
        }

        private void ApplyBlast()
        {
            float radius = _p.ExplosionRadius; // world units (m), §5.3
            int count = Physics2D.OverlapCircleNonAlloc(_context.Body.position, radius, BlastBuffer,
                LayerMask.GetMask(nameof(Layer.Piece)));
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
            {
                Rigidbody2D target = BlastBuffer[i].attachedRigidbody;
                if (target == null || target == _context.Body)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                Vector2 dir = (Vector2)target.position - _context.Body.position;
                float r = Mathf.Max(dir.magnitude, 0.01f);
                float falloff = Mathf.Max(0f, 1f - r / radius)
                    / Mathf.Pow(Mathf.Max(r, 0.01f), _p.FalloffExponent);
                target.AddForce(dir.normalized * _p.ExplosionImpulse * falloff,
                    ForceMode2D.Impulse);
            }
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

### 8.6 B4 — Gravity-inverting

Documented: "the gravity shape inverts gravity" ([official 3DS About](https://web.archive.org/web/20151029143537/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24); gravity levels have "platforms at top AND bottom of screen and flip the stack", with the Wii U edition nudging players to turn the GamePad ([Cubed3 Wii U](http://www.cubed3.com/review/1648/1/art-of-balance-wii-u.html), accessed 2026-09-24 — control flavour is historical, see §11).

| Aspect | Specification |
|--------|---------------|
| Trigger | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (exact original moment unknown): the flip fires the fixed step after the gravity piece first *settles* (support contact + under settle velocity, §6) — i.e., when it becomes part of the structure |
| Effect | Global gravity sign inversion: `Physics2D.gravity = -Physics2D.gravity` applied at a physics-step boundary via `PhysicsStepper` (§6); all dynamic bodies re-fall toward the ceiling platform; `GravityInverted(pieceId)` raised; each gravity piece flips once, so a queue with N gravity pieces yields up to N flips |
| Visual | 0.4 s world-space hue-wave (no full-screen strobe, §14), directional arrow flip on the gravity piece, water surface keeps its position (the basin stays put — only gravity inverts); camera does a subtle 15° dip-and-recover, not a 180° roll |
| Audio | Deep whoosh + low sub swell; music tension layer steps up one band (§9 adaptive layers) |
| Counter-play | Flip early, before the tower is tall; pre-place light pieces on the ceiling platform so the flipped stack lands on prepared footing; use a flip to rescue a leaning tower (the re-fall re-settles geometry); remember stress axes flip too (§8.2) |

| Parameter | Default | Range | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
| `inversionDurationSeconds` | 0 | 0–30 | §5.3; 0 = latched until the piece is destroyed or the level ends; >0 = auto-flip-back after N seconds |
| `usesTopPlatformAnchor` | true | bool | §5.3; when true, LevelEditor requires a ceiling platform in the level (documented top+bottom platforms, §8.1.4 validation) |
| `flipOn` | Settle | Settle / Placement | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); per-piece trigger-mode toggle; Settle is the shipped default |
| `flipCount` | 1 | 1–3 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); flips per gravity piece |
| `cameraDipDegrees` | 15 | 0–30 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); presentation only |

**Global vs local gravity — decision.** **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** The original documents a stack-wide flip ("flip the stack") with ceiling platforms, which is *global* inversion; we implement exactly that (`Physics2D.gravity` sign flip — one engine call, deterministic, affects the stress axis and timer arming direction automatically). A *local* alternative (region-limited inversion via an effector volume) was rejected for v1: it contradicts the documented whole-stack flip, complicates the support graph, and buys no level vocabulary the global version lacks. It remains a candidate sequel extension implemented as an additional behaviour, not a parameter.

**Physics interactions & edge cases.** (1) *Application point:* the flip is scheduled through `IBlockGameplayServices.RequestGravityFlip` → `LevelManager` → `PhysicsStepper`, executed between fixed steps so the solver never sees gravity change mid-step (§6 determinism; replays stay bit-identical). (2) *Water:* the basin does not move; after a flip, unfinished stacks fall *up*, away from the water — flipping becomes a rescue tool, which is the core of the level grammar. Pieces that were mid-fall downward when the flip lands still carry downward momentum and can hit water; the kill trigger is position-based and unchanged. (3) *Buoyancy cosmetics:* water-surface splash/debris effects use `BuoyancyEffector2D` (2D native, §6); its behaviour under negative global gravity is not captured in the physics research and is cosmetic-only in our clone (water contact fails the level before buoyancy can matter). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: BuoyancyEffector2D force direction under flipped Physics2D.gravity — the submerged-fraction formula was not captured in the physics track; verify in a scratch scene, or replace with the manual splash raycast if it inverts wrongly. --> (4) *Win window:* a flip during the 3-second window resets it (any destabilizer does, §6). (5) *Input:* pointer/cursor mapping stays screen-relative, so controls are unchanged by the flip — the modern analogue of the original's "turn the GamePad" hint is a no-op on our platforms (§7, §11). (6) *Multiple simultaneous settles:* flips are queued and applied one per step, deterministically ordered by piece id.

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>B4: inverts global gravity once the piece settles (§8.6).</summary>
    public sealed class GravityBehaviour : IBlockBehaviour
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private BlockContext _context;
        private BlockBehaviourParams _p;
        private int _flipsRemaining;
        private bool _wasSettled;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType => BlockBehaviourType.GravityInverter;
        public bool FlipConsumed => _flipsRemaining <= 0; // test hook, §8.9

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void Initialize(BlockContext context, BlockBehaviourParams parameters)
        {
            _context = context;
            _p = parameters; // flat §5.3 class; PropertyDrawer shows only the GravityInverter group
            _flipsRemaining = _p.FlipCount;
            _wasSettled = false;
        }

        public void OnPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt) { }

        public void OnNeighborContact(in BlockContactEvent evt) { }

        public void OnTimerTick(float deltaTime)
        {
            bool settled = _context.Body.IsAwake == false
                || _context.Body.velocity.sqrMagnitude < 0.0025f; // 0.05 m/s, §6 settle predicate

            if (_flipsRemaining > 0 && _wasSettled == false && settled)
            {
                _wasSettled = true;
                _flipsRemaining--;
                _context.Services.RequestGravityFlip(_context.PieceId); // applied at step boundary
            }
        }

        public void OnStress(ref BlockStressSample sample) { }
        public void OnDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt) { }
        public void Teardown() => _context = default;

        #endregion
    }
}
```

### 8.7 B5 — Linked seesaw pairs

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** in its entirety (chief-architect decision: the original's fifth special is unverified — the archived official sentence truncates after the gravity shape — so the seesaw is our extension, designed to fill a vocabulary gap none of the four documented specials covers: *distributed balancing across two locations*).

Concept: two blocks tagged with the same `linkGroupId` (§5.3) are mechanically linked so their rotations are anti-phase — tilt one and its partner counter-tilts, like two ends of an invisible balance beam. A pair member may optionally be pinned to a world pivot (a fixed anchor), turning it into a true seesaw platform; the classic configuration is one anchored platform receiving load while its free-floating partner (or a second anchored platform elsewhere) counter-rotates, so mass placed on one end visibly tips the other.

| Aspect | Specification |
|--------|---------------|
| Trigger | Passive constraint — always active from `OnPlaced` of the second member; no discrete trigger |
| Effect | Anti-phase rotation coupling `θ_A + θ_B = Θ₀` enforced by equal-and-opposite corrective torques each fixed step; if either member is destroyed, the link shatters (`OnDestroyed` → `LinkBroken`) and the survivor becomes a free regular block |
| Visual | Faint dashed arc of light between partners (readability of the invisible linkage); pivot members show a pin cap; both glow briefly when the link engages |
| Audio | Soft ratchet ticks proportional to coupled angular speed; a metallic snap on link break |
| Counter-play | Balance torques deliberately: place mass on the partner to level a tipping platform; exploit the coupling to sense load remotely (the partner's tilt telegraphs overload before B1 thresholds trip) |

**Constraint approach: joint vs custom torque coupling — decision.** Unity 2D joints offer no primitive expressing anti-phase coupling between two free rigidbodies: `RelativeJoint2D` drives *relative* rotation toward a target (parallel coupling) and motorized hinge configurations fight the solver and jitter under load. We therefore use a **custom soft constraint**: a PD controller applying equal-and-opposite torques, which conserves angular momentum, composes cleanly with contacts, and degrades gracefully (a momentarily violated constraint self-corrects) instead of exploding. The one place a *native* joint is correct is the **pivot**: an anchored member rotates about a fixed world point via `HingeJoint2D` to a static `Rigidbody2D` — native, stable, and exactly the semantics a pivot needs.

Math (game-designer rule: show the formulas). Error against the anti-phase target, shortest-arc:

```
e   = DeltaAngle(Θ₀ − (θ_A + θ_B))                       [rad]
τ   = k_p · e − k_d · (ω_A + ω_B)                        [N·m]
apply +τ to A, −τ to B                                   (equal-opposite ⇒ momentum conserved)
```

Tuning for a coupled period `T_c` and the smaller partner inertia `I_min`: `k_p = I_min · (2π/T_c)²`, critical damping `k_d = 2·√(k_p · I_min)` (ζ = 1). Worked default: a 1 kg, 0.4 m plank has `I = mL²/12 ≈ 0.0133 kg·m²`; with `T_c = 0.4 s`, `k_p = 0.0133 · (15.71)² ≈ 3.3 N·m/rad` and `k_d = 2·√(3.3 · 0.0133) ≈ 0.42 N·m·s`. Under-damping (ζ ≈ 0.6) is deliberately available via `dampingRatio < 1` — a springier link reads better at small amplitudes at the cost of oscillation the player must then damp by hand (tension/rest pacing, §8.8).

Serialized-contract note: the seesaw group in the §5.3 flat class is period/damping-authored (`linkGroupId`, `coupledPeriodSeconds`, `dampingRatio`, `targetSumDegrees`, `anchored`, `breakOnPartnerLoss`); `k_p` is always derived per the formula above. This parameterization replaces the raw-stiffness trio an earlier §5.3 draft carried (`couplingStiffness`, `maxPivotAngleDegrees`, `pivotOffset`): designer-legible periods beat raw stiffness as an authoring surface, `maxPivotAngleDegrees` has no consumer here (break-on-partner-loss governs link severing), and the pivot anchor point is the member's own position (`hinge.anchor = Vector2.zero`), not a serialized offset.

| Parameter | Default | Range | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
| `linkGroupId` | — | 0–255 | §5.3; must occur exactly twice per level (LevelEditor validation, §5) |
| `coupledPeriodSeconds` | 0.4 | 0.2–1.0 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); drives derived `k_p` per above |
| `dampingRatio` | 1.0 | 0.5–1.5 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); 1.0 = critical |
| `targetSumDegrees` | 0 | ±180 | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); `Θ₀`; 0 = mirrors |
| `anchored` | false | bool | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); if true, member gets a `HingeJoint2D` to a static anchor |
| `breakOnPartnerLoss` | true | bool | §8-only (homed, §8.1.4); link-sever semantics |

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Gameplay.Blocks
{
    /// <summary>B5: anti-phase torque coupling between two paired blocks (§8.7).</summary>
    public sealed class SeesawBehaviour : IBlockBehaviour
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private BlockContext _context;
        private BlockBehaviourParams _p;
        private float _kp;
        private float _kd;
        private bool _linked;

        #endregion

        #region Public Properties

        public BlockBehaviourType BehaviourType => BlockBehaviourType.LinkedSeesaw;
        public bool IsLinked => _linked; // test hook, §8.9

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        public void Initialize(BlockContext context, BlockBehaviourParams parameters)
        {
            _context = context;
            _p = parameters; // flat §5.3 class; PropertyDrawer shows only the LinkedSeesaw group
            float inertia = Mathf.Min(context.Definition.RotationalInertia, PartnerInertiaOrDefault());
            _kp = inertia * Mathf.Pow(2f * Mathf.PI / _p.CoupledPeriodSeconds, 2f); // derived, not serialized
            _kd = 2f * _p.DampingRatio * Mathf.Sqrt(_kp * inertia);
            _linked = false;
        }

        public void OnPlaced(in BlockPlacementEvent evt)
        {
            // Link engages only when both members are live and dynamic.
            if (_context.Services.TryGetPartner(_p.LinkGroupId, out Rigidbody2D partner)
                && partner != null && partner.bodyType == RigidbodyType2D.Dynamic)
            {
                _linked = true;
                if (_p.Anchored)
                {
                    AttachPivot();
                }
            }
        }

        public void OnNeighborContact(in BlockContactEvent evt) { }

        public void OnTimerTick(float deltaTime)
        {
            if (!_linked || !_context.Services.TryGetPartner(_p.LinkGroupId, out Rigidbody2D partner)
                || partner == null)
            {
                return;
            }

            float error = Mathf.DeltaAngle(_p.TargetSumDegrees,
                _context.Body.rotation + partner.rotation);             // shortest arc [deg]
            float torque = (_kp * error * Mathf.Deg2Rad)
                         - (_kd * (_context.Body.angularVelocity + partner.angularVelocity));
            _context.Body.AddTorque(torque);
            partner.AddTorque(-torque);                                  // equal-opposite pair
        }

        public void OnStress(ref BlockStressSample sample) { }

        public void OnDestroyed(in BlockDestructionEvent evt)
        {
            if (evt.PairId == _p.LinkGroupId && evt.Reason != BlockDestructionReason.LinkBroken)
            {
                // Partner died: sever silently; survivor keeps physics as a plain block.
                _linked = false;
                _context.Services.RaiseBehaviourTriggered(BlockBehaviourType.LinkedSeesaw,
                    _context.PieceId, 0f);
            }
        }

        public void Teardown()
        {
            _linked = false;
            _context = default;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private float PartnerInertiaOrDefault()
        {
            return _context.Services.TryGetPartner(_p.LinkGroupId, out Rigidbody2D partner) && partner != null
                ? partner.inertia
                : _context.Definition.RotationalInertia;
        }

        private void AttachPivot()
        {
            var hinge = _context.Body.GetComponent<HingeJoint2D>();
            if (hinge == null)
            {
                hinge = _context.Body.gameObject.AddComponent<HingeJoint2D>();
            }

            hinge.connectedBody = _context.Services.GetStaticAnchor(_context.Body.position);
            hinge.autoConfigureConnectedAnchor = false;
            hinge.anchor = Vector2.zero;
            hinge.connectedAnchor = _context.Body.position;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

**Physics interactions & edge cases.** (1) *Torque magnitudes:* both torques are applied in the same fixed step; because they are equal-opposite, the pair's total angular momentum is conserved and the solver never receives net free energy. (2) *Sleeping bodies:* Box2D-line island sleeping (§6) can sleep one partner while the other is disturbed; the coupling torque wakes both (`AddTorque` wakes the body), so a sleeping pair cannot silently desynchronize. (3) *Determinism:* coupling runs only in the fixed step with parameters derived from serialized data — no frame-rate dependence (§6 replay tests). (4) *Partner destroyed:* `OnDestroyed` fires on the survivor with the partner's `linkGroupId`; the survivor de-links and continues as a plain block (weight unchanged). (5) *Pair in queue together:* linking waits for the second `OnPlaced`; the first member behaves as a plain block until then, so partial-pair states are stable. (6) *Win window:* coupling is continuous dynamics — it neither needs nor gets special window handling beyond the normal settle predicate, but a still-oscillating link (ζ < 1 setups) will legitimately delay the settle window, which is the intended skill test.

### 8.8 Puzzle-design grammar

Each behaviour adds a distinct verb to the level vocabulary. Placement of specials across the campaign is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — the original never published its world themes or per-world special introduction (only "8 worlds each with its own unique lounge style", [official microsite](https://web.archive.org/web/20201019172749/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/3ds/), accessed 2026-09-24), and the Wii original shipped with only the first two specials (load-break, timer; [official Wii About](https://web.archive.org/web/20091116220135/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24), proving the two oldest behaviours can carry a full campaign alone.

| Behaviour | Core skill it teaches | Grammar role | Example levels |
|-----------|----------------------|--------------|----------------|
| B1 Breakable | load distribution, mass planning | "soft ground" — forces wide, bridged bases; sacrificial layers | *Three's Company*: single breakable pedestal, queue of 3 regulars + 1 long plank — the plank must take the 4th load off the pedestal. *Hollow Pyramid*: breakable cores inside a pyramid; solve by cantilevering. *Shock Absorber*: breakable sandwiched under a tall column absorbs a deliberate slam, dropping the column onto a wide base intact |
| B2 Timed | tempo, routing order, urgency spikes | "ticking ground" — tension curve with a hard climax; pairs naturally with Time Challenges (documented challenge types, [official Wii About](https://web.archive.org/web/20091116220135/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com:80/about.php), accessed 2026-09-24) | *Staircase*: three timers with staggered lifetimes under ascending steps — finish the tower before the ground leaves. *Keystone Bridge*: timers as bridge piers; rebuild the span twice as the piers vanish. *Last Light*: everything rests on one 4 s timer; the 3-second win window must start before expiry — teaches racing the documented countdown |
| B3 Fire | spatial separation, controlled demolition | "live cargo" — two pieces that must never meet (or must meet *exactly* once, on purpose) | *Bookends*: fire pair anchors opposite ends of a long bridge; the middle must be built first. *Controlled Burn*: detonate the pair to shed a leaning side before placing the finale. *Hot Rails* (Swift Stacker): fire pair mid-queue forces both teams to re-route under time pressure (§11 mode parity) |
| B4 Gravity | planning upside-down, momentum rescue | "world flip" — re-frames the whole basin; strongest single-behaviour difficulty spike | *Ceiling Garden*: ceiling platform only — build top-down after an early flip. *Double Journey*: two gravity pieces; the solution flips mid-solve to relocate the effective base. *Upstream*: a pre-built leaning tower on the water's edge must be flipped to be saved before adding the finale |
| B5 Seesaw | remote load sensing, counterweighting | "distributed scale" — two-place balancing none of the other verbs covers | *Counterweight*: anchored seesaw platform + free partner; three units left must be balanced by one unit at thrice the arm on the partner. *Seesaw Relay*: chain of two pairs where loading one platform un-tips the next. *Twin Scales* (Height Challenge, documented type): build equally on both partners to keep both level while climbing |

**World-arc plan [ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (aligns with the §3.8.2/§5.6.1 content plan of 8 worlds × 25 levels): W1 base blocks only (pure stacking tuition); W2 introduces B1; W3 introduces B2; W4 introduces no new block behaviour — its content is the documented swaying/floating platform bases (§3.8.2, §5.6.1; platform vocabulary specified in §5/§6, excluded from this section's scope), which re-frame stacking on a moving reference frame without adding a block verb; W5 introduces B3 (fire); W6 introduces B4 (gravity); W7 introduces B5 (seesaw); W8 mixes all five at maximum density. Cross-behaviour pairing is not a dedicated world: it lives inside the §3.8.3 twist beat — levels 11–17 of each world combine that world's verb with the previous world's (B1+B2 cascades from W3 on, B3+B4 flip-detonations from W6 on) — and culminates in W7's twist/climax levels and throughout W8. Pacing follows the game-designer tension/rest rule: each introduction world spends its first 3 levels (the §3.8.3 teach beat) on single-behaviour teaching puzzles with oversized platforms, then interleaves; each world's final levels are climax mixes, and the first level after a climax is a rest level using only familiar verbs. Mode gating: Endurance draws specials only from worlds the player has unlocked (§3); Tower Tumble's random piece generation excludes B3 fire and B4 gravity until round 5+ (a mid-round gravity flip in a pass-the-parcel mode is a chaos spike, not a puzzle — deliberate exclusion **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**); Infinity uses base + B1 only, since its height-scoring loop (§12) punishes disappearance and flips.

### 8.9 Test matrix and automated test hooks

Rows are behaviours; columns are the lifecycle states from §3/§6. Every cell is an executable expectation wired to the automated hooks below.

| Behaviour | In queue/tray | Carried | Falling (released, airborne) | Resting/stacked | Water contact | Win window (3 s) | Post-win | Paused |
|-----------|---------------|---------|------------------------------|-----------------|---------------|------------------|----------|--------|
| B0 Base | inert | kinematic, no sim | dynamics on | normal | **fail level** (documented) | settle predicate applies (§6) | frozen | sim frozen |
| B1 Breakable | inert | dormant (no stress eval) | stress eval on (slam can trip on landing impact) | crack stages telegraph; break when `L_s` or `L_d` over | piece fails level before any shatter scoring | shatter resets window; destroyed ≠ un-placed | dormant | frozen; crack state persists |
| B2 Timed | not armed | dormant — carrying does not arm | not armed (no support contact) | arms on first contact-from-above; ticks; vanishes at zero | fail first; armed timer in water never expires | keeps ticking; expiry resets window | dormant | tick frozen; armed state persists |
| B3 Fire | inert | kinematic — cannot detonate while carried | can detonate on fire↔fire mid-air contact | detonates on fire↔fire contact only | fail first (blast never pre-empts water) | detonation resets window; both count placed | dormant | frozen; no contacts processed |
| B4 Gravity | inert | dormant | dormant (flip waits for settle) | fires on settle; queue flips one/step; axes re-derive | piece fails level; queued flips cancelled | flip resets window | dormant | frozen; queue preserved |
| B5 Seesaw | inert (pair incomplete) | dormant | link can engage at second member's `OnPlaced` | coupling torque each step; partner-loss severs | piece fails level; link severs (`LinkBroken`) | oscillation legitimately delays settle | dormant | frozen; torque not applied |

**Automated hooks.** (1) *Edit Mode (pure logic, no scene):* every behaviour is constructible with a hand-built `BlockContext` (null `Rigidbody2D` allowed for non-physics paths); `BlockTestHarness` drives `OnTimerTick`/`OnStress` sequences deterministically — this is why behaviours take delta time as a parameter instead of reading the clock. (2) *Deterministic seeded inputs:* any randomness (none in v1 behaviours, but future ones may add it) comes from a `Random.State` injected via services, so replay tests (§6, §14) reproduce runs bit-identically. (3) *CI categories:* tests carry `[Category("Blocks.Breakable")]`-style markers matching the §16 `-testCategory` invocation; the full matrix above maps 1:1 to category-prefixed test names (`Blocks.Timed.WinWindow_KeepsTicking_ResetsWindowOnExpiry`). (4) *Inspector/debug overlay:* the §8.1.4 gizmo toggles (load bar for B1, countdown ring for B2, link arc for B5) double as manual verification aids during milestone reviews (§10).

Representative Edit Mode test (NUnit, mirrors §14 conventions):

```csharp
using NUnit.Framework;
using UnityEngine;
using Aob.Gameplay.Blocks;

public sealed class TimedBehaviourTests
{
    [Test]
    [Category("Blocks.Timed")]
    public void ArmsOnlyOnContactFromAbove_ThenExpiresAtZero()
    {
        var behaviour = new TimedBehaviour();
        // Default-valued §5.3 params (timerSeconds = 6); the harness reconfigures
        // serialized fields via SerializedObject when a test needs non-defaults.
        var harness = BlockTestHarness.Create(behaviour, new BlockBehaviourParams());

        harness.Tick(1f);
        Assert.IsTrue(float.IsNaN(behaviour.RemainingSeconds), "Must not tick before arming.");

        harness.Contact(fromAbove: true);
        harness.Tick(4.5f);
        Assert.AreEqual(1.5f, behaviour.RemainingSeconds, 1e-4f, "Lifetime must count down.");

        harness.Tick(1.5f);
        Assert.AreEqual(BlockDestructionReason.Expired, harness.LastDestructionReason);
    }

    [Test]
    [Category("Blocks.Timed")]
    public void SideContact_DoesNotArm()
    {
        var behaviour = new TimedBehaviour();
        var harness = BlockTestHarness.Create(behaviour, new BlockBehaviourParams());

        harness.Contact(fromAbove: false);
        harness.Tick(5f);
        Assert.IsTrue(float.IsNaN(behaviour.RemainingSeconds));
    }
}
```

`BlockTestHarness` is an Editor-test-assembly helper that builds the context, fakes `IBlockGameplayServices` with recording stubs (`LastDestructionReason`, raised-event log), and exposes `Tick`/`Contact(fromAbove)`/`SetStress` — the single seam that makes the whole matrix automatable without Play Mode physics. Physics-coupled expectations (slam trips, cascade timing, seesaw settle) run as Play Mode tests on the §14 scripted-input rig instead, seeded through `PhysicsStepper`. One such Play Mode test is mandatory so the §8.2 slam arithmetic cannot regress silently: `Blocks.Breakable.SlamNormalization_OneBlockDropSafe_FireBlastTrips` asserts (a) a one-block-height drop onto a breakable (`Δy` = 0.5 m, the §8.2 world-scale pin; expected `L_d ≈ 6.4` at `h_ref` = 0.05 s) lands **below** `maxSupportedMassRmu × slamFactor` (= 7.5 at defaults), and (b) a fire blast detonating near a breakable lands **above** it — pinning both sides of the "mild drops safe, hard slams break" band at both §6 simulation tiers (240 Hz and the 120 Hz mobile tier).

Cross-references: data authoring and validation for all parameters live in §5 (`PieceDefinition`, `BlockBehaviourType`, `LevelEditor`); execution timing, settle predicate, and event plumbing live in §6 (`LevelManager`, `StabilityMonitor`, `PhysicsStepper`); win/lose precedence and destruction scoring live in §3; visuals/audio cues in §9; accessibility caps (pulse rates, palettes) in §14; implementation tasks in §20; historical behaviour of the specials on Wii U/PS4/Switch in §11–§13.

## 9. Visual & Audio Recreation Plan

This section specifies everything the player sees and hears: art direction, URP configuration per quality tier, the water and block shader recipes, lighting, the UGUI presentation layer, VFX, audio direction with the adaptive-music system, and the Blender→Unity asset pipeline. Factual grounding is the T10 (URP/UGUI/settings) and T01 (franchise presentation) research tracks, corrected by the adversarial verify pass. Version baseline throughout: Unity 6.6 (6000.6) with the URP 17.x generation, on a release train of 6.0/6.3 LTS through 6.6 stable and 6.7 Beta as of 2026-09-24 ([URP asset reference, Unity 6.0 Manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Platform scope follows the chief-architect order — Windows + macOS (Steam) first, then Android, iOS, Xbox last — with Switch/PS4/Wii U treated only as historical study (§11–§13).

What is **[DOCUMENTED]** about the original's presentation is thin but load-bearing: "relaxing lounge soundtrack", "8 beautiful environments", "each with its own unique lounge style" ([Shin'en Switch microsite](https://web.archive.org/web/20201015074209/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/switch/), accessed 2026-09-24; [Shin'en press sheet, Switch](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), live 2026-09-24); reviewer descriptions of "jazzy, relaxing" music and satisfying wooden clunk placement SFX in the HD editions ([Nintendo Life Wii U review](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), 2014-10-03); and the three-green-light countdown UI ([Nintendo Life WiiWare review](https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192755/https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2010/02/art_of_balance), 2010-02-18). What is NOT documented anywhere — world names/themes, exact palettes, the composer credit, any internal render configuration — is designed here and flagged **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

The composer of the original soundtrack is not named in any fetched source (T01 open thread: MobyGames bot-walled, in-game credits unreachable, archived press "credits" sheet empty). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: composer credit via in-game credits before any historical attribution appears in shipped docs. --> For the clone this is moot by policy: we compose original music **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** in the documented lounge idiom. We clone mechanics and mood, never Shin'en's audio-visual assets.

#### 9.1.2 Style pillars **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

1. **Toy-box readability first.** Blocks read as painted wooden/plastic toys on a spa table: flat-shaded low-poly, beveled edges, saturated but desaturated-back palette, no PBR roughness maps. Every piece type is identifiable by silhouette alone (shape first, color second, icon overlay last) — this doubles as the colorblind-safety rule (§14).
2. **Calm water, honest boundary.** The water is the fail boundary (§3); its visual surface must coincide with the physics contact plane within a fixed tolerance (math in §9.3.5). Calm gradients, gentle waves, no opaque spray that hides the waterline.
3. **Spa lighting.** One warm "window" key light per world, soft shadows, low-contrast ambient — directly extending anchor A5.
4. **Lounge mood per world.** Each of the 8 worlds swaps palette, water tint, key-light temperature, and music bank; within a world all 25 levels share the theme so progression reads as travel (content structure per §5).
5. **60 fps everywhere.** Anchor A10 makes 60 fps the feel baseline; visual budget decisions below never trade below 60 on any v1 target platform.

World names/themes are undocumented (A1), so all eight are original designs. Hex values are sRGB authoring values (project is Linear color space, §4). "Water S→D" is the shallow→deep gradient pair consumed by the water shader (§9.3.3).
