#### 9.1.4 `WorldThemeSO` — theme data model **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

One asset per world; consumed by `LevelManager` on scene load (§6), the water controller (§9.3.6), the light rig (§9.5), and `AudioDirector` (§6 system map; layer clips selected here). Referenced from `WorldDefinition` (§5).

```csharp
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Audio;

/// <summary>
/// Per-world art and audio direction. Single source of truth for palette,
/// water tints, light rig values and music bank selection (see §5 WorldDefinition, §6 LevelManager).
/// </summary>
[CreateAssetMenu(fileName = "WorldTheme_W0", menuName = "AoB/World Theme")]
public class WorldThemeSO : ScriptableObject
{
    #region Serialized Fields

    [Header("Identity")]
    [SerializeField] private string worldCodename = "W1_SpaDawn";
    [SerializeField, Range(0, 7)] private int worldIndex;

    [Header("Palette (sRGB authoring)")]
    [SerializeField] private Color backgroundTint = Color.white;
    [SerializeField] private Color platformTint = Color.white;
    [SerializeField] private Color accentTint = Color.gray;

    [Header("Water (§9.3)")]
    [SerializeField] private Color waterShallow = new Color(0.35f, 0.72f, 0.84f);
    [SerializeField] private Color waterDeep = new Color(0.06f, 0.31f, 0.47f);
    [SerializeField, Range(0f, 0.12f)] private float waveAmplitude = 0.045f;
    [SerializeField, Range(0.05f, 1f)] private float waveFrequency = 0.25f;

    [Header("Lighting (§9.5)")]
    [SerializeField] private Color keyLightColor = Color.white;
    [SerializeField, Range(-180f, 180f)] private float keyLightAzimuthDeg = 35f;
    [SerializeField, Range(0f, 90f)] private float keyLightElevationDeg = 55f;
    [SerializeField, Range(0f, 3f)] private float keyLightIntensity = 1.2f;
    [SerializeField] private Color ambientColor = new Color(0.55f, 0.55f, 0.55f);

    [Header("Post FX volume profile (§9.2.5)")]
    [SerializeField] private VolumeProfile postFxProfile;

    [Header("Music bank (§9.8)")]
    [SerializeField] private AudioClip calmLoop;
    [SerializeField] private AudioClip tensionLoop;
    [SerializeField] private AudioClip menuLoop;
    [SerializeField] private AudioMixerGroup musicMixerGroup;

    #endregion

    #region Public Properties

    public int WorldIndex => worldIndex;
    public Color WaterShallow => waterShallow;
    public Color WaterDeep => waterDeep;
    public float WaveAmplitude => waveAmplitude;
    public float WaveFrequency => waveFrequency;
    public AudioClip CalmLoop => calmLoop;
    public AudioClip TensionLoop => tensionLoop;
    public AudioMixerGroup MusicMixerGroup => musicMixerGroup;

    #endregion

    #region Public Methods

    /// <summary>Elevation/azimuth to a directional-light rotation, Y-up, forward = -Z.</summary>
    public Quaternion KeyLightRotation()
    {
        float elev = Mathf.Clamp(keyLightElevationDeg, 0f, 90f);
        return Quaternion.Euler(elev, keyLightAzimuthDeg, 0f);
    }

    #endregion
}
```

`VolumeProfile` reference requires `using UnityEngine.Rendering;` in the real file (kept out of the excerpt for brevity — the shipped skeleton includes it).

#### 9.1.5 Readability constraints **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

- The waterline must hold luminance contrast ≥ 3:1 against every block color of the current world (checked by the §5 level-validation tool at authoring time, not at runtime).
- Special-block telegraphy is never color-only: timer blocks also pulse scale, fire blocks emit ember particles, gravity blocks show an arrow field (§8 behaviours define the events; §9.4.3 the shaders).
- The three countdown lights (A7) render at fixed HUD anchor bottom-center, green #3FBF5F, each accompanied by an audio tick (§9.8.6) — visual+audio redundancy.

### 9.2 URP configuration and quality-tier matrix

#### 9.2.1 Rendering path decision

The path is chosen on the Universal Renderer asset (renderer data), not the URP asset; options are Forward / Forward+ / Deferred (+ Deferred+ in newer 17.x) (T10). **Decision: Forward on every tier [ORIGINAL DESIGN]**, on documented facts:

- MSAA is forward-only — "MSAA is supported only in forward rendering paths" ([Quality settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — and MSAA is the right AA for hard-edged low-poly toys (no TAA ghosting on falling pieces).
- Deferred trades g-buffer bandwidth for per-pixel light count; this scene has one directional key plus ≤2 accents, the exact wrong trade for low-poly stylized content (T10 analysis of the [rendering paths reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/RenderingPaths.html), accessed 2026-09-24).
- Forward+'s clustered grid makes the Additional Lights Per Object Limit irrelevant — "Unity ignores this setting if you select the Forward+ rendering path" ([URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — but we don't have enough lights to need the grid, and its fixed overhead is pure loss on mobile.
- The experimental 2D Renderer is explicitly not needed for a 3D stylized water game — with it enabled, "some of the options related to 3D rendering in the URP Asset don't have any impact" ([URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Our presentation is 3D even though the simulation is a 2D single plane (§6 physics decision).
- Rendering-path dropdown wording and Render Graph default status in 6.6 could not be verified — the Universal Renderer asset reference page never resolved during research (T10 open thread). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Universal Renderer asset page slug + exact rendering-path dropdown wording + Render Graph/Compatibility Mode defaults under 6000.6. -->

#### 9.2.2 Quality mechanics

One URP Asset per quality level, assigned in Edit > Project Settings > Quality ("Render Pipeline: Sets the Render Pipeline Asset to use at this quality level"); the levels×platforms matrix takes one green default per platform ([Quality settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Texture-streaming knobs live here too (defaults: Memory Budget 512 MB, Renderers/Frame 512, Max Level Reduction 2, Max IO Requests 1024 — documented on the same page). Switch player settings and budgets are NDA-gated by design ([Player settings hub](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-PlayerSettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24), so any Switch numbers below are community conventions, not citations (T10).

#### 9.2.3 Quality-tier table **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Setting names are the exact URP asset fields (documented semantics per the [URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), docs built 2026-09-23); values are our tier recipe.

| URP asset setting | T1 PC-High | T2 PC-Low / Steam Deck | T3 Mobile-High | T4 Mobile-Low | T5 Console-class (Xbox; §13 Switch study envelope) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HDR | On | On | Off | Off | On (Off fallback if bandwidth-bound) |
| HDR Precision | 32-Bit | 32-Bit | n/a | n/a | 32-Bit |
| Anti Aliasing (MSAA) | 4x | 2x | 4x | 2x | 2x |
| Render Scale | 1.0 | 0.9 | 0.85 | 0.7 | 0.75–0.9 |
| Upscaling Filter | FSR 1.0 (sharpen at 1.0 permitted — stays active at Render Scale 1.0) | FSR 1.0 | FSR 1.0 | FSR 1.0 | FSR 1.0 |
| Depth Texture | On | On | On | On | On |
| Opaque Texture | On | On | On | On | On |
| Opaque Downsampling | None | None | 2x Bilinear | 2x Bilinear | None |
| Main Light | Pixel + Cast Shadows | Pixel + Cast Shadows | Pixel + Cast Shadows | Pixel + Cast Shadows | Pixel + Cast Shadows |
| Main Light Shadow Resolution | 2048 | 1024 | 1024 | 512 | 1024 |
| Shadow Max Distance | 50 | 30 | 25 | 15 | 20–30 |
| Cascade Count | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Additional Lights | Per Pixel, limit 8 | Per Vertex, limit 4 | Per Vertex, limit 2 | Disabled | Per Vertex, limit 2–4 |
| Post-processing | Full set (§9.2.5) | Bloom + Tonemapping | LDR grading + Bloom | LDR grading | Bloom (low) + Tonemapping |
| SRP Batcher | On | On | On | On | On |
| Terrain Holes | Off (variant stripping) | Off | Off | Off | Off |
| Adaptive Performance section | — | — | Enabled (Android package) | Enabled | — |

Documented constraints baked into this table: "Render Scale … scales the render target resolution (not the resolution of your current device)"; STP 1.0 "forces camera TAA" (only worth it on T1, and we prefer MSAA, so STP stays off); "The Nearest-Neighbour filter doesn't work if Post-processing is enabled"; on mobile without StoreAndResolve, "MSAA is ignored at runtime if Opaque Texture is enabled" — the reason T3/T4 keep Opaque Downsampling at 2x Bilinear and accept that some devices silently drop MSAA (all quoted from the [URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Increasing cascade count reduces performance and cascades affect only the main light (same page) — hence 1 cascade everywhere but T1. The Adaptive Performance section appears in the URP asset when the package is installed and "adjusts the rendering quality at runtime" (same page) — T3/T4 leverage it for Android thermal management (§18 budgets).

Dynamic batching: the 6.0-documented Dynamic Batching toggle under advanced properties is reported removed in Unity 6.6 by the 6000.6.0f1 release notes (T02 digest; [What's new 6000.6.0f1](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1)). We treat SRP Batcher + GPU instancing + static batching on basin meshes as the complete batching strategy; SRP Batcher takes precedence when both exist anyway (documented, URP asset reference). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: presence/absence of the Dynamic Batching toggle in the URP asset under 6000.6 in-editor (docs 6.0 page lists it; 6.6 release notes report removal). -->

#### 9.2.4 Platform assignments and runtime scaling

| Platform (§2 order) | Default tier | Switchable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows (Steam) | T1 | T2 via options | Graphics API order per §19 |
| macOS (Steam) | T1 | T2 | Metal-only in practice (verify-pass: Apple rejects GLES; Unity defaults to Metal) |
| Steam Deck | T2 | — | Deck Verified checklist in §19 |
| Android | T3 | T4 via Adaptive Performance floor | Vulkan + GLES3 fallback (§18) |
| iOS | T3 | T4 | ProMotion 120 Hz is gated OFF by default — 60 Hz is our target anyway (documented: [Application.targetFrameRate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Xbox | T5 | — | Last in the v1 order; §19 |
| Switch (historical study §13) | T5 | — | Docked 1080p / handheld 720p budget envelope = community convention (low-medium confidence, NDA-gated; T10) |

Runtime dynamic resolution sets `UniversalRenderPipeline.renderScale` (0.5–1.0) with the FSR upscaler active — the API name is long-standing URP but could not be verified on-page this run (T10 flagged). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: UniversalRenderPipeline.renderScale API doc page under 6000.6 (URP package API docs 404; T10 wall). -->

Frame pacing per platform (all documented semantics, [Application.targetFrameRate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24): desktop uses `QualitySettings.vSyncCount = 1` ("Always use vSyncCount > 0 when smooth frame pacing is needed"; "If vSyncCount != 0, targetFrameRate is ignored"); mobile and console-class use `vSyncCount = 0` + `Application.targetFrameRate = 60`; never ship a non-divisor target (25 → renders at 20 on 60 Hz); leave `-1` (fixed 30 fps battery mode) to the OS-level battery states, not our code.

#### 9.2.5 Post-processing stack **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Per-scene Global Volume + Volume Profile; effects added via Volume > Add Override, where enabling a property writes it into the profile ([Volume Overrides reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/VolumeOverrides.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Override set: **Bloom** (subtle — lanterns/neon/timer pulses only), **Color Adjustments** (per-world grading driven by `WorldThemeSO`'s profile reference), **Tonemapping** (Neutral), **Vignette** (very light, tightens focus on the basin). Kept off: Motion Blur, DoF, lens flares — allocate those variants only if used ("Data Driven / Screen Space Lens Flare" rows exist for that; URP asset reference). URP asset Post-processing: Grading Mode = **High Dynamic Range** on HDR tiers ("grading before tonemapping"), LDR grading on T3/T4; LUT Size 32 default is fine for stylization; Alpha Processing off (needs 64-bit HDR precision; we don't ship alpha). Volume Update Mode = **Via Scripting** — our volumes are static per scene, which saves the per-frame cost (documented option, same page); the one exception is the fail-state volume (§9.8.3) whose weight is animated, on a separate Every Frame volume.

#### 9.2.6 Shader variant hygiene

Graphics settings strip lightmap modes and fog modes Automatically and instancing variants Strip Unused by default — which matters because our content loads through Addressables: shaders referenced only by Addressables groups and not by built scenes can arrive stripped ([Graphics settings reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-GraphicsSettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Mitigation: every world's water/theme materials are referenced by the boot scene's pre-warm list, plus a `ShaderVariantCollection` warmed on Boot (§4 scene flow). LOD Cross Fade dithering type 2x2 Stencil if cross-fade is ever used (variant-count rationale, T10).

### 9.3 Water rendering

#### 9.3.1 Requirements

The water is simultaneously (a) the fail boundary — any piece touching it fails the level (documented rule, §3) — and (b) the calm spa surface. It must read depth (how close to drowning the stack is), support gentle waves, produce splash VFX on contact, and stay cheap: it covers 30–60% of screen area on a portrait phone.

#### 9.3.2 Technique comparison

| Technique | Fidelity | Cost | Physics coupling | Risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transparent unlit Shader Graph surface + depth fade + fresnel + screen-space refraction (Ameye method) | High stylized | Low-mid (opaque texture bandwidth) | Visual-only; contact plane separate | Version drift URP 14→17 (nodes stable; T10 medium confidence) | **Chosen** |
| Opaque animated-normal plane (no transparency/refraction) | Medium | Lowest | Same | Loses depth gradient = loses "how deep is the stack" readability | Fallback for T4 if fill-rate profiling fails |
| BoatAttack-style full Gerstner + flow-map water | Highest | High | Complex | Reference repo stale since 2020-11-09 (376 stars; T10 via GitHub API) | Overkill; historical reference only |
| 2D sprite/quad water | Flat | Lowest | Trivial | Contradicts 3D presentation (§9.2.1) | Rejected |

#### 9.3.3 Chosen recipe — exact URP prerequisites and Shader Graph node list

URP asset prerequisites (all tiers, §9.2.3): **Depth Texture ON** and **Opaque Texture ON** — the docs describe the opaque texture as "works like the GrabPass in the built-in render pipeline", existing precisely for "frosted glass, water refraction, or heat waves" ([URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

Node graph (Unlit Shader Graph; technique documented by [Ameye, "Stylized Water Shader", March 2023, built on Unity 2022.2.6f1 + URP 14.0.6](https://alexanderameye.github.io/notes/stylized-water-shader/), accessed 2026-09-24; T10 rates the node-level technique as mapping 1:1 to URP 17, medium confidence):

1. Master stack: Surface Type **Opaque inside the graph**; the material's Advanced Options > Render Queue set to **Transparent (3000)** — the documented trick that keeps an unlit graph compatible while sorting as water.
2. **Depth fade (camera-relative, documented):** `Scene Depth (Eye)` − `Screen Position (Raw).a` (ray distance camera→bottom minus camera→surface) → Divide by `DepthRange` → `Saturate` → `One Minus` → shore-white/deep-black mask.
3. **Depth fade (world-space variant, chosen):** camera-independent vertical depth (author's preferred variant; our puzzle camera is near-fixed so both work, but world-space survives any future camera orbit): `WaterPlaneY` − `Absolute World Position.y` → Divide `DepthRange` → `Saturate`.
4. Wrap 2/3 as a reusable **Depth Fade subgraph** (documented recommendation).
5. **Color:** `Lerp(ShallowColor, DeepColor, DepthFade)` — colors from `WorldThemeSO`.
6. **Horizon:** `Fresnel Effect` node (Power ~2.5) → `Lerp` toward a horizon tint.
7. **Refraction (documented chain):** `Gradient Noise` (tiled, scrolled by `Time`) → `Remap(0,1,−1,1)` → `Multiply` by `RefractionStrength` → `Add` to `Screen Position` (Default) UVs → feed both the `Scene Color` UV input and the `Scene Depth` UV input.
8. **Foam band:** `DepthFade` → `Subtract(FoamWidth)` → `Saturate` → `One Minus` → add foam color (shore band; T10 notes the article's shoreline foam).
9. **Vertex displacement:** Simple Noise (or 3-amp Gerstner) `Position` output, amplitude/frequency from material floats set by `WaterSurfaceController`; plane mesh subdivided ~96×96 over the basin span (see §9.3.5 math).
10. **Sparkle:** normal perturbation (`Normal From Height` on the scrolled noise) feeding a light `Dot` term (article's normal-based sparkle).

#### 9.3.4 Depth-fade custom function (HLSL) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

For the world-space variant as a Shader Graph Custom Function node (avoiding node-spaghetti for the core math):

```hlsl
// WaterDepthFade.hlsl — Custom Function node, type: Single (per-pixel).
// Implements the world-space vertical variant of the documented depth-fade
// technique (Ameye 2023): factor 0 at surface, 1 at DepthRange below.
void WaterDepthFade_float(float3 AbsoluteWorldPos, float WaterPlaneY,
                          float DepthRange, out float DepthFactor01)
{
    float depthBelow = WaterPlaneY - AbsoluteWorldPos.y;   // >0 under water
    DepthFactor01 = saturate(depthBelow / max(DepthRange, 1e-4));
}
```

#### 9.3.5 Vertex waves vs the physics boundary — the honesty math **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

The visual surface oscillates; the fail contact plane is flat (§6). If the visual crest rises above the contact plane next to the stack, players see "touching water" without a fail — perceived unfairness; the reverse hides real fails. Rule (1 block edge = 1 Unity unit):

- Visual surface: `y_v(x,t) = WaterPlaneY + Σᵢ Aᵢ·cos(kᵢ·x − ωᵢ·t)` with `Σ Aᵢ ≤ A_max = 0.05` units (5% of a block; enforced by `WorldThemeSO.waveAmplitude` clamp).
- Fail contact plane: `WaterPlaneY + A_max/2 = WaterPlaneY + 0.025` units — the physics water trigger (§6 StabilityMonitor water-contact check) sits at the wave midpoint, so neither direction of mislead exceeds half the crest.
- Plane tessellation: basin span L ≈ 24 units; shortest wave we render has wavelength λ_min = 3 units; segment size ≤ λ_min/8 → 96 segments across (hence 96×96).
- Wave phase is render-only; the simulation never reads it (determinism discipline, §6).

#### 9.3.6 Buoyancy coupling and `WaterSurfaceController`

The physics-side water is owned by §6 (2D `BuoyancyEffector2D` with `surfaceLevel`, `density`, `linearDamping`, `angularDamping`, `flow*` — built-in only in 2D per the T11 digest of Unity 6.6 2D physics docs — T11 source #9 is [BuoyancyEffector2D, Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuoyancyEffector2D.html), built 2026-09-21, accessed 2026-09-24, the same citation §6.1 uses; Unity 6.6 also added new 2D Buoyancy/Wind APIs per the T02 digest of the 6000.6.0f1 notes). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: doc URLs for the new 6000.6 2D Buoyancy/Wind/PhysicsSpace script-reference pages (the T02 digest carries API names only, no URLs). --> §9's contract with §6: the effector's `surfaceLevel` and the shader's `WaterPlaneY` are the same value, pushed by one component:

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>
/// Single owner of the water plane height. Pushes WaterPlaneY and wave
/// parameters to the water material and keeps the §6 buoyancy effector's
/// surfaceLevel in sync so the visual and fail boundaries never diverge.
/// </summary>
public class WaterSurfaceController : MonoBehaviour
{
    #region Constants

    private static readonly int WaterPlaneYId = Shader.PropertyToID("_WaterPlaneY");
    private static readonly int AmplitudeId = Shader.PropertyToID("_WaveAmplitude");
    private static readonly int FrequencyId = Shader.PropertyToID("_WaveFrequency");

    #endregion

    #region Serialized Fields

    [Header("References")]
    [SerializeField] private Renderer waterRenderer;
    [SerializeField] private WorldThemeSO theme;

    [Header("State")]
    [SerializeField] private float waterPlaneY;

    #endregion

    // NOTE: no MaterialPropertyBlock at runtime — MPB on renderers breaks SRP
    // Batcher compatibility; theme changes write sharedMaterial floats once per
    // load boundary instead (see §9.4.2).

    #region Unity Lifecycle

    private void Awake()
    {
        if (theme == null || waterRenderer == null)
        {
            Debug.LogError($"{nameof(WaterSurfaceController)} missing references on {gameObject.name}", this);
            return;
        }
        ApplyTheme();
    }

    #endregion

    #region Public Methods

    /// <summary>Apply world theme tints/waves; called on level load by LevelManager (§6).</summary>
    public void ApplyTheme()
    {
        Material mat = waterRenderer.sharedMaterial;
        mat.SetFloat(WaterPlaneYId, waterPlaneY);
        mat.SetFloat(AmplitudeId, theme.WaveAmplitude);
        mat.SetFloat(FrequencyId, theme.WaveFrequency);
        mat.SetColor(Shader.PropertyToID("_ShallowColor"), theme.WaterShallow);
        mat.SetColor(Shader.PropertyToID("_DeepColor"), theme.WaterDeep);
    }

    #endregion
}
```

Splash VFX on water contact is specified in §9.7; the trigger is the §6 water-contact event, with emission position and entry velocity passed by the `VFXDirector` (§4 system map).

### 9.4 Block and environment shaders

#### 9.4.1 Block shader family **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Surface | Shader | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Standard blocks | URP **Simple Lit** (Shader Graph variants of it) | Cheaper BRDF than Lit; toy plastic/wood needs no specular GGX |
| Base platforms / basin | URP **Lit**, static, baked GI | Receives the nice shadows (§9.5) |
| Special blocks | Simple Lit + per-type overlay layers (§9.4.3) | One shared base keeps variant count low |
| Water | §9.3 unlit graph | — |
| Background | Unlit gradient skysphere per world | Zero lighting cost |

Color variation across 16 shapes × 8 worlds is delivered by **material variants + a per-shape 128×128 albedo atlas**, not per-piece materials: one material per (shader family) per world keeps draw calls inside the SRP Batcher's compatible-shader set. Gradient tint variants (top-lighter ramp baked into the atlas) replace realtime rim effects on T3/T4.

Triplanar mapping is **not** used — low-poly primitives unwrap cleanly with planar/projection UVs from the §9.9 generator; triplanar's three-sample cost buys nothing here and would be revisited only if organic carved shapes entered the set.

#### 9.4.2 SRP Batcher discipline

SRP Batcher ON on all tiers (§9.2.3; documented as taking precedence over dynamic batching and advisable to disable only with unoptimized assets — URP asset reference). Our rules: all block shaders are Shader Graph or hand-written with the standard `UnityPerMaterial` CBUFFER layout; runtime never calls `MaterialPropertyBlock` on renderers (breaks SRP-batcher compatibility — standard URP guidance, community-consistency level per T10's canvas/perf-hygiene caveat class); theme changes go through `sharedMaterial` writes at load boundaries only (as in §9.3.6), never per-frame.

#### 9.4.3 Special-block telegraphy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Each `IBlockBehaviour` (§8) drives a visual channel on its block's overlay layer; events come from the behaviour lifecycle hooks, rendering stays dumb:

| Block (§8) | Idle visual | Warning phase | Terminal event visual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Breakable (load) | hairline grain in atlas | stress cracks fade in as `OnStress` reports load fraction → shader `_CrackAmount` | shatter: mesh swap to debris + §9.7 burst |
| Timer | slow amber pulse (emission sin, 0.5 Hz) | pulse accelerates as remaining time → 0 (frequency = f(remaining), documented trigger: countdown starts when a piece is placed atop) | vanish puff + drop shadow of pieces above |
| Fire | ember particle loop, faint heat distortion via the water refraction machinery (screen-space, opaque texture reuse) | distortion radius grows on proximity to another fire block | explosion flash (photosafety-guarded, §9.7.3) |
| Gravity-inverter | violet arrow field; UI global flip cue | field intensity ramps 0.4 s before flip | full-screen flip transition (§9.7.3) |
| Linked/seesaw pair [ORIGINAL DESIGN extension] | shared cyan link-glow; faint line between pair | glow intensifies as pair angle diverges | glow snap on re-sync |

#### 9.4.4 Outline / stylization options **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Option | Cost | Looks | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inverted-hull outline (scaled back-face pass) | Extra pass per outlined object | Crisp toy-outline | **Chosen** — but only on special blocks (telegraphy) and the dragged piece (focus) |
| Full-screen post outline (depth/normal edge detect) | One fullscreen pass | Uniform, can shimmer on AA | Rejected: fights MSAA edges, costs a pass on T3/T4 |
| No outlines | Zero | Pure flat | Baseline for standard blocks |

#### 9.4.5 Dragged-piece presentation (documented anchor A5)

While carrying, the piece: (a) lifts 0.5 units along the view axis, (b) gains the inverted-hull focus outline, (c) still casts the realtime key-light shadow — recreating the documented Wii U detail "window light casts real-time shadows of dragged pieces" ([NL Wii U](https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/wiiu-eshop/art_of_balance), 2014-10-03). Rotation ticks snap the outline glow once per 45° step (§3 rotation model).

### 9.5 Lighting

#### 9.5.1 Rig **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

One main directional light per scene (the "window light"), parameters from `WorldThemeSO`; one low-intensity fill or ambient-only on T3/T4 (Additional Lights Disabled on T4 means the fill is ambient-skybox only). Realtime shadows from the main light on all tiers (shadow budgets per §9.2.3) because the dragged-piece shadow (A5) is a realtime requirement.

#### 9.5.2 Baked vs realtime per element **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Element | GI / shadows | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Basin, static platforms, background | **Baked** GI + baked shadowmaps | Never moves; saves realtime cost on all tiers |
| Swaying/floating platforms (documented 3DS+ feature, §3) | Realtime (main light) | Moves; too few for deferred anything |
| All dynamic pieces | Realtime cast + **light probes** receive | Pieces travel a bounded volume above the basin; one Light Probe Group ring (probes ~0.75-unit grid over play volume) is sufficient |
| Special-block emissives | Emission (bloom-gated) | Cheap, no lights added |

Baked volumes keep the scene under the Additional-Lights limits; the only realtime per-pixel extras are W4/W7 accent point lights (≤2), inside T3's Per Vertex ≤2 budget.

#### 9.5.3 Shadow strategy summary per tier

See the tier table (§9.2.3): shadow resolution 2048→512, max distance 50→15, cascades 2→1 across T1→T4; main light always casts (MSAA-compatible, forward-only — documented). On T4, if profiling shows shadow-map cost, the fallback is a blob-proxy shadow on the dragged piece only, but the documented anchor makes full shadows a fidelity target, so T4 ships shadows at 512 and re-evaluates on device (§18 budgets).

#### 9.5.4 Probes and reflections **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

One baked Reflection Probe per world scene (resolution 128 on T1/T2/T5, 64 on T3/T4), positioned above the water at the default camera eye. Water does not use it (unlit + screen color), blocks sample it via Simple Lit's environment handle — giving the toy plastic its faint sheen at near-zero runtime cost.

### 9.6 UGUI visual system

#### 9.6.1 Canvas architecture and the scaler math

One root Canvas per context (HUD, menus): Render Mode **Screen Space - Overlay** (no camera cost; ordering via Canvas sort order) with a per-canvas **Canvas Scaler**: UI Scale Mode = **Scale With Screen Size**, Reference Resolution **1920×1080**, Screen Match Mode = **Match Width or Height**, **Match = 0.5** (all per T10's exact recipe for the scaler whose semantics are documented in the [Canvas Scaler reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/script-CanvasScaler.html), accessed 2026-09-24). The official multi-resolution HOWTO demonstrates why 0.5: with Match 0 the scaler "compares the current screen width with the Canvas Scaler width" and a 640×960 portrait reference on a 960×640 landscape screen yields a 1.5× (too-big) factor, while "If the Match property is set to 0.5 … it will compare both … and choose a scale factor that's in between" — factor 1 ([Designing UI for Multiple Resolutions](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/HOWTO-UIMultiResolution.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Applying the same documented width-vs-height comparison to our 21:9 case: 2560×1080 against the 1920×1080 reference gives width ratio 1.33 and height ratio 1.0 — width-only (Match 0) would enlarge HUD elements 33%; Match 0.5 lands between, which is the intended look **[ORIGINAL DESIGN application of documented semantics]**. Reference Pixels Per Unit stays at the default 100.

#### 9.6.2 Aspect and anchor rules

Corner/edge anchoring is mandatory: the docs' aspect-adaptation guidance is that corner-anchored buttons survive aspect changes while unanchored center layouts "can fall off-screen" ([HOWTO-UIMultiResolution](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/HOWTO-UIMultiResolution.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

| Aspect / device class | Layout behavior **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
|---|---|
| 16:9 (reference) | Exact 1920×1080 design |
| 21:9 / 32:9 ultrawide (PC) | Basin framed by §6 camera (letterbox-free); HUD corners stretch to edges; queue tray max-width clamped to 400 px from screen edge |
| 16:10 (some laptops/Deck at 1280×800) | Same as 16:9; vertical margin absorbs |
| 4:3 / 3:2–ish tablets, 19.5:9–21:9 phones | Portrait/landscape layouts per orientation lock (§18); queue tray moves bottom-center on portrait phones (3-row strip) — extends the documented 3DS lower-screen-tray concept (A8) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| 5:4 (rare) | Expand-style fallback: HUD must never crop → per-canvas exception Screen Match Mode = Expand ("canvas will never be smaller than the reference", documented) |

#### 9.6.3 Safe area and TV title-safe

`Screen.safeArea` already accounts for "non-rectangular [displays] … or … TV displays … overscan", origin bottom-left — which matches UGUI's RectTransform convention (no inversion needed; UI Toolkit would need it) ([Screen.safeArea](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Screen-safeArea.html), accessed 2026-09-24). One `SafeAreaFitter` component on each root canvas maps safeArea into anchorMin/anchorMax; its full skeleton is specified in §18. Additional rules: on Android we enable "Render outside safe area" and handle cutout insets via the fitter, because safeArea interacts with that Player setting on Android (documented on the [Android Player settings page](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsAndroid.html), accessed 2026-09-24); on TVs/consoles we add a hard 10% inset for critical HUD (the three countdown lights, timer) beyond safeArea — industry convention, flagged as such in T10, since Unity surfaces overscan only through safeArea.

#### 9.6.4 Theme SOs and TextMeshPro

`WorldThemeSO` (§9.1.4) feeds a `UIThemeSO` (same shape, plus TMP color styles and sprite refs) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; menus restyle per world selection. TMP setup per the documented fallback chain — resolution order: object's primary Font Asset → the asset's Fallback Font Assets (recursive) → the text object's Sprite Asset (sprites matched by assigned unicode) → General Fallback Font Assets from TMP settings (recursive) ([Font Assets fallback, com.unity.ugui@2.0](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/TextMeshPro/FontAssetsFallback.html), accessed 2026-09-24; rows beyond 4 were truncated in capture). We author one Latin primary (SDF) per style with per-script fallbacks covering the §5 localization set (the Switch edition shipped 8 languages including Japanese — documented language list, T01; the shipped-language subset is §5's call); CJK glyphs live in fallback assets, exactly the documented use case. In-text icons (the countdown lights, mode icons) use one TMP Sprite Asset with assigned unicode values (documented mechanism).

#### 9.6.5 Prompt glyph sets

Four sprite sets — Keyboard/Mouse, Xbox, PlayStation, generic gamepad — as atlases with a TMP Sprite Asset each **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; the Switch set exists for the §13 historical study and Steam Input edge cases but is not shipped in v1 glyphs. Runtime swap subscribes to §7's device-change notification; §7 owns the API side (`GetBindingDisplayString` with `out deviceLayout`/`out controlPath` plus `InputSystem.IsFirstLayoutBasedOnSecond(deviceLayout, "Gamepad")` for icon selection — documented Input System APIs per T09). Glyph monochrome tinting follows `UIThemeSO.accent`.

#### 9.6.6 Navigation and focus visuals

Controller/keyboard navigation uses Selectable > Navigation = **Explicit** (wired per screen) with the Scene-view **Visualize** overlay used during layout QA; None disables focus reception and is reserved for decorative elements ([Navigation options reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/script-SelectableNavigation.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Every menu sets EventSystem first-selected so gamepad users start focused (§7 wiring). Focus visuals: 3-px accent outline + 8% background lightening, animated at ≤ 2 Hz (§14 photosensitivity).

#### 9.6.7 UGUI performance hygiene

Standard canvas guidance applied (community-consistency level per T10): Raycast Target disabled on all non-interactive graphics; rarely-changing UI (titles, tray backgrounds) split into its own Canvas to isolate rebuilds; no nested LayoutGroups in the HUD hot path (anchors instead); fades via Canvas Group alpha rather than per-graphic color tweens.

### 9.7 VFX

#### 9.7.1 Inventory **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Effect | Trigger (event per §4 catalog) | Tech | Particle budget (T1 / T4) | Pool size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Splash + expanding ripple ring | Water contact (fail) | Shuriken + shader ring quad | 120 / 60 | 4 |
| Idle water shimmer | continuous | water shader (§9.3) | — | — |
| Settle dust puff | Piece settled | Shuriken one-shot, soft sprite | 24 / 10 | 8 |
| Placement "clunk" micro-squash | Piece placed | Animation scale-curve, no particles | 0 | — |
| Shatter debris | Breakable destroyed | Shuriken + 6-chunk non-colliding debris meshes (§8) | 90 / 40 | 4 |
| Fire explosion | Fire-fire contact | Shuriken burst + heat-distortion quad | 150 / 60 | 2 |
| Gravity-flip hue-wave + camera dip | Gravity block flip | 0.4 s world-space hue-wave sweep + 15° camera dip-and-recover (§8.6) | 1 pass | 1 |
| Countdown light pulses | Stability window ticks (3) | UI sprite pulse + audio tick (A7) | 0 | — |
| Win celebration | Level cleared | Shuriken confetti, world-tinted | 200 / 80 | 2 |
| Menu transitions | UI flow | Canvas Group fades | 0 | — |

#### 9.7.2 VFX Graph vs Particle System decision **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

**Particle System (Shuriken) for everything gameplay-facing; VFX Graph not used in v1.** Rationale: all our effects are one-shot, CPU-triggered bursts under 200 particles — Shuriken's cost profile fits; VFX Graph's strengths (100k+ GPU particles, simulation over time) are unused; Shuriken needs no render-pipeline feature verification per tier; and a single-developer pipeline (§2) benefits from one mental model. Revisit trigger (§21 risk): if the gravity-flip sweep or the water sparkle demand sustained GPU emission, VFX Graph enters at T1/T2 only.

#### 9.7.3 Photosensitivity guard on the gravity flip **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

The gravity-inverter's flip presentation is the one flash-adjacent moment: §8.6's 0.4 s world-space hue-wave plus 15° camera dip-and-recover, with the hue-wave limited to one luminance step ≤ 10 cd/m²-equivalent per frame, no red↔blue alternation, total on-screen luminance change rate capped, and the reduce-motion accessibility setting replacing the hue-wave and dip with a 250 ms orientation cross-fade (§14.3.4). Fire-explosion flash is a single ≤ 80 ms bloom pulse, no strobing.

#### 9.7.4 Pooling

All effect prefabs sit in `VFXDirector`-owned pools (generic pool per §6); sizes above are pre-warm counts. Burst counts per tier come from the §14 performance budgets; T4 halves emission via a quality-scaled multiplier on pool checkout, not per-system edits.

### 9.8 Audio direction

#### 9.8.1 Documented character and our stance

Target idiom, documented: lounge/jazzy/electronic chill per world (A2/A3) — "booming bass" on Wii, "jazzy, relaxing" on Wii U, "catchy upbeat tunes that calm the mind" on 3DS; wooden clunk placement SFX; the 3DS edition even had voiceovers (A9). We compose **original music** in this idiom **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — a loop pair per world (calm + tension) at the BPM/instrumentation in §9.1.3 — and design an original SFX set. Optional low-key announcer voiceover ("World clear") ships behind an accessibility toggle, extending the documented 3DS voiceover precedent **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

#### 9.8.2 Adaptive layer architecture **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Vertical layering (skill taxonomy: adaptive music = vertical intensity layers + horizontal segment transitions). Per world: **calm layer** (default), **tension layer** (same key/tempo, added percussion + filtered pad), **stingers** (one-shots: level start, each green light, third-light success, collapse), **menu loop**. Layers play sample-locked on twin AudioSources; the mix moves, the clips never re-seek.

#### 9.8.3 Tension parameter and the math

The tension value is computed by §6's `StabilityMonitor` — §9 hereby requires it to expose `Tension01` (interface request into §6 **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**). Definition:

- Wobble energy over awake pieces: `E(t) = Σᵢ ( |vᵢ|² + (r_ω·|ωᵢ|)² )`, `r_ω = 0.25 m` (angular-to-linear equivalence radius); `W(t) = saturate(E(t) / E_ref)`, `E_ref = 0.05` (tuning constant, exposed in GameConfig §4).
- Countdown pressure during the documented 3-second stability window (§3): `D(t) = t_window / 3.0` (the 3 s duration is **[DOCUMENTED]**, multiply-sourced — A7 sources).
- `Tension01(t) = max(W(t), 0.6 · D(t))` — wobble dominates; the countdown alone only lifts tension to 60%.

Layer gains use smoothstep gates (show-the-math rule): `g_calm = 1 − S(T; 0.45, 0.65)`, `g_tension = S(T; 0.45, 0.65)` where `S(T; a, b) = clamp01((T−a)/(b−a))² · (3 − 2·clamp01((T−a)/(b−a)))`. At `T ≤ 0.45` calm-only; `T ≥ 0.65` tension-only; the 0.20-wide gate plus a 1.2 s gain slew prevents audible pumping. Stingers are event-driven, never gain-driven.

#### 9.8.4 `AdaptiveMusicController` **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>
/// Crossfades the calm/tension music layers from StabilityMonitor.Tension01 (§6).
/// Per-frame work is allocation-free; gains slew linearly toward the smoothstep
/// targets so the gate is traversed over ~1.2 s (no audible pumping).
/// </summary>
public class AdaptiveMusicController : MonoBehaviour
{
    #region Constants

    private const float GateLow = 0.45f;
    private const float GateHigh = 0.65f;
    private const float SlewPerSecond = 0.8f;  // 0→1 gain in ~1.25 s ≈ the 1.2 s design slew (§9.8.3)
    private const float Epsilon = 1e-5f;

    #endregion

    #region Serialized Fields

    [Header("Sources (sample-locked twin loops)")]
    [SerializeField] private AudioSource calmLayer;
    [SerializeField] private AudioSource tensionLayer;

    [Header("Tension input (§6)")]
    [SerializeField] private StabilityMonitor stabilityMonitor;

    #endregion

    #region Private Fields

    private float _calmGain = 1f;
    private float _tensionGain;

    #endregion

    #region Unity Lifecycle

    private void Update()
    {
        float tension = stabilityMonitor != null ? stabilityMonitor.Tension01 : 0f;
        float s = SmoothStep(GateLow, GateHigh, tension);
        _calmGain = Mathf.MoveTowards(_calmGain, 1f - s, SlewPerSecond * Time.deltaTime);
        _tensionGain = Mathf.MoveTowards(_tensionGain, s, SlewPerSecond * Time.deltaTime);

        // Direct writes; AudioSource.volume is not an allocation path.
        calmLayer.volume = _calmGain;
        tensionLayer.volume = _tensionGain;
    }

    #endregion

    #region Private Methods

    private static float SmoothStep(float edge0, float edge1, float x)
    {
        float t = Mathf.Clamp01((x - edge0) / Mathf.Max(edge1 - edge0, Epsilon));
        return t * t * (3f - 2f * t);
    }

    #endregion
}
```

The `AudioDirector` (§4 map, §6 runtime) owns clip-bank swaps from `WorldThemeSO`, stinger one-shots, and mixer snapshot transitions; this controller owns only the continuous mix.

#### 9.8.5 Mixer groups and snapshots **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Group | Content | Snapshot behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Master | Limiter | Constant |
| Music | calm+tension layers, menu loop | Paused snapshot −6 dB; Fail snapshot adds 1.5 s low-pass sweep to 800 Hz then release |
| SFX | gameplay one-shots | Untouched by snapshots |
| UI | navigation ticks, menu confirms | +2 dB in menus vs gameplay (Menu snapshot) |
| Ambience | water lap loop, room tone | Fail snapshot ducks −8 dB |

Snapshots transition 0.4 s (menus) / 1.5 s (fail sweep). Ambience water-lap intensity follows `WaterSurfaceController` wave frequency per world.

#### 9.8.6 SFX inventory **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Cue | Character | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pick-up | soft felt "pop" | |
| Rotate tick | dry wood click, one per 45° step | pitch-varied ±3% to avoid machine-gun sameness |
| Drop / place | wooden clunk (A6) | layer: impact thud + surface creak on heavy pieces |
| Water contact | splash + muffled collapse | triggers fail snapshot |
| Breakable shatter | brittle crack + debris scatter | |
| Timer expire | spring "boing" collapse | |
| Fire explosion | soft-thump + sizzle tail | photosafety-paired with §9.7.3 |
| Gravity flip | whoosh + riser | |
| Three countdown lights | three rising ticks, third resolves to win jingle if stable | A7 redundancy |
| Win / world clear | short lounge fanfare in world's key | |
| UI navigate / submit / back | muted ticks, one set platform-wide | |

SFX are 2D except splash and explosion, which take a 1-unit-falloff 3D blend at the event position (basin is acoustically small; full 3D panning is wasted here).

#### 9.8.7 Loudness targets and platform quirks

Loudness targets **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: Master integrated **−16 LUFS** on mobile, −16 to −14 LUFS on PC/console, true peak ≤ −1 dBTP; Music bus −18 LUFS integrated during gameplay (SFX headroom), SFX peaks ≤ −6 dBTP. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: current platform loudness guidance for Steam, Apple/Google, and Xbox XRs — no certification audio-loudness document was captured in research; confirm before submission (§19/§21). --> Platform quirks: the historical evidence shows the SFX set itself can scale by platform (3DS shipped minus the Wii water effects — A4), so T4 devices load the reduced cue bank (no ambience layer, mono splash); iOS hardware-mute and Android audio-focus interplay is standard platform behavior we must respect (pause music on focus loss). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact Unity 6.6 APIs/flags for iOS mute-switch and Android audio-focus handling were not captured in T07/T10 research; verify during §18 implementation. -->

### 9.9 Asset pipeline: Blender → Unity

#### 9.9.1 Toolchain pin

Blender **5.2 LTS** (released 2026-07-14, maintained to July 2028; bpy 5.2.2 on PyPI 2026-09-15) per the T04 digest — pinned for the whole project; 4.5 LTS remains maintained but 5.2 gives the longer runway. Version pinning, lockfiles and Docker image pinning are §16's concern; §9 fixes only the artistic contract: block meshes are parametric primitives (bevel-enabled), unit-scale 1 block = 1 m exported at 1:1.

#### 9.9.2 Format decision and export settings

**FBX primary** (Unity-native, normals-control), **GLB secondary** (quick review drops). Export parameters follow the verified defaults of the core exporters (T04 digest: FBX `bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx` with `axis_forward='-Z'`, `axis_up='Y'`, `apply_unit_scale=True`, `use_mesh_modifiers=True` — which blocks shape keys — `mesh_smooth_type='OFF'` i.e. Normals-Only; glTF `export_scene.gltf` defaults `export_format='GLB'`, `export_yup=True`, and has no batch mode — loop files in the script):

| Concern | FBX (primary) | GLB (review) |
|---|---|---|
| Axis/units | -Z forward / Y up, apply unit scale | Y-up automatic |
| Modifiers | baked (`use_mesh_modifiers=True`) | `export_apply=True` |
| Smoothing | Normals-Only (`mesh_smooth_type='OFF'`) | as-mesh |
| Batch | `batch_mode='COLLECTION'` per shape family | loop per file |
| Animation | none exported (blocks are rigid) | none |

#### 9.9.3 Unity import preset and naming **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

Model Importer preset `AoB_Block.fbpreset`: Scale Factor 1, Convert Units off, Mesh Compression Off (pieces are tiny), Read/Write disabled, Normals = Import, Tangents = Calculate Mikktspace, Weld Vertices on, no collision in-mesh (colliders are §5 `PieceDefinition` profiles, 2D/3D per §6). Naming: `blk_<family>_<variant>_v<n>` meshes (e.g. `blk_tri_r90_v3`), materials `mat_<surface>_<world>` or atlas-shared `mat_blocks_atlas`, textures `t_<purpose>_<size>`; folders follow §4's `Assets/_Project/Art/{Models,Materials,Textures,Shaders}` split. `.fbx`, `.blend`, textures, and audio are LFS-tracked (§4 git plan).

#### 9.9.4 Texture strategy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

The game is nearly textureless: palette lives in materials/theme SOs; the only atlases are the block albedo atlas (128²/shape), water noise (256² tiling), UI sheets, and glyph sets. Compression per the unity-game-dev-expert standard: **ASTC** on mobile, **BC7** desktop/console; never uncompressed in production. Total v1 texture budget < 24 MB.

#### 9.9.5 Headless thumbnail renders for UI icons

Piece-definition icons (§5) and store/screenshots come from headless renders: **Cycles CPU** renders need no graphical display and work in `--background`; **EEVEE is GPU-only with no CPU fallback and "Headless rendering is not supported on headless Windows systems"** (all T04 digest, current Blender manual) — so CI icon jobs run Cycles CPU on Linux runners, and any EEVEE beauty shots are interactive-session work. The render scripts are §16 deliverables (`render_thumbnails.py` invoked on asset change).

#### 9.9.6 Automation hooks (§15–§17)

- **§16 CLI:** `generate_blocks.py` regenerates parametric mesh variants → `batch_export.py` walks `.blend` dirs → FBX per §9.9.2 → `render_thumbnails.py` emits icons; CI ordering (Blender step → Unity import/build step) and artifact caching are specified in §16.
- **§17 MCP:** interactive block-variant sculpting sessions (model → viewport screenshot via `get_viewport_screenshot` → adjust) and scene screenshot QA; the MCP-vs-CLI decision table lives in §17.
- **§15 Unity CLI:** project bootstrap consumes the import presets and `Quality`/URP assets defined in §9.2 as version-controlled assets.

Task breakdown, estimates and acceptance criteria for everything in this section live in §20; risks (URP 17 doc drift, MSAA-on-mobile-opaque-texture behavior, headless-render constraints) are registered in §21.

## 10. Phased Development Roadmap

This section sequences the designs of §2–§19 into eight phases, P0–P7, with measurable exit criteria, per-phase risk gates, a milestone-review protocol, the content-production arithmetic that makes a 200-level game feasible for one developer, and a definition-of-done contract per artifact class. §20 expands every phase into hierarchical task IDs (`P<phase>.<epic>.<task>`) keyed to the phases defined here (its worked example, `P1.E3-physics-core` — timestep, stepper, stability monitor — is P1 work in this roadmap); §21 carries the risk register these gates feed. All durations, rates, and thresholds in this section are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** planning values unless marked otherwise, and are re-baselined at every phase gate (rolling-wave estimation).

### 10.1 Roadmap principles, team model, and engine-version strategy

Principles (in priority order):

1. **Kill-risk first.** The physics feel and its determinism envelope (§6) are the project's only existential risks; they are proven in P1 with a playable vertical slice before any content or platform spend.
2. **Automation before content.** 200 levels are not authorable by hand at single-dev scale; the §15 (Unity CLI), §16 (batch-mode CI + Blender CLI), and §17 (MCP) toolchains are P0–P2 deliverables, not post-hoc conveniences. The original franchise itself demonstrates the volume expectation: the Switch edition ships 200 levels across 8 worlds ([Shin'en press sheet](http://shinen.com/press/sheet.php?p=art_of_balance(Switch)), accessed 2026-09-24, per T01 src 9) **[DOCUMENTED]**; the 25-levels-per-world split used in our content plan is inference over that documented 200/8 structure, not a documented per-world count **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.
3. **Platform order is fixed.** Windows + macOS via Steam first → Android → iOS → Xbox last, gated on ID@Xbox access (chief-architect decision; rationale and settings in §18/§19). No phase reorders this train.
4. **Every exit criterion is machine-checkable or checklist-checkable.** A gate that cannot be measured is a vibe, not a gate (protocol in §10.3, DoD in §10.5).
5. **Estimates are re-baselined, not defended.** Each phase gate ends with a re-estimate of all downstream phases; slippage absorbed by scope levers identified per phase, never by silently dropping exit criteria.

Team model **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (the §2 "small-team pipeline" pillar made concrete):

| Role | Allocation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Senior developer (the user) | 30–40 productive h/week | Full-stack + DevSecOps background; systems, levels, platform work |

### 10.2 Phase definitions (P0–P7)

Master table (durations are single-dev working weeks at the §10.1 loading, re-derived from §20.10's per-phase dev-day estimates at the 5 dev-days/week loading §20.10 itself states; cumulative to Steam v1.0 = 337 dev-days ≈ 67 weeks, ±20% ≈ 54–81 weeks ≈ 12.5–18.5 months — P4 exception noted below):

| Phase | Theme | Duration | Primary exit criterion (summary) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Pre-production & toolchain bootstrap | 4–5 wks | Clean clone → editor-openable project via one script, CI green, first automated asset round-trip |
| P1 | Vertical slice (feel gate) | 10–11 wks | 5-level greybox slice fully playable on Win64 + macOS smoke; 100/100 scripted settle runs correct |
| P2 | Core systems + automation online | 16–17 wks | All §4–§8 systems in, specials matrix green, ≥4 levels/day authoring rate measured, 3-platform CI |
| P3 | Content production I (worlds 1–4) | 8–9 wks | 100/100 levels validated + double-passed; world-1 completion ≥ 90% in cohort |
| P4 | Content II (worlds 5–8 + modes) | 10–12 wks (see note below) | 200/200 levels + 5 modes E2E; content freeze declared; 6.7-upgrade window executed |
| P5 | Multiplatform hardening (Android → iOS) | 13–14 wks | Device-matrix perf/thermal budgets met (§14); soak tests clean |
| P6 | Certification & submission (Steam first) | 5–6 wks | Steam build review passed; mobile submissions in review; launch |
| P7 | Post-launch | first 8 wks defined | Crash-free ≥ 99.8% rolling; patch 1 shipped; Xbox track decision |

P4 duration note: §20.10's raw P4 estimate is 41 dev-days ≈ 8–9 weeks, which excludes the mode-engineering and star-calibration overlap that §10.4's independent content-production arithmetic builds in; §10.2 therefore carries P4 at §10.4's 10–12 weeks — the ~2–4-week delta sits inside the ±20% band — rather than silently quoting both numbers.

#### P0 — Pre-production (4–5 weeks)

|---|---|

(4) §2/§3 docs committed and unchanged-in-substance for 5 working days (design-stability check). (5) `Time.fixedDeltaTime = 1f / 240f` pinned in boot code (§6) and visible in a profiler capture |

#### P1 — Vertical slice (10–11 weeks)

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| Goals | Prove the feel. Five greybox levels, end to end, placeholder art: offer → carry → rotate (45°) → release → settle → 3-second stability window → win/lose, on mouse and gamepad |
| Deliverables | `PhysicsStepper` (fixed 1/240 s; the Time manager's Fixed Timestep is the standard knob — [Unity 6.6 docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-TimeManager.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**); `StabilityMonitor` with the explicit velocity + waterline + contact-island predicate (never `IsSleeping` alone — §6); minimal `PieceDefinition`/`LevelDefinition` SOs (§5); `IPieceInputProvider` + `MousePointerInputProvider` + `GamepadInputProvider` (§7); `GameStateMachine` core path; `ScoreController` v1 on the §3 formula **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; `BuoyancyEffector2D` water recipe + fail trigger (§6); the documented 3-lights/3-second countdown rule (multiply documented across editions — research digest T01, 2026-09-24; citations in §22) **[DOCUMENTED]**; Win64 build + macOS Mono smoke build from CI |

(2) Median latency rest→window-start ≤ 0.5 s. (3) Input latency on min-spec PC at 60 fps meets the §2.6.1 budgets — pointer/cursor follows within 1 rendered frame (≤ 16.7 ms), rotate acknowledged within 1 frame, pick-up/drop within 2 frames (≤ ~33 ms) — per §7.8's processing-point analysis (input-to-sim hop ≤ one render frame + 4.2 ms at 60 Hz/240 Hz), captured with §14's day-one profiler markers; §2 remains the authority. (4) Physics CPU ≤ 2 ms/frame at 60 fps with 100 active bodies at the 240 Hz step (§14 budget; the reproduction math — ≤ 0.085 mm fall/step at 1 g, ~5× physics cost of 50 Hz being trivial under ~100 bodies — is §6's). (5) Feel gate: ≥ 4 of 5 external players rate the slice "feels like stacking real blocks" **[ORIGINAL DESIGN threshold]**. (6) Same-device ghost replay of one full level reproduces the final stack pose within tolerance 10/10 runs (the same-device-only determinism envelope is the documented Unity position — "not 100% deterministic across devices… deterministic on the same device given the same set of inputs", [MelvMay, Unity Discussions 2023-02-27](https://discussions.unity.com/t/fully-deterministic-physics/910507/10), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**; cross-device replays stay descoped to pose snapshots, §6) |

### 10.3 Milestone review protocol

Every phase ends with a gate review. Solo-dev adaptation: the review is adversarial-by-checklist — the developer reviews their own work against pre-committed criteria while an AI pair counter-reviews (code review + console-read loops per §17), so criteria cannot be quietly relaxed under deadline pressure.

Protocol (fixed order, half-day timebox):

1. **Freeze the candidate.** Tag `phase-gate/P<N>`; CI builds from the tag only.
2. **Run the machine checks.** `PhaseGateRunner` (§10.7) + full test suites + perf captures on the §14 device set; XML reports archived as gate evidence.
3. **Walk the DoD checklists** for every artifact class produced in the phase (§10.5); any unchecked item becomes either a blocker or a written waiver with a §21 risk entry.
4. **Demo the phase artifact** (table below) to the external cohort when the phase calls for one (P1, P3, P4, P6); record the playtest numbers into the gate evidence.
5. **Re-baseline.** Re-estimate downstream phases against measured rates (authoring levels/day, defect rates); pick scope levers, not quality levers.
6. **Update the registers.** §21 risks re-scored; decisions logged; next phase's gates confirmed or amended in writing.

Demo criteria per phase — what must be playable/provable:

| Gate | Demo artifact | Provable on the spot |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Screen-recorded clean-machine bootstrap + CI run | Clone-to-Editor ≤ 30 min; green pipeline; block round-trip twice |
| P1 | Playable 5-level Win64 build (mouse + pad) | Win + lose paths; countdown lights; feel-gate ratings; scripted-run report |
| P2 | 10-level internal slice authored in-tool | Live level authoring in LevelEditor; specials matrix report; 3-platform CI artifacts |
| P3 | Worlds 1–4 RC build | World map, unlocks, star screens; completion/crash-free metrics; calibration notebook |
| P4 | Content-complete build, all modes | 5 modes E2E; 4-player Tower Tumble session live; freeze tag reproduces byte-identical build |
| P5 | Device-matrix builds | Budget traces on real devices; thermal soak logs; accessibility checklist walkthrough |
| P6 | Store RC + live store pages (staged) | Install-from-store smoke on retail configs; signed/notarized binaries; review statuses |
| P7 | Live product | Dashboards (crash-free, telemetry); patch train executing |

### 10.4 Content-production math and automation leverage

The §5 tooling turns level authoring into a measured production line. Model **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (all values are planning assumptions, replaced by measured rates from P2 onward):

```
T_level   = T_author + T_validate + T_test × N_passes + T_integrate
T_author  = 20–30 min   (LevelEditor graybox, after 10-level ramp)
T_validate≈  2 min      (human glance; schema + queue-mass-budget are CI-side, §5)
T_test    = 15–25 min   per full pass; N_passes = 2 (author pass + calibration pass)
T_integrat=  5–10 min   (theme assignment, Addressables group, string keys)
→ T_level ≈ 65–95 min  → 5–7 levels per 8-h day at 100% focus

Throughput = (focus factor) × levels/day
P3/P4 content-focus factor ≈ 0.6 (remainder = systems, tooling, playtest ops)
→ effective 3.0–4.2 levels/day
→ 100 levels ≈ 24–33 working days ≈ 5–7 weeks pure authoring
+ 20% first-levels-of-a-new-special premium (bespoke design, §8 grammar)
+ theme/gating integration and 20% buffer
→ P3 = 8–10 weeks; P4 = 10–12 weeks (adds mode engineering ~2 wks + calibration)
```

Star-threshold calibration math (hooks into §3's **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** formula): per level, collect ≥ 20 recorded completions (nightly headless bot runs in CI + human cohort); compute the time-and-pieces distribution; set thresholds at fixed percentiles (e.g., 3-star = 90th-percentile time with zero sunk pieces; 2-star = 75th; 1-star = completion) and re-cut after every balance patch. The requirement drives P2 deliverables: replay recording, bot scripts, and a threshold-computation tool are content tooling, not post-launch niceties.

Automation leverage (the reason one developer can carry 200 levels):

| Task | Manual cost | Automated cost | Mechanism (section) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Block mesh variants | ~30 min each in Blender GUI | ~0 (regenerate on param change) | `generate_blocks.py` parametric, headless (§16) |
| UI icon thumbnails | render + import per block | nightly batch | `render_thumbnails.py` headless (Cycles CPU; EEVEE is GPU-only headless — digest T04) (§16) |
| Level SO creation ×200 | 5–10 min each by hand incl. typos | seconds each, validated | MCP `manage_scriptable_object` bulk generation (CoplayDev/unity-mcp exposes it among 47 tools — [repo](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp), per digest T05/verify, accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**) or C# editor batch, trade-off table in §17 |
| Level validation | minutes/level, error-prone | 0 (CI gate) | editmode validation suite on every PR (§5 rules, §16 runner) |
| Builds ×3 platforms | ~1 h each, manual | 0 | `unity build` / batch-mode matrix with exit-code contract (§15/§16) |
| Scene QA screenshots | open scene, look | minutes, batched | MCP screenshot/scene reads in the review loop (§17) |
| Test execution | manual runs | 0 | `unity test` with NUnit XML + `--affected` watch loop (§15) |

Net effect: the human spends time only on graybox design, feel judgment, and calibration reading — the three things automation cannot do.

### 10.5 Definition of done per artifact class

**Runtime system** (anything from the §4 system map — `LevelManager`, `StabilityMonitor`, `ScoreController`, …):

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| 1 | Lives in its asmdef with declared dependencies only; no cyclical references (§4) |
| 2 | unity-game-dev-expert conventions: `#region` blocks, `[SerializeField] private`, PascalCase, XML `<summary>` docs, `nameof()`, null-safe patterns, zero hot-path allocations |
| 3 | Emits/consumes only the named event channels (§4 list); no direct cross-system references |
| 4 | Editmode tests for deterministic logic; one playmode loop test through `GameStateMachine` |
| 5 | Custom Profiler markers added on day one (§14 profiling protocol) |
| 6 | Telemetry hooks (if player-facing) wired to the §14 schema |
| 7 | AI-pair code review pass + self-review; findings triaged |
| 8 | Documented in the system table (owner, data, events, tick model) |

**Level**:

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| 1 | Passes LevelEditor validation: schema, queue mass budget vs platform heuristic, allowed-rotation sanity (§5) |
| 2 | Two full human passes (author + calibrator) completed |
| 3 | Star thresholds computed from ≥ 20 recorded runs (§10.4) |
| 4 | Specials used match the world's introduced grammar (§8); no untaught mechanics |
| 5 | Theme + env assigned; localization keys, no hard-coded strings |
| 6 | Body count ≤ 100 active; per-level frame budget spot-check green (§14) |
| 7 | Addressables group + load path verified by automated cold-load test |

**Platform port**:

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| 1 | Build produced by CI from clean clone, exit codes honored (§16) |
| 2 | §14 perf budgets met on that platform's device matrix; traces archived |
| 3 | Input: correct provider + glyph set + rebinding persisted (§7) |
| 4 | Save location + cloud round-trip + conflict path verified (§14) |
| 5 | Store requirements: signing/notarization/privacy manifests per §18/§19 complete |
| 6 | Platform cert checklist (Steam Deck, Play, App Store, XR if Xbox) walked with zero unwritten waivers |

**Automation script** (anything in §15–§17):

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| 1 | Idempotent; safe to re-run on a dirty tree |
| 2 | Non-zero exit on failure; documented exit-code mapping (§16 contract) |
| 3 | Secrets via environment/keystore, never CLI args (DevSecOps rule, §14/§16) |
| 4 | Tool versions pinned (editor patch, CLI beta, Blender LTS) and recorded |
| 5 | Flags/keys documented; smoke test in CI exercising it at least weekly |

### 10.6 Critical path, float, and the release train

Critical chain: **P0 → P1 (physics-feel gate) → P2 → P3 → P4 (freeze) → P5 → P6 (Steam launch)** — ≈ 67 weeks to v1.0 (337 dev-days at 5 dev-days/week per §20.10; ±20% ≈ 54–81 weeks). Everything else carries float:

| Float item | Slack | Constraint it protects |
|---|---|---|
| ID@Xbox application | ≥ 28 wks (submitted in P0, §20 P0.E4.4; ≥ 20 wks slack remains even if deferred to the P4 drop-dead fallback) | Xbox being last is already the decision; approval timing is unverified publicly `<!-- TODO-VERIFY: realistic ID@Xbox onboarding timeline; FAQ details beyond 18+/NDA/country were collapsed in research (T08 gap) -->` |
| macOS self-hosted runner + hardware | must exist by P2 (notarization dry run); P1 macOS smoke can ride a GitHub-hosted macOS job | IL2CPP same-platform build rule (P5 gate G5.3) |
| Localization (non-launch languages) | can trail into P6 | Launch-language set fixed at P4 freeze |
| Steam demo, motion-pointer provider | P7 | Both are post-launch parity items with documented franchise precedent (§10.2 P7) |
| Achievements art/metadata | P5–P6 | Achievements functional from P3 (leaderboard hooks) |

Release train (fixed order, decoupled launches): Steam Windows+macOS v1.0 (day 0) → Google Play (≈ +2–4 wks) → App Store (≈ +4–6 wks) → Xbox (opportunistic, only with access). Each launch reuses the same RC evidence set; only store-specific checklists rerun. Buffers: 2 weeks per store review inside P6 (G6.1), one global 2-week contingency week held outside all phase estimates.

### 10.7 Phase-gate automation

Gates must be executable, not aspirational. The runner below is registered as a Unity CLI command — any static method in namespace `Unity.Pipeline.Commands` decorated with `[CliCommand("name", "description")]` and `[CliArg]` parameters is auto-discovered by the experimental com.unity.pipeline package (requires Unity 6.0 LTS+; no registration code) ([Meet the Unity CLI](https://unity.com/blog/meet-the-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24; CLI docs, [docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24; track note T02 C14 **[DOCUMENTED]**) — and doubles as a batch-mode `-executeMethod` target for the §16 pipeline (batch mode is version-stable regardless of CLI beta churn; the attribute surface may still shift across betas — the open marshalling questions are tracked at §15.4.6's note). The `-- phase P3` argument-forwarding form in the doc comment below is our convention: the CLI reference documents `unity run --command <name>` but not yet argument passing (T02 C12) — confirm via `unity run --help` at P0. Exit codes follow the CLI contract where 8 = "tests ran and failed — never retry" ([CLI reference, via T02] **[DOCUMENTED]**).

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.IO;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEngine;
using Unity.Pipeline.Commands; // [CliCommand]/[CliArg] namespace per T02 C14 (com.unity.pipeline,
                               // experimental as of CLI 1.0.0-beta.11); the attribute surface may
                               // shift across CLI betas (open questions tracked at §15.4.6's note);
                               // batch-mode path below is version-stable regardless.

namespace ArtOfBalance.EditorTools
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Executes the measurable phase-gate checks (content validation, body-budget spot
    /// checks) against a tagged tree and writes a CI-consumable report + exit code.
    /// Invoked headless: `unity run --command phase-gate -- phase P3` or
    /// `-executeMethod ArtOfBalance.EditorTools.PhaseGateRunner.RunBatchMode`.
    /// </summary>
    public static class PhaseGateRunner
    {
        private const int ExitSuccess = 0;
        private const int ExitValidationFailed = 8; // Never-retry contract (§16).
        private const int MaxActiveBodies = 100;    // §14 budget ceiling per level.
        private const string ReportDirectory = "Reports/PhaseGates";

        #region Public API

        /// <summary>
        /// Runs all gates for the given phase (e.g. "P3") and returns the exit code.
        /// </summary>
        [CliCommand("phase-gate", "Validate content and budgets for a phase gate")]
        [CliArg("phase", "Phase identifier, e.g. P3", Required = true)]
        public static int Run(string phase)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(phase))
            {
                Debug.LogError($"[{nameof(PhaseGateRunner)}] phase argument is required");
                return ExitValidationFailed;
            }

            List<string> failures = new List<string>(capacity: 64); // Reused; no hot-path growth.

            if (!LevelValidationDatabase.ValidateAll(failures))     // §5 rules: schema, mass budget.
            {
                AppendReport(phase, failures);
                return ExitValidationFailed;
            }

            if (!ValidateBodyBudget(failures))                      // §14 spot check per scene.
            {
                AppendReport(phase, failures);
                return ExitValidationFailed;
            }

            AppendReport(phase, failures);
            return ExitSuccess;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Batch-mode entry point; maps <see cref="Run"/> onto the process exit code
        /// so CI can branch without parsing logs (§16 exit-code contract).
        /// </summary>
        public static void RunBatchMode()
        {
            string phase = CommandLineReader.GetValue(nameof(phase));
            EditorApplication.Exit(Run(phase));
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        /// <summary>
        /// Counts simulated bodies per gameplay scene against the §14 ceiling.
        /// </summary>
        private static bool ValidateBodyBudget(List<string> failures)
        {
            foreach (string scenePath in GameplaySceneLocator.AllLevelScenePaths())
            {
                int activeBodies = SceneBodyCounter.CountActiveRigidbodies(scenePath);
                if (activeBodies > MaxActiveBodies)
                {
                    failures.Add($"{scenePath}: {activeBodies} bodies exceeds {MaxActiveBodies}");
                }
            }

            return failures.Count == 0;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Writes the gate report next to the CI artifacts; failure detail is the contract.
        /// </summary>
        private static void AppendReport(string phase, List<string> failures)
        {
            Directory.CreateDirectory(ReportDirectory);
            File.WriteAllLines(
                Path.Combine(ReportDirectory, $"gate-{phase}.txt"),
                failures.Count == 0
                    ? new[] { $"PASS {phase} {System.DateTime.UtcNow:o}" }
                    : failures);
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Wiring: the §16 workflow calls the runner on every `phase-gate/P*` tag and on the nightly content job that also refreshes star-threshold distributions (§10.4). `LevelValidationDatabase`, `CommandLineReader`, `GameplaySceneLocator`, and `SceneBodyCounter` are P2 tooling tasks enumerated in §20; their absence is a P2 exit-criterion failure, which is exactly the point of writing the gate before the content it will judge.

## 11. Deep Dive — Wii U Edition

The Wii U eShop release (2014) is the franchise's multiplayer and control high-water mark: it named and expanded the competitive modes our clone inherits, ran the broadest simultaneous input-device matrix of any edition, and is the edition around which a persistent "240 fps physics" reputation exists. Per the architecture decision in §2, Wii U is **not** a v1 target platform — Windows/macOS (Steam) → Android → iOS → Xbox — so this section is a historical study whose output is design input: a mode-parity matrix (§11.7), two full mode specifications (§11.6), and a physics-feel replication path (§11.5, feeding §6).

### 11.1 Historical release profile

**[DOCUMENTED]** Release dates, pricing, and content below are verified against the official Shin'en microsite captures and Nintendo's product pages; the Wikipedia "25 September 2013" date is a year-typo refuted by the official microsite news items ("2014-Sep-25 Game now available in Europe!"), Nintendo.com's Oct 09 2014 dating, and review dates Oct–Dec 2014 ([Shin'en Wii U microsite, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20201016200640/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/wiiu/), [Nintendo.com Wii U detail, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20160619195926/http://www.nintendo.com/games/detail/art-of-balance-wii-u), accessed 2026-09-24). The 2013 date must not appear anywhere in this project's documents.

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Developer/publisher | Shin'en Multimedia GmbH (self-published) | [Shin'en Wii U microsite](https://web.archive.org/web/20201016200640/http://art-of-balance.shinen.com/wiiu/), accessed 2026-09-24 |
| Release | EU 2014-09-25, NA 2014-10-09, AU 2014-12-18 | microsite news items + Nintendo.com (above) |
