Non-Switch reuse: the same controller serves Android tablet-vs-phone tiering and any future deck-class device, which is why it binds an interface instead of a platform define.

### 13.6 Switch as a clone target: access, certification, connectivity, controllers

**Developer access (brief, factual).** Nintendo gates the platform behind its developer program: registration, an NDA, and approval before development units and the platform SDK/documentation become available; Unity's Switch build support arrives as a platform module plus the Nintendo SDK. Everything requirement-specific (dev hardware models, firmware, submission tooling) is NDA material with no public primary — the research notes' only public anchor is Unity's own statement that closed-platform player settings live in platform-specific documentation (§13.5 source). Treat the access-model description above as general platform knowledge to be re-verified inside the portal once (and if) a Switch target is greenlit.

**Certification flavor.** Nintendo's submission gate (lotcheck) is the Switch analog of Xbox XRs (§19) and PlayStation TRCs (§12): it checks functional stability, age-rating metadata consistency, input behavior, and store-content correctness before granting release. Scope note for our plan: cert *categories* are public knowledge, but the requirement texts themselves are NDA-gated; nothing below cites specifics because none are publicly verifiable. Design implications we can lock in now, independent of exact wording: mandatory controller support with correct glyphs (§7), rumble that stops on suspend/pause (§13.4), no touch-only interactions in TV mode (§13.5), and save-data behavior compatible with cloud sync semantics (§14).

**Connectivity: local wireless vs online vs single system.** The original's matrix is documented (§13.2): 1–4 on one console, 2 over local wireless, 2 online. Notably the Switch edition's *online* ceiling (2) is smaller than Wii U's (up to 5, §11) — the modes, not the transport, set the player counts. Our clone's v1 scope (§2) makes online netcode a non-goal; the mode parity we commit to is the single-system 1–4 surface (Arcade drop-in co-op, Swift Stacker split-screen, Tower Tumble hotseat) via `PlayerInputManager` pairing and `MultiplayerEventSystem` per-player UI (§7). If a Switch target were ever greenlit:

| Transport | Original (documented) | Our extension point | Gating |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single system 1–4 | Yes | `PlayerInputManager`, per-player cursors (§7) | Public Unity APIs |
| Local wireless (2) | Yes | Transport behind the §2 netcode abstraction | Nintendo SDK, NDA — <!-- TODO-VERIFY: local-wireless session API is platform-SDK-only; no public Unity surface exists. --> |
| Online (2) | Yes (NSO membership) | Non-goal v1 (§2); leaderboards-only online if revisited | NSO service integration, NDA |

**Joy-Con gyro provider.** The motion-patch study (§13.3) defines the shape: an attitude source injected into `MotionPointerInputProvider`. Desktop development uses the documented stand-ins — `SwitchProControllerHID` over Bluetooth (wired USB inert; T09) for button/layout verification, and `<AttitudeSensor>/attitude` on Android/iOS for actual gyro testing, since sensors do not exist on desktop platforms in the public Input System (**[DOCUMENTED]**, T09/§7). The on-console Joy-Con binding (per-Joy-Con attitude, dual-controller grip merging, HD-rumble motor mapping) is console-package territory and stays behind the provider interface until SDK access exists.

**Play-mode input availability matrix** (original-derived, our provider mapping):

| Play mode | Touch | Joy-Con buttons/sticks | Motion pointer | Pro Controller |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Handheld | Yes (documented controller) | Yes | Post-Patch 1.1 | N/A (not attached) |
| Tabletop | Console-in-hand only | Yes | Post-Patch 1.1 | Yes (Bluetooth) |
| TV | No | Yes | Post-Patch 1.1 | Yes |

The launch-window row (no motion in TV mode) is the exact scenario our provider registry prevents: no input-dead play mode, because every scheme is data-bound to devices that report presence at runtime.

### 13.7 Mapping the 8-world / 200-level structure to our content model

**Documented structure.** 200 levels across 8 worlds with a unique lounge style and environment per world (§13.2). World *names/themes* were never published — official copy only says "8 beautiful environments / each with its own unique lounge style" — so our world identities are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (§5 environment themes; §9 per-world mood tables). Progression semantics are documented from the 3DS era and likely shared: within a world the player chooses level order, individual levels can be skipped, and the next world unlocks after enough successes (**[DOCUMENTED]**, [Der Spiegel review, 2012-07-12](https://www.spiegel.de/netzwelt/games/3ds-spiel-art-of-balance-touch-im-test-a-843861.html), accessed 2026-09-24; medium-high confidence for cross-edition sharing).

**Mapping to `WorldDefinition` / `LevelDefinition` (§5).** The Switch structure translates one-to-one into the content SOs, with the unlock rule quantified as our own design:

| Switch fact | Our data model | Marker |
|---|---|---|
| 8 worlds | 8 `WorldDefinition` assets, ids W01–W08, each referencing an environment theme SO (§9) | [DOCUMENTED count] |
| 25 levels per world | 25 `LevelDefinition` refs per world; level index free-ordered at runtime (queue + basin + par targets per §5) | [DOCUMENTED total: 200 across 8 worlds; equal 25-per-world split is our convention **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (§5 — sources state only 200/8)] |
| Unique lounge style per world | Theme SO: palette, lighting rig, music layer set (§9 adaptive music), water tint | [DOCUMENTED existence] / [ORIGINAL DESIGN specifics] |
| Skippable levels, ordered freely | `LevelDefinition` has no prerequisite field; completion stats per level in SaveSystem (§6) | [DOCUMENTED rule] |
| "Enough successes" unlocks next world | `WorldDefinition.unlockCompletionsRequired` — see math below | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** quantification |
| 16 shapes + 5 specials available per level | `PieceDefinition` refs in each level's queue; behaviours per §8 `IBlockBehaviour` | [DOCUMENTED inventory] |
| 8 languages | String tables per §5: `ja`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr-FR`, `fr-CA`, `de`, `es-ES`, `es-419` — exactly the documented Switch language list, giving day-one localization parity with the original SKU | [DOCUMENTED list] |

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Unlock math** (the original never publishes thresholds; we derive a curve from the documented skip-anywhere freedom and 25-level worlds): world *n+1* unlocks at `U(n) = ceil(r × 25)` completions in world *n* with ratio `r = 0.6`, i.e. **15 of 25** — `ceil(0.6 × 25) = ceil(15.0) = 15`. Cumulative completions to reach world *k*: `C(k) = 15 × (k − 1)`, so world 8 opens after `15 × 7 = 105` of the first seven worlds' 175 levels (60%, mirroring the per-world ratio). The 60% ratio is chosen so a stuck player can skip any 10 levels per world and still progress — preserving the documented "you can skip individual levels" freedom as a real escape valve rather than a trap. Final thresholds get playtest tuning under the §3 difficulty-curve framework; the derivation method is the deliverable here. Note: this flat `r = 0.6` → 15 derivation and its 105/175 (60%) cumulative are the historical-analysis method demonstration only — the shipped schedule is §5.6.1's escalating 15 → 21 thresholds (Σ = 130/175 = 74%), which §3.9.1 instantiates.

**Content-volume discipline.** The original's entire game fits a 200 MB eShop envelope (**[DOCUMENTED]**, §13.1). Our budget is per-platform and owned by §14, but the Switch figure is a useful historical anchor: a 2D-plane stacker with 8 environments and a lounge soundtrack is inherently small, and our Addressables-per-world grouping (§5) plus the §16 asset pipeline should keep the PC/mobile builds in the same order of magnitude. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: adopt "200 MB-class" as the internal sanity ceiling for the base-game content pack.

| Element | Disposition for our clone |

| Five-mode set (Arcade, Endurance, Infinity, Swift Stacker, Tower Tumble) | Adopt — the Switch press-sheet copy is the canonical `GameModeDefinition` contract (§5); mechanics spec in §3/§11 |

## 14. Cross-Cutting Concerns

This section covers the concerns that span every platform target and every runtime system: save/cloud synchronization, performance budgets and the profiling protocol, accessibility, the testing strategy, optional telemetry/crash reporting, and the security/DevSecOps posture (save integrity, leaderboard anti-cheat, secret hygiene, supply chain). Platform-specific mechanics (Player Settings tables, store submission steps) live in §18 and §19; CI pipeline implementation lives in §16; the numbers here are the budgets those sections must hit. All external facts carry inline sources accessed 2026-09-24; anything the original game's public record cannot supply and we design ourselves is flagged **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

### 14.1 Save data and cloud synchronization

#### 14.1.1 Save file taxonomy

`SaveSystem` (§6) persists to `Application.persistentDataPath` per platform. The file split below is deliberate: Valve documents that Steam Cloud "keep[s] saves small and split frequently-changed vs rarely-changed data into separate files," because sync happens before/after each session and per-user byte + file-count quotas are configured in App Admin ([Valve, Steam Cloud](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]** (mechanism) + **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (file layout).

| File | Contents | Written when | Approx. size | Cloud class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profile.json` | Settings: audio volumes, language, UI scale, accessibility flags, input binding overrides (§7) | On change, debounced 2 s | ~4 KB | Sync always |
| `progress.json` | Per-level best score/stars/time, world unlocks, medal counts, achievement mirror state | Level end only | ~30 KB at 200 levels | Sync always |
| `stats.json` | Aggregate playtime, attempt counts, telemetry install id | Level end, throttled | ~2 KB | Sync always |
| `ghosts/<level>.aor` | One input-tape replay per level best (§3 ghost replays) | New personal best only | ~8–40 KB each | Sync always, additive-only |
| `save.meta` | Schema version, per-file content hashes, HMAC signatures (§14.6.2) | With every write | <1 KB | Sync always |

Total cloud footprint per user: well under 5 MB — far inside the documented hard limits (100 MB max single `FileWrite` call; files >256 MB "may route to non-optimal storage endpoints", which we will never approach) ([Valve, Steam Cloud](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]** (limits).

#### 14.1.2 Steam Cloud configuration (primary cloud target)

v1 ships Steam first (§2 target order), so Steam Cloud is the only cloud backend wired at launch. **[DOCUMENTED]** facts that drive the configuration:

- Steam offers two mechanisms: **Steam Auto-Cloud** (zero code, configured in App Admin with Root paths and Root Overrides) and the **Steam Cloud API** (`ISteamRemoteStorage`: `FileWrite`/`FileReadStream`, `BeginFileWriteBatch`/`EndFileWriteBatch`, `SetSyncPlatforms`, local-change query APIs `GetLocalFileChangeCount`/`GetLocalFileChange`) ([Valve, Steam Cloud](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), accessed 2026-09-24).
- With distinct per-OS roots, the default for new files is **per-OS sync — no cross-platform saves**. To get cross-platform (Windows ↔ macOS) save sync you must define **one root** (typically the Windows path) plus **Root Overrides** mapping the other OS's path onto it ([Valve, Steam Cloud](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), accessed 2026-09-24).
- **Dynamic Cloud Sync** covers the Steam Deck suspend/resume case: upload happens at suspend, and remote changes are delivered at wake via the local-file-change notification APIs ([Valve, Steam Cloud](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), accessed 2026-09-24).
- Unique-per-Steam-user save paths are achievable via `ISteamUser::GetSteamID` → `GetAccountID` ([Valve, Steam Cloud](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), accessed 2026-09-24).

Decision **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: use **Auto-Cloud only**, no `ISteamRemoteStorage` code path in v1. Rationale: our files are tiny and session-boundary-synced, Auto-Cloud needs zero shipping code, and Dynamic Cloud Sync's wake-delivery case is exactly what our boot-time conflict resolver (§14.1.3) already handles. The persistent-data layout uses a fixed subdirectory (`<persistentDataPath>/saves/`) with identical inner structure on both desktop OSes; App Admin configures the Windows root plus a macOS Root Override pointing at the macOS-equivalent directory. Because `persistentDataPath` differs per OS ( `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\...` vs `~/Library/Application Support/...`), the exact root/override strings are filled in at partner-account time. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact Auto-Cloud Root / Root Override path strings against the logged-in App Admin Cloud settings page; the public doc describes the mechanism but not per-OS path examples. --> Shared-family-machine multi-profile separation (multiple Steam accounts on one PC) is handled by Auto-Cloud's own per-user pathing plus a `steam_account_id` stamp inside `save.meta` written via the wrapper's identity call so a mismatched directory is detected rather than merged.

#### 14.1.3 Conflict resolution

Auto-Cloud is file-level: when both machines wrote since last sync, both versions exist and the game must reconcile. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — policy table:

| File | Strategy on divergence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `profile.json` | Newest-writer-wins by embedded `writtenAtUnixUtc`; loser copied to `profile.<n>.bak` (keep 2) | Settings are low-stakes and user-preference bound |
| `progress.json` | **Structural union merge**: per level take max(score), max(stars), min(time); world unlock = logical OR; conflicting identical-key entries resolved by later `writtenAtUnixUtc` | Progress is monotone by construction; union never loses work |
| `stats.json` | Take the file with the greater `playtimeSeconds`; merge attempt counters by max | Counters are monotone |
| `ghosts/*.aor` | Additive-only union; dedupe by content hash in `save.meta` | Replays are immutable artifacts |
| Signature/hash mismatch on any file | Quarantine to `quarantine/`, log, treat as absent (fresh where safe) | Integrity failure must not brick progress (§14.6.2) |

The resolver runs at `Bootstrap` before `MainMenu` (GameStateMachine, §6). If, after union, a same-level score exists in both files with equal timestamps but different values (astronomically rare), keep the higher and surface a one-line notice in the level-select footer — no modal dialog for an auto-mergeable class. A modal choice is shown only when `progress.json` fails schema parse on both candidates. The merge itself is pure C# (no Unity API) living in the Core asmdef so it is EditMode-testable (§14.4.2).

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Aob.Core.Persistence
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Pure-logic merge of two save-file candidate dictionaries produced by a
    /// Steam Cloud conflict (both sides changed). No Unity API — EditMode-testable.
    /// [ORIGINAL DESIGN]
    /// </summary>
    public static class SaveMerger
    {
        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>
        /// Union-merges two per-level progress maps: max score/stars, min time,
        /// latest timestamp wins ties.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="a">Candidate A (local).</param>
        /// <param name="b">Candidate B (remote).</param>
        /// <returns>Merged map; input dictionaries are not mutated.</returns>
        public static Dictionary<string, LevelProgressRecord> MergeProgress(
            IReadOnlyDictionary<string, LevelProgressRecord> a,
            IReadOnlyDictionary<string, LevelProgressRecord> b)
        {
            var merged = new Dictionary<string, LevelProgressRecord>(a.Count + b.Count);
            foreach (KeyValuePair<string, LevelProgressRecord> entry in a)
            {
                merged.Add(entry.Key, entry.Value);
            }

            foreach (KeyValuePair<string, LevelProgressRecord> entry in b)
            {
                if (!merged.TryGetValue(entry.Key, out LevelProgressRecord existing))
                {
                    merged.Add(entry.Key, entry.Value);
                    continue;
                }

                merged[entry.Key] = UnionLevel(existing, entry.Value);
            }

            return merged;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private static LevelProgressRecord UnionLevel(LevelProgressRecord x, LevelProgressRecord y)
        {
            bool xNewer = x.LastPlayedUnixUtc >= y.LastPlayedUnixUtc;
            LevelProgressRecord newer = xNewer ? x : y;
            return new LevelProgressRecord(
                BestScore: Math.Max(x.BestScore, y.BestScore),
                BestStars: Math.Max(x.BestStars, y.BestStars),
                BestTimeSeconds: Math.Min(x.BestTimeSeconds, y.BestTimeSeconds),
                Attempts: Math.Max(x.Attempts, y.Attempts),
                LastPlayedUnixUtc: newer.LastPlayedUnixUtc);
        }

        #endregion
    }

    /// <summary>Immutable per-level progress record (serialization model, §6).</summary>
    [Serializable]
    public readonly record struct LevelProgressRecord(
        int BestScore,
        int BestStars,
        float BestTimeSeconds,
        int Attempts,
        long LastPlayedUnixUtc);
}
```

#### 14.1.4 Mobile and Xbox cloud posture

- **iOS/Android v1: local saves only, no cloud.** The research sweep captured no iCloud/Google-Play-Games cloud-save facts for Unity 6.6 (nothing in T07/T08), so v1 ships without them rather than guessing at entitlement flows. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: iCloud KVS/cloud-docs requirements via Apple docs + Unity iCloud plugin status before any mobile cloud save is scheduled; Google Play Games Services v2 save-game surface likewise. --> If iCloud is added later, the hook point is already verified as available in Unity's Xcode post-processing API — `ProjectCapabilityManager.AddiCloud` exists in the current `UnityEditor.iOS.Xcode` capability list ([Unity, ProjectCapabilityManager](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/iOS.Xcode.ProjectCapabilityManager.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — and the merge policy of §14.1.3 is backend-agnostic. **[DOCUMENTED]** (API existence) + **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (deferral).
- **Xbox:** platform-managed title storage/cloud saves are part of Xbox services configured in Partner Center ([Microsoft, Xbox services overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/services/fundamentals/live-xbl-overview), accessed 2026-09-24), but the concrete API/requirements sit inside the NDA-gated GDK area (§19); the same `SaveSystem` file layout is reused so the platform adapter only changes the transport. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Xbox title-storage quotas and API shape under ID@Xbox NDA access; do not design further from public sources. -->

#### 14.1.5 Privacy, GDPR, and data-safety touchpoints

- **Apple privacy manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`)**: required at App Review; declare collected-data types and required-reason API usage. Unity Engine auto-includes its own required-reason declarations since Editors 2021.3.35f1/2022.3.18f1/2023.2.7f1: User defaults APIs **CA92.1** (PlayerPrefs), File timestamp APIs **0A2A.1 + C617.1**, System boot time **35F9.1**, Disk space **E174.1** ([Unity, Apple privacy manifest policy](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/apple-privacy-manifest-policy.html), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]** Our own obligations: (a) if `SaveSystem` or telemetry calls the C# File/Directory timestamp APIs the Unity page enumerates (`File.GetLastWriteTime` etc.), we must declare those reasons ourselves; (b) third-party SDKs (any crash SDK on iOS, §14.5) must ship their own manifests or the build risks rejection ([Unity, Apple privacy manifest policy](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/apple-privacy-manifest-policy.html), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]**
- **Baseline GDPR posture [ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: no personal data in saves (no names, emails, free-text); telemetry (if enabled, §14.5) uses a random install id created at first consent; consent is requested before the first network call ever fires; a "wipe data / revoke consent" control exists in settings on every platform; a public privacy policy URL is a store-listing requirement on all four stores. Because v1 collects nothing without opt-in, the default answer to every data-collection declaration is "none."
- **Google Play Data safety form**: with telemetry off, declare no data collected; with opt-in telemetry shipped in an update, the form must be re-declared (analytics + crash logs, data encrypted in transit, deletable). The form's exact 2026 field requirements were not captured by research. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: current Play Console Data safety form questions and the personal-developer-account closed-testing requirement (reported 20-tester/14-day rule) against support.google.com before the Android submission milestone (§10 P6). -->
- **Android permission minimization**: Unity auto-adds permissions from settings/API usage — INTERNET (Internet Access = Require in dev builds, UnityWebRequest, `Ping`, `System.Net.Sockets`, Analytics/Cloud Diagnostics), VIBRATE (`Handheld.Vibrate`), ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (LocationService), CAMERA (WebCamTexture), RECORD_AUDIO (Microphone) ([Unity, Android App Manifest](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-manifest.html), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]** Policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: production Android builds keep only VIBRATE (haptics, §7) plus ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE; INTERNET is compiled in only in the telemetry-enabled flavor (§14.5); location/camera/microphone never enter the manifest — verified in CI by asserting the merged manifest of each AAB (§16).

### 14.2 Performance budgets and profiling protocol

#### 14.2.1 Frame-time budgets

The game is a calm physics puzzle: 60 fps is the target on every v1 platform (the Wii original ran 60 fps — see §1), with the 240 Hz effective physics rate decoupled from render via `PhysicsStepper` (§6: at 1/240 s a piece falls ≤0.085 mm/step at 1 g; ~4 substeps per 60 fps frame). Budget values are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** planning targets derived from the tier settings defined in §9 (URP asset per quality level; per-level Render Pipeline assignment — [Unity, Quality settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

| Platform (tier) | FPS | Total ms | Sim (physics substeps) | Game logic | Render CPU | Render GPU | UGUI | Audio | Headroom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Windows, 1080p, PC tier | 60 | 16.67 | 2.5 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 6.0 | 1.2 | 0.8 | ≥3.2 |
| macOS Apple silicon, PC tier | 60 | 16.67 | 2.5 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 6.5 | 1.2 | 0.8 | ≥2.7 |
| Steam Deck, Deck tier (render scale 0.8–0.9 + FSR) | 60 | 16.67 | 2.5 | 1.0 | 1.8 | 6.0 | 1.2 | 0.8 | ≥3.0 |
| Android upper-mid (SD 7-class), Mobile tier (0.75–0.85) | 60 | 16.67 | 3.0 | 1.2 | 1.8 | 5.5 | 1.5 | 0.8 | ≥2.2 |
| iOS A15-class, Mobile tier | 60 | 16.67 | 3.0 | 1.2 | 1.8 | 5.5 | 1.5 | 0.8 | ≥2.2 |
| Xbox Series S, Console tier (1440p) | 60 | 16.67 | 2.5 | 1.0 | 1.8 | 5.5 | 1.2 | 0.8 | ≥3.0 |

Notes: MSAA costs are inside the GPU column (MSAA is forward-path only — [Unity, Quality settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**); Render Scale "scales the render target resolution (not the resolution of your current device)" ([Unity, URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**). Xbox budgets are provisional pending GDK guidance. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Xbox Series performance guidance is NDA-gated; revisit budgets when ID@Xbox access lands (§19). --> Physics budget scales with active body count; the Endurance/Infinity queues (§5) are capped so active rigid bodies stay ≤100 — beyond that the sim budget doubles and the 30 fps ladder engages (§14.2.3).

#### 14.2.2 Memory and load-time budgets

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** targets (texture-streaming knob names documented: Memory Budget, Renderers Per Frame, Max Level Reduction, Max IO Requests; defaults 512 MB / 512 / 2 / 1024 — [Unity, Quality settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Metric | Windows | macOS | Steam Deck | Android | iOS | Xbox Series |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total resident target | ≤1.2 GB | ≤1.2 GB | ≤1.5 GB | ≤900 MB sustained | ≤900 MB (jetsam margin) | TBD (NDA) |
| Texture streaming budget | 512 MB (default) | 512 MB | 256 MB | 128 MB | 128 MB | TBD |
| Managed heap ceiling | 128 MB | 128 MB | 128 MB | 96 MB | 96 MB | 128 MB |
| GC allocs in steady-state gameplay | 0 B/frame | 0 B/frame | 0 B/frame | 0 B/frame | 0 B/frame | 0 B/frame |
| Cold boot → main menu | ≤6 s (HDD PC) | ≤6 s | ≤6 s | ≤5 s | ≤5 s | TBD |
| Level load (Addressables, §5) | ≤1.5 s warm / ≤3 s cold | same | same | ≤1.5 s / ≤3 s | ≤1.5 s / ≤3 s | TBD |

Zero-allocation steady state is enforced by review checklist (unity-game-dev-expert standard: no allocations in Update/FixedUpdate/hot paths) and by a PlayMode test that takes GC samples across 600 frames of a scripted loop (§14.4.3).

#### 14.2.3 Frame pacing and the degradation ladder

Documented pacing rules we build on:

- `QualitySettings.vSyncCount != 0` makes `Application.targetFrameRate` ignored; Unity recommends `vSyncCount > 0` when smooth pacing is needed on desktop; on mobile with vSync 0 and `targetFrameRate = -1` the player renders a fixed 30 fps battery-saving mode; non-divisor rates round down to a divisor of the refresh (25 → 20 on 60 Hz); iOS 120 Hz requires enabling ProMotion, which is off by default ([Unity, Application.targetFrameRate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]**
- iOS Player Settings expose "Adjust iOS FPS based on thermal state," default on, with Serious thermal → 30 FPS and Critical → 15 FPS defaults ([Unity, iOS Player settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]**
- Android has an Optimized Frame Pacing toggle in Player Settings ([Unity, Android Player settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsAndroid.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**), and the URP asset exposes an Adaptive Performance section when the package is installed for runtime quality scaling ([Unity, URP asset reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/urp/universalrp-asset.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**).

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** ladder (applied in order, one step per 2 s of sustained overrun, hysteresis of 5 s before stepping back up): (1) render scale −0.10 down to 0.60; (2) MSAA 4x → 2x; (3) bloom/postFX off (keep tonemapping); (4) additional-light count → 0; (5) 30 fps cap (`targetFrameRate = 30`, `vSyncCount = 0` on mobile/Deck). On iOS the built-in thermal governor runs beneath this ladder and is left at its documented defaults; we never fight it. Desktop keeps `vSyncCount = 1` (or 2 for a 30 Hz cap on high-refresh displays) per the documented recommendation; `targetFrameRate` is the mobile/Deck authority. The 3-second stability window (§3) is wall-clock-driven through `Time.timeScale`-independent timers so a 30 fps drop never stretches the actual countdown — the feel of the original's three-green-lights cadence must survive the ladder.

#### 14.2.4 Profiler markers from day one

Custom markers land in P1 (vertical slice phase, §10) — retrofitting profiling is how budgets rot. All markers are static `readonly` `ProfilerMarker`s (created once; `using (marker.Auto())` pattern; zero allocation when no profiler is attached). **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

| Marker | Subsystem (owner section) | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `AoB.SimFrame` / `AoB.SimStep` | PhysicsStepper (§6) | Cost of all substeps this frame vs per-step cost |
| `AoB.StabilityEvaluate` | StabilityMonitor (§6) | Settle-predicate scan cost per frame |
| `AoB.BehaviourTick` | BlockBehaviourDriver (§8) | `IBlockBehaviour` update fan-out |
| `AoB.PieceSpawn` / `AoB.PieceRelease` | LevelManager (§6) | Pool get/return + collider setup spikes |
| `AoB.ScoreRecompute` | ScoreController (§6) | Event-driven scoring cost |
| `AoB.WaterContacts` | StabilityMonitor (§6) | Water-trigger volume processing |
| `AoB.Save.Write` / `AoB.Save.Sign` | SaveSystem (§6, §14.6.2) | Disk + HMAC cost (must be off main-thread spikes) |
| `AoB.Cloud.CheckConflict` | Boot flow (§14.1.3) | Merge cost at bootstrap |
| `AoB.UI.HudRefresh` | UGUI HUD (§9) | Canvas rebuild cost |
| `AoB.AudioDirector.Update` | AudioDirector (§6) | Adaptive-layer mixing cost |
| `AoB.Telemetry.Flush` | TelemetryService (§14.5) | Batched upload cost (only if enabled) |


### 14.3 Accessibility

The original's core feedback is already multi-channel (the three sequential green stability lights are visual, documented across reviews — see §1/§3), which this design preserves and extends. Everything below except where cited is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

#### 14.3.1 Block identity is never color-only

Five special block types plus base blocks (§5, §8) must be distinguishable under the three common color-vision deficiencies. Identity channels: silhouette/shape family, surface pattern, icon glyph, then color last.

| Block type | Primary (non-color) cue | Secondary cue | Palette constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base blocks | Shape family per `PieceDefinition` (16 shapes, §1) + material pattern per world theme | Color | Okabe-Ito-derived palette entries |
| Breakable (load-break) | Cracked-surface decal pattern, distinct silhouette | Audible rattle under stress (§9) | Not red-only |
| Timed/disappearing | Shrinking arc dial on top face + tick audio in warning phase | Emits particles as lifetime burns | Warning state changes geometry, not just tint |
| Gravity-inverter | Up/down arrow glyph on every face | Global hue-wave + camera dip on flip (§8.6, §14.3.4) | Arrow contrast ≥4.5:1 against all world themes |
| Fire | Flame icon + emissive pulse | Distinct ignition SFX | Warm/cool pairing for deuteranopia |
| Linked/seesaw (our extension) | Matching engraved symbol pair (◇–◇) + dashed connector line rendered between partners | Shared chime on link stress | Symbols differ by shape, never by hue alone |

Validation: a color-deficiency simulation pass (deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia matrix filters) is part of the screenshot-QA automation loop (§17) over every block icon and one gameplay capture per world; the check is human-reviewed on failure. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

#### 14.3.2 Vision support

- **UI scale**: the UGUI layer is authored at 1920×1080 reference with Canvas Scaler "Scale With Screen Size," Match Width or Height, Match 0.5 — the documented blend that keeps element size across aspect changes ([Unity, Canvas Scaler](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/script-CanvasScaler.html); [Unity, Designing UI for Multiple Resolutions](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/HOWTO-UIMultiResolution.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**). A user-facing UI-scale multiplier (0.8×–1.4×) applies as a reference-resolution delta so anchors still hold; minimum body text ≥24 px at 1080p equivalent. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**
- Deck Verified makes legibility an explicit review criterion ("text should be legible" at 1280x800/720 default resolution — [Valve, Steam Deck Verified](https://www.steamdeck.com/en/verified), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**), so the smallest supported default (not just the largest slider step) must pass review.
- TextMeshPro fallback chains cover extended alphabets (primary asset → per-asset fallbacks → sprite asset → general fallbacks — [Unity, TMP fallback fonts](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/TextMeshPro/FontAssetsFallback.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**); dyslexia-friendly font option is a settings toggle.
- Safe-area handling (§9's `SafeAreaFitter` over `Screen.safeArea`, bottom-left origin, includes notches/cutouts/TV overscan — [Unity, Screen.safeArea](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Screen-safeArea.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**) doubles as the low-vision margin: nothing interactive sits inside the inset band.

#### 14.3.3 Motor support

- Full input remapping and device hot-swap come from §7's `IPieceInputProvider` architecture (rebinding persisted as JSON binding overrides). Gamepad navigation of all menus uses Selectable Explicit/Automatic navigation with a set first-selected object ([Unity, Selectable navigation](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/script-SelectableNavigation.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**).
- **One-hand presets [ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: (a) gamepad single-hand scheme — left stick moves the cursor, two face buttons rotate CW/CCW, trigger drops (mirrored variant for right/left); (b) touch one-hand — drag anywhere to move, tap-left/tap-right screen halves to rotate, dedicated drop button reachable by thumb; (c) keyboard one-hand — arrows + Z/X/Space cluster. Presets are provider-configuration data (§7), not separate code paths, so the Switch Patch 1.1-style late control addition pattern (§7 case study) applies to accessibility schemes too.
- No timed QTEs anywhere in the core loop: carrying time is unbounded, rotation is incremental, and the 3-second window is a wait state, not an input test — inherited from the original's design (§3).

#### 14.3.4 Photosensitivity and reduced motion

The gravity-inverter flip is the highest-risk effect: the canonical presentation is §8.6's 0.4 s world-space hue-wave plus subtle 15° camera dip-and-recover (explicitly not a 180° roll), implemented in §9.7; this section owns only the caps and the reduce-motion replacement — the hue-wave is eased, never a strobe or full-screen flash, its per-frame luminance step capped per §9.7.3, and shatter/collapse VFX contain no >3-per-second luminance transitions and no red/black alternation. A "reduce motion" toggle disables the camera dip and hue-wave sweep (250 ms orientation cross-fade), collapse shake, and idle water bobbing (§9). Console certification photosensitivity requirements were not captured by public research (Xbox XR deep pages unfetched). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: photosensitivity and captioning XRs against the public XR listings (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/store/policies/gc-policies-nav) once the exact XR documents are reviewed pre-submission; Steam/App Store have no hard gate, Xbox likely does. -->

#### 14.3.5 Hearing support

Every gameplay-relevant audio cue has a visual twin: timer-block warning → arc dial + particle pulse; stress creak → crack overlay opacity; gravity flip → arrow glyph animation; water contact → ripple VFX + HUD edge flash; stability countdown → the three-light indicator (original-documented, §1). Music/SFX sliders plus a master "audio cues → visual only" summary toggle. Subtitles are moot (no voice), but caption-style text for stingers exists in the accessibility flavor. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

#### 14.3.6 Certification and store expectations

Xbox Requirements (XRs) are binding "policies, technical requirements, and product component-related requirements" identical across devices with device-specific test cases ([Microsoft, Policies and XRs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/store/policies/gc-policies-nav), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**); accessibility-specific XR text was not captured publicly and is treated as a pre-submission checklist item (§19). Steam imposes no accessibility gate beyond Deck Verified's legibility criterion above. Our internal bar: ship the accessibility settings menu on all platforms identically, so no platform port (§18/§19) ever strips a feature to pass cert.

### 14.4 Testing strategy

#### 14.4.1 Layout

Two test asmdefs mirroring the runtime ones (§4): `Aob.Tests.EditMode` (references Core + Gameplay + Data assemblies; no scene dependencies) and `Aob.Tests.PlayMode` (references everything plus test-scene fixtures under `Assets/_Project/Scenes/TestScenes/`). Test categories map 1:1 to suites below so `-testFilter`/`-testCategory` selection in CI (§16) is stable. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

#### 14.4.2 EditMode suites

| Suite (category) | Covers | Key assertions |
|---|---|---|
| `PhysicsRules` | Pure predicates extracted from `StabilityMonitor` (settling thresholds, hysteresis, waterline tests as static functions — §6) | Settle predicate state tables; hysteresis boundary cases |
| `ScoringMath` | `ScoreController` + §3 formula (base points, height bonus, time bonus, multipliers, Swift Stacker chain — §3.7.5) | Hand-computed expected values incl. star-threshold derivation; overflow/rounding policy |
| `SaveRoundTrip` | `SaveSystem` serialize→deserialize equality; `SaveMerger` union cases (§14.1.3); migration v1→v2 fixtures; `SaveSigner` verify/tamper cases (§14.6.2) | Field-by-field equality; tampered payload fails verify; older schema migrates idempotently |
| `ContentValidation` | All `LevelDefinition`/`PieceDefinition` assets (§5): queue mass budget vs platform heuristic, star-threshold monotonicity, required localization keys | Every one of the 200 levels passes; failures name the asset GUID |
| `BehaviourMatrix` | §8 test matrix: each `IBlockBehaviour` × state (falling/stacked/water-contact/win-window), driven by direct invocation with fake context | Spec-table transitions hold; no behaviour mutates state outside its hooks |
| `TelemetrySchema` | Event payloads fixed-size, no PII fields (§14.5) | Struct field count/type stability across versions |

#### 14.4.3 PlayMode integration tests

A `ScriptedInputProvider : IPieceInputProvider` replays recorded input tapes (the same `.aor` format as ghost replays — one format, two consumers) through the real `InputRouter` → `LevelManager` → `PhysicsStepper` chain; tests drive the stepper with fixed dt directly (per §6's simulation-mode discipline), so PlayMode tests are deterministic on a given machine by construction. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Aob.Gameplay.Input;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Tests.PlayMode
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Deterministic input provider for PlayMode tests and soak bots: replays a
    /// fixed tape of timed commands through the real InputRouter (§7).
    /// [ORIGINAL DESIGN]
    /// </summary>
    public class ScriptedInputProvider : IPieceInputProvider
    {
        #region Nested Types

        private readonly struct TimedCommand
        {
            public readonly float TimeSeconds;
            public readonly InputCommand Command;

            public TimedCommand(float timeSeconds, InputCommand command)
            {
                TimeSeconds = timeSeconds;
                Command = command;
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private readonly List<TimedCommand> _tape;
        private int _cursor;
        private float _elapsed;

        #endregion

        #region Constructor

        public ScriptedInputProvider(IReadOnlyList<(float t, InputCommand cmd)> tape)
        {
            _tape = new List<TimedCommand>(tape.Count);
            foreach ((float t, InputCommand cmd) in tape)
            {
                _tape.Add(new TimedCommand(t, cmd));
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Advances the tape by dt and returns commands whose time arrived.</summary>
        public int Poll(float dt, InputCommand[] buffer)
        {
            _elapsed += dt;
            int count = 0;
            while (_cursor < _tape.Count && _tape[_cursor].TimeSeconds <= _elapsed && count < buffer.Length)
            {
                buffer[count++] = _tape[_cursor].Command;
                _cursor++;
            }

            return count;
        }

        /// <summary>Resets the tape to t=0 for replay-determinism assertions.</summary>
        public void Reset()
        {
            _cursor = 0;
            _elapsed = 0f;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Canonical loop test: load `TestScenes/Loop_BasicTower`, replay a 90 s tape, assert `GameStateMachine` reaches `Cleared`, score matches the EditMode-computed expectation, GC allocations over the window are zero, and all §14.2.4 markers stay inside budget.

#### 14.4.4 Determinism and replay tests

Physics determinism posture (from the physics research folded into §6): built-in engines are deterministic on the same device for identical inputs/state, but not guaranteed across devices; simulations must step a fixed dt. Consequences for tests **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: (1) **same-device replay tests** — record state-hash at level start, run a tape, hash final state; replay the tape; hashes must match exactly (nightly, per platform runner in §16); (2) **golden corpus** — a checked-in set of ~50 ghost tapes; each nightly job replays them and compares end-state hashes against per-platform baselines, catching engine-version drift when Unity 6.6 patch releases land (§21 risk: tech-stream churn); (3) cross-device hash equality is explicitly *not* asserted — online leaderboards never compare client-side simulation, only reported scores plus optional replay artifacts (§14.6.3).

#### 14.4.6 Soak, thermal, and interruption tests

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (gated in CI nightly/RC): 8 h menu-idle (memory slope must be flat — leak gate); 2 h Endurance loop with the scripted bot (thermal + GC + pool-growth gates); battery profile: 60 fps → documented 30 fps mobile battery mode acceptance ([Unity, Application.targetFrameRate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**); iOS thermal walk (outdoor-warm device until the governor steps to 30/15 — documented defaults in §14.2.3) verifying the ladder hands over cleanly; Steam overlay open/close mid-level 100× (overlay hooks the process once Steamworks initializes — [Valve, Steamworks API overview](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**); Deck suspend/resume exercising Dynamic Cloud Sync wake (§14.1.2); Android backgrounding/Doze and iOS call-interruption save-integrity checks (signed save must verify after restore).

#### 14.4.7 CI wiring

All suites run headless via the batch-mode/CLI invocation contracts specified in §16 (NUnit XML results; editmode on every OS runner, playmode on Windows + Android; device-lab and soak jobs nightly/RC). Code coverage runs only on a dedicated test job — coverage instrumentation is documented as crash-prone in the GameCI tooling per the CI research (see §16). Flaky tests are quarantined by category with a 14-day fix SLA rather than deleted. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (policy) with mechanisms defined in §16.

### 14.5 Telemetry and crash reporting (optional, Steam-first)

The SDK contents captured in T08 (track-t08-desktop-console-platforms.md) list no analytics or crash-aggregation component, so any telemetry is a deliberate addition (inference from the captured API/contents surface, not a documented Valve statement). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: the Steamworks docs nav captured with the SDK page lists a 'Steam Error Reporting' feature (https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/error_reporting) that was never fetched; check its scope before treating 'no first-party crash reporting' as absolute. --> **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** decision: v1.0 ships **opt-in, minimal, self-hostable** — crash reports first, gameplay telemetry second, both behind one consent gate (§14.1.5).

| Event | Fields (fixed, non-PII) | Trigger | Privacy class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session_start` | platform, app version, quality tier, locale, install id | First level entry post-consent | Anonymous analytics |
| `level_result` | level id, outcome enum, duration, score, fail-reason taxonomy (§3) | Level end | Anonymous analytics |
| `settings_delta` | anonymized setting keys changed (no free text) | Settings close | Anonymous analytics |
| `perf_sample` | avg/99th frame ms, tier, thermal state where available | Every 5 min in gameplay | Anonymous diagnostics |
| `crash` | stack, breadcrumbs (last 20 events), device class | Unhandled exception | Crash diagnostics |

Implementation options weighed: Unity Cloud Diagnostics (convenience, but flips Android INTERNET/Analytics permission behavior documented in §14.1.5 and routes data through Unity) vs a self-hosted Sentry (data control fitting the DevSecOps lens; skill-standard crash tooling with Sentry/Bugsnag/Crashlytics alternatives) vs none. Choice: **Sentry self-hosted** for crash, custom minimal JSON-lines event sink for the analytics table (batched, flushed on level end; zero allocation in the recording path). If telemetry is disabled at build time, the Android flavor compiles without INTERNET. GDPR mechanics per §14.1.5. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Text;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Core.Telemetry
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Opt-in telemetry recorder. Fixed-size ring buffer, no per-event allocations;
    /// serialization happens only at flush time off the hot path. [ORIGINAL DESIGN]
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class TelemetryService : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Nested Types

        private struct TelemetryEvent
        {
            public int EventId;
            public int LevelId;
            public int PayloadA;
            public float PayloadB;
            public long UnixUtc;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Serialized Fields

        [Header("Configuration")]
        [SerializeField] private int capacity = 256;
        [SerializeField] private float flushIntervalSeconds = 180f;

        #endregion

        #region Private Fields

        private TelemetryEvent[] _buffer;
        private int _head;
        private int _count;
        private bool _consented;

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void Awake()
        {
            _buffer = new TelemetryEvent[capacity];
        }

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Enables recording; called only after explicit user consent.</summary>
        public void SetConsent(bool granted)
        {
            _consented = granted;
            if (!granted)
            {
                Array.Clear(_buffer, 0, _buffer.Length);
                _head = 0;
                _count = 0;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>Records one event; struct copy only, no allocation.</summary>
        public void Record(int eventId, int levelId, int payloadA, float payloadB)
        {
            if (!_consented)
            {
                return;
            }

            _buffer[_head] = new TelemetryEvent
            {
                EventId = eventId,
                LevelId = levelId,
                PayloadA = payloadA,
                PayloadB = payloadB,
                UnixUtc = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
            };
            _head = (_head + 1) % _buffer.Length;
            _count = Math.Min(_count + 1, _buffer.Length);
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private IEnumerator FlushRoutine()
        {
            var wait = new WaitForSeconds(flushIntervalSeconds);
            while (true)
            {
                yield return wait;
                // … serialize _count events to JSON lines and POST off-thread;
                // marked with AoB.Telemetry.Flush profiler marker (§14.2.4).
            }
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

### 14.6 Security and DevSecOps

The user's DevSecOps background sets the bar: integrity where players are adversarial, secret hygiene in automation, and supply-chain control on everything between git clone and shipped binary.

#### 14.6.1 Threat model

| Asset | Adversary | Attack | Impact | Mitigation (this section) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Save progress | Casual player / save editor | Inflate stars/scores locally | Polluted leaderboards, broken unlocks | HMAC signing (§14.6.2) + server-tolerant merge |
| Leaderboard entries | Cheater with debugger | Forged `UploadLeaderboardScore` calls | Corrupt rankings | §14.6.3 mitigations |
| Cloud saves | Curious/malicious sync target | Tampered remote file | Crash/progress loss on merge | Hash + signature verify before merge (§14.1.3) |
| Build secrets (keystore, signing ids, Steam keys) | CI compromise / repo leak | Signed malicious updates | Catastrophic | §14.6.4 |
| Packages & dev tooling | Supply-chain actor | Compromised UPM package / MCP RCE pivot | Source/build compromise | §14.6.5 |

#### 14.6.2 Save-file integrity (signing)

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: every save file ships in a signed envelope — canonical (sorted-key, fixed-culture) JSON payload + HMAC-SHA256 over `header || schemaVersion || payload`, keyed by a per-install key derived from a random install GUID plus a build-embedded pepper. Honest scope: this is integrity against casual editing, not cryptographic protection — a determined attacker with the binary can extract the pepper. It exists because it is cheap, removes the script-kiddie class of leaderboard pollution, and makes cloud-merge corruption detectable (§14.1.3).

```csharp
using System;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

namespace Aob.Core.Persistence
{
    /// <summary>
    /// HMAC-SHA256 signing for save envelopes: integrity against casual editing,
    /// not secrecy. Keys derived per-install; comparison is constant-time.
    /// [ORIGINAL DESIGN]
    /// </summary>
    public static class SaveSigner
    {
        #region Constants

        private const string Header = "AOBSAVE1";
        private const int KeySizeBytes = 32;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>Computes the hex HMAC for a canonicalized payload.</summary>
        public static string ComputeSignature(string canonicalPayload, byte[] key)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(canonicalPayload)) { throw new ArgumentException(nameof(canonicalPayload)); }
            if (key == null || key.Length == 0) { throw new ArgumentException(nameof(key)); }

            using var hmac = new HMACSHA256(key);
            byte[] mac = hmac.ComputeHash(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(Header + canonicalPayload));
            return Convert.ToHexString(mac);
        }

        /// <summary>Constant-time verification of a signature over a payload.</summary>
        public static bool Verify(string canonicalPayload, byte[] key, string signatureHex)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(signatureHex)) { return false; }

            string expected = ComputeSignature(canonicalPayload, key);
            return CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(
                Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(expected.ToUpper(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)),
                Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(signatureHex.ToUpper(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)));
        }

        /// <summary>Derives the per-install key (install GUID + build pepper).</summary>
        public static byte[] DeriveInstallKey(Guid installId, byte[] buildPepper)
        {
            byte[] guidBytes = installId.ToByteArray();
            using var derived = new Rfc2898DeriveBytes(
                Convert.ToHexString(guidBytes), buildPepper, 100_000, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
            return derived.GetBytes(KeySizeBytes);
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Notes: canonicalization is produced by `SaveSystem` (sorted keys, `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`, no whitespace) so signing is deterministic across platforms; the PBKDF2 iteration count is a one-time cost at first boot, not a hot path; verify failures quarantine rather than delete (§14.1.3). PlayerPrefs, where used at all (input bindings), is covered on iOS by Unity's own CA92.1 required-reason declaration (§14.1.5). **[DOCUMENTED]** (that declaration) + **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (envelope).

#### 14.6.3 Leaderboard integrity

Documented Steam leaderboard mechanics we build on: `FindOrCreateLeaderboard` (or App Admin pre-creation), `UploadLeaderboardScore` with keep-best vs force-replace semantics, `DownloadLeaderboardEntries` (global/friends/around-user), and `AttachLeaderboardUGC` for attaching UGC (replays) to entries ([Valve, Leaderboards](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/leaderboards), accessed 2026-09-24). **[DOCUMENTED]** (mechanics above) — for a client-authoritative single-player game, no server-side score-validation service appears in the T08-captured leaderboard API surface (inference from the captured surface, not a documented Valve statement), and there is no game server in our architecture to provide one. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** mitigations, in layers:

1. **Keep-best uploads only** for score leaderboards (documented mode) so replaying can't lower a rank and re-submit spam is bounded.
2. **Plausibility clamp**: §3's formula is closed-form; the ContentValidation suite (§14.4.2) computes the theoretical maximum score per level (perfect time bonus, max multipliers); the client refuses to upload values above `max × 1.05` (tolerance for formula revisions). This clamps the lazy-forgery class.
3. **Replay-or-rank**: entries above a per-leaderboard rank threshold (e.g. top 100 global) are expected to carry a ghost-replay attachment via `AttachLeaderboardUGC`; the replay format is the input-tape + state-hash pair (§14.4.4), so a human reviewer (or future automated same-device re-simulation service) can audit disputed records.
4. **Signed local source**: leaderboard submissions originate from `ScoreController` values stored in signed saves (§14.6.2), raising the tamper bar one more step.
5. **No economy**: nothing purchasable or tradeable exists, so the cheat payoff is bragging rights only — proportionate defense.

#### 14.6.4 CI and signing secret hygiene

- **Unity batch/CLI**: licenses and secrets reach the editor via environment variables / GitHub Actions secrets, never as command-line arguments (process listings leak args) — enforcement pattern specified in §16. **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (policy; mechanisms in §16).
- **Android keystore**: created via Keystore Manager (Player Settings > Publishing Settings), ASCII passwords, key validity default 50 years, same key signs all updates ([Unity, Keystore Manager](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-keystore-manager.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**). The `.keystore` file lives in secret storage (CI secret/secure artifact), never in the repo; passwords as masked CI variables; rotation impossible in practice (Play upgrade compatibility) — so its leak-response plan is documented in §21.
- **Apple**: notarytool credentials stored in the Keychain of the Mac runner via `notarytool store-credentials`; Developer ID Application certificate in a CI-secure keychain created per job and destroyed after ([Apple, Notarizing macOS software](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]** for notarytool-only since 2023-11-01).
- **Windows**: Azure Artifact Signing (formerly Trusted Signing) requires a paid Azure subscription (no free/trial tiers) and passes individual identity validation (Authenticator Verified ID + FaceCheck) or organization validation — operational onboarding lead time is a schedule item, not an afterthought; billing is full-SKU non-prorated ([Microsoft, Artifact Signing FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/trusted-signing/faq), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**). **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** enrichment from the verify pass: pricing is now confirmed — Basic $9.99/mo (5,000 signatures/mo), Premium $99.99/mo (100,000/mo), $0.005/signature overage, canonical docs at ([Microsoft, Artifact Signing overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/overview); [Azure pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/artifact-signing/), accessed 2026-09-24).
- **Steam partner credentials / steam_appid.txt**: App Admin credentials are 2FA-protected and never automated; `steam_appid.txt` (dev-only, contains only the AppID, must never ship) is CI-injected for test runs only and excluded from depot manifests by the §16 build script. **[DOCUMENTED]** (dev-only rule) per ([Valve, Steamworks API overview](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api), accessed 2026-09-24).

#### 14.6.5 Supply chain

- **UPM package policy [ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: runtime dependencies are few by design (§4 manifest): Unity-bundled (URP 17.x, uGUI 2.x, Input System as a built-in module from Unity 6.6 per the verify correction — no `com.unity.inputsystem` package in new 6.6 projects), Newtonsoft JSON, Test Framework, Addressables, plus one Steamworks wrapper. Policy: pin exact versions in `packages-lock.json` (committed); no floating versions; no git-URL dependencies in release branches; no scoped registries in production manifests; every version bump is a reviewed PR including release-notes diff.
- **Steamworks wrapper** (choice made in §19; supply-chain facts here): both candidates are MIT and actively maintained as of 2026-09-24 — Steamworks.NET (release 2025.164.1, 2026-08-02; repo pushed 2026-08-07; near-1:1 C++ parity, builds against Steamworks SDK 1.65) and Facepunch.Steamworks (release 2.5.2, 2026-04-23; pushed 2026-09-15; single managed DLL, IL2CPP-verified) ([Steamworks.NET](https://github.com/rlabrecque/Steamworks.NET); [Facepunch.Steamworks](https://github.com/Facepunch/Facepunch.Steamworks), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**). CI verifies the vendored `steam_api64.dll` / `libsteam_api.dylib` / `libsteam_api.so` redist binaries against SHA-256 hashes pinned from a first-party SDK download; the macOS dylib is a verified universal Mach-O (x86_64 + arm64 slices confirmed by binary inspection in the verify pass), so no Rosetta dependency and no per-arch substitution risk. **[DOCUMENTED]** (binary facts) + **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (hash gate).
- **Dev tooling attack surface (MCP, §17)**: every Unity MCP option grants effectively arbitrary C# execution in the Editor process, and the canonical Blender MCP server's `execute_blender_code` is arbitrary Python by design over a localhost TCP socket (port 9876) — "port 9876 = RCE for anyone who can reach it" — with the AST sandbox shipped only as an opt-in env var `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE` ([mcp-for-blender addon](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/addon.py); [safe_mode.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/src/blender_mcp/safe_mode.py), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**). Rules **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: MCP servers run only on the interactive dev workstation, never on CI runners that hold signing secrets; all tool sockets stay loopback-bound (CoplayDev's Unity plugin WebSocket range 6400–6499 and the mcp-for-blender TCP port are localhost-only by default and stay that way — architecture verified in the MCP research, §17); `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=1` is set in the dev environment default profile; dev machines that run MCP servers do not hold production keystores — signing happens on a separate runner/profile.
- **IL2CPP everywhere** (all shipping targets; Mac-editor-only for macOS builds per the IL2CPP cross-compilation rule — [Unity, IL2CPP introduction](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html), accessed 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**) doubles as a mild tamper barrier: no CIL to patch trivially. Managed stripping level is tuned with reflection-survival tests (`[Preserve]`/link.xml) — level names Minimal/Low/Medium/High per the stripping hub ([Unity, managed code stripping](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/managed-code-stripping.html), accessed 2026-09-24; exact per-backend level table not re-verified <!-- TODO-VERIFY: stripping level names against the "Configure managed code stripping" page when the slug is located. -->).

#### 14.6.6 Release signing chain per platform

| Platform | Signing mechanism | Notes | Source (accessed 2026-09-24) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | signtool + Azure Artifact Signing dlib integration | SmartScreen will still warn "unrecognized app" until publisher/hash reputation accrues; EV no longer bypasses SmartScreen — set stakeholder expectations for launch | [Microsoft, SmartScreen reputation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation) **[DOCUMENTED]** |
| macOS | Developer ID Application cert + Hardened Runtime + notarytool submit → staple; ship .dmg | altool rejected since 2023-11-01; IL2CPP is AOT so no JIT entitlement; add `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` only if third-party native plugins ship (medium-confidence inference — flag for the §19 entitlement review) | [Apple, notarization](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution); [Apple, Hardened Runtime](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/hardened-runtime) **[DOCUMENTED]** |
| Android | Play App Signing via uploaded AAB; local keystore for CI artifact signing | Keystore validity 50-year default; same key for all updates | [Unity, Keystore Manager](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-keystore-manager.html) **[DOCUMENTED]** |
| iOS | Automatic Signing with Team ID in Player Settings; capabilities via `ProjectCapabilityManager` (wrap calls in try-catch — repeated calls throw) | Certs/profiles in CI-secure keychain | [Unity, iOS Player settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html); [Unity, ProjectCapabilityManager](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/iOS.Xcode.ProjectCapabilityManager.html) **[DOCUMENTED]** |
| Steam | No binary signing; optional Steamworks DRM wrapper from `tools/drm` in the SDK | Depots/build integrity is Valve-side via SteamPipe manifests (SHA-1 content hashing per build) | [Valve, Steamworks SDK](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk); [Valve, Builds/Depots](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/builds) **[DOCUMENTED]** |

Task hooks for this section land in §20 as the cross-cutting epics (profiler instrumentation, accessibility settings, test suites, signing/integrity, telemetry gate); risk entries (keystore loss, Unity 6.6→LTS migration churn, cert timelines) live in §21.

## 15. Unity Automation — The New Unity CLI

This section specifies how the official **Unity CLI** — the standalone `unity` binary Unity began shipping in 2026 — automates Editor installation, project bootstrap, licensing, builds, and tests for this game, and where it hands off to the legacy Editor batch mode (§16), the GameCI / Unity Build Automation ecosystems (§16), and the MCP tooling layer (§17). Every external fact below was captured live on 2026-09-24 and survived (or was corrected by) the adversarial verification pass. The CLI is **experimental**; the churn risk and the batch-mode fallback live in §21.

### 15.1 Identity, status, and installation

**What it is.** The Unity CLI ("Unity command-line interface (CLI)") is Unity's official standalone, self-contained `unity` binary for macOS, Linux, and Windows (x64 + Arm64; the runtime is Bun-packaged per the release notes' Bun references). It is *not* a .NET tool, and *not* the Hub's embedded CLI. **[DOCUMENTED]** — "The Unity CLI is a standalone command-line tool for installing and managing Unity Editors and modules from a terminal. The Unity Hub now automatically installs the Unity CLI." ([Unity CLI introduction](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). It is free — "Both the CLI and MCP will be free, with no concurrency limits on the MCP server" ([Unity staff announcement, Jul 15, 2026](https://discussions.unity.com/t/announcing-the-unity-cli-a-new-way-to-connect-your-tools-and-agents/1731104), accessed 2026-09-24) — and "Installing the CLI doesn't require a Unity AI subscription" ([Meet the Unity CLI](https://unity.com/blog/meet-the-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). Docs set: [Introduction](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli), [Use](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), [Reference](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference), [Release notes](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/release-notes), [CLI-replaces-Editor-MCP-server](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/replace-mcp-server-unity-cli) (all accessed 2026-09-24).

**Release status.** Every docs page carries the banner "The Unity CLI is experimental." Version history **[DOCUMENTED]** ([CLI release notes](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/release-notes), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Milestone | Version | Date |
|---|---|---|
| First public beta | 0.1.0-beta.1 | 2026-04-04 |
| Moved to 1.0 versioning | 1.0.0-beta.1 | 2026-06-30 |
| Latest at research time | 1.0.0-beta.11 | 2026-09-22 |
| Stable channel | — | does not exist yet; "install.sh and install.ps1 now install the latest beta when you don't choose a release channel, until the CLI has a stable release" (beta.11 notes) |

**Hub bundling.** **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** The T02 sweep left "which Hub version first auto-installed the CLI" unresolved; the verify pass pinned it: **Hub 3.21.0** (announced Aug 18, 2026) is the first version that ships and auto-installs the CLI — "The CLI ships with Hub and installs automatically on first launch, so no download is required" — bundling CLI 1.0.0-beta.6 (bumped in 3.21.1) ([Hub 3.21.1 announcement](https://discussions.unity.com/t/now-available-unity-hub-3-21-1/1734183), accessed 2026-09-24). Hub 3.20.x did **not** bundle it (the [3.20 beta thread](https://discussions.unity.com/t/now-available-unity-hub-3-20-beta/1731828) pointed to the separate download); [Hub 3.22 beta](https://discussions.unity.com/t/now-available-unity-hub-3-22-beta/1736658) (Sep 15, 2026) continues bundling. Hub 3.21.0 also added the "Use Unity CLI" New Project checkbox (Unity 6+ projects; adds `com.unity.pipeline`) and a Tools > Unity CLI submenu — relevant to our one-dev setup because a Hub-installed CLI still lands on PATH and shares the same command surface documented here.

**Installation.** All commands below are the documented forms **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Unity CLI intro](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli) and [Use](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Channel | Command |
|---|---|
| macOS / Linux script | `curl -fsSL https://unity.com/install.sh \| bash` |
| macOS / Linux script, pinned channel (blog-era form) | `curl -fsSL https://public-cdn.cloud.unity3d.com/hub/prod/cli/install.sh \| UNITY_CLI_CHANNEL=beta bash` |
| Windows PowerShell | `irm https://unity.com/install.ps1 \| iex` |
| Homebrew (macOS; Linux needs Homebrew 6.0+; cask is named `unity-cli` because `unity` is taken) | `brew install --cask unity-cli` |
| Windows winget (MSIX) | winget package (see docs) |
| Linux repos | apt/dnf (`.deb`/`.rpm`), AppImage |
| Via Unity Hub | automatic on first Hub launch, Hub 3.21.0+ (see above) |

Post-install: binary at `~/.local/bin/unity` on Linux (older `~/.unity` migrated); `unity self-update` (alias `unity upgrade`); `unity self-uninstall -y`; `unity config update-check off` to disable update prompts (we set this on CI images for determinism). OS floors **[DOCUMENTED]**: Windows 10 21H1+; Linux RHEL 9 / Ubuntu 22.04+ with glibc 2.34+ (Debian 11, CentOS 8, Amazon Linux 2 unsupported); macOS 14+.

**Adoption risk.** Because the tool is experimental and pre-1.0-stable, its surface "might change" (docs banner). Our mitigations **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: (a) pin the CLI version in CI and in the bootstrap script (§15.5) rather than tracking latest-beta; (b) route every CLI call through one thin wrapper script so a flag rename is a one-file fix; (c) keep the §16 batch-mode path buildable as a fallback; (d) re-run `unity changelog` review as a scheduled task whenever the pin is bumped. Risk entry lives in §21.

### 15.2 Command surface (verified reference)

The full surface below is from the official reference **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Unity CLI reference](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference) and [Use](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). The CLI "manages any Editor version" — editor management is not version-gated; only the features noted otherwise are.

**Editors and modules**

| Command | Syntax (exact where documented) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| install | `unity install lts` / `unity install 6000.6.2f1` / aliases `latest\|lts\|default\|6\|6.5\|2022` | modules via `-m android ios webgl`; child modules `--cm`; changeset `-c`; arch `-a arm64\|x86_64` (macOS); unattended `--accept-eula --yes` |
| install-modules | `unity install-modules -e <editorVersion> -m ...` | add modules to an installed Editor |
| uninstall | `unity uninstall <editor>` | |
| editors | `unity editors` (list), `-r` releases, `-i` installed, `editors add <path...>`, `editors default [ver]`, `editors upgrade`, `editors prune --remove-missing` | Hub-installed and CLI-installed Editors share one registry |
| modules | `unity modules list <ver>` | |
| releases | `unity releases` | |
| install-path / hub | `unity install-path`; `unity hub install [--hub-version 3.20.0+]` | `unity hub install` installs the Hub desktop app |

**Projects, templates, assets**

| Command | Syntax | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| open / close | `unity open ./MyProject` (bare-path shorthand: `unity ./MyProject`) | `--wait` **not available on Windows yet** (docs) |
| projects | `unity projects list\|create\|clone\|open\|link\|pin` + disk size | `projects create` **defaults to enabling a Unity Cloud project**; exits 3 if not signed in; use `--no-cloud` or env `UNITY_NO_CLOUD` to keep it local; service accounts cannot create cloud projects |
| templates | `unity templates list\|inspect\|create` | project-template management |
| assets | `unity assets inspect\|export\|import` (.unitypackage) | .unitypackage import/export from the shell |

**Build, test, run**

| Command | Syntax | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| build | `unity build` (batch mode; Android signing flags) | `--list-targets`, `--list-profiles`, `--create-profile <target>` — creates a Unity 6 **Build Profile** asset; requires **Unity 6000.0+** |
| build run | `unity build run` | serves/launches the last recorded build (incl. WebGL serving with correct compression headers) |
| run | `unity run --command <name> --log-file <path>` | batch-mode or headless registered-command execution |
| recompile | `unity recompile [--strict]` | exit 6 = compile errors; exit 7 = no Editor responded |
| test | `unity test` | Edit + Play modes via the Editor test runner; NUnit report; `--affected` selects tests affected by pending changes |
| watch | `unity watch test` | re-runs `unity test --affected` on file change; ignores `Library/`, `Temp/`, `Logs/`, `Build/`, `obj/` |

**Identity, licensing, cloud**

| Command | Notes |
|---|---|
| `unity auth login\|status\|logout\|consumers\|revoke` | interactive auth; OS-keyring credential storage; resident auth broker (TPM/Secure Enclave-sealed token store, DPoP proofs) |
| `unity license list\|status\|activate\|return` | serial, Personal, floating, offline file / offline request; license-server status. `-returnlicense` semantics of the Editor CLI explicitly do not apply to floating licenses (§16) |
| `unity cloud orgs\|projects`, `unity cloud org create` | Unity Cloud org/project management |
| `unity collab` | Unity Collaboration (Plastic) operations |

**VCS suite** (15 verbs): `unity vcs setup --vcs github --git-namespace my-org --non-interactive`, `status`, `sync`, `switch`, `doctor [--fix]`, `merge-setup` (configures UnityYAMLMerge), `conflicts`, `explain`, `resolve`, `diff`, `blame`, `summarize`, `affected`, `hooks`, `providers git\|uvcs...` (Git, GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted, UVCS).

**Connected Editors and AI** (requires `com.unity.pipeline`, experimental, **Unity 6.0 LTS+**; `unity pipeline install` / `unity pipeline list`)

| Command | Notes |
|---|---|
| `unity command` / `unity command <name> [--result-only]` | list / run registered commands in a *running* Editor |
| `unity commands --format json` | machine-readable manifest of the whole CLI for agents |
| `unity list` | Editor-registered tools + parameter schemas |
| `unity command eval "return Application.version;"` | Roslyn-compiled C# evaluated live in the running Editor, main thread, **no recompile or domain reload**; `--json`; `eval_file <path>`; security-token gated |
| `unity command --runtime <playerExecName>` | targets a dev Player build (localhost-only, off by default, dev/QA only — never production): live logs, runtime status, hot-reload in a playing build |
| `unity status` | live state of connected Editors: port, project path, version, PID |
| `unity mcp` / `unity mcp configure <client>` | built-in MCP server (stdio); writes configs for 16 clients incl. Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code; `--server issue-tracker` variant — see §17 |
| `unity job` / `unity job wait` | detached jobs |
| `unity skill show\|install <agent>` | ships an agent skill |
| `unity pipeline cloud-build` / `unity pipeline automation` | read-only views of Unity Build Automation (§16) |

**Diagnostics, config, lifecycle**: `doctor`; `diagnose accelerator\|proxy`; `logs`; `env`; `context save\|use\|list\|current\|delete`; `config get\|set\|list\|unset\|resolve` (+ `config accelerator`); `analytics`; `cache key\|clean`; `bug`; `language`; `completion bash\|zsh\|fish\|PowerShell`; `shell`; `changelog`; `docs [--url\|--manual\|--search]` (opens docs matched to the project's Unity version); `plugin`; `self-update`; `self-uninstall`; `version (version/channel/commit/platform/arch/runtime)`; `help`.

**Automation contract** (what makes the CLI scriptable) **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Use](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24):

- *Output formats*: `human` (interactive), `tsv` (automatic when piped), `json` (`--format json` / `--json`; envelope `{success, command, data, errors, warnings}` — branch on `errors[0].code`, e.g. `INVALID_COMMAND_ARGS`), `ndjson` (streamed progress frames + result frame), `github` (GitHub Actions `::error::` annotations). Errors → stderr; data → stdout.
- *Exit codes*: 0 success; 1 general error; 2 usage error; 3 auth failure (e.g. unsigned-in `projects create`); 4 configuration required; 6 primary operation failed (install failed, Editor error, **test run didn't finish — retryable**); 7 Unity service unreachable / no Editor responds (**retryable**); 8 `unity test` only — tests ran and failed (**never retry**); 130 SIGINT; 143 SIGTERM.
- *Environment variables*: `UNITY_FORMAT` (alias `HUB_FORMAT`), `UNITY_NON_INTERACTIVE`, `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH`, `UNITY_CLOUD_ORG` / `UNITY_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `UNITY_BUILD_TIMEOUT`, `UNITY_NO_CLOUD`, `UNITY_ACCELERATOR` (host:port, default port **10080**), `UNITY_CLI_HOME`, `UNITY_PEER_AUTH_MODE` (peer code-signature verification; enforce default on macOS/Windows), `UNITY_NO_AUTH_BROKER`, `UNITY_PAGER` / `UNITY_NO_PAGER`, and CI service-account credentials `UNITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` + `UNITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET` (same service-account type as other Unity services).
- *Per-project defaults*: `ProjectSettings/UnityCliConfig.json` declares `unity build`/`unity test` defaults (target, output, profile, timeout, test mode, report format, coverage); `unity config resolve <key>` prints the effective value plus the source layer.
- *Logs*: `cli-log.json` in the Hub logs directory (Windows: `%UserProfile%\AppData\Roaming\UnityHub\logs`).

### 15.3 What it covers — and what it does not (vs batch mode §16)

The `unity build` / `unity run` verbs wrap the Editor's own batch mode (the `-batchmode` flag set fully specified in §16); the CLI adds installation, identity, structured output, and an exit-code contract on top. Coverage matrix:

| Capability | Unity CLI | Editor batch mode (§16) |
|---|---|---|
| Editor/module install & version management | yes (`install`, `editors`, `modules`) | no — manual or scripted downloads |
| Licensing | yes (`auth`, `license`; service accounts; floating-server status) | yes (`-serial`/`-username`/`-password`, `.ulf` flow, `-returnlicense`) |
| Project creation / cloning | yes (`projects create --no-cloud`, `templates`) | partial (`-createProject`, `-cloneFromTemplate`) |
| Builds | wraps batch mode; Build Profile creation (`--create-profile`, 6000.0+); Android signing flags | full control — `BuildScript.cs`, `BuildPlayerOptions` per target, `BuildReport` telemetry, custom `EditorApplication.Exit` codes |
| Tests | `unity test` (NUnit report, `--affected`, `watch`) | `-runTests -testPlatform ... -testResults` flag set |
| Machine output / exit codes | JSON/TSV/NDJSON/GitHub + documented 10-code contract | log parsing; `EditorApplication.Exit(int)` |
| Driving a *running* Editor / Player | yes (`command`, `eval`, `status`, `--runtime`) | no |
| VCS helper (UnityYAMLMerge, conflict resolution) | yes (`vcs` suite) | no (manual mergespecfile.txt wiring) |
| MCP server hosting | yes (`unity mcp`, §17) | no (the old in-Editor server in `com.unity.ai.assistant` is deprecated, replaced by `unity mcp` — [docs](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/replace-mcp-server-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24) |

**Gaps we must design around:**

1. **No package add/remove verb.** The verified command surface has no `unity package` verb. Package mutation is done by editing `Packages/manifest.json` (version-controlled; the §4 package table is its source of truth) followed by `unity recompile --strict`, or interactively inside the Editor. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: whether `unity command eval` can drive `UnityEditor.PackageManager` Client.Add-style APIs for one-off package adds without opening the Editor; the eval path exists but the PackageManager eval snippet is untested. -->
2. **UPM CLI is a different product.** The Unity Package Manager CLI (new in Unity 6.6) only packs/signs UPM tarballs (`.tgz`) and `.unitypackage` signatures outside the Editor, authenticating via a Unity org service account **[DOCUMENTED]** ([What's New 6.6](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/WhatsNewUnity66.html), [UPM CLI docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/upm-cli.html), accessed 2026-09-24). It is irrelevant to our inner loop (we consume packages, we don't publish any) and must not be conflated with the Unity CLI. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: UPM CLI install command (likely a .NET tool — the upm-cli-install page was not fetched). -->
3. **Connected-Editor commands need the Pipeline package + Unity 6.0 LTS+**; pure `unity build`/`unity test` appear batch-mode-based, but the docs do not state it per-command. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: confirm with `unity build --help` / `unity test --help` on 6000.6 whether the Pipeline package is required for build/test or only for `unity command`/`eval`/`status`. -->
4. **`unity open --wait` is not on Windows yet** — our primary dev host is Windows, so scripts cannot block on open; §15.5 works around it.
5. **`eval` is security-token gated and `--runtime` Player targeting is localhost-only, off by default, dev/QA only** — never enable it in production or release players (DevSecOps; expanded in §17's MCP security analysis).
