6. **No asset-pipeline coverage** — Blender batch generation/export stays in §16; no CLI verb touches DCC tools.
7. **No cloud build execution** — Unity Build Automation is driven from its own console (§16); the CLI only surfaces read-only `pipeline cloud-build` / `pipeline automation` views.

**Disambiguation table** (2026-09 state) **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Hub CLI overview](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/hub/cli-overview), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Name | Kind | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Unity CLI (`unity` binary) | official standalone: editors, modules, projects, builds, tests, licensing, VCS, MCP, eval | experimental, free, 1.0.0-beta.11 (2026-09-22) — recommended path |
| Unity Hub CLI (`"Unity Hub.exe" -- --headless`) | official CLI inside the Hub desktop app | deprecated, minimal support since Hub 3.18.0 |
| UPM CLI | official package pack/sign tool | new in 6.6; separate product |
| Editor command line (`Unity.exe -batchmode ...`) | official Editor invocation flags | long-standing; `unity run`/`unity build` wrap this (§16) |
| `com.unity.pipeline` | official experimental package: CLI ↔ Editor/Player command channel + eval | requires Unity 6.0 LTS+ |
| `unity mcp` | official MCP server inside the Unity CLI | current; replaces the deprecated `com.unity.ai.assistant` MCP server |

### 15.4 Where the CLI fits our pipeline

#### 15.4.1 Version pinning policy

Editor line choice is set in §4; the CLI is the enforcement mechanism. Facts that shape the pin: Unity 6.6 (6000.6) shipped 6000.6.0f1 on 2026-08-31 **[DOCUMENTED]** ([release notes](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), accessed 2026-09-24); latest patch 6000.6.2f1 on 2026-09-18 ([eosl.date cross-check](https://eosl.date/eol/product/unity/), accessed 2026-09-24 — tertiary). Unity staff guidance on the 6.6 announcement thread: "Use Unity 6.3 LTS version for projects that are in production or about to ship. Use Unity 6.6 Supported Update for New Projects." ([Unity Discussions, Sep 1, 2026](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-6-6-is-now-available/1735357), accessed 2026-09-24). **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** the sweep framed "6.7 is the next LTS" as single-source; verification found it multi-source (the 6000.6.0f1 release notes' "after Unity 6.7 LTS" wording and the CoreCLR article's "Unity 6.7LTS Alpha" naming), so the migration expectation is firm even though only the Sep 1 post says "final supported release of the Unity 6 family" verbatim.

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** Pin policy: (1) the repo pins `6000.6.2f1` in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` (the file of record — GameCI reads it too, §16); (2) the bootstrap script installs exactly that version, never an alias; (3) patch bumps (`6000.6.x`) are a reviewed PR that changes one line and re-runs `unity test`; (4) the 6.7 LTS migration is scheduled after 6.7 GA with 6.3 LTS (supported until December 2027, [support page](https://unity.com/releases/unity-6/support), accessed 2026-09-24) as the emergency rollback target — see §21.

#### 15.4.2 Editor + module bootstrap (worked example)

Our v1 platform order is Windows+macOS (Steam) → Android → iOS → Xbox (§2/§18/§19). The Windows dev host needs the Android module now; macOS and iOS builds require a macOS Editor host because IL2CPP macOS players must be built on macOS (cross-compilation "generally not supported"; [Unity 6.3 IL2CPP introduction](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — that host is provisioned later as a CI runner (§16).

```bash
# Windows dev host — unattended install, documented form:
unity install 6000.6.2f1 -m android --accept-eula --yes
unity editors default 6000.6.2f1     # pin the default Editor
unity editors -i                     # verify: lists installed Editors
# macOS host (later, for macOS/iOS targets):
unity install 6000.6.2f1 -m android ios --accept-eula --yes
```

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact module token names beyond `android`/`ios`/`webgl` (e.g., mac-il2cpp / windows-il2cpp spellings) were not captured in research; enumerate with `unity modules list 6000.6.2f1` before scripting them. -->

#### 15.4.3 Project creation and package operations

```bash
# Local-first creation (cloud is the DEFAULT; without --no-cloud this exits 3 unsigned-in):
unity projects create AoBClone --no-cloud
# or from a template (URP per §4):
unity templates list
```

Package changes are manifest-driven (§4 owns the package table). One verified correction applies to the manifest contents: **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** the sweep said "new Unity 6 projects default to the Input System package"; verification established that from Unity 6.6 the `com.unity.inputsystem` package **no longer exists in new projects** — Input System ships as a built-in module, and code should gate on the `ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` define rather than package presence ([Planned breaking changes in Unity 6.7, staff post Jun 16, 2026](https://discussions.unity.com/t/planned-breaking-changes-in-unity-6-7/1723293); [Input System package docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest), accessed 2026-09-24). So our 6.6 manifest simply omits it, and `unity recompile --strict` is the post-edit verification:

```bash
$EDITOR Packages/manifest.json   # add/remove pinned packages (§4 table)
unity recompile --strict          # exit 6 on compile errors, exit 7 if no Editor — CI-safe
```

#### 15.4.4 Build invocation (Win64 + Android)

Build Profiles (Unity 6 replacement for Build Settings; per-platform profiles are version-controllable assets — §4) are first-class in the CLI **[DOCUMENTED]**: `--create-profile <target>` requires Unity 6000.0+, and `unity build` accepts Android signing flags ([reference](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference), accessed 2026-09-24).

```bash
unity build --list-targets                 # enumerate buildable targets for this Editor
unity build --list-profiles                # enumerate the project's Build Profile assets
unity build --create-profile win64         # scaffold the Windows profile asset (commit it)
unity build --create-profile android       # scaffold the Android profile asset (commit it)
unity build                                # uses ProjectSettings/UnityCliConfig.json defaults
```

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact `unity build` flag spellings for target/profile/output selection on the command line (e.g. `--target win64`, `--profile <name>`, `--output <path>`); the three flags above are the documented ones, the per-run overrides were not fully captured — confirm with `unity build --help` on 6000.6. -->

Per-project defaults keep the CI invocation argument-free **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (keys per docs; exact spellings to confirm):

```jsonc
// ProjectSettings/UnityCliConfig.json — committed; single source for CI build/test defaults.
<!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact key names against `unity config list` output (fields documented: target, output, profile, timeout, test mode, report format, coverage). -->
{
  "build": { "profile": "windows-steam", "output": "Builds/Win64", "timeout": 3600 },
  "test":  { "mode": "editmode", "reportFormat": "nunit", "coverage": false }
}
```

Android signing secrets never appear on the command line — keystore paths/passwords ride in CI secrets and the runner environment (DevSecOps rule from §16; the CLI's own pattern of env-var credentials over args matches). macOS/iOS builds run on the macOS host (§15.4.2); Xbox waits on ID@Xbox access (§19).

#### 15.4.5 Test invocation and the dev loop

`unity test` runs Edit + Play modes through the Editor test runner with NUnit reports; `--affected` narrows to tests impacted by pending changes; `unity watch test` re-runs affected tests on save ([Use docs](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). The §14 test strategy maps: editmode suites (physics rules, scoring math, save round-trip) run via `unity test` in CI; playmode loop-integration tests run nightly; determinism replay tests run on the Windows host only (same-device determinism per §6). Exit-code discipline: 6/7 are retryable infrastructure failures; **8 means tests executed and failed — never retry** ([automation contract](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact mode-selection flag for `unity test` (editmode vs playmode on the command line vs UnityCliConfig.json only) — confirm via `unity test --help`. -->

#### 15.4.6 Driving a running Editor: custom [CliCommand]s and eval

With `unity pipeline install` (adds `com.unity.pipeline`; requires Unity 6.0 LTS+), any static method in namespace `Unity.Pipeline.Commands` decorated with `[CliCommand("name", "description")]` and `[CliArg]` parameters is auto-discovered — no registration code ([Meet the Unity CLI](https://unity.com/blog/meet-the-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). We expose our validation entry points this way so both Claude (via §17) and CI (via `unity run --command`) invoke the same code:

```csharp
using System.Text;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Unity.Pipeline.Commands
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Project-authored CLI commands, auto-discovered by com.unity.pipeline.
    /// Invoked headless via `unity run --command aob.validate-content --log-file ...`
    /// or interactively via `unity command aob.validate-content --result-only`.
    /// Validation rules are specified in §5 (content model) and §8 (behaviours).
    /// </summary>
    public static class AobCliCommands
    {
        #region Constants

        private const string LevelRoot = "Assets/_Project/ScriptableObjects/Levels";
        private const int MaxQueueMassBudget = 120;

        #endregion

        #region Public Methods

        /// <summary>
        /// Validates every LevelDefinition asset: queue mass budget vs platform
        /// stability heuristic, star-threshold monotonicity, and piece-queue
        /// references (rules per §5). Fails the command on any violation.
        /// </summary>
        [CliCommand("aob.validate-content",
            "Validates all LevelDefinition assets against mass-budget and star-threshold rules.")]
        public static bool ValidateContent(
            [CliArg("strict", "Treat warnings as failures.")] bool strict = false,
            [CliArg("world", "Restrict validation to one world id.")] int world = -1)
        {
            StringBuilder report = new StringBuilder(capacity: 4096);
            int violations = CountLevelViolations(report, strict, world);
            Debug.Log(report.ToString());
            return violations == 0;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Regenerates the Addressables content groups after bulk level edits (§5).
        /// </summary>
        [CliCommand("aob.rebuild-content-groups", "Rebuilds Addressables groups for worlds/modes.")]
        public static void RebuildContentGroups()
        {
            // …
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private static int CountLevelViolations(StringBuilder report, bool strict, int world)
        {
            // … walks LevelDefinition assets under LevelRoot, applies §5 rules
            return 0;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: return-value serialization for [CliCommand] methods (bool vs void vs string) and the exact [CliArg] property set beyond name/description/Required — the attributes' existence and auto-discovery are documented; the result marshalling details are not. -->

Live inspection without a recompile: `unity command eval "return Application.version;"` (Roslyn, main thread, token-gated, `--json` for structured output) and `unity status` for the connected Editor's port/path/version/PID. Dev-player debugging uses `unity command --runtime <playerExecName>` — localhost-only and disabled by default; we enable it only on QA machines, never in shipped builds.

#### 15.4.7 Licensing and secrets (DevSecOps lens)

| Context | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Dev workstation (this repo) | `unity auth login` once; `unity license activate` for the Personal/Pro seat; credentials in the OS keyring, broker-sealed token store |
| CI (GitHub Actions, §16) | `UNITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` + `UNITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET` env vars — never CLI arguments; branch on exit 3 (auth) to fail fast with a clear message |
| Floating / offline | `unity license` floating + offline file/request flows; Licensing Server details in §16 |
| Cloud-project creation | `--no-cloud` / `UNITY_NO_CLOUD` unless the Unity Cloud link is intentionally wanted (service accounts cannot create cloud projects) |

Secret hygiene follows §14/§16: no credential ever appears in a command line (process-list visible) or in a log; the CLI's `github` output format maps errors to `::error::` annotations without echoing secrets.

### 15.5 The bootstrap script (clean clone → editor-ready)

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** `tools/bootstrap.sh` — the single entry point a fresh machine (or a wiped CI runner) runs after `git clone`. Bash throughout (Git Bash on the Windows dev host, bash on Linux/macOS runners). It encodes: CLI presence + pin, Editor install from `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`, deterministic config, YAML-merge setup, first import, strict recompile, smoke test, and the documented exit-code retry contract.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tools/bootstrap.sh — clean clone -> editor-ready (AoB Unity clone).
# Docs basis: https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli (accessed 2026-09-24).
# Disk: ~25 GB free for one Editor + Android module + Library.
set -euo pipefail

# ---------- 0. Deterministic environment ------------------------------------
export UNITY_NON_INTERACTIVE=1
export UNITY_NO_CLOUD=1                       # local-first; no cloud project churn
export UNITY_ACCELERATOR="${UNITY_ACCELERATOR:-}"  # set host:port (default port 10080) if you run one
readonly ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly UNITY_CLI_PIN="1.0.0-beta.11"        # CLI version this script is tested against

# ---------- 1. Unity CLI present and pinned ----------------------------------
if ! command -v unity >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux*|Darwin) curl -fsSL https://unity.com/install.sh | bash ;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
      powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "irm https://unity.com/install.ps1 | iex" ;;
  esac
  hash -r   # re-resolve PATH in Git Bash
fi
# `unity version` reports version/channel/commit/platform/arch/runtime; abort on drift.
unity version | grep -q "${UNITY_CLI_PIN}" || { echo "Unity CLI != ${UNITY_CLI_PIN}; run: unity self-update"; exit 4; }

unity config update-check off                 # no update prompts mid-script

# ---------- 2. Editor install pinned by the repo ------------------------------
EDITOR_VERSION="$(awk -F': ' '/m_EditorVersion:/ {print $2}' "${ROOT}/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt")"
: "${EDITOR_VERSION:?ProjectVersion.txt missing m_EditorVersion — clone corrupt}"
unity install "${EDITOR_VERSION}" -m android --accept-eula --yes
unity editors default "${EDITOR_VERSION}"

# ---------- 3. VCS merge hygiene (UnityYAMLMerge as the merge driver) ---------
unity vcs merge-setup --non-interactive || unity vcs doctor --fix || true   # advisory, not fatal

# ---------- 4. First import + compile gate ------------------------------------
# `unity open --wait` is not available on Windows yet (docs), so open detached
# and poll `unity status` until the project reports a connected Editor.
unity open "${ROOT}"
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do                    # up to ~10 min for first Library import
  unity status >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 5
done
run_cli unity recompile --strict             # exit 6 = compile errors (fatal here)

# ---------- 5. Smoke test (editmode via UnityCliConfig.json defaults) ----------
run_cli unity test                            # exit 8 = tests failed -> never retry

# ---------- 6. Ready ----------------------------------------------------------
echo "Editor ${EDITOR_VERSION} ready. Open with: unity ${ROOT}"

# ---------- helper: exit-code contract wrapper --------------------------------
# 0 ok | 1 general | 2 usage | 3 auth | 4 config | 6/7 retryable | 8 tests failed
run_cli() {
  local attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    "$@" && return 0
    local rc=$?
    case "${rc}" in
      6|7) echo "retryable CLI failure (rc=${rc}), attempt ${attempt}/3" >&2; sleep $((attempt * 10)) ;;
      *)   return "${rc}" ;;
    esac
  done
  return 1
}
```

Notes: the `run_cli` retry wrapper encodes the documented contract (6/7 retryable, 8 never retried, 3 auth and 4 config fail fast) **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Use docs](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24); the `unity status` polling loop and the CLI-version pin gate are our design **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** because `--wait` is Windows-absent. CI runners cache `Library/` between runs (§16) so step 4 collapses to a no-op import check. Task breakdown for wiring this lives in §20 (P0 bootstrap tasks).

### 15.6 Tool selection: Unity CLI vs Hub CLI vs batch mode vs GameCI vs UBA

| Tool | What it is | Status (2026-09-24) | Use it for | Skip it when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Unity CLI** | official standalone `unity` binary | experimental 1.0.0-beta.11, free; recommended by Unity | everything in §15.1–15.5: installs, pinning, builds, tests, licensing, VCS helpers, connected-Editor commands, `unity mcp` (§17) | a surface you need is still batch-mode-only (custom `BuildScript.cs` logic beyond profile defaults — §16); or a runner where the beta churn is unacceptable without the wrapper |
| **Hub CLI** (`-- --headless`) | CLI inside the Hub desktop app | deprecated, minimal support since Hub 3.18.0 ([overview](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/hub/cli-overview), accessed 2026-09-24) | nothing in this project — legacy scripts only | always (migrate per table below) |
| **Editor batch mode** (`Unity.exe -batchmode ...`, §16) | direct Editor invocation flags | long-standing, stable | custom `BuildScript.cs` builds with `BuildReport` telemetry + custom exit codes; `-runTests` with full flag control; anything needing exact `-executeMethod` semantics | when you want installs/licensing/structured output — use the CLI wrapper instead |
| **GameCI** (`game-ci/unity-builder` / `unity-test-runner`, §16) | community GitHub Actions + `unityci/editor` Docker images | builder v6.0.0 (2026-09-10; docs still show @v4), test-runner v4.3.2 (2026-09-09), both now wrap `game-ci/cli` ([repos](https://github.com/game-ci/unity-builder), accessed 2026-09-24) | turnkey GitHub Actions matrices with license-secret handling and `Library/` caching conventions; Linux-container reproducibility | Windows/macOS-hosted steps (macOS IL2CPP needs a real mac anyway); when you'd rather own the YAML over the actions' abstraction |
| **Unity Build Automation (UBA)** | Unity-hosted cloud CI ([docs](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/build-automation), accessed 2026-09-24) | current; supports LTS + latest Unity 6 update only | zero-infra auto-build on VCS change; Xbox/PS5 cloud targets later; Slack/Discord/Jira notifications | while we're on 6000.6 (a Supported Update, not LTS — support policy mismatch); when build-minute costs or NDA-scoped console SDKs matter (§19) |

**Hub CLI → Unity CLI migration map** (for any legacy script we inherit) **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Hub CLI overview](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/hub/cli-overview), accessed 2026-09-24): `"Unity Hub.exe" -- --headless <cmd>` → `unity <cmd>`; `install -v <version>` → positional `unity install <version>`; `install-modules --version/-v` → `-e/--editor-version`; `editors --add <path>` → `editors add <path...>`. Removed with no equivalent: `--headless`, `--errors`, `--silent`, `--logLevel/-l`, `--bugReporter`, `--debugMode`, `--inspect`, `--userEmail`, `--theme`, `--editorLicense`, `--servicesUrlInterval`, `--cloudEnvironment`. Piped output is TSV by default and errors now go to stderr.

**Community tools (unofficial, evaluated, not adopted)** **[DOCUMENTED]** (GitHub metadata via gh api, 2026-09-24): [DragonBox/u3d](https://github.com/DragonBox/u3d) (Ruby install/build CLI, ★363, last push 2026-03-27 — the long-standing pre-official option); [hatayama/unity-cli-loop](https://github.com/hatayama/unity-cli-loop) (★569, "Let AI Drive Unity, from Editor to Play Mode", active); [youngwoocho02/unity-cli](https://github.com/youngwoocho02/unity-cli) (★313, single-binary Editor control, "No MCP, no Python"); [akiojin/unity-cli](https://github.com/akiojin/unity-cli) (★104, Rust over Unity TCP); [nuskey8/UnityAgentClient](https://github.com/nuskey8/UnityAgentClient) (★277, Agent Client Protocol for Gemini CLI/Claude Code/Codex); version managers [Larusso/unity-version-manager](https://github.com/Larusso/unity-version-manager) (★43) and [educup/uvm](https://github.com/educup/uvm) (★5). All are superseded for us by the official CLI's install/editors verbs plus §17's MCP layer; they remain §21 watch-items only if official coverage regresses.

**Decision rules for this project** **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: interactive dev-machine ops and CI entry points use the Unity CLI (via `tools/bootstrap.sh` and the `run_cli` wrapper); build logic that must inspect `BuildReport`, run per-target `BuildPlayerOptions`, or post-process artifacts stays in `BuildScript.cs` invoked through §16 batch mode (with `unity run --command` promoted once our `[CliCommand]` set covers it); GitHub Actions hosting starts GameCI-style with license secrets per §16; UBA is deferred until we're on an LTS line and only revisited if console cloud targets justify it (§19); the Hub CLI is banned outright.

## 16. Unity & Blender Automation — Traditional CLI

This section is the reproducible spine of the project's automation: Unity Editor batch mode for builds and tests, GameCI for hosted CI, and Blender background mode for parametric asset generation, batch export, and headless thumbnail rendering. It is deliberately split from the interactive lanes — the new standalone Unity CLI (§15) and the MCP servers (§17). The division of labor is fixed: anything that must produce a deterministic artifact from a clean checkout lives here; anything that needs an agent in the loop lives in §17. External facts carry inline sources (access date 2026-09-24); items designed because the original's internals are unknown are flagged **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; uncertain API surfaces carry `<!-- TODO-VERIFY -->`.

Two verify-pass corrections are load-bearing here. First, Unity 6.6 (6000.6) is the final Supported/Update release of the Unity 6 family, with 6.7 as the next LTS — multi-source confirmed ([Unity 6.6 announcement](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-6-6-is-now-available/1735357); [6000.6.0f1 release notes](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), accessed 2026-09-24) — which elevates editor-version pinning (§16.12) to a first-class concern. Second, the project's editor pin is 6000.6.2f1 (latest 6.6 patch as of 2026-09-24 per the research digest), and every flag below was verified against the current Unity 6.6 CLI reference.

### 16.1 Unity Editor command-line reference (Unity 6.6)

#### 16.1.1 Documentation state (read before linking anything)

The Unity Manual was restructured during the Unity 6.x era: the old single page `Manual/CommandLineArguments.html` is now a "Command-line interface" landing page, and the full reference lives at "Unity Editor command line arguments reference", still reachable via the legacy anchor `EditorCommandLineArguments.html` **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Unity Editor command line arguments reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/EditorCommandLineArguments.html), accessed 2026-09-24). The packages doc tree also moved — every `docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.4`–`1.6` URL now 404s. Consequence: any URL this plan persists (runbooks, CI annotations) uses the versioned form `/6000.6/Documentation/...`; unversioned `/Manual/` and `/Packages/@x.y` URLs are actively moving targets.

#### 16.1.2 The flag set we actually use

All flags in this subsection are **[DOCUMENTED]** against the CLI reference above unless a row says otherwise.

Batch-mode core:

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-batchmode` | "Always run Unity in batch mode when using command line arguments" | Every CI invocation |
| `-nographics` | No GPU initialization; Enlighten GI baking impossible | Builds, editmode tests, mesh/prefab export steps. Never where a GPU is required (§16.5) |
| `-quit` | Quit after `-executeMethod` returns; documented to kill `-runTests` runs early and to hang on in-flight async code | Build invocations only; never combined with `-runTests` |
| `-quitTimeout <sec>` | Timeout for pending async tasks at quit (default 300 s) | Raised when post-build steps are async |
| `-projectPath <path>` | Project to open | Always; quote paths containing spaces |
| `-executeMethod <Class.Method\|Ns.Class.Method>` | "Execute the static method as soon as Unity opens the project… You can use this for tasks such as continuous integration, performing Unit Tests, making builds or preparing data." | Entry into `BuildScript` (§16.2) |
| `-logFile <path\|->` | Log destination; `-` writes to stdout | `-` on CI for inline annotations; file when archiving logs as artifacts |
| `-upmLogFile <path>` | Separate Package Manager log | Archived on package-resolution failures |
| `-timestamps` | Timestamps in log lines | Always — log forensics |
| `-accept-apiupdate` | Run the API updater in batch mode | Mandatory on editor version-bump builds |
| `-rebuildLibrary` | Force Library rebuild | Cache-corruption recovery only; never in the normal path |
| `-disable-assembly-updater <asm...>` | Skip assembly update for listed assemblies | Escape hatch only |
| `-silent-crashes` | Suppress crash dialogs | Always on headless CI |
| `-version` | Print editor version | Runner smoke test |

Build:

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-buildTarget <name>` | Platform for import/activation; documented names include `android, ios, linux64, osxuniversal, win64` (plus closed-platform names) | Must match the C# `BuildPlayerOptions.target` so imports and texture compression match the target; passed on every build |
| `-activeBuildProfile <path>` | Activate a Unity 6 Build Profile asset; its scripting defines apply **before compilation and thus before `-executeMethod`** | Per-target define sets (§4) — cleaner than mutating defines inside the build method (which does not work; see §16.1.3) |
| `-build <pathName>` | Build directly from `-activeBuildProfile` with no `-executeMethod` at all; extension must match the platform | Fallback lane for compile-broken branches; no telemetry, so not the primary path |
| `-buildWindows64Player <path.exe>`, `-buildOSXUniversalPlayer <path.app>`, `-buildLinux64Player <path>` | One-shot player builds | Documented alternative to BuildScript; we keep BuildScript for `BuildReport` telemetry and exit codes |
| `-standaloneBuildSubtarget Player\|Server` | Standalone subtarget | `Player` always (no dedicated-server lane in v1) |
| `-releaseCodeOptimization` / `-debugCodeOptimization` | Code-optimization preset for the run | `-releaseCodeOptimization` on release builds |
| `-setDefaultPlatformTextureFormat dxt\|atc\|etc\|etc2\|astc` | Android default texture compression | `astc` pre-pass lane validating Android imports (ties into §9/§14) |
| `-overrideMaxTextureSize <px>`, `-overrideTextureCompression <mode>` | Texture import overrides | Available; unused by default |

Tests:

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-runTests` | Start a Test Framework run | Editmode and playmode jobs (§16.3) |
| `-testPlatform EditMode\|PlayMode` | Which suite runs | One job per platform |
| `-testResults <path>` | NUnit3-format XML results | Always; CI treats the XML, not the process code, as the source of truth |
| `-testFilter <regex>`, `-testCategory <cat>` | Suite filtering | `smoke` category for the PR fast path (§14) |
| `-runSynchronously`, `-automated` | Synchronous, automation-oriented execution | Always on CI |
| `-enableCodeCoverage -coverageOptions <opts>` | Coverage API + semicolon-separated options (`generateHtmlReport;generateBadgeReport;generateAdditionalMetrics;assemblyFilters:+Ns.*`) | Weekly job only — documented crash risk on Unity 6 (§16.3) |

Licensing:

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-serial <key>` `-username <email>` `-password <pwd>` | Activate a serial license | One-time per runner; values supplied via environment-variable indirection, never literal in scripts (§16.4) |
| `-createManualActivationFile` | Manual flow step 1 of 3: writes a `.alf` | Personal-license onboarding only |
| `-manualLicenseFile <file>` | Manual flow step 3: consume `.ulf` (serial) or `.xml` (seat) | Preferred CI flow — the file is materialized from a secret, so no credential ever appears on a command line |
| `-returnlicense` | Return a serial/named-user license; explicitly not for floating licenses | Runner decommissioning |

Caching / GPU (self-hosted fleet only):

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-EnableCacheServer` + `-cacheServerEndpoint <host:port>` (and `-cacheServerWaitForConnection <ms>`) | Unity Accelerator client flags | Import caching across the self-hosted fleet, beyond the `Library/` CI cache |
| `-force-d3d11` / `-force-d3d12` / `-force-metal` / `-force-clamped` | Force a graphics API | Only on the GPU-equipped interactive worker (§17); never on build runners |

Notably absent from the current 6.6 reference: `-forgetProjectPath`, which older manuals documented (clearing the recently-opened list). It may still be accepted by the binary, but it is undocumented in 2026 docs — do not build tooling on it **[DOCUMENTED]** (same source).

#### 16.1.3 Invocation grammar and ordering rules

1. `-buildTarget` must equal the target later passed in C# (`BuildPlayerOptions.target`); passing it makes imports, texture compression, and platform activation consistent with the build.
2. Never combine `-quit` with `-runTests` — "then `-quit` causes the Editor to quit immediately, before in-progress tests have chance to complete" **[DOCUMENTED]** (CLI reference, accessed 2026-09-24). Test runs exit on their own.
3. Scripting-define changes (`PlayerSettings.SetDefineSymbolsForGroup`) only take effect after a domain reload, so symbol edits immediately before `BuildPlayer` do not apply; per-target defines come from `-activeBuildProfile`, which is applied before compilation **[DOCUMENTED]** ([BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer.html), accessed 2026-09-24).
4. `-executeMethod` methods live in an Editor assembly — ours is `ArtOfBalance.EditorTools` in the §4 asmdef plan — and must be static.
5. Quote paths with spaces; `-logFile -` is the stdout form.

#### 16.1.4 Canonical invocations

Release build, Windows host (pattern per current docs; the editor pin and profile names are ours **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**) **[DOCUMENTED]** for the flag surface (CLI reference, accessed 2026-09-24):

```bash
"C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.6.2f1\Editor\Unity.exe" \
  -batchmode -nographics -quit \
  -projectPath "D:\src\art-of-balance" \
  -executeMethod ArtOfBalance.EditorTools.Editor.Build.BuildScript.BuildWindows64 \
  -buildTarget win64 \
  -activeBuildProfile "Assets/Settings/Build Profiles/AoB-Windows64.asset" \
  -releaseCodeOptimization \
  -logFile -
```

Android pass: identical shape with `-buildTarget android` and `…BuildScript.BuildAndroid`. Editor version-bump pass adds `-accept-apiupdate`.

One-time serial activation per runner (credential values arrive via environment variables — §16.4):

```bash
"$UNITY_EXE" -batchmode -quit \
  -username "$UNITY_EMAIL" -password "$UNITY_PASSWORD" -serial "$UNITY_SERIAL" \
  -logFile activate.log
```

Editmode test run (no `-quit`):

```bash
"$UNITY_EXE" -batchmode -nographics -projectPath "$PROJECT_PATH" \
  -runTests -testPlatform EditMode \
  -testResults "$RESULTS_DIR/results-editmode.xml" \
  -runSynchronously -automated \
  -logFile "$LOGS_DIR/test-editmode.log"
```

### 16.2 The canonical `BuildScript.cs`

The build entry point is a static class in the `ArtOfBalance.EditorTools` Editor assembly (asmdef per §4). It exists for three reasons the pure-CLI flags cannot cover: `BuildReport` telemetry, a typed exit-code contract, and version stamping from environment variables. The API surface it uses is fully documented: `BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer(BuildPlayerOptions)` is the recommended overload ("Builds a player… Use this function to programatically create a build"); `BuildPlayer(BuildPlayerWithProfileOptions)` is the Build Profiles path in namespace `UnityEditor.Build.Profile`; the legacy 4-argument overload is "still supported, but will be replaced" **[DOCUMENTED]** ([BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer.html), [BuildPlayerOptions](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuildPlayerOptions.html), accessed 2026-09-24). `BuildPlayerOptions` has exactly six properties: `scenes`, `locationPathName`, `target`, `targetGroup`, `subtarget`, `options`.

The plan's six build targets — Windows 64, macOS universal, Linux 64 (SteamOS-native lane for Deck verification flexibility; the primary Deck path is Proton over the Windows build, see §19), Android, iOS, and Xbox (last, gated on ID@Xbox per §2) — each get one entry method **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**. `BuildTarget` enum names used below are the documented set: `StandaloneWindows64, StandaloneLinux64, StandaloneOSX, Android, iOS, XboxOne` **[DOCUMENTED]** (BuildPipeline page, accessed 2026-09-24); the Xbox Series X|S build-target name and module workflow are NDA-gated and flagged below.

```csharp
using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEditor.Build.Reporting;
using UnityEngine;

namespace ArtOfBalance.EditorTools.Editor.Build
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Canonical CI build entry point. Invoked via
    /// Unity -batchmode -executeMethod ArtOfBalance.EditorTools.Editor.Build.BuildScript.Build&lt;Target&gt;.
    /// Reads all configuration from environment variables (never CLI arguments) so no
    /// build metadata or secret appears in process listings. Exit codes:
    /// 0 ok, 1 build failed, 2 tests failed, 3 licensing failed, 4 environment invalid.
    /// </summary>
    public static class BuildScript
    {
        #region Constants

        private const int ExitOk = 0;
        private const int ExitBuildFailed = 1;
        private const int ExitTestsFailed = 2;
        private const int ExitLicensingFailed = 3;
        private const int ExitEnvironmentInvalid = 4;

        private const string BuildRoot = "Builds";
        private const string GeneratedAssetsManifest = "Assets/_Project/Art/Generated/manifest.json";
        private const string SourceAssetSpecRoot = "Tools/Blender/specs";

        #endregion

        #region Public API — one entry point per build target

        /// <summary>Windows 64-bit standalone (Steam primary target, §19).</summary>
        public static void BuildWindows64() => BuildFor(BuildTarget.StandaloneWindows64,
            BuildTargetGroup.Standalone, StandaloneSubtarget.Player, $"{BuildRoot}/Win64/AoB.exe");

        /// <summary>macOS universal (Apple Silicon + x86_64; never Intel-only, see §19).</summary>
        public static void BuildMacOSUniversal() => BuildFor(BuildTarget.StandaloneOSX,
            BuildTargetGroup.Standalone, StandaloneSubtarget.Player, $"{BuildRoot}/macOS/AoB.app");

        /// <summary>Linux 64-bit standalone (SteamOS-native verification lane).</summary>
        public static void BuildLinux64() => BuildFor(BuildTarget.StandaloneLinux64,
            BuildTargetGroup.Standalone, StandaloneSubtarget.Player, $"{BuildRoot}/Linux64/AoB");

        /// <summary>Android AAB (Play submission form, §18).</summary>
        public static void BuildAndroid() => BuildFor(BuildTarget.Android,
            BuildTargetGroup.Android, 0, $"{BuildRoot}/Android/AoB.aab");

        /// <summary>iOS Xcode project folder; requires a macOS host (IL2CPP, §18).</summary>
        public static void BuildIOS() => BuildFor(BuildTarget.iOS,
            BuildTargetGroup.iOS, 0, $"{BuildRoot}/iOS/XcodeProject");

        /// <summary>Xbox (module-gated; verify enum and module against GDK docs, see TODO-VERIFY).</summary>
        public static void BuildXbox() => BuildFor(BuildTarget.XboxOne,
            BuildTargetGroup.XboxOne, 0, $"{BuildRoot}/Xbox/AoB");

        /// <summary>Builds every target valid for the current host OS and installed modules.</summary>
        public static void BuildAllHostTargets()
        {
            // Host dispatch mirrors the §16.6 CI matrix:
            // macOS runner -> macOS universal + iOS; any docker-capable runner -> Win64/Linux64/Android;
            // Windows runner with Xbox module -> Xbox (post ID@Xbox).
            // …
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private static void BuildFor(BuildTarget target, BuildTargetGroup group, int subtarget, string locationPathName)
        {
            if (!ValidateEnvironment())
            {
                EditorApplication.Exit(ExitEnvironmentInvalid);
                return;
            }

            ApplyVersionMetadata();

            var options = new BuildPlayerOptions
            {
                scenes = EditorBuildSettings.scenes.Select(s => s.path).ToArray(),
                locationPathName = locationPathName,
                target = target,
                targetGroup = group,
                subtarget = subtarget,
                options = BuildOptions.None,
            };

            BuildReport report = BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer(options);
            BuildSummary summary = report.summary;

            WriteBuildReport(target, summary);

            if (summary.result != BuildResult.Succeeded || summary.totalErrors > 0)
            {
                Debug.LogError($"[{nameof(BuildScript)}] Build FAILED for {target}: "
                    + $"{summary.totalErrors} error(s) in {summary.totalTime}.");
                EditorApplication.Exit(ExitBuildFailed);
                return;
            }

            Debug.Log($"[{nameof(BuildScript)}] Build OK: {target}, {summary.totalSize} bytes, "
                + $"started {summary.buildStartedAt}, ended {summary.buildEndedAt}, output {summary.outputPath}.");
            EditorApplication.Exit(ExitOk);
        }

        /// <summary>Stamps bundle version and numeric build codes from env vars (git-derived in CI, §16.6).</summary>
        private static void ApplyVersionMetadata()
        {
            string version = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AOB_VERSION");
            string buildNumber = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AOB_BUILD_NUMBER");
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(version) || string.IsNullOrEmpty(buildNumber))
            {
                return; // local build: keep Player Settings values
            }

            PlayerSettings.bundleVersion = version;
            if (int.TryParse(buildNumber, out int numeric) && numeric > 0)
            {
                PlayerSettings.Android.bundleVersionCode = numeric; // keep < 100000 (arch-split offset rule, §18)
                // iOS CFBundleVersion is stamped in the Xcode post-process step (§18).
            }
        }

        /// <summary>Guards the Blender-to-Unity contract: generated meshes must match the checked-in spec.</summary>
        private static bool ValidateEnvironment()
        {
            if (!File.Exists(GeneratedAssetsManifest))
            {
                Debug.LogError($"[{nameof(BuildScript)}] Missing generated-asset manifest at "
                    + $"{GeneratedAssetsManifest}. Run the Blender asset stage (§16.11) first.");
                return false;
            }
            // Compare manifest.sourceSpecHash against hash(SourceAssetSpecRoot/*.json); mismatch => false.
            // …
            return true;
        }

        /// <summary>Writes the documented BuildSummary fields to a JSON CI artifact.</summary>
        private static void WriteBuildReport(BuildTarget target, BuildSummary summary)
        {
            // Fields: result, totalSize, totalTime, totalErrors, totalWarnings,
            // outputPath, platform, platformGroup, options, buildStartedAt, buildEndedAt.
            // Serialized to Builds/report-{target}.json and uploaded as a CI artifact (§16.6).
            // …
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Skeleton conventions follow the unity-game-dev-expert standard: `#region` blocks, XML `<summary>` docs on every public member, `nameof()` in log strings, `const` for fixed values, no wasted allocations (this is an editor-time one-shot class, so hot-path rules are trivially satisfied). The structure and env-var contract are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; the `BuildReport`/`BuildSummary`/`EditorApplication.Exit` surfaces are **[DOCUMENTED]** ([BuildSummary](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Build.Reporting.BuildSummary.html), [EditorApplication.Exit](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/EditorApplication.Exit.html) — the latter: "This function is mostly useful for exiting out of a commandline process with a specific error", accessed 2026-09-24).

Documented gotchas applied by this design **[DOCUMENTED]** ([BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer.html), accessed 2026-09-24):

- Calling `BuildPlayer` invalidates editor-script variables that reference GameObjects — the build path never caches scene-object references.
- Scripting-define edits immediately before `BuildPlayer` do not apply (they need a domain reload); defines come from `-activeBuildProfile` on the command line instead (§16.1.3).
- Build hooks available to the pipeline: `IPreprocessBuildWithContext` (the generated-asset guard also runs here), `IProcessSceneWithReport`, `IPostprocessBuildWithContext`, `BuildPlayerProcessor`. §18's Xcode post-processing and §19's platform stitching hang off the same hooks.
- The success check is the canonical `summary.result == BuildResult.Succeeded` (`BuildResult`: Succeeded/Failed/Cancelled/Unknown).

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: Xbox Series X|S build-target enum name and Unity 6.6 Xbox-module build-from-CLI specifics are NDA-gated (the public BuildTarget list documents XboxOne only; Unity Build Automation separately lists "Xbox Series X|S" as a cloud target). Confirm against GDK/Xbox docs once ID@Xbox access lands (§19). -->

### 16.3 Test runs on CI (editmode + playmode)

The Unity Test Framework is invoked as an Editor argument set, not through `-executeMethod`. The canonical run for each suite (pattern corroborated against the Editor CLI reference and the GameCI implementation **[DOCUMENTED]**, [Unity Editor command line arguments reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/EditorCommandLineArguments.html) and [game-ci/unity-test-runner](https://github.com/game-ci/unity-test-runner), accessed 2026-09-24):

```bash
"$UNITY_EXE" -batchmode -nographics -projectPath "$PROJECT_PATH" \
  -runTests -testPlatform PlayMode \
  -testResults "$RESULTS_DIR/results-playmode.xml" \
  -testCategory smoke \
  -runSynchronously -automated \
  -logFile "$LOGS_DIR/test-playmode.log"
```

Rules the pipeline obeys:

- **Never pass `-quit`** with `-runTests` — the Editor would exit before in-flight tests complete (documented warning); the run exits on its own **[DOCUMENTED]** (CLI reference, accessed 2026-09-24).
- Results are NUnit3 XML at `-testResults`; CI fails the job on any failed/broken test node in that XML — the process exit code alone is not the contract for tests.
- PR fast path uses `-testCategory smoke` (physics invariants for `StabilityMonitor`, scoring math in `ScoreController`, save round-trips — the editmode suites defined in §14); nightly runs the full tree plus playmode loop-integration tests with scripted input through `IPieceInputProvider` fakes.
- Coverage is a separate, weekly job only: `unity-test-runner`'s own docs state coverage instrumentation "has been the root cause of crashes and compile errors on some Unity versions (obsolete-API-as-error issues in com.unity.testtools.codecoverage, and a PlayMode SIGSEGV on Unity 6)" **[DOCUMENTED]** ([game-ci/unity-test-runner action](https://github.com/game-ci/unity-test-runner), accessed 2026-09-24). We therefore set `coverageEnabled: false` in CI and run coverage manually with `-enableCodeCoverage -coverageOptions "generateAdditionalMetrics;generateHtmlReport;generateBadgeReport;assemblyFilters:+ArtOfBalance.Gameplay.*;+ArtOfBalance.Core.*"`.
- GameCI's `testMode: All` runs PlayMode+EditMode; `Standalone` runs tests inside a built player — our playmode determinism replay tests (§14) eventually move there.

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: The Unity 6.6 Manual contains a "Test Framework command-line arguments reference" page whose URL could not be located during research (all slug guesses 404; Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.4-1.6 doc URLs are dead). The flag set above is corroborated by the Editor CLI page plus GameCI's implementation source, but re-verify against the Unity page once its URL is found. -->

### 16.4 Licensing on CI (2026-current flow)

Four documented paths; which one we use depends on license tier and runner ownership **[DOCUMENTED]** ([CLI reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/EditorCommandLineArguments.html), [GameCI activation docs](https://game.ci/docs/github/activation), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Path | Mechanism | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| Personal `.ulf` | Generate the license file once (Hub "Get a free personal license"), store file *contents* as the `UNITY_LICENSE` secret (+ `UNITY_EMAIL`/`UNITY_PASSWORD`); runner writes it to the OS path | Default for GitHub-hosted runners while on a personal license. `.ulf` locations: Windows `C:\ProgramData\Unity\Unity_lic.ulf`, macOS `/Library/Application Support/Unity/Unity_lic.ulf`, Linux `~/.local/share/unity3d/Unity/Unity_lic.ulf` |
| Pro serial | Secrets `UNITY_SERIAL` (format XX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) + `UNITY_EMAIL` + `UNITY_PASSWORD` | If the project moves to Pro/Industry |
| Floating | Unity Licensing Server: an on-network ASP.NET HTTP/HTTPS server managing a license pool; the client ships inside the Editor (2019.4+) and Hub (3.1+); v2.0+ supports offline checkout. GameCI actions accept `unityLicensingServer: <address>` | Only if a multi-seat team emerges; single dev does not need it |
| Hosted | Unity Build Automation handles licensing internally (§16.7) | If we offload the console lane |

Return licenses with `-returnlicense` when decommissioning a self-hosted runner — explicitly documented as not applicable to floating licenses. One documented disagreement to keep in mind: GameCI states licenses are "not tied to a specific Unity version or platform" (activate on Windows, use on Linux CI), while Unity's own license docs historically tie `.ulf` activation to machine entropy; in practice GameCI's docker activation regenerates per container. Treat cross-OS license reuse as GameCI-specific behavior, not a general Unity guarantee **[DOCUMENTED]** ([GameCI activation](https://game.ci/docs/github/activation), accessed 2026-09-24).

DevSecOps rules for this pipeline (user's lens; rules themselves **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**):

1. **Credentials never appear as literal CLI arguments in scripts.** `-serial`/`-username`/`-password` values come exclusively from environment variables populated from GitHub encrypted secrets — process listings on shared/self-hosted runners must not leak them. The `.ulf`-file path (`-manualLicenseFile`) is preferred over credential flags wherever possible because it puts no credential on a command line at all.
2. Secret names are minimal and rotation-ready: `UNITY_LICENSE`, `UNITY_EMAIL`, `UNITY_PASSWORD`, `UNITY_SERIAL`, `AOB_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `AOB_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `AOB_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS_NAME`, `AOB_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS_PASSWORD` (keystore flow in §18). No secret is ever echoed into logs; build logs are scanned once in CI as a tripwire (`grep` for serial-format regexes).
3. Keystore and signing material live only in GitHub secrets + a backed-up offline copy (§18/§19); never in the repo, never in a Docker layer.
4. Fork PRs get no access to secrets (GitHub default) — fork builds run the Blender lane and editmode tests only.

### 16.5 Log capture, `-nographics` limits, exit-code contract

**Log capture.** Every batch invocation uses `-logFile -` (stdout, so failures annotate the CI run inline) plus `-timestamps`; failures additionally archive the per-step log file and `-upmLogFile` output as CI artifacts. Parsing greps for the canonical failure lines (compiler errors, licensing failures) before the process code is consulted **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** for the pattern; the flags are **[DOCUMENTED]** (CLI reference, accessed 2026-09-24).

**`-nographics` limits.** Documented: no GPU initialization and Enlighten GI baking is impossible **[DOCUMENTED]** (CLI reference, accessed 2026-09-24). Consequences for this project:

- Lightmaps for the static basins (§9 lighting plan) are baked on the GPU-equipped interactive dev machine (or an interactive worker, §17) and committed; CI never bakes.
- Playmode tests that render through URP execute with software-level safety — our playmode suite asserts gameplay/logic (via `GameStateMachine`, `ScoreController`, `StabilityMonitor` signals), not pixels; screenshot QA runs on the interactive worker via MCP (§17) instead.
- Blender's separate headless-rendering constraint is handled in §16.9 — it is a different product's rule with a different shape.

**Exit-code contract.** `EditorApplication.Exit(int)` is the documented mechanism for a specific exit code from a command-line process **[DOCUMENTED]** ([EditorApplication.Exit](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/EditorApplication.Exit.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Our contract **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Code | Meaning | Emitted by |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Success (`BuildResult.Succeeded`, zero errors) | `BuildScript` |
| 1 | Build failed | `BuildScript` |
| 2 | Test run failed (reserved; test jobs actually fail on the NUnit3 XML, which is authoritative) | CI step logic |
| 3 | Licensing/activation failure | Activation step |
| 4 | Environment invalid (missing env vars, generated-asset manifest/spec hash mismatch) | `BuildScript.ValidateEnvironment` |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: Unity's own batch-mode numeric exit codes beyond EditorApplication.Exit (e.g., crash/launcher-failure codes and their precise 0/1/2 semantics) were not captured from a primary page during research. CI treats any non-zero, non-contract code as "infra failure" and retries once before failing. -->

### 16.6 CI pipeline: GitHub Actions matrix

**Runner matrix.** Host assignment is dictated by one verified platform constraint — building an IL2CPP Player for a platform requires an Editor on that platform ("to build a macOS Player with IL2CPP, you must build on macOS"; the Linux cross-compiler is the documented exception) **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Introduction to IL2CPP](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html), accessed 2026-09-24). iOS additionally needs macOS/Xcode (§18). The assignment below is otherwise **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Target | Runner | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| StandaloneWindows64 | `ubuntu-latest` (game-ci docker) | Documented GameCI example builds Windows targets in the linux container; cheaper than Windows runners |
| StandaloneLinux64 | `ubuntu-latest` (docker) | Native lane |
| Android | `ubuntu-latest` (docker) | Documented GameCI pair with `androidExportType: androidAppBundle`; keystore via action inputs |
| StandaloneOSX (universal) | `macos-latest` (no container) | IL2CPP same-OS rule; macOS runners run the actions without containers (documented GameCI capability); also where notarization would later run (§19) |
| iOS | `macos-latest` (no container) | IL2CPP + Xcode requirement; produces the Xcode project artifact for the §18 signing lane |
| XboxOne/Series | `windows-latest` (no container) | Module + GDK availability are Windows-hosted; disabled until ID@Xbox (§19) |

**GameCI action state (2026-09-24)** **[DOCUMENTED]** ([game-ci/unity-builder](https://github.com/game-ci/unity-builder), [game-ci/unity-test-runner](https://github.com/game-ci/unity-test-runner), [game-ci/cli](https://github.com/game-ci/cli), [game-ci/docker](https://github.com/game-ci/docker), accessed 2026-09-24): `unity-test-runner` latest release v4.3.2 (2026-09-09); `unity-builder` latest release v6.0.0 (2026-09-10) while docs examples still show `@v4`; the deleted `unity-activation` repo (404) means activation is built into the runner/builder actions via secrets; both actions are now thin wrappers over the cross-platform `game-ci/cli` (`game-ci test --docker --engine=unity …`); docker images publish as `unityci/editor` on Docker Hub with tag format `ubuntu-<editorVersion>-<targetPlatformImage>-<imageRevision>`. We pin `@v4` (docs-aligned); the v6 upgrade is tracked in §21 (OQ-E08, risk ENG-10 — fetch changelog/Docker Hub inventory + CI matrix run before adopting), not as a §20 task.

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: unity-builder v6.0.0 breaking changes vs v4 are unreviewed (docs lag the release); and whether unityci/editor tags exist yet for 6000.6.x patch releases (tag inventory not enumerated during research). Mitigations: macos/windows runners run without containers; unityVersion: auto reads ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt; customImage allows a hard pin. -->

**`build.yml`** — the full working sketch (GameCI input names verified from action.yml, 2026-09-24; job structure, caches, env plumbing, and version stamping are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**) **[DOCUMENTED]** for the GameCI surface ([GameCI getting started](https://game.ci/docs/github/getting-started), accessed 2026-09-24):

```yaml
name: build
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  pull_request:

env:
  AOB_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}   # tag name on releases; branch name otherwise
  AOB_BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}

jobs:
  blender-assets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { lfs: true }
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: '3.13' }          # bpy 5.2.2 requires Python ==3.13.*
      - run: pip install -r Tools/Blender/requirements.lock   # pins bpy==5.2.2
      - run: python Tools/Blender/generate_blocks.py --spec Tools/Blender/specs/blocks.json --out Generated
      - run: python Tools/Blender/render_thumbnails.py --in Generated --out Generated/Thumbnails --size 512
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: generated-assets
          path: Generated/
          retention-days: 14

  unity-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { lfs: true }
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: Library
          key: Library-Tests-${{ hashFiles('Assets/**', 'Packages/**', 'ProjectSettings/**') }}
          restore-keys: Library-Tests-
      - uses: game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4
        env:
          UNITY_LICENSE: ${{ secrets.UNITY_LICENSE }}
          UNITY_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.UNITY_EMAIL }}
          UNITY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.UNITY_PASSWORD }}
        with:
          testMode: All                  # PlayMode + EditMode
          coverageEnabled: false         # documented crash risk on Unity 6 (§16.3)
          artifactsPath: test-artifacts
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with: { name: test-results, path: test-artifacts, retention-days: 14 }

  unity-build:
    needs: [blender-assets, unity-tests]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { target: StandaloneWindows64, os: ubuntu-latest }
          - { target: StandaloneLinux64,   os: ubuntu-latest }
          - { target: Android,             os: ubuntu-latest }
          - { target: StandaloneOSX,       os: macos-latest }
          - { target: iOS,                 os: macos-latest }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { lfs: true }
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { name: generated-assets, path: generated }
      - name: Place generated assets
        run: rsync -a generated/ Assets/_Project/Art/Generated/   # manifest guard then passes (§16.2)
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: Library
          key: Library-${{ matrix.target }}-${{ hashFiles('Assets/**', 'Packages/**', 'ProjectSettings/**') }}
          restore-keys: Library-${{ matrix.target }}-
      - uses: game-ci/unity-builder@v4
        env:
          UNITY_LICENSE: ${{ secrets.UNITY_LICENSE }}
          AOB_VERSION: ${{ env.AOB_VERSION }}
          AOB_BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ env.AOB_BUILD_NUMBER }}
        with:
          targetPlatform: ${{ matrix.target }}
          unityVersion: auto                       # reads ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt
          buildMethod: ArtOfBalance.EditorTools.Editor.Build.BuildScript.BuildWindows64  # dispatched per-target in a later step wrapper
          androidExportType: androidAppBundle      # AAB for Play (§18)
          versioning: Custom
          allowDirtyBuild: false
          androidKeystoreName: user.keystore       # materialized by the action from the base64 secret
          androidKeystoreBase64: ${{ secrets.AOB_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          androidKeystorePass: ${{ secrets.AOB_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          androidKeyaliasName: ${{ secrets.AOB_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS_NAME }}
          androidKeyaliasPass: ${{ secrets.AOB_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS_PASSWORD }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: build/
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Upload build report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with: { name: report-${{ matrix.target }}, path: Builds/report-*.json, retention-days: 30 }

  release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: unity-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: { pattern: build-*, merge-multiple: true, path: dist }
      - run: gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" dist/* --generate-notes
        env: { GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} }
```

Pipeline notes:

- **Build numbers from git:** `github.run_number` + tag/branch name flow as `AOB_BUILD_NUMBER`/`AOB_VERSION` env vars into `BuildScript.ApplyVersionMetadata` (§16.2). Releases are tagged `v*`; the release job packages artifacts through `gh release create`. GameCI's own `versioning: Semantic` default remains available as a fallback; `androidVersionCode` derives from the same number, staying under 100000 per the §18 arch-split rule.
- **`Library/` cache:** keyed per target on `hashFiles('Assets/**','Packages/**','ProjectSettings/**')` with `restore-keys` fallback — the documented GameCI cache pattern **[DOCUMENTED]** ([GameCI getting started](https://game.ci/docs/github/getting-started), accessed 2026-09-24). On the self-hosted fleet we add Unity Accelerator (`-EnableCacheServer -cacheServerEndpoint`, §16.1.2).
- **The `buildMethod` per matrix entry** is a small wrapper step selecting the matching `BuildScript.Build*` method name for `matrix.target` (the YAML sketch shows one for brevity); the six method names are fixed in §16.2.
- **Self-hosted variant:** the same job graph runs against a self-hosted Windows runner with the pinned editor at `C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.6.2f1` and secrets supplied the same way; this is the lane that later hosts Xbox module builds and any GPU-requiring step.
- **Trigger policy:** `blender-assets` additionally runs on path filters `Tools/Blender/**` and `ArtSource/**/*.blend`; Unity jobs consume its artifact so mesh regeneration never happens inside a Unity job (ordering rationale in §16.13).

### 16.7 Unity Build Automation (cloud) — when to prefer

Unity Build Automation (formerly Cloud Build) is Unity's hosted CI: point it at Git/Perforce/UVCS, toggle Auto-build under Build Automation > Configurations > Basic Info, get notifications via Slack/Discord/Jira; supported platforms include Windows, macOS, UWP, Linux, iOS, Android, XR, Xbox One (via UWP), Xbox Series X|S, PS5, WebGL; a REST API and an Editor package exist **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Unity Build Automation](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/build-automation), accessed 2026-09-24).

Our stance **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: GitHub Actions + GameCI remains the primary lane because it lives next to the code, runs the Blender lane and tests in the same graph, and costs runner minutes instead of a separate product. UBA becomes preferred for exactly two cases: (1) the console lane once ID@Xbox access lands — Series X|S cloud builds without maintaining a GDK-equipped Windows runner; (2) burst capacity when the self-hosted runner is busy. Constraint to respect: UBA's support policy covers LTS releases plus the latest Unity 6 update only — our 6000.6 pin is currently the latest Unity 6 update, but when 6.7 LTS ships, verify 6.6 buildability persists before relying on UBA (risk tracked in §21). UBA's per-Unity-version Xcode/Android tool availability was not captured during research.

### 16.8 Blender command surface (5.2 LTS)

Version pin first, because the Python coupling is a hard constraint: the project pins **Blender 5.2 LTS** (released 2026-07-14; maintained through July 2028) with **bpy 5.2.2 from PyPI** (published 2026-09-15) as the CI-side implementation, and keeps 4.5 LTS (4.5.14, 2026-09-15) in mind as the documented fallback still receiving fixes **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Blender 5.2 LTS release notes](https://www.blender.org/releases/5-2/), [bpy on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/bpy/), accessed 2026-09-24). Python coupling: Blender 4.5/5.0 embed Python 3.11; 5.1+ embeds 3.13 (aligned to VFX Platform 2026); the pip wheel `bpy 5.2.2` requires `Python ==3.13.*` and publishes wheels for Windows x64/ARM64, manylinux_2_28 x86_64, and macOS 11+ ARM64. That wheel coverage is what makes "Windows CI without a Blender install" first-class.

#### 16.8.1 Flags we use (exact, from the current manual)

All **[DOCUMENTED]** against the Blender manual command-line reference (captured from the manual's RST source, 2026-09-24 — [Blender manual: Command Line Arguments](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/advanced/command_line/arguments.html)).

Core / batch:

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-b` / `--background` | Run without UI; **audio is disabled** in this mode | Every CI invocation |
| `-P <file.py>` / `--python` | Execute a script; arguments after `--` are passed to it in `sys.argv` | All asset scripts (§16.11) |
| `--python-exit-code <n>` | Set the exit code for a script that raises an unhandled exception | Always `1` — the CI lynchpin: without it a crashed script still exits 0 |
| `--factory-startup` | Ignore user preferences/startup file | Always on CI — reproducibility |
| `-y` / `-Y` | Enable/disable automatic Python script execution on file load | `-Y` on untrusted file lanes |
| `--addons <addon1,addon2>` | Enable specific addons at startup | Not needed for FBX/glTF (core now — see below) |
| `--disable-depsgraph-on-file-load` | Skip ViewLayer depsgraph build on background file load (documented as temporary; scripts needing evaluated data must call `context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()`) | Batch export of large `.blend` libraries |
| `--disable-crash-handler` | Disable crash handler (crashes then behave per-OS) | Self-hosted runner stability |
| `--log <mask>` `--log-level <n>` `--log-file <path>` | Logging subsystem control | Debug lanes; note 5.x changed log output format — do not parse stdout on it |

Render (invoked directly by the render farm lane, not by our Python scripts):

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-a` | Render animation (or `-f` last) | Not used — stills only |
| `-f <frame>` | Render frame (accepts lists and `a..b` ranges) | `-f 1` thumbnails |
| `-o <path>` | Output path; `//` = relative to the `.blend` file; `#` padded to digits (`frame_####`) | `//renders/thumb_####` |
| `-F <format>` | Output format — **case-sensitive** (`PNG`, not `png`) | `PNG` |
| `-x 1` / `-x 0` | Add / suppress filename extension | `-x 1` |
| `-E <engine>` | Render engine by id (`CYCLES`, `BLENDER_EEVEE`, `BLENDER_WORKBENCH`) | `CYCLES` (see §16.9) |
| `-S <scene>` | Scene name | Multi-scene thumbnail files |
| `-t <threads>` | Thread count (`0` = all, negative = all-but-n) | Pinned per-runner on the self-hosted lane |
| `--` separator then `--cycles-device CPU\|CUDA\|OPTIX\|HIP\|ONEAPI\|METAL` | Cycles device selection, **must appear after `--`**; `+CPU` suffix enables hybrid GPU+CPU | `CPU` on CI (§16.9) |

Extension provisioning:

| Flag | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `-c` / `--command <sub>` | Extension sub-command interface; **implies `--background`** (`blender -c extension install-file <path.mcpb>`) | Headless provisioning of extensions on runners — not needed for our FBX/glTF flow |

#### 16.8.2 Argument semantics that break pipelines

Three rules from the manual, each a classic CI bug **[DOCUMENTED]** (same source):

1. **Arguments execute in the order given.** A `-P` before the `.blend` path runs against the startup scene; the file loads after.
2. **Loading a `.blend` resets `-o`.** Any output path must come after the blend file argument.
3. **`-F` vs `-f` are different flags** (format vs frame) — case-sensitive; and flag clustering (`-ba`, `-bA`) does not work — always separate arguments. Canonical ordering used everywhere below:

```bash
blender -b scene.blend -S Thumbnails -E CYCLES \
  -o //renders/thumb_#### -F PNG -x 1 -f 1 \
  -- --cycles-device CPU
```

"Always position `-f` or `-a` as the last arguments" — render flags after everything else, then `--` for Cycles device flags.

#### 16.8.3 Environment variables and studio deployment

| Variable | Meaning | Our use |
|---|---|---|
| `BLENDER_SYSTEM_SCRIPTS` | Override the `scripts/` directory | Self-hosted runners: point at a shared, versioned scripts dir |
| `BLENDER_USER_SCRIPTS` | User scripts path | Dev machines (per-user add-ons) |
| `--app-template` + `bl_app_templates_system` | Application templates at a system location | Not used in v1 |
| `startup/enable_addons.py` + `addon_utils.enable` | Programmatic addon enablement from a startup script | Legacy addons on the interactive lane |
| `blender -c extension install-file <file>` | Headless extension install (extensions may bundle pip wheels under `./wheels/`) | Only if an extension-based tool lands later |

FBX and glTF IO live as **core addons** at `scripts/addons_core/io_scene_fbx` and `io_scene_gltf2`, enabled by default — no `--addons io_scene_fbx` flag is needed on 5.x **[DOCUMENTED]** ([Blender manual: Deploying Blender — captured from the manual's RST source, 2026-09-24](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender-manual/raw/branch/main/manual/advanced/deploying_blender.rst); the `addons_core` paths are independently evidenced by the fetched exporter sources themselves — track-t04 #10 `scripts/addons_core/io_scene_fbx/__init__.py`, #11 `scripts/addons_core/io_scene_gltf2/__init__.py`).

### 16.9 Headless rendering matrix and the bpy module decision

#### 16.9.1 What renders headless

| Engine | Headless behavior | Verdict for CI |
|---|---|---|
| Cycles CPU | Command-line rendering needs no graphical display; CPU device works fully headless | **Our thumbnail engine** |
| Cycles GPU | Device flags `CUDA/OPTIX/HIP/ONEAPI/METAL` after `--`; 5.0 raised minimum GPU driver/architecture floors; hybrid `+CPU` supported | Only on the GPU-equipped interactive worker (§17), not CI |
| EEVEE | GPU-only — no CPU path, none planned; no multi-GPU; and verbatim: "Headless rendering is not supported on headless Windows systems." | Never in CI; interactive worker only |
| Workbench | Headless behavior not documented in fetched primaries | Not used |

**[DOCUMENTED]** for all rows except the Workbench verdict ([Blender manual: Command Line Rendering / GPU rendering — captured from the manual's RST source, 2026-09-24](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender-manual/raw/branch/main/manual/advanced/command_line/render.rst)). Engine-id note: 5.0 renamed `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` → `BLENDER_EEVEE`; scripts must use the new id on 5.x.

Conclusion: all CI thumbnails render with `CYCLES` on `CPU` — deterministic, container-friendly, and speed is irrelevant for 512px block stills. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: EEVEE headless on Linux (EGL/`--gpu-backend` interplay) and Workbench headless behavior were not confirmed from fetched primary sources — only matters if we later want EEVEE-look thumbnails from CI, which we do not. -->

#### 16.9.2 bpy as a pip module vs the blender binary

| Criterion | `blender -b -P script.py` (binary) | `pip install bpy==5.2.2` (module) |
|---|---|---|
| Environment | Needs Blender installed and version-matched | Any Python 3.13 env; wheels for win x64/arm64, linux x86_64, macOS arm64 |
| Startup state | Startup file applies unless `--factory-startup` | Behaves as `--factory-startup`; import gives the default startup scene — call `bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)` for an empty scene |
| Flags | Full CLI surface (threads, log, render flags) | No Python equivalents for `--threads`/`--log` — configure via API or don't use |
| Import discipline | n/a | Import `mathutils`/`gpu` **after** `bpy` |
| Crash semantics | Signal handlers + crash log | No signal handlers, no crash log |
| Re-initialization | New process per file | `importlib.reload(bpy)` unsupported; one `.blend` at a time — use `bpy.data.libraries.load`, `temp_data`, or `multiprocessing` |

**[DOCUMENTED]** (captured from the API-docs RST source `info_advanced_blender_as_bpy.rst`, 2026-09-24 — [Blender API docs: Blender as a Python Module](https://docs.blender.org/api/current/info_advanced_blender_as_bpy.html)).

Decision **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: **CI uses the pip module** (`setup-python 3.13` + `requirements.lock` with `bpy==5.2.2`, installed from the main index; Blender versions outside the current LTS window are removed from PyPI but archived, so pinning an older bpy requires `--extra-index-url https://download.blender.org/pypi/`). Rationale: one less runner dependency, wheel coverage includes Windows, and scripts are plain `python script.py` — trivially unit-testable. The **binary lane is kept** for two cases: rendering directly with the render flags (`-o/-F/-f`, §16.8.2) on the render lane, and any future step needing `--cycles-device` GPU selection. Every script therefore has a dual-mode entry (§16.11 pattern).

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: whether the pip `bpy` wheel ships the `io_scene_fbx`/`io_scene_gltf2` addons in the same enabled-by-default state as the binary distribution (the manual documents module-vs-binary differences but this specific addon-inclusion question was not confirmed from a fetched primary). Fallback: use the binary lane for FBX export if the wheel lacks the addon. -->

### 16.10 Context overrides (`temp_override`) — the 4.x/5.x pattern

Headless scripts frequently need an operator that requires a UI context (a specific area/region). The only supported mechanism is the `temp_override` context manager; `bpy.ops` poll failures surface as `RuntimeError: Operator bpy.ops.*.poll() context is incorrect` **[DOCUMENTED]** (verified from the Blender source tree — the rendered `bpy.context` API page was Cloudflare-walled and never fetched: `Context.temp_override` docstring/implementation in [bpy_rna_context.cc](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/raw/branch/main/source/blender/python/intern/bpy_rna_context.cc), fetched 2026-09-24; poll-failure guidance per the [Using Operators gotchas (API-docs RST source)](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/raw/branch/main/doc/python_api/rst/info_gotchas_operators.rst), fetched 2026-09-24).

```python
import bpy

def _first_area(type_):
    for window in bpy.context.window_manager.windows:
        screen = window.screen
        for area in screen.areas:
            if area.type == type_:
                return window, screen, area
    return None, None, None

window, screen, area = _first_area("VIEW_3D")
region = next(r for r in area.regions if r.type == "WINDOW") if area else None

with bpy.context.temp_override(window=window, screen=screen, area=area, region=region):
    bpy.ops.view3d.view_all()
```

Guidance for our scripts:

- `temp_override(*, window, screen, area, region, **keywords)` — overrides stack when nested; pass exactly the context members the operator's poll requires, nothing more.
- Import/export operators (`bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx`, `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf`) do **not** need a temp override — they poll fine in background mode. We reserve `temp_override` for viewport and a handful of editor operators.
- Every helper that hunts for an area returns `None` cleanly — in `--factory-startup` background mode, screens exist, but a missing area type must raise an explicit script error (paired with `--python-exit-code 1`), never a silent skip.

### 16.11 The three asset scripts (full working sketches)

All three live in `Tools/Blender/`, run dual-mode (pip `bpy` on CI, `blender -b -P` locally), and share one contract: read the checked-in spec `Tools/Blender/specs/blocks.json`, emit meshes + a `manifest.json` into `Assets/_Project/Art/Generated/`. Script structure and the schema are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; every API call used is from the documented/verified surfaces above.

#### 16.11.1 `blocks.json` — the single source of truth **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**

```json
{
  "specVersion": 3,
  "unit": "blender-meter",
  "shapes": [
    { "pieceId": "cube_s1", "family": "basic", "sizeCells": [1,1,1],
      "mass": 1.0, "material": "wood", "bevel": 0.02 },
    { "pieceId": "bar_l3",  "family": "basic", "sizeCells": [3,1,1],
      "mass": 3.0, "material": "wood", "bevel": 0.02 },
    { "pieceId": "load_break", "family": "special", "specialKind": "load_break",
      "maxStacked": 3 },
    { "pieceId": "timer_5s",  "family": "special", "specialKind": "timer", "seconds": 5 },
    { "pieceId": "fire",      "family": "special", "specialKind": "fire" },
    { "pieceId": "grav_inv",  "family": "special", "specialKind": "gravity_inverter" },
    { "pieceId": "linked_pair", "family": "special", "specialKind": "linked",
      "partnerPieceId": "linked_pair" }
  ]
}
```

Shape inventory follows the documented franchise facts: 16 regular shapes on the 3DS+ editions, with four documented specials — load-break (holds max ~3 regulars), timer (starts when stacked atop, vanishes at zero), fire (explodes on contact with another fire shape), gravity-inverter (flips the stack to the platform at screen top) **[DOCUMENTED]** (franchise track notes, §3). The fifth special, `linked` (a pair acting as a rigid linked/seesaw unit), is the chief-architect **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** addition. `mass`, `material`, and per-shape gameplay tuning are design inputs, not citations — `PieceDefinition` (§5) is the Unity-side consumer of this file.

#### 16.11.2 `generate_blocks.py`

```python
"""Generate AoB block meshes from blocks.json into the Unity Generated folder.

Dual-mode: `python generate_blocks.py --spec ... --out ...` (pip bpy) or
`blender -b --factory-startup -P generate_blocks.py -- --spec ... --out ...`.
Exits non-zero on any error (CI pairs this with --python-exit-code 1).
"""
import argparse, hashlib, json, sys
import bpy                          # import FIRST (module-mode rule, §16.9)
import bmesh

def main() -> int:
    args = parse_argv()                                  # argv after `--` in binary mode
    spec = json.loads(args.spec.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)     # empty scene (module-mode rule)

    for shape in spec["shapes"]:
        mesh = build_block_mesh(shape)                   # bmesh.ops.create_cube per cell,
        obj = bpy.data.objects.new(shape["pieceId"], mesh)   # remove_doubles, bevel,
        bpy.data.collections.new(shape["family"]).objects.link(obj)  # validate()/update()

    manifest = {
        "specVersion": spec["specVersion"],
        "sourceSpecHash": sha256_file(args.spec),
        "pieces": [{"pieceId": s["pieceId"], "mesh": f"{s['pieceId']}.fbx",
                    "collider": "box", "sizeCells": s.get("sizeCells")} for s in spec["shapes"]],
    }
    export_fbx(args.out)
    (args.out / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return 0

def export_fbx(out_dir) -> None:
    # Verified operator parameters (§16.11.4): unit scale baked, Y-up -Z-forward for Unity.
    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(
        filepath=str(out_dir / "AoB_Blocks.fbx"),
        use_selection=False,
        apply_unit_scale=True,
        apply_scale_options='FBX_SCALE_NONE',
        axis_forward='-Z', axis_up='Y',
        use_mesh_modifiers=True,          # NOTE: blocks shape keys -> modifier bake
        mesh_smooth_type='OFF',           # "Normals Only"
        colors_type='SRGB',
        bake_anim=False,
    )
```

Mesh construction notes (per the verified 5.x bmesh surface): `bmesh.new()`, `bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=cell)`, `bmesh.ops.remove_doubles`, bevel via `bmesh.ops.bevel`, then `me.validate()` + `me.update()` before object creation — never leave an unvalidated mesh for the exporter **[DOCUMENTED]** for the API surface (bmesh as corroborated via the source tree and 5.0 release notes, 2026-09-24 — full bmesh doc page was unfetchable; treat exact op signatures as verify-on-first-run). The collider hint (`"collider": "box"`) feeds the Unity-side prefab generation in §9: box colliders per `sizeCells`, no convex mesh colliders needed for cuboid pieces.

#### 16.11.3 `batch_export.py` and `render_thumbnails.py`

`batch_export.py` — re-exports a whole `.blend` library; FBX gets the native batch mode, glTF is looped (no batch parameter exists on the glTF exporter — ~140 params, `export_format='GLB'` default, `export_yup=True`):

```python
bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(
    filepath=str(out), batch_mode='SCENE', use_batch_own_dir=True, ...)
for f in files:
    bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=str(out / f"{f.stem}.glb"), export_format='GLB')
```

Invoked with `--disable-depsgraph-on-file-load` (the documented performance flag) and `--python-exit-code 1`; scripts call `context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()` when they need evaluated data.

`render_thumbnails.py` — 512px PNG per piece, Cycles CPU:

```python
scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
scene.cycles.device = 'CPU'
scene.render.film_transparent = True
scene.render.resolution_x = scene.render.resolution_y = 512
# camera 3/4 view + sun light per piece ...
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
# Blender 5.0+ ORDER MATTERS: set scene.render.image_settings.media_type
# BEFORE file_format when targeting still image types.
```

Icons are trimmed/imported on the Unity side as `PieceDefinition.iconSprite` (§5). The pure-CLI equivalent (no script) for one file: `blender -b scene.blend -o //renders/thumb_#### -F PNG -x 1 -f 1 -- --cycles-device CPU` (§16.8.2).
