Deliberately deferred to the asset pipeline section (§9) whose research track captured the Unity import surface; do not finalize importer values here. -->

#### 16.11.4 Verified FBX/glTF export parameters

From the core addon source (`scripts/addons_core/io_scene_fbx`, `io_scene_gltf2`), 2026-09-24 **[DOCUMENTED]**: FBX `axis_forward='-Z'`, `axis_up='Y'`, `apply_unit_scale=True`, `apply_scale_options='FBX_SCALE_NONE'` (Unity scale-correction neutral), `use_mesh_modifiers=True` (bakes modifiers but **blocks shape keys** — irrelevant for rigid blocks), `mesh_smooth_type='OFF'` = "Normals Only", `colors_type='SRGB'`, `batch_mode ∈ {OFF, SCENE, COLLECTION, SCENE_COLLECTION}` + `use_batch_own_dir` (FBX-only). glTF exporter has no `batch_mode` — loop. DevSecOps note: no network, no secrets, no shell-outs in any Blender script; they read and write only within the workspace.

#### 16.11.5 CI invocation on asset change

The `blender-assets` job (§16.6) triggers on any push but only *does work* when the spec or sources change — a path-filtered workflow (`Tools/Blender/**`) or, in the always-run form, a `git diff --quiet Tools/Blender` guard that skips generation and marks the manifest `unchanged` **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**. Either way the Unity jobs consume the artifact, never a locally generated folder, so `Assets/_Project/Art/Generated/` contents are always CI-produced (policy discussion in §16.13).

### 16.12 Version pinning and reproducibility ledger

Everything in this section exists to make "same commit → same artifacts" true two years from now.

| Component | Pin | Mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unity Editor | `6000.6.2f1` | `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` (canonical, checked in) + self-hosted runner path + GameCI `customImage: unityci/editor:ubuntu-6000.6.2f1-<target>-<rev>` | 6.6 is the final Supported/Update release of the Unity 6 family (6.7 is the next LTS) — see §21 for the upgrade-window strategy |
| Unity modules | Windows/Mac/Linux/Android/iOS (+Xbox post-ID@Xbox) | Runner image + Hub install manifest | Android toolchain rides with the editor (NDK r27c, JDK 17 — §18) |
| GameCI actions | `game-ci/unity-builder@v4`, `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` | YAML ref pins | v6/v4.3.2 exist; upgrade tracked in §21 (OQ-E08) |
| Docker images | `unityci/editor` tagged by editor version + target platform + image revision | `customImage` input | Tag inventory to verify (§16.6 TODO) |
| Blender (binary lane) | 5.2 LTS | Runner install script pinning the 5.2.x download | 4.5 LTS documented fallback |
| Python | 3.13 | `setup-python` + lockfile metadata | VFX Platform 2026 alignment |
| bpy | `bpy==5.2.2` | `Tools/Blender/requirements.lock` | Requires `Python ==3.13.*`; versions outside the current LTS window are removed from PyPI but archived — `--extra-index-url https://download.blender.org/pypi/` when pinning an older version |
| Render engine ids | `CYCLES`, `BLENDER_EEVEE` (5.0 renames) | Constants in scripts | Post-5.0 ids pinned in code |

**[DOCUMENTED]** for the factual pins (Unity 6.6 status per §16 intro sources; Blender/Python/bpy per §16.8 sources; GameCI per §16.6 sources); the ledger mechanism itself is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

Additional reproducibility rules:

- **API-update discipline:** editor version bumps run with `-accept-apiupdate` first, on a sacrificial branch; the diff of the API-updated files is reviewed before the pin moves.
- **URL discipline:** every persisted link uses versioned `/6000.6/Documentation/` Unity URLs (§16.1.1). Blender manual content was captured from the manual's RST source on the main branch via projects.blender.org (docs.blender.org rendered pages were unreachable all session — Cloudflare; equivalence to the rendered manual is assumed, not verified); the `/manual/en/latest/` links in §16.8–§16.10 are therefore pointers to the generated pages pending verification — once the rendered pages are reachable, re-verify them and repoint citations to the versioned `/manual/en/5.2/` paths (open thread: track-t04 line 234).
- **Checksum verification of the bpy wheel** (hash pinned in the lockfile comment, verified after install) — supply-chain hygiene for a binary wheel that will parse our only authoritative game-data file **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.
- **No floating references anywhere:** no `@main`, no `latest`, no `docker pull unityci/editor:latest`, no unpinned `pip install bpy`.
- **6.6 → 6.7 LTS churn:** when the pin eventually moves, the checklist is: new editor pin → `-accept-apiupdate` pass → package manifest diff (Input System becomes a built-in module in 6.6+; Mono removal lands in 6.8 per the CoreCLR roadmap) → full CI green → re-pin GameCI image. Tracked in §21.

### 16.13 Orchestration: ordering, the generated-asset contract, and cache policy

The pipeline's execution graph **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

```
push / PR
  └─> blender-assets        (generate_blocks.py + render_thumbnails.py, pip bpy 5.2.2)
        └─ uploads artifact generated-assets (FBX + PNGs + manifest.json)
  └─> unity-tests           (editmode + playmode, NUnit3 XML gates)
        └─ uploads test-results
  └─> unity-build  needs: [blender-assets, unity-tests]
        └─ matrix of 5 targets (6th post-ID@Xbox)
              ├─ download-artifact generated-assets -> Assets/_Project/Art/Generated/
              ├─ Library cache restore
              ├─ unity-builder -> BuildScript.Build*  (AOB_VERSION / AOB_BUILD_NUMBER env)
              └─ upload build-<target> + report-<target>
tag v*  └─> release  (needs unity-build; gh release create from artifacts)
```

**Pre-build ordering.** The generated assets land in the project *before* the Editor ever imports them, so there is exactly one import pass and no mid-build regeneration. `BuildScript.ValidateEnvironment` (§16.2) enforces the contract at the last moment before `BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer`: `manifest.json` must exist and its `sourceSpecHash` must equal the hash of `Tools/Blender/specs/blocks.json` at HEAD — mismatch fails with exit code 4 (environment invalid) rather than shipping meshes that disagree with the spec. The same check also runs as an `IPreprocessBuildWithContext` hook so a developer-triggered local build without the CI step fails identically.

**Commit-vs-ephemeral policy for `Assets/_Project/Art/Generated/`.** The folder is gitignored; its contents are always CI artifacts (or a local `make assets` run). Rationale: committing generated FBX creates merge conflicts and stale-mesh drift; pure ephemerality with the manifest-hash guard gives the same reproducibility with none of the drift. The one exception planned: lightmaps baked on the interactive GPU worker (§16.5) are committed, since CI cannot bake them at all (`-nographics`).

**Cache keys.** Unity `Library/` caches key on source hashes (§16.6). The Blender lane adds its own cache keyed on `hashFiles('Tools/Blender/**')` **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — an unchanged spec with a changed Python interpreter version still regenerates (the wheel install is cached separately by pip). The generated-assets artifact is never cached across runs: it is cheap to produce and must reflect HEAD.

**Where each consumer plugs in.** `manifest.json` → §9 (AssetPostprocessor/prefab generation for `PieceDefinition`), thumbnails → §5 (`iconSprite`), `report-*.json` → §21 (build-size trend tracking), NUnit3 XML → §14 (test dashboards). Nothing downstream of this section reads Unity or Blender logs as a data interface — logs are forensics only (§16.5).

This section's deliverables, restated as the task list for §20: the BuildScript.cs file, the build.yml file, the three Blender scripts + blocks.json schema, the licensing secrets set, the runner matrix, and the pinning ledger above.

## 17. Unity & Blender MCP Servers

This section selects and wires up the Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers used for agent-assisted development of the Art of Balance clone: which Unity and Blender servers we run, how Claude Code connects to them, the security posture they impose on the dev machine (the user's DevSecOps lens applied in full), and the concrete day-to-day recipes they enable for a one-developer team. Everything here is **development-time tooling only** — no MCP package, addon, socket, or server may exist in a shipping player build; enforcement rules are in §17.4.5. The companion automation surfaces are the new Unity CLI (§15) and the traditional Unity batch-mode + Blender CLI pipeline (§16); §17.5.6 is the binding decision table that allocates work between MCP and CLI.

### 17.1 MCP primer

**[DOCUMENTED]** MCP is an "open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems," described by its authors as "a USB-C port for AI applications" ([modelcontextprotocol.io, spec version 2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro), accessed 2026-09-24). The protocol defines three participant roles — **host** (the AI application), **client** (the per-server connector inside the host), and **server** (the program exposing capabilities) — and two layers: a data layer of primitives and a transport layer.

| Primitive | What it is | Example in this project |
|---|---|---|
| **Tool** | Executable function the model chooses to call | `manage_scriptable_object`, `execute_blender_code` |
| **Resource** | Read-only data addressed by URI | `unity://menu-items`, `unity://packages` (CoderGamester) |
| **Prompt** | Reusable prompt template | `gameobject_handling_strategy` (CoderGamester) |
| **Notification** | Server-pushed events, e.g. `tools/list_changed` | Tool registry changes |

Transports: **stdio** (host launches the server as a child process) and **streamable HTTP** (server listens on an endpoint; OAuth exists for remote servers) ([modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro), accessed 2026-09-24). All servers adopted here run stdio or loopback HTTP; this project uses **no remote MCP endpoints** — that is a hard policy rule (§17.4.5). Clients that matter to us — all cited as MCP-compatible by the surveyed server docs — include Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot CLI ([CoplayDev README](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp), [CoderGamester README](https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity), accessed 2026-09-24). The working client throughout this plan is **Claude Code**.

### 17.2 Unity MCP server landscape

#### 17.2.1 The official server — and its 2026 deprecation pivot

Unity Technologies shipped an official MCP server inside the AI Assistant package (`com.unity.ai.assistant`). MCP went public in 2.0.0-pre.1 (changelog dated 2026-03-03); an MCP *client* was added in 1.6.0-pre.3; the docs ladder runs 1.0 (6000.2.0a8+) → 1.5/1.6 (6000.3.0f1+) → 1.7 → 2.0–2.20 (6000.0.60f1+) ([package docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.assistant@2.0/manual/unity-mcp-overview.html), [changelog](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.assistant@2.0/changelog/CHANGELOG.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Documented architecture **[DOCUMENTED]**:

```
Claude Code ─(MCP / stdio)─ relay binary in ~/.unity/relay/ (relay.exe --mcp)
                          ─(IPC: named pipe on Windows, Unix socket on macOS/Linux)─
                          Unity Editor MCP bridge ─ McpToolRegistry (built-in + custom tools,
                          dynamic discovery at startup, multiple simultaneous clients)
```

Relay paths for inventory/firewall purposes: Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.unity\relay\relay_win.exe`; macOS `~/.unity/relay/relay_mac_arm64…` / `…relay_mac_x64…`; Linux `~/.unity/relay/relay_linux` ([Unity docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.assistant@2.0/manual/unity-mcp-overview.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Configuration lives at Edit > Project Settings > AI > Unity MCP (bridge status, start/stop, pending/connected clients, per-tool toggles); note this is a different page from AI > MCP Client, which configures servers the in-editor Assistant connects *to*.

Two corrections govern how we treat this server:

1. **Gating (verified nuance).** The launch blog lists four prerequisites — "Unity 6 (6000.0) or later with the AI Assistant package installed", an MCP-compatible client, "A Unity project connected to Unity Cloud", and "An active trial or subscription to Unity's AI tools beta" ([Unity blog, 2026-05-11](https://unity.com/blog/unity-ai-mcp-how-to-get-started), accessed 2026-09-24). The current 2.0.0-pre.1 get-started docs list only two (Unity 6 + package, MCP client) and do not restate the Cloud/subscription requirements — docs and blog disagree as of 2026-09-24, a free trial exists ("open to all Unity 6 developers"), and whether the relay enforces the subscription at connection time is unpublished ([get-started docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.assistant@2.0/manual/unity-mcp-get-started.html), accessed 2026-09-24; adversarial verify pass, 2026-09-24). Correct cost framing: **trial-gated with a free tier** — not "free", not "paid-only". <!-- TODO-VERIFY: whether the relay enforces the AI-tools-beta subscription at connection time or only the Assistant UI does; test in-editor at setup. -->
2. **[VERIFIED-REFUTED] Deprecation.** This in-editor server is now deprecated: "Unity has deprecated the MCP server component of the in-editor AI assistant package com.unity.ai.assistant. … The `unity mcp` command in the Unity CLI replaces the in-Editor server" ([Unity CLI docs](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/replace-mcp-server-unity-cli), accessed 2026-09-24). The replacement, `unity mcp`, is a built-in MCP server in the Unity CLI: stdio transport, exposes connected-Editor commands as MCP tools, built on `com.unity.pipeline` (Unity 6.0 LTS+), free with no Unity AI subscription and no MCP concurrency limits; `unity mcp configure <client>` writes configs for 16 clients including Claude Code; third-party GitHub MCP packages are unaffected ([Unity CLI reference](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference), accessed 2026-09-24; see §15).

The official server's built-in tool set is documented **only at category level** — scene management, script editing, console access (the single concrete name published is `Unity_ReadConsole`), GameObject/component read-write, build-settings inspection — and the custom-tool registration page (fetched by the verify pass) does not enumerate built-ins; no public per-tool schema exists anywhere in the 2.0.0-pre.1 docs set. Custom tools register via `[McpTool(name, description)]` + `[McpDescription]`/`[McpSchema]`/`[McpOutputSchema]` attributes with `McpToolRegistry` TypeCache scanning and four registration approaches ([tool-registration docs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.assistant@2.0/manual/unity-mcp-tool-registration.html), accessed 2026-09-24). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact built-in tool names/schemas must be introspected live (MCP tools/list against the relay, or the Project Settings > AI > Unity MCP tool-list UI) if this path is ever used. -->

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Project decision:** do not build on the deprecated assistant-package server. Use (a) CoplayDev "MCP for Unity" as the primary Editor bridge (§17.2.2) and (b) `unity mcp` as the official, subscription-free complement driven through the Unity CLI/pipeline stack already adopted in §15. Custom editor-exposed commands are authored as `[CliCommand]` static methods (§17.5.5), which both `unity command` and `unity mcp` expose — one implementation, two consumption paths.

Install paths (all documented): UPM git URL `https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp.git?path=/MCPForUnity#main` (pin `#v10.2.0` for release tracking; `#beta` for prerelease), Unity Asset Store "MCP for Unity", or `openupm add com.coplaydev.unity-mcp`; then the setup wizard and `Window → MCP for Unity → Configure All Detected Clients`. Claude Desktop is stdio-only and is silently configured that way; **Claude Code auto-connects after wizard configuration** ([install docs](https://coplaydev.github.io/unity-mcp/getting-started/install/), accessed 2026-09-24).

Tool surface — 47 tool entrypoints in 9+ groups ([tool reference, updated 2026-07-13](https://coplaydev.github.io/unity-mcp/reference/tools/), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Group | Count | Tools (exact names) |
|---|---|---|
| core (always on) | 30 | `manage_scene`, `manage_gameobject`, `manage_components`, `manage_asset`, `manage_prefabs`, `manage_material`/`manage_shader`/`manage_texture`, `manage_build`, `manage_packages`, `manage_editor`, `manage_camera`, `manage_physics`, `manage_graphics`, `execute_menu_item`, `execute_code`, `execute_custom_tool`, `read_console`, `refresh_unity`, `run_tests` + `get_test_job` (async test jobs), script tools (`manage_script`, `manage_script_capabilities`, `create_script`, `delete_script`, `apply_text_edits`, `script_apply_edits`, `validate_script`, `find_in_file`, `get_sha`), `find_gameobjects`, `batch_execute`, `manage_tools` |
| asset_gen (BYO API key) | 5 | `generate_image` (fal.ai/OpenRouter), `generate_model` (Tripo/Meshy), `generate_audio` (fal.ai), `import_model` (Sketchfab), `import_model_file` (local FBX/OBJ/glTF) |
| scripting_ext | 2 | incl. **`manage_scriptable_object`** + execute-adjacent |

| vfx | 3 | `manage_shader`, `manage_texture`, `manage_vfx` |
| animation / probuilder / profiling / ui | 1 each | `manage_animation`; `manage_probuilder` (needs com.unity.probuilder); `manage_profiler` (sessions, counters, memory snapshots, Frame Debugger); `manage_ui` (UXML/USS/UIDocument) |

`manage_scriptable_object` is the load-bearing tool for this project's content plan (§5): actions `create|modify`; params `type_name` (namespace-qualified), `folder_path`, `asset_name`, `overwrite`, `target` ({guid|path}), `patches` (list; object refs via `{"ref":{"guid":"…"}}`; Sprite sub-assets via `spriteName`), and `dry_run` to validate without applying ([tool reference](https://coplaydev.github.io/unity-mcp/reference/tools/), accessed 2026-09-24).

Script-safety ladder **[DOCUMENTED]**: a fast structural validator checks LLM-generated scripts by default; an optional one-click Roslyn DLL install (Window → MCP for Unity) adds strict validation catching undefined namespaces/types/methods at write time without a full Unity compile; `validate_script` returns diagnostics and `get_sha` returns a script's SHA256 without content ([Roslyn guide](https://coplaydev.github.io/unity-mcp/guides/roslyn), accessed 2026-09-24). Note: this is a *correctness* ladder, not a security boundary (§17.4).

#### 17.2.3 IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP ("AI Game Developer") — runtime hooks and a documented CI recipe

| Fact | Value (2026-09-24) |
|---|---|
| Repo | https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP — 4,332 stars, Apache-2.0, last push 2026-09-24, v0.93.0 released 2026-09-24 (0.89.0 was 2026-08-19 — next-day cadence at times) (gh api) |
| Distribution | OpenUPM `com.ivanmurzak.unity.mcp`; `.unitypackage` installer; npm `unity-mcp-cli` (install-plugin, setup-skills, create-project, install-unity, login, open); Docker `aigamedeveloper/mcp-server`; cloud service ai-game.dev (OAuth device flow) |
| Constraint | **Project path must not contain spaces** (Windows gotcha) |

**[DOCUMENTED]** Architecture: a standalone .NET server binary installed at `<unityProject>/Library/mcp-server/<platform>/gamedev-mcp-server[.exe]`; the MCP client launches it over stdio (`claude mcp add ai-game-developer "<…>/gamedev-mcp-server.exe" port=<port> client-transport=stdio`) or reaches it via streamable HTTP (default url http://localhost:8080). Plugin↔server link defaults to port 8080. Key env/flags: `MCP_PLUGIN_PORT`/`--port` (8080), `MCP_PLUGIN_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` (10000 ms), `MCP_PLUGIN_CLIENT_TRANSPORT` (stdio|streamableHttp), `MCP_AUTHORIZATION` (**none**|oauth|token — default none), `MCP_PLUGIN_TOKEN`, `MCP_PLUGIN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (600); Unity-side `UNITY_MCP_CLOUD_URL`, `UNITY_MCP_CONNECTION_MODE` (Cloud|Custom), `UNITY_MCP_KEEP_CONNECTED`, `UNITY_MCP_AUTH_OPTION`, `UNITY_MCP_TOKEN`, `UNITY_MCP_TRANSPORT`, `UNITY_MCP_START_SERVER`, `UNITY_MCP_TOOLS` (runtime-only tool-ID allowlist, never persisted). Documented headless CI recipe:

```bash
Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics \
  -UNITY_MCP_CLOUD_URL=http://localhost:8080 \
  -UNITY_MCP_KEEP_CONNECTED=true \
  -UNITY_MCP_AUTH_OPTION=token \
  -UNITY_MCP_TOKEN=my-secret-token
```

Tool surface (70+): package add/list/remove/search; scene ops; **`screenshot-game-view` / `screenshot-scene-view`**; `console-get-logs`/`console-clear-logs`; `editor-application-get/set-state` (play/pause/compile control); `editor-selection-get/set`; `reflection-method-find` / `reflection-method-call` ("Call any C# method with input parameters"); `script-execute` ("Compiles and executes C# code dynamically using Roslyn"); `script-read`/`script-update-or-create`/`script-delete`; `tests-run` (EditMode/PlayMode with filtering); `type-get-json-schema`; 11 profiler tools; ten extension packs (AI Animation, Cinemachine, InputSystem, Navigation, ParticleSystem, ProBuilder, Splines, Terrain, Tilemap, Timeline). Custom tools: `[AiToolType]` on a class + `[AiTool("name", Title=…)]` on methods + `[Description]` per argument, with Unity-API work wrapped in `MainThread.Instance.Run(()=>…)` ([README v0.93.0](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP), accessed 2026-09-24). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact Unity version floor and per-tool parameter schemas (in-repo docs/default-mcp-tools.md was not fetched); confirm 6000.6 support before any adoption. -->

**[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** The sweep claim that this server "genuinely executes arbitrary C# in the compiled player at runtime" is refuted as worded. Verified reality: the runtime (in-game) mode connects the compiled player to the MCP server and exposes **developer-authored, pre-compiled** C# tools — `UnityMcpPluginRuntime.Initialize(builder => builder.WithToolsFromAssembly(...))` with `[AiTool]` attributes in player code, main-thread marshaled; "By default there are no tools" at runtime. The arbitrary-execution tools (`script-execute`, `reflection-method-call`) live in the **Editor assembly** (`Editor/Scripts/API/Tool/`) and are stripped from player builds. Consequence for us: if we ever want in-game AI debugging (e.g., a live StabilityMonitor probe during playtests, §6), we must author and ship those tools ourselves — deliberately, as reviewed code.

#### 17.2.4 CoderGamester/mcp-unity — Node.js option with resources and prompts

**[DOCUMENTED]** 1,910 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-09-03; requires Unity 6+ and Node.js 18+ ([repo](https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity), accessed 2026-09-24). This server inverts the usual topology: a **WebSocket server runs inside the Unity Editor** (default port 8090; settings in `ProjectSettings/McpUnitySettings.json`; env overrides `UNITY_PORT`, `UNITY_HOST`, `UNITY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `MCP_UNITY_SETTINGS_PATH`, `MCP_UNITY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH`) and a Node.js MCP server acts as the WebSocket client, speaking stdio to the AI client. In batch mode the Unity-side WebSocket starts but npm install/build never runs there — the Node side must be prebuilt for CI.

```
Claude Code ─(stdio)─ Node.js MCP server (WS client) ─(WebSocket :8090)─ Unity Editor WS server
```

~30 tools plus a dashboard: `execute_menu_item`, `select_gameobject`, `update_gameobject`, `update_component`, `add_package`, `run_tests`, `send_console_log`/`get_console_logs`, `add_asset_to_scene`, `create_prefab`, `create/load/delete/unload/save_scene`, `get_scene_info`, `get_gameobject`, `recompile_scripts`, `duplicate/delete/reparent/move/rotate/scale_gameobject`, `set_transform`, `create/assign/modify material`, `get_material_info`, `batch_execute` (atomic operations with optional rollback), `show_unity_dashboard` (VS Code 1.109+ MCP App). It is the only top server shipping MCP **Resources** (`unity://menu-items`, `unity://packages`) and **Prompts** (`gameobject_handling_strategy` et al.). Security: HTTP Basic (username `mcp-unity`) + token file, WebSocket handshakes carrying an `Origin` header are rejected, token rotation via the Server Window; remote mode binds 0.0.0.0 but stays unencrypted ws:// — docs advise VPN/SSH tunnel only. Setup: UPM git URL from the repo README, then Tools > MCP Unity > Server Window → Start Server, then the per-client auto-config buttons (project-scoped for Cursor/Claude Code/Codex CLI; `.vscode/mcp.json` with `${workspaceFolder}` for VS Code). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact UPM git URL string for this package was not captured in research; copy from the README before use. -->

CoderGamester is not adopted (adds a Node toolchain for a smaller tool surface; its Resources/Prompts pattern is nice-to-have, not needed).

### 17.3 Blender MCP server landscape

#### 17.3.1 Canonical server: ahujasid mcp-for-blender (formerly blender-mcp)

**[DOCUMENTED]** The canonical project renamed itself on **2026-09-16**: PyPI `blender-mcp` → `mcp-for-blender`, repo ahujasid/blender-mcp → [ahujasid/mcp-for-blender](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender) (issue [#366](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/issues/366), 2026-09-16). "TL;DR — nothing breaks": `uvx blender-mcp` still resolves via a PyPI compatibility wrapper (old name frozen at 2.0.0, `requires_dist: mcp-for-blender>=2.0.0`); old links/clones/configs keep working via GitHub redirect ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/mcp-for-blender/json), accessed 2026-09-24). Verified state: 29,280 stars, 2,686 forks, MIT, created 2025-03-07, last push 2026-09-24 (research day); current version **2.0.4** (uploaded 2026-09-01), `requires-python >=3.10`, Blender 3.0+ supported; no GitHub tags — it ships from main via PyPI. Release history has no 3.x, so no wrapper break has materialized; README recommends pinning `--python 3.11` + `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed`.

Architecture **[DOCUMENTED]** (verified from source):

```
Claude Code ─(MCP / stdio, FastMCP)─ mcp-for-blender Python server (uvx mcp-for-blender)
  ─(TCP JSON {type,params} → {status,result}, default localhost:9876)─
  addon socket server inside Blender ("Interface: MCP for Blender")
    - accepts connections in a daemon thread, queues commands,
      drains them on Blender's MAIN THREAD via a persistent bpy.app.timers callback
      (bpy is not thread-safe); per-command lock; listen backlog 5
```

**GUI Blender is required.** `BlenderMCPServer.start()` opens with a hard refusal under `bpy.app.background` — "cannot start server in background mode (blender -b) - commands would never execute … run Blender with a GUI, or use a virtual display: xvfb-run -a blender" ([addon.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/addon.py), accessed 2026-09-24; the refusal was deliberately introduced by merged PR #272). Consequence: MCP-driven Blender work is an **interactive-workstation pattern**; CI uses the §16 CLI (`blender --background --python`), and the only suggested headless-MCP route is `xvfb-run -a blender` on Linux. There is no tested Windows virtual-display equivalent. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Windows xvfb-equivalent (virtual display driver / scheduled interactive session) for GUI-required addon in CI — unverified; treat as blocked, keep Blender MCP off CI. -->

Tool inventory — **32 `@mcp.tool` functions** on main (2026-09-24); note that third-party directories and early-2026 blogs still describe the outdated 5–6-tool surface ([server.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/src/blender_mcp/server.py), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Core inspection/control | `get_addon_status`, `get_scene_info`, `get_object_info(object_name)`, `get_viewport_screenshot(max_size=1000) -> Image`, `execute_blender_code(code)`, `describe_node_type(bl_idname)` (node socket schemas), `bpy_api_lookup(query)` (runtime bpy API reference search) |
| Export | `export_scene(filepath, format="glb"|"fbx", object_names, selection_only, apply_modifiers=True)` |
| Poly Haven (CC0, no API key) | `get_polyhaven_status`, `get_polyhaven_categories`, `search_polyhaven_assets`, `get_polyhaven_asset_preview`, `download_polyhaven_asset`, `set_texture` |

| Hyper3D Rodin (text/image→3D) | `get_hyper3d_status`, `generate_hyper3d_model_via_text`, `generate_hyper3d_model_via_images`, `poll_rodin_job_status`, `import_generated_asset` |
| Hunyuan3D | `get_hunyuan3d_status`, `generate_hunyuan3d_model`, `poll_hunyuan_job_status`, `import_generated_asset_hunyuan` |
| Misc | `disable_telemetry`, `record_trajectory_feedback` |

`export_scene` parameters (verified on main, 2026-09-24 — main additionally carries a `user_prompt` param added after the 2.0.4 PyPI upload, so pin language to "main, 2026-09-24" when quoting the signature): `filepath` (absolute, `.glb`/`.fbx`, parent folders auto-created), `format` (`"glb"` default | `"fbx"`), `object_names` (export only these, children included; overrides `selection_only`), `selection_only`, `apply_modifiers=True` (set `False` for rigged/shape-key meshes). The addon handler maps it to `bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(..., bake_space_transform=apply_modifiers, use_mesh_modifiers=apply_modifiers)` / `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(..., export_apply=apply_modifiers)`. Returns JSON `{path, bytes, selection_only, object names}`. **For Unity we always export `format="fbx"`** (native FBX import; glb would need the glTF package — §4/§9).

Viewport screenshots work even when Blender's window is not foregrounded: the addon renders the viewport offscreen with `gpu.types.GPUOffScreen.draw_view3d` (window-compositing independent) and falls back to a window grab when no GPU context exists, reporting which path produced the image; the server writes a temp PNG and returns it as an MCP `Image` ([addon.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/addon.py), accessed 2026-09-24). This closes the visual feedback loop for iterative modeling (§17.5.3). Precision: the signature default `max_size` is **1000** (a docstring says 800 — do not cite 800).

**Safe mode** (opt-in, `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=1`; values true/1/yes/on) enables an AST validator before every `execute_blender_code` ([safe_mode.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/src/blender_mcp/safe_mode.py), accessed 2026-09-24): scripts may import only `bpy`, `bmesh`, `mathutils`, and an allowlisted pure-stdlib set (math, cmath, random, colorsys, json, itertools, functools, collections, statistics, string, re, enum, dataclasses, typing, decimal, fractions, textwrap, unicodedata, uuid, copy, heapq, bisect, array — **numpy deliberately absent** because `numpy.load` on pickled .npy is arbitrary deserialization); builtins are deny-by-default (`eval`/`exec`/`compile`/`__import__`/`open`/`input`/`breakpoint`/`globals`/`locals`/`dir`/`help`/`super`/`object`/`memoryview` forbidden; getattr/setattr only with literal names); dunder-ladder attributes blocked; `os`/`subprocess`/`socket`/network blocked; timers/handlers/drivers that persist, class/property registration, and loading external .blend datablocks blocked (e.g. `bpy.utils.modules_from_path`, `script_directory` assignment); blocked operator prefixes cover `bpy.ops.script.*`, `bpy.ops.text.*`, addon-install paths — while **every import/export operator, rendering, saving, and datablock `.load()` stays allowed** ("they are what this tool is for"). Rejected scripts bounce back to the LLM with the reason so it can retry. With the env var unset (the default), `execute_blender_code` runs arbitrary Python unvalidated — safe mode is a project-mandated setting (§17.4.5).

Telemetry: on by default at a minimal anonymous level (random install ID, session ID, tool name, success, duration, mcp-for-blender + Blender versions, OS, timestamp); prompts/code/screenshots/scene data only after explicit opt-in; hard kill switch `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` (or the `disable_telemetry` tool). Configuration: env `BLENDER_HOST` (default localhost), `BLENDER_PORT` (9876), `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE`, plus asset-credential vars (`BLENDERMCP_SKETCHFAB_API_KEY`, `BLENDERMCP_POLYPIZZA_API_KEY`, `BLENDERMCP_HYPER3D_API_KEY`, `BLENDERMCP_HUNYUAN3D_SECRET_ID/SECRET_KEY/API_URL`); CLI `--host`/`--port` override env; multiple Blender instances run side by side on distinct addon ports, one MCP client entry each — and **only one MCP client connection at a time** per instance ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp/main/README.md), accessed 2026-09-24).

Known operational limits (README troubleshooting): the first command after connect is sometimes dropped; complex requests can time out — break work into smaller steps; Poly Haven downloads run on Blender's main thread and freeze the UI (file size ~4x per resolution step — prefer 1k/2k); the Poly Pizza CDN (static.poly.pizza) sits behind Cloudflare bot protection and blocks datacenter/VPN IPs (manual .glb download + File → Import → glTF 2.0 is the workaround). Poly Haven holds ~2,400 CC0 assets with no API key/account/rate-limit concern (models import best from source `.blend`; textures build Principled BSDF; attribution metadata lands as custom properties); Poly Pizza holds ~10,600 low-poly models (~69% CC-BY — filter `licence="CC0"` for attribution-free assets).

#### 17.3.2 The official Blender Lab server

**[DOCUMENTED]** Blender core has no built-in LLM/MCP connectivity and the official stance is external-tools-only: "Blender does not have any built-in functionality for connecting to LLMs." ([blender.org lab page](https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/), accessed 2026-09-24). The Blender Foundation's innovation label **Blender Lab** (announced 2025-11-10 by Francesco Siddi as "an innovation space within the Blender project" — a label, not visibility inside Blender; [devtalk](https://devtalk.blender.org/t/introducing-blender-lab/43260)) hosts **lab/blender_mcp** on projects.blender.org (Gitea): created 2026-02-21, updated 2026-09-11, 25 stars / 23 forks (a drifting live counter — not an adoption signal). Releases: v1.0.0 (2026-04-27), v1.0.2 "MCP SDK Fix" (2026-09-08), **v1.0.3 "Screenshot Fix" (2026-09-11)** shipping `blender-1.0.3.mcpb` (MCP Bundle format for newer clients; the reference client llama.cpp does not support .mcpb yet) and `mcp-1.0.3.zip`. Requires **Blender 5.1+** (our §16 pin of Blender 5.2 LTS — stable since 2026-07-14 per the research digest — satisfies this). Scope is "deliberately small" (scene analysis, data-block renaming, natural-language scene queries, geometry-nodes documentation); same two-component TCP architecture as the community server; reference client llama.cpp (GPL-friendly local-LLM emphasis). Security posture — explicit, and materially worse than the community server's: "The MCP server will execute LLM generated code in Blender without any guards in place to protect your data from removal or being sent to a remote location. To keep your data safe it is recommended to use a virtual machine, or a system without access to sensitive information." The Foundation's 2026 outlook corroborates the external-only direction ("The experiment aims to develop an MCP server for Blender, with communication handled via the existing Python API" — [Projects to Look Forward to in 2026](https://www.blender.org/development/projects-to-look-forward-to-2026/), accessed 2026-09-24). Do not blend the two projects' security stories: official = no guards; ahujasid = opt-in AST sandbox.

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Project decision:** stay on ahujasid mcp-for-blender (Claude-first docs, safe mode, asset integrations, 29k★ vs 25★ traction); track the Lab server quarterly — if it ships in core distributions or adds guards, re-evaluate. The bpy-dev/blender-mcp distribution (94★, created 2026-09-09) is watched as the pattern-proof for headless layering over the official base (`_for_cli` tools operating on .blend files in fresh subprocesses, `BLENDER_MCP_CLI_BACKEND` selecting Blender executable vs the standalone `bpy` pip module) — its ideas, not its 0-star-adjacent maturity, inform §16's hybrid pipeline.

| Project | Stars (2026-09-24) | Character |
|---|---|---|
| arjun988/blender-skills | 214 (TS, v1.3.0, pushed 2026-07-10) | Skill layer, not a server: 94 specialist skill packages for Cursor/Claude Code/Kiro/Codex riding on top of a Blender MCP |
| HoldMyBeer-gg/blend-ai | 145 (pushed 2026-09-21) | 175 tools / 24 modules incl. mesh-quality analysis (non-manifold edges, loose verts, zero-area faces, duplicate verts); sandboxed `execute_blender_code` (blocks os/subprocess/socket; blocks exec/eval/open); render-aware command queueing; Blender 4.2+ extension tested vs 5.1; custom port default 9876 |
| AIGODLIKE/GenesisCore | 136 | One-click installer distribution supporting DeepSeek/Claude et al. (CN community) |
| dhakalnirajan/blender-open-mcp | 119 | Open-models (Ollama) focused variant |

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Selection:** ahujasid mcp-for-blender as the only Blender MCP in the default setup. blend-ai's mesh-quality analysis tools are a noted candidate add-on for §9 asset QA (non-manifold/zero-face checks on exported block meshes) if our own §16 validators prove insufficient — decide at §10 phase P3.

### 17.4 Security model analysis (DevSecOps lens)

#### 17.4.1 Arbitrary code execution surfaces

Every surveyed server grants effectively **arbitrary code execution inside a host process with the developer's full OS privileges** — an MCP client config is equivalent to a shell entry ([CoplayDev README](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp), accessed 2026-09-24). Inventory:

| Surface | Execution primitive | Default auth | Validation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Official assistant MCP (deprecated) | script-editing tools + custom tools | AI-Gateway connections auto-approved; direct external clients need a per-connection approval dialog (remembered) | n/a | Deprecated → `unity mcp` (§17.2.1) |
| `unity mcp` (current official) | exposes `[CliCommand]`s + `unity command eval` (Roslyn, main thread) | token-gated eval; pipeline channel local | n/a | Free, no subscription; CLI-borne |
| CoplayDev | `execute_code`, script tools | localhost; remote-server mode uses API keys | structural validator default; optional Roslyn — **correctness-oriented, not a security boundary** | 47 tools incl. build triggers |
| IvanMurzak | `script-execute` (Roslyn), `reflection-method-call` (any method incl. private) | `MCP_AUTHORIZATION=none` by default on localhost; token/oauth available | none | Editor-only arbitrary exec (verified); runtime mode = reviewed `[AiTool]` code only |
| CoderGamester | tool surface (menu items, scene ops) | HTTP Basic user `mcp-unity` + token; Origin-header handshakes rejected | none | Remote = 0.0.0.0 unencrypted ws:// — VPN/SSH only (we never enable) |
| mcp-for-blender | `execute_blender_code` | none on TCP socket — "anyone who can reach that port can run Python inside Blender" | opt-in AST sandbox (§17.3.1) | README: "**ALWAYS save your work before using it**" |
| Blender Lab (official) | LLM-generated code | none | **none — "without any guards in place"** | Foundation advises a VM/disposable system |

#### 17.4.2 Prompt injection through read channels

MCP read tools (console logs, scene graphs, object names, asset metadata) return content that the agent then reasons over — a classic injection path. Concrete exposures in our stack: (a) Unity console output echoed from play-mode logs; (b) GameObject/scene names and serialized fields read via `get_scene_info`-class tools; (c) **web-sourced asset metadata** — Sketchfab/Poly Pizza model descriptions and Poly Haven attribution fields are third-party text that flows into agent context during §17.5 workflows; (d) our own level JSON if it ever carries free-text fields. Mitigations **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: agents treat all tool-returned content as data (the same discipline the research toolkit's UNTRUSTED DATA banners enforce); destructive operations (`execute_code`, `execute_blender_code`, `batch_execute`, asset deletion) require the human's review in the transcript — the single-operator workflow makes this cheap; safe mode caps the Blender blast radius (no network, no os/subprocess); no secrets exist in either host process (§17.4.4).

#### 17.4.3 Network exposure and the port plan

All adopted components default to loopback binds — keep them there; verify with `netstat -ano | findstr` after setup (Windows). Never port-forward, never disable the CoderGamester Origin check (we do not run that server anyway), never switch IvanMurzak to `0.0.0.0`. Remote access, if ever needed, is SSH-tunnel-only (the mcp-for-blender README's own recommendation).

| Port | Owner | Bind | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9876 (→ 9877…) | mcp-for-blender addon | localhost | Multi-instance = distinct addon ports, one MCP client each (§17.3.1); only one MCP client connection at a time per instance |
| 6400–6499 | CoplayDev Unity↔Python link | 127.0.0.1 | PortManager allocation persisted in `unity-mcp-port.json` |
| 8080/mcp | CoplayDev client-facing HTTP | localhost | <!-- TODO-VERIFY: config.py default is 6500 — confirm actual bind at runtime --> |
| (none) | `unity mcp` | stdio child process | No listening socket; pipeline channel to Editor |
| Named pipe / Unix socket | deprecated official relay | local IPC | Not adopted |

#### 17.4.4 Supply chain, secrets, telemetry

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Rules:** (1) Pin versions — UPM git URL pinned to `#v10.2.0` (not `#main`); PyPI invocations reference `mcp-for-blender` (and we track 2.0.x; the wrapper name is tolerated but not written into new configs); log the pinned hashes via CoplayDev's `get_sha` for scripts that matter. (2) Secrets never live in committed files — the project `.mcp.json` contains only localhost URLs; asset-creation API keys (if ever used) go in user-scope env vars, matching §14/§16 secret hygiene; no keys are required for our adopted workflows (Poly Haven needs none; we do not use Sketchfab/Hyper3D/Hunyuan by default). (3) Telemetry off: `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` in the Blender MCP environment — the minimal anonymous record is unnecessary chatter on a corporate machine. (4) CoplayDev has a SECURITY.md private-reporting channel; subscribe to release notes for the monthly cadence and re-pin deliberately. (5) All MCP packages sit in Editor-only assemblies/assemblies excluded from builds; the Blender addon never exists in any build path; a pre-release checklist item (§20) verifies no `MCPForUnity`/`com.ivanmurzak*`/runtime-mcp remnants in the manifest of release branches.

#### 17.4.5 Project MCP security policy (binding)

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | MCP tooling is dev-time only; nothing ships | Editor-only asmdefs; release-manifest audit (§20 task) |
| 2 | Loopback binds only; no remote MCP ever | netstat check in §17.6 smoke test; configs in repo carry only localhost URLs |
| 3 | `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=1` and `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` always set | Env set in the launcher script + §17.6 verification step |
| 4 | Treat all tool-returned content as untrusted data; human reviews destructive calls | Agent session convention; single-operator review |
| 5 | Versions pinned; upgrades are deliberate | UPM `#v10.2.0`; quarterly review task (§20) |
| 6 | No secrets in Editor/Blender host processes or committed configs | Secret scan in §16 CI |
| 7 | IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP not installed in the shipping project | Manifest audit; exception requires §17.2.3's reviewed-`[AiTool]` path |

### 17.5 Workflow incorporation for this project

#### 17.5.1 Recipe A — level design review loop (Unity)

The canonical MCP loop is the console-read → fix → re-read cycle the Unity blog demonstrates with `Unity_ReadConsole` ([blog, 2026-05-11](https://unity.com/blog/unity-ai-mcp-how-to-get-started), accessed 2026-09-24); we run the same loop with CoplayDev on our levels **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: (1) open the level scene authored via the §5 LevelEditor window; (2) agent pulls state — `get_scene_info`-equivalent scene read + `read_console` + `find_gameobjects` on layer `Water`/`Platform`; (3) agent checks the §5 validation rules (queue mass budget vs platform stability heuristic, waterline clearances, spawn heights) and proposes patches; (4) execute as one `batch_execute` (atomic, with CoplayDev's rollback semantics for its grouped ops) or targeted `manage_gameobject`/`manage_components` calls; (5) `run_tests` fires the EditMode level-validation test suite as an async job (`get_test_job` to poll); (6) `read_console` again — zero errors/failures closes the loop. Budget: minutes per level, applicable across the 200-level content plan (§5) during §10 phases P3–P4.

#### 17.5.2 Recipe B — bulk ScriptableObject content generation: MCP vs C# importer

The 200 `LevelDefinition`/`PieceDefinition` assets (§5) can be produced two ways. Trade-off:

| Dimension | MCP (`manage_scriptable_object` patches) | C# editor importer (JSON → SO, `-executeMethod`) |
|---|---|---|
| Reproducibility | Agent-session-dependent; not byte-stable across runs | Deterministic; same JSON → same assets |
| Reviewability | Patches visible in transcript only | Source JSON diffs in git; assets regenerate |
| Scale to 8×25 levels | Slow, token-costly, error-prone at bulk | One command; CI-replayable (§16) |
| Spot-fix / iteration | Excellent — inspect + patch one asset with `dry_run` | Requires JSON round-trip |
| Agent autonomy | High (agent reads/writes directly) | Low (agent edits JSON instead) |
| Failure mode | Partial application (dry_run mitigates) | Importer validation errors, actionable |

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Decision:** the authoritative source for level content is JSON in git; a C# editor importer (running under §16's batch mode and the §15 CLI) generates/regenerates all ScriptableObjects deterministically; MCP `manage_scriptable_object` is reserved for interactive spot work — inspection, single-field patches, and `dry_run` validation during design sessions. Example patch payload shape (fields per §5's `LevelDefinition`):

```json
{
  "action": "modify",
  "type_name": "AoB.Core.Data.LevelDefinition",
  "target": { "path": "Assets/_Project/ScriptableObjects/Levels/W03/L14.asset" },
  "patches": [
    { "path": "parTimeSeconds", "value": 95 },
    { "path": "waterLevelY", "value": -1.25 },
    { "path": "queuePieces", "value": [
        { "ref": { "guid": "<PieceDefinition guid W3-07>" } },
        { "ref": { "guid": "<PieceDefinition guid B2-loadbreak>" } }
    ]}
  ],
  "dry_run": true
}
```

#### 17.5.3 Recipe C — Blender block-variant modeling sessions

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN] Session protocol** (workstation, GUI Blender open, safe mode on): (1) open the canonical block `.blend` from the §16 source tree; (2) agent reads `get_scene_info`/`get_object_info` for the base block; (3) agent emits parametric `execute_blender_code` in small chunks (the intended usage pattern) — bmesh/modifiers/geometric-variant scripts that safe mode explicitly permits; (4) `get_viewport_screenshot` returns the offscreen render for visual iteration against the §9 art brief (stylized low-poly toy-like blocks); (5) on approval, `export_scene` with `format="fbx"`, `apply_modifiers=True`, `object_names=[...]` writes directly into `Assets/_Project/Art/Models/Blocks/`; Unity's import preset picks it up; (6) the **winning script is frozen and promoted** into §16's `generate_blocks.py` CLI suite (`blender --background --python`) so every variant is regenerable headless in CI — the hybrid author-interactively / regenerate-deterministically pattern. Representative session snippet (illustrative, marked **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; safe-mode-legal — bmesh + mathutils only):

```python
import bpy, bmesh
from mathutils import Vector

obj = bpy.context.active_object
bm = bmesh.new()
bm.from_mesh(obj.data)
# Bevel top edge ring of the 1x1 block variant "square_r1"
for e in bm.edges:
    if abs(e.verts[0].co.z - e.verts[1].co.z) < 1e-6 and abs(e.verts[0].co.z - 0.5) < 1e-6:
        bm.edges.ensure_lookup_table()
        e.select_set(True)
bmesh.ops.bevel(bm, geom=[e for e in bm.edges if e.select], offset=0.04, segments=2)
bm.to_mesh(obj.data)
bm.free()
```

The `bpy_api_lookup` and `describe_node_type` tools cut hallucinated enums/socket orders during these sessions — a documented differentiator of keeping MCP in the loop for exploratory work.

#### 17.5.4 Recipe D — automated screenshot QA of scenes

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** Visual smoke capture runs on the workstation (not CI — CI uses headless assertions per §16): after loading a level scene or a play-mode run, the agent triggers `screenshot-scene-view` / `screenshot-game-view` (IvanMurzak tool names — available in that server; on our CoplayDev-only default this recipe instead uses the §15 `unity command` channel with a small `[CliCommand]` capture wrapper, same pattern as §17.5.5) and Blender-side `get_viewport_screenshot` for asset turntables. The agent checks each capture against a written checklist (water plane visible and calm-colored per §9 palette; queue UI present; no magenta/missing-material; safe-area margins respected on the target aspect) and files failures as console-annotated notes. This is a triage pass, not a pixel test — pixel-diff regression stays in §14's test suite.

#### 17.5.5 Custom exposed command — level audit via the Unity CLI/MCP path

One implementation, two consumption paths (`unity command` from §15 scripts, and as an MCP tool via `unity mcp`). Skeleton per the documented `[CliCommand]`/`[CliArg]` auto-discovery API (namespace `Unity.Pipeline.Commands`), Editor-only, unity-game-dev-expert conventions:

```csharp
using System.Text;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEngine;
using Unity.Pipeline.Commands;

namespace AoB.EditorTools.PipelineCommands
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Editor-exposed CLI/MCP commands for auditing level content.
    /// Auto-discovered by com.unity.pipeline; callable via `unity command aob-level-audit`
    /// and exposed as an MCP tool through `unity mcp`.
    /// </summary>
    public static class LevelAuditCommands
    {
        #region Commands

        [CliCommand("aob-level-audit", "Validates LevelDefinition assets against the §5 content rules and returns a report.")]
        public static string AuditLevels(
            [CliArg("world", "World index to audit (-1 for all worlds)")] int world = -1)
        {
            var report = new StringBuilder();
            int failures = LevelAuditRunner.RunAudit(world, report);
            Debug.Log($"[aob-level-audit] {report}");
            return failures == 0 ? "PASS" : $"FAIL: {failures} rule violation(s)";
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

`LevelAuditRunner` reuses the exact validation code paths as the §5 LevelEditor window and the EditMode tests (queue mass budget vs platform stability heuristic, waterline clearance, piece-reference integrity) so the agent, the editor UI, CI, and the test suite all enforce one rule set. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact [CliCommand]/[CliArg] attribute signatures and namespace spelling against the installed com.unity.pipeline version; the older [McpTool(name, description)] + McpToolRegistry API applies only to the deprecated assistant server (§17.2.1). -->

#### 17.5.6 MCP vs CLI — the decision table

| Task | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive console-fix loop, scene tweaking by prompt | **MCP** (CoplayDev) | Read–think–act loop needs the agent inside the Editor |
| Iterative block-shape modeling with visual feedback | **MCP** (mcp-for-blender) | Screenshots + live scene state; `bpy_api_lookup` cuts hallucinations |
| Bulk SO generation from JSON | **CLI/C# importer** (§16) | Deterministic, reviewable, CI-replayable (§17.5.2) |
| CI builds, tests, FBX export batches | **CLI** (§15/§16) | No GUI, no sockets, no LLM; addon refuses `blender -b` |
| Quick Editor probe ("what's the player version?") | **`unity command eval`** (§15) | Roslyn REPL, no recompile, lighter than an MCP round-trip |
| Exposing project commands to agents | **`[CliCommand]` + `unity mcp`** | Official, free, one code path (§17.5.5) |
| In-game/runtime debugging | Reviewed `[AiTool]` code (IvanMurzak pattern) if ever adopted | Verified: no built-in arbitrary exec in players (§17.2.3) |

### 17.6 Setup files and smoke test

**Unity side (CoplayDev).** Add the package by UPM git URL pinned to the release tag: `https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp.git?path=/MCPForUnity#v10.2.0` in Package Manager → Add package from git URL. Run the setup wizard, then `Window → MCP for Unity → Configure All Detected Clients` — Claude Code auto-connects after configuration ([install docs](https://coplaydev.github.io/unity-mcp/getting-started/install/), accessed 2026-09-24). The committed project `.mcp.json` (documented client config, HTTP default):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "unityMCP": { "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp" }
  }
}
```

Stdio alternative (documented; on Windows GUI clients need the absolute uvx path, e.g. `C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Links/uvx.exe`, or wrap via `cmd /c uvx` to avoid `spawn uvx ENOENT`): server command `uvx --from mcpforunityserver mcp-for-unity --transport stdio`. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact `claude mcp add` spelling for an HTTP-transport server entry (the research notes document the wizard, the JSON config, and the stdio uvx command, but not Claude Code's HTTP add flag); confirm with `claude mcp add --help`. -->

**Unity side (official complement).** With the Unity CLI installed (§15): `unity pipeline install` (adds com.unity.pipeline to the project), then `unity mcp configure --list` and configure the Claude Code client. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact client slug for Claude Code in `unity mcp configure <client>` (notes list "claude, claude code, cursor, vscode, windsurf, codex…" without the exact token); read it from `unity mcp configure --list`. -->

**Blender side (mcp-for-blender).** Install uv on Windows: `powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"` and ensure `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` is on PATH. Addon: `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon`, then Blender → Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → enable **"Interface: MCP for Blender"**. Start: 3D viewport → N-key → "MCP for Blender" tab → **Start MCP Server** (auto-start option exists via the `blendermcp_auto_start_server` scene property; port property `blendermcp_port`; port-in-use detection skips auto-start). Claude Code registration (documented):

```bash
claude mcp add blender uvx mcp-for-blender
# Claude Desktop settings JSON (Settings → Developer → Edit Config):
# { "mcpServers": { "blender": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["mcp-for-blender"] } } }
# Codex: codex mcp add blender -- uvx mcp-for-blender
```

Launch the addon with safe mode + telemetry off **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: set `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=1` and `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` in the environment before starting Blender (launcher script), keeping the default `localhost:9876`.

**Smoke test procedure** (run after any fresh clone/machine setup; expected result per step):

1. Unity Editor open on the project; `Window → MCP for Unity` shows the bridge connected and the instance registered (`unity-mcp-port.json` exists under the project; port in 6400–6499). 
2. In Claude Code, ask: "Read the Unity console" → expect a `read_console` tool result with current log lines. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: step 2 also confirms the actual client-facing port (8080 vs 6500, §17.4.3). -->
3. Ask: "Create a throwaway test SO via manage_scriptable_object with dry_run=true" → expect a validation report, no asset written; then a real create + delete round-trip in a scratch folder.
4. `unity mcp` path: `unity status` shows the connected Editor; `unity command aob-level-audit --result-only` returns `PASS` once §17.5.5's command exists.
5. Blender open with the addon started; in Claude Code: "Call get_addon_status" → expect connected status on port 9876.
6. "Call get_scene_info" then "take a viewport screenshot" → expect scene listing and a returned image (GPUOffScreen path when backgrounded).
7. Safe-mode check: ask the agent to run `execute_blender_code` containing `import os` → expect a rejection message listing the reason (safe mode active), not execution.
8. Network check: `netstat -ano | findstr "9876 6400 8080"` → every listed bind is on the loopback interface; no 0.0.0.0 entries.
9. Env check: confirm `BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE` and `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` are set in the Blender process environment (launcher script prints them).
10. Export round-trip: `export_scene` a block as FBX into `Assets/_Project/Art/Models/Blocks/SmokeTest/` → Unity imports it without warnings; then delete the test folder.

Failure notes (documented behaviors): only one MCP client may be connected to a Blender instance at a time (do not run Claude Desktop and Claude Code against the same addon); the first command after connect is sometimes dropped — retry once; complex single requests time out — decompose; if Unity's CoplayDev client fails to connect, re-run the client configuration wizard and confirm the port from step 2. Task IDs for this setup and the quarterly version re-pin live in §20; risk entries for MCP/CLI tool maturity live in §21.

## 18. Multiplatform Master Reference — iOS & Android

**Section scope:** everything needed to take the Art of Balance clone (Unity 6000.6.x, URP, Input System, 2D-physics core per §6) from "runs on my dev machine" to "shippable on Google Play and the iOS App Store": Player Settings, Xcode and Gradle layers, signing, store submission, safe area, touch integration, mobile UI scaling, performance/thermal budgets, and the device test matrix. All facts carry the research provenance of the 2026-09-24 sweep; where the adversarial verify pass corrected the sweep, the correction is marked **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** and wins. In the v1 target order (Windows+macOS/Steam → Android → iOS → Xbox, per §2), Android and iOS are the second and third ports — this section is written to be executed twice, once per platform, against the already-hardened Steam build.

Build-host consequence, stated once and binding for §16's CI: **the iOS build is a macOS-hosted workflow.** IL2CPP cross-compilation is generally unsupported — "to build an IL2CPP Player for a particular platform you must build from an Editor running on the same platform" ([Unity 6.3 Manual: IL2CPP introduction](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html), accessed 2026-09-24) — and Unity's own iOS build docs frame the pipeline as macOS + Xcode, with Unity Build Automation as the cloud alternative ([Unity Manual: Build an iOS application](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/iphone-BuildProcess.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Android builds run anywhere (Windows CI included). Plan the build matrix accordingly: Windows runner → Win64 + Android; macOS runner → iOS (+ macOS per §19).

### 18.1 Platform strategy recap for mobile

- **What ships on mobile:** the full Arcade experience — 8 worlds × 25 levels (§5), Endurance, Infinity, and single-device 2-player Swift Stacker (split-screen is out on phones; Tower Tumble pass-and-play remains viable) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — see §3 for mode parameterization. Online features are v1-out on mobile (§2 non-goals).
- **Leaderboards are local-only on mobile v1** (top-N per level/mode stored in the save file, §6). No Play Games Services / Game Center in v1. This decision cascades everywhere: no network permission, no account system, a trivially clean Data-safety form (§18.12), and no online-cert review surface **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.
- **Monetization:** premium, one-time purchase, matching the original's $6.99–$8.99 positioning (§1). No ads, no IAP — which keeps the entire ads/IAP compliance surface out of scope.
- **Orientation:** Portrait + Landscape Left + Landscape Right supported; Portrait-upside-down excluded. The basin framing camera (§6) reframes per aspect via the Canvas Scaler + camera letterboxing strategy defined in §9 **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.
- **Minimum OS:** iOS 15 (Unity 6.6's floor — setting `Target Minimum iOS Version` below 15 is unsupported); Android min API 24 (Android 7.0) chosen to cover effectively the entire active install base while allowing modern APIs (Vulkan, ASTC) on the median device; target API 36 forced by Play policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (floor choice) + ([Play Console Help](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878), accessed 2026-09-24) (ceiling).

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: Android API-24 minimum — re-check Play Console's device-distribution pane at P5 entry (distribution data was not part of the 2026-09-24 research sweep) and raise the floor if the <API-24 tail is negligible for puzzle audiences. -->
