### 18.2 iOS Player Settings — complete set-list

Every field we touch, the value we set, and why. All field descriptions verified against the Unity 6.6 (6000.6) Player Settings reference ([class-PlayerSettingsiOS](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

| Group | Field | Our value | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identification | Company Name / Product Name | as shipped | Feeds default bundle id |
| Identification | Bundle Identifier | `com.<studio>.artofbalance` (reverse-DNS, no wildcards) | Wildcard ids would force disabling "Automatically add capabilities" |
| Identification | Version / Build | `1.0.0` / auto-increment from CI (`CFBundleShortVersionString` / `CFBundleVersion`) | Build number must monotonically increase per upload |
| Configuration | Architecture | **ARM64** (the only option) | "Only ARM64 is available for iOS" |
| Configuration | Simulator Architecture | ARM64 (x86_64/Universal deprecated) | Apple-silicon Macs; deprecated options exit the toolchain soon |
| Configuration | Target SDK | **Device SDK** (Simulator SDK only for editor-loop tests) | Ship builds target hardware |
| Configuration | Target Minimum iOS Version | **15.0** | Unity 6.6 floor is iOS 15; Apple's store floor (13) is looser, so Unity's binds |
| Configuration | Scripting Backend | **IL2CPP** | The iOS backend; Mono is not offered for iOS device builds |
| Configuration | IL2CPP Code Generation | Faster runtime (ship) / Faster (smaller) builds (dev) | Master-class runtime perf at ship |
| Configuration | C++ Compiler Configuration | **Master** for release archives | Unity's own ship recommendation (MSVC-analog LTCG-class opts in Xcode) |
| Configuration | Api Compatibility Level | .NET Standard 2.1 | Current Unity 6.x TFM; Newtonsoft and all deps conform |
| Configuration | Active Input Handling | **Both** → defines `ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` + `ENABLE_LEGACY_INPUT_MANAGER` (§4.8) | Input System is a built-in module in 6.6; no package in manifest; no legacy input in first-party code (§7); Both is §4.8's transitional setting — flip to Input System only after the §14 supply-chain audit confirms no legacy Input consumers (§20 P2.E9-automation-ci.10) |
| Configuration | Application Entry (n/a iOS) | — | Android-only concept, see 18.9 |
| Rendering | Graphics APIs | **Metal** (default; do not add GLES) | Apple rejects GLES apps at review; Unity defaults to Metal |
| Rendering | Metal API Validation | Editor-only debugging aid; off for CI | Apple-side validation comes from Xcode Run scheme = Debug (18.8) |
| Rendering | Metal Write-Only Backbuffer (`frameBufferOnly`) | Enabled (default) | Perf; we do not sample the backbuffer |
| Rendering | Force hard shadows on Metal | off | Our shadow strategy is tier-driven (§9) |
| Rendering | Render Extra Frame on Pause | **Enabled** (default) | Keeps the pause menu composited correctly on iOS suspend |
| Rendering | Memoryless Render Textures | Enabled (default) | Free perf on Tile-based GPUs; URP uses them internally |
| Resolution | Enable ProMotion Support | **off** (default) for v1 | 60 Hz cap is the battery-correct choice for a calm puzzle game; revisit for 120 Hz menus **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Resolution | Aspect Ratio Mode / orientations | via Info.plist: Portrait + Landscape L/R; upside-down excluded | See 18.4; `UIRequiresFullScreen` interplay |
| Behaviour | Adjust iOS FPS based on thermal state | **Enabled** (default: Serious → 30 FPS, Critical → 15 FPS) | Documented defaults are exactly the graceful-degradation ladder we want; do not fight thermal state |
| Behaviour | Defer system gestures on edges | Enabled in Gameplay | Prevents an edge-swipe from invoking Control Center mid-placement |
| Behaviour | Hide home button on iPhone X+ | Enabled in Gameplay state only | Keeps the indicator from overlapping the queue UI |
| Behaviour | Requires ARKit support | off | No AR |
| Behaviour | Enable Custom Background Behaviors | off | We handle suspend/resume via Unity lifecycle (§6 SaveSystem autosave hook) |
| Signing | Signing Team ID | Studio Apple Developer team ID | Required for automatic signing + Build And Run |
| Signing | Automatically Sign | **on** (local dev + Xcode archives) | Manual signing reserved for CI keychain profiles (18.6) |
| Signing | Automatically add capabilities | **on** | Generates entitlements; must be **disabled** only for enterprise certs or wildcard bundle ids (not our case) |
| Debug | Script Call Optimization | Fast but no exceptions (ship) / Slow and Safe (dev) | Release hygiene <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Script Call Optimization option names ("Fast but no exceptions" / "Slow and Safe") are not in the T07 Player Settings field inventory (track-t07-mobile-platforms.md) — verify against class-PlayerSettingsiOS --> |
| Debug | Metal API Validation / stack traces | per-build profile | Dev profiles only |
| Other | Xcode project type | **Objective-C** (default) | Swift template is Experimental in 6.6; do not ship on it |
| Other | Variant map for app slicing | off | App thinning handled by App Store from the single archive; no ODR v1 (§18.12) |

Per-platform scripting defines (set in the platform Build Profile, §4): `UNITY_IOS;ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM;AOB_MOBILE` — `AOB_MOBILE` gates the touch provider registration and mobile-only UI (§7). 

### 18.3 iOS build path and the Windows-editor question

The pipeline, stated as a hard rule with its evidence:

1. **Unity-side build runs on macOS.** The IL2CPP same-platform rule ("cross-compilation is generally not supported… you must build from an Editor running on the same platform", [Unity 6.3 IL2CPP introduction](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html), accessed 2026-09-24) plus Unity's documented iOS workflow (macOS + Xcode; cloud alternative Unity Build Automation, [Build an iOS application](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/iphone-BuildProcess.html), accessed 2026-09-24) make the macOS host non-negotiable for CI. Daily development still happens on Windows (play in editor, Android device builds); only the iOS build step lands on a Mac runner or mac mini (§16).
2. **Unity generates an Xcode project; it does not produce the IPA.** Build Profiles (§4) → iOS → Build writes the project; **Build And Run** installs to a tethered device. Repeated builds default to **Append** mode — custom native code in the `Classes/` subdirectory survives; **Replace** wipes the folder. Append is only supported between identical Unity iOS versions ([class-PlayerSettingsiOS](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html), accessed 2026-09-24). CI consequence: every build job starts from a clean generated project — never rely on Append state.
3. **The Xcode project is the integration point.** Everything Apple-specific (signing, capabilities, Info.plist keys, privacy manifest, frameworks) is either generated by Unity or applied by our post-processor (18.4) at generation time — never hand-edited, because CI regenerates it.

### 18.4 Xcode post-processing — `iOSPostProcessor` (editor C#)

Unity's current API surface for this lives in `UnityEditor.iOS.Xcode` ([PBXProject](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/iOS.Xcode.PBXProject.html), [ProjectCapabilityManager](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/iOS.Xcode.ProjectCapabilityManager.html), Unity 6.6 ScriptReference, accessed 2026-09-24). One static editor class owns all mutations; it runs after every iOS build, is version-controlled, and is the only sanctioned place native settings change.

Load-bearing API notes from the ScriptReference:

- `PBXProject.GetPBXProjectPath(pathToBuiltProject)` → `ReadFromFile` → mutate → `WriteToFile`; target GUIDs via `GetUnityMainTargetGuid()` / `GetUnityFrameworkTargetGuid()` / `GetUnityAPITargetGuid()`.
- Frameworks: `AddFrameworkToProject(targetGuid, "FrameworkName", weak: false)`.
- Build settings: `AddBuildPropertyForConfig` / `SetBuildProperty` (+ `ForConfig` variants) using suffixed setting names to scope to the app (`APP_`) or framework (`FRAMEWORK_`) targets — the documented mechanism for per-target values.
- Files: `AddFile` → `AddFileToBuild` (used below to register the privacy manifest into the bundle).
- `ProjectCapabilityManager(capabilityPath, entitlementsFileName, targetGuid)` then `Add<Capability>()`; **wrap every call in try-catch** — repeated calls throw (documented note). ~55 `Add*` methods exist (GameCenter, GameControllers, iCloud, PushNotifications, SignInWithApple, …). **v1 adds none** — no Game Center, no iCloud (leaderboards local, §18.1) — the try/catch block below is where they would land post-v1.

```csharp
#if UNITY_IOS || UNITY_EDITOR
using System.IO;
using System.Xml;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEditor.Callbacks;
using UnityEditor.iOS.Xcode;

namespace Aob.Platform.iOS
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Single integration point for all post-generation mutations of the
    /// Unity-produced Xcode project. Runs in the Unity Editor on the macOS
    /// build host after every iOS build. Never hand-edit the generated
    /// project — change this class, rebuild, review the diff in git.
    /// </summary>
    public static class iOSPostProcessor
    {
        private const string EntitlementsFileName = "artofbalance.entitlements";
        private const string PrivacyManifestFileName = "PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy";

        #region Entry Point

        [PostProcessBuild(1)]
        public static void OnPostprocessBuild(BuildTarget buildTarget, string pathToBuiltProject)
        {
            if (buildTarget != BuildTarget.iOS)
            {
                return;
            }

            string projectPath = PBXProject.GetPBXProjectPath(pathToBuiltProject);
            var project = new PBXProject();
            project.ReadFromFile(projectPath);

            string mainGuid = project.GetUnityMainTargetGuid();
            string frameworkGuid = project.GetUnityFrameworkTargetGuid();

            PinBuildSettings(project, mainGuid, frameworkGuid);
            AddSystemFrameworksIfNeeded(project, mainGuid);
            ApplyCapabilities(pathToBuiltProject, mainGuid);
            PatchInfoPlist(pathToBuiltProject);

            project.WriteToFile(projectPath);

            WritePrivacyManifest(pathToBuiltProject, project, mainGuid);
        }

        #endregion

        #region Build Settings

        /// <summary>
        /// Pins Xcode build settings we require. Suffixed setting names scope
        /// values to the app target (APP_) or framework target (FRAMEWORK_).
        /// </summary>
        private static void PinBuildSettings(PBXProject project, string mainGuid, string frameworkGuid)
        {
            // Bitcode is dead; assert no template remnant re-enables it.
            // TODO-VERIFY: bitcode references were absent from 2026-09 research notes —
            // confirm ENABLE_BITCODE is unset (not merely "NO") in the generated project.
            project.AddBuildPropertyForConfig(mainGuid, "ENABLE_BITCODE", "NO");

            // Ship configuration mirrors Unity's "Master" C++ recommendation (18.2).
            project.AddBuildPropertyForConfig(mainGuid, "GCC_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL", "s");
            project.AddBuildPropertyForConfig(mainGuid, "LLVM_LTO", "YES");

            // CI signs via a stored distribution identity; local dev uses automatic signing.
            // The signing style itself is set here so the project never defaults to
            // "manual" with a mismatched profile in cloud builds.
            project.AddBuildPropertyForConfig(mainGuid, "CODE_SIGN_STYLE", System.Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AOB_CI") == "1" ? "Manual" : "Automatic");
        }

        #endregion

        #region Frameworks

        private static void AddSystemFrameworksIfNeeded(PBXProject project, string mainGuid)
        {
            // v1 needs nothing beyond Unity's defaults: no GameKit (no Game Center),
            // no GameController.framework (Input System's iOS rumble path needs Unity
            // 6000.7+ anyway — see 18.14), no CoreBluetooth. Kept as the canonical
            // pattern for when a capability lands post-v1:
            // project.AddFrameworkToProject(mainGuid, "GameKit.framework", false);
            _ = mainGuid;
        }

        #endregion

        #region Capabilities / Entitlements

        private static void ApplyCapabilities(string pathToBuiltProject, string mainGuid)
        {
            string capabilityPath = Path.Combine(pathToBuiltProject, "Entitlements.plist");
            var capabilities = new ProjectCapabilityManager(capabilityPath, EntitlementsFileName, mainGuid);

            try
            {
                // v1: intentionally empty. All Add* calls (AddGameCenter,
                // AddGameControllers, AddiCloud, AddPushNotifications, ...) belong
                // here, each individually try-caught — repeat calls throw.
            }
            catch (System.Exception e)
            {
                UnityEngine.Debug.LogError($"[iOSPostProcessor] capability application failed: {e.Message}");
            }
            finally
            {
                capabilities.WriteToFile();
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Info.plist

        private static void PatchInfoPlist(string pathToBuiltProject)
        {
            string plistPath = Path.Combine(pathToBuiltProject, "Info.plist");
            var plist = new PlistDocument();
            plist.ReadFromFile(plistPath);

            // Orientations: Portrait + Landscape L/R; upside-down portrait excluded.
            var orientations = plist.root.CreateArray("UISupportedInterfaceOrientations");
            orientations.AddString("UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait");
            orientations.AddString("UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft");
            orientations.AddString("UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight");

            // Full-screen only for v1: a physics puzzle must not be resized by
            // Split View mid-stack. [ORIGINAL DESIGN] — revisit with §3 if a
            // resize-safe pause-and-reframe loop is added.
            plist.root.SetBoolean("UIRequiresFullScreen", true);

            plist.WriteToFile(plistPath);
        }

        #endregion

        #region Privacy Manifest

        /// <summary>
        /// Writes the app-level PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. The Unity ENGINE's own
        /// required-reason declarations are auto-included since Editors
        /// 2021.3.35f1 / 2022.3.18f1 / 2023.2.7f1; this file covers OUR code only.
        /// </summary>
        private static void WritePrivacyManifest(string pathToBuiltProject, PBXProject project, string mainGuid)
        {
            string manifestPath = Path.Combine(pathToBuiltProject, PrivacyManifestFileName);
            var doc = new XmlDocument();
            doc.AppendChild(doc.CreateXmlDeclaration("1.0", "UTF-8", null));
            XmlElement plist = doc.CreateElement("plist");
            plist.SetAttribute("version", "1.0");
            doc.AppendChild(plist);
            XmlElement dict = doc.CreateElement("dict");
            plist.AppendChild(dict);

            // No tracking, no collected data: local-only leaderboards, no network
            // permission, no ads/analytics (18.1, 18.12).
            AppendKeyValue(doc, dict, "NSPrivacyTracking", "false", "NSPrivacyTracking");

            // Accessed APIs: our code path uses PlayerPrefs (settings, §6) → the
            // UserDefaults category, reason CA92.1. We deliberately avoid
            // File/Directory timestamp APIs in C# (no save-slot sorting by mtime)
            // so no file-timestamp declaration is required from the app layer.
            // TODO-VERIFY: exact top-level key spelling (NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes /
            // NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes / NSPrivacyTrackingDomains) against the
            // current Apple privacy-manifest spec at submission time.
            XmlElement apis = AppendKeyValueArray(doc, dict, "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes");
            XmlElement api0 = doc.CreateElement("dict");
            apis.AppendChild(api0);
            AppendKeyValue(doc, api0, "NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType", "NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults", "value");
            AppendKeyValueArrayValue(doc, api0, "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons", "CA92.1");

            doc.Save(manifestPath);

            // Register the manifest into the app bundle via the project.
            string fileGuid = project.AddFile(PrivacyManifestFileName, PrivacyManifestFileName);
            project.AddFileToBuild(mainGuid, fileGuid);
            // NOTE: WriteToFile already ran in OnPostprocessBuild; this class
            // re-writes below to persist the file registration.
            string projectPath = PBXProject.GetPBXProjectPath(pathToBuiltProject);
            project.WriteToFile(projectPath);
        }

        #endregion

        #region XML helpers

        private static void AppendKeyValue(XmlDocument doc, XmlElement dict, string key, string value, string valueElementName)
        {
            XmlElement k = doc.CreateElement("key");
            k.InnerText = key;
            dict.AppendChild(k);
            XmlElement v = doc.CreateElement(valueElementName == "NSPrivacyTracking" ? "false" : "string");
            if (valueElementName != "NSPrivacyTracking")
            {
                v.InnerText = value;
            }
            dict.AppendChild(v);
        }

        private static XmlElement AppendKeyValueArray(XmlDocument doc, XmlElement dict, string key)
        {
            XmlElement k = doc.CreateElement("key");
            k.InnerText = key;
            dict.AppendChild(k);
            XmlElement array = doc.CreateElement("array");
            dict.AppendChild(array);
            return array;
        }

        private static void AppendKeyValueArrayValue(XmlDocument doc, XmlElement dict, string key, string value)
        {
            XmlElement k = doc.CreateElement("key");
            k.InnerText = key;
            dict.AppendChild(k);
            XmlElement array = doc.CreateElement("array");
            XmlElement s = doc.CreateElement("string");
            s.InnerText = value;
            array.AppendChild(s);
            dict.AppendChild(array);
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
#endif
```

Privacy-manifest facts driving the code above ([Unity Manual: Apple privacy manifest policy](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/apple-privacy-manifest-policy.html), accessed 2026-09-24):

- Unity's engine auto-declares (since 2021.3.35f1 / 2022.3.18f1 / 2023.2.7f1): UserDefaults **CA92.1** (PlayerPrefs), File timestamp **0A2A.1** (C# timestamp APIs) + **C617.1** (file checks), System boot time **35F9.1** (event timing), Disk space **E174.1** (AssetBundle disk checks).
- The app must declare its **own** collected data and any required-reason API its **own** C# calls hit — the enumerated Unity list covers `File/Directory.GetCreationTime/GetLastAccessTime/GetLastWriteTime[+Utc]` and `FileInfo/DirectoryInfo` `.CreationTime/.LastAccessTime/.LastWriteTime[+Utc]`. Our save system (§6) writes/reads JSON only and sorts by an in-file timestamp field, so the app-level manifest stays at UserDefaults/CA92.1. **Coding rule for the whole team: no C# file-timestamp APIs on Apple platforms without updating `WritePrivacyManifest`.**
- Third-party SDKs must ship their own manifests — with v1's zero-SDK dependency list this is vacuously satisfied; re-audit if a mobile SDK is ever added (§21 risk).
- macOS is exempt from required-reason declarations (matters for §19, not here).

### 18.5 Xcode project + scheme settings we pin

### 18.6 Signing, provisioning, and App Store Connect submission

**Signing model (Apple-side mechanics = standard Apple flow; Unity-side settings = documented):**

- **Certificates:** Apple Development (device installs during development) and Apple Distribution (App Store archives) from the studio Apple Developer Program account. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: certificate/profile lifecycle details were outside the 2026-09 research sweep; follow Apple Developer docs at setup time. -->
- **Local dev:** Player Settings → Signing Team ID + Automatically Sign + Automatically add capabilities **on** — documented behavior ([class-PlayerSettingsiOS](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html), accessed 2026-09-24). The auto-capabilities path generates an entitlements file and would add Game Center if detected; disable it only for enterprise certificates or wildcard bundle ids (neither applies).
- **CI:** distribution identity + provisioning profile imported into the runner keychain as secrets (base64 at rest, §16); `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual` via the `AOB_CI` branch of 18.4. The profile is a standard App Store profile for the explicit bundle id.
- Unity-side signing config is stored per-project/machine (the Android analog is documented in 18.11); treat Xcode-side signing as the source of truth for iOS.

**Submission flow (v1):**

1. macOS runner builds the archive from the generated project (§16); `xcodebuild archive` + export to IPA. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact export-plist keys not captured in research notes; standard App Store method. -->
2. Upload via **Xcode Organizer** (documented primary path, [iphone-BuildProcess](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/iphone-BuildProcess.html), accessed 2026-09-24) or Apple's **Transporter** app / App Store Connect API (Transporter/ASC-API existence noted in research; current tool detail not re-verified — same caveat the track recorded). CI uses the ASC API path via `altool`-successor tooling <!-- TODO-VERIFY: current upload binary name/flags -->.
3. App Store Connect: create the app record (bundle id, name, primary locale), fill the privacy "nutrition" labels (mirror of 18.4: no collection, no tracking), screenshots per required device class, age rating questionnaire, description/keywords.
4. **TestFlight:** internal testers (build arrives in minutes) for the P5 hardening pass; external beta before review if desired.
5. Submit for App Store review. Rejection surfaces to plan for (from the documented Unity manifest guidance): missing required-reason declarations — our 18.4 manifest plus the engine's auto-included declarations cover the enumerated set ([apple-privacy-manifest-policy](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/apple-privacy-manifest-policy.html), accessed 2026-09-24).
6. Phased 7-day release, then full. Post-launch: the April-2027 SDK-floor shift (18.0) forces an Xcode 27 rebuild for the first post-April-2027 update — already a §21 risk row.

### 18.7 Safe-area implementation — `SafeAreaFitter`

The verified API contract: `Screen.safeArea` is a `Rect` with **bottom-left origin**, already folding in notches, cutouts, and TV overscan; max value is the full screen; on Android it interacts with `renderOutsideSafeArea` (disabled → player window is resized to the safe area and `safeArea` then typically returns full-screen). Coordinates invert for UI Toolkit (top-left origin) but match uGUI RectTransforms directly ([Screen-safeArea](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Screen-safeArea.html), accessed 2026-09-24).

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Aob.Platform
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Fits a root RectTransform into Screen.safeArea. Attach to the root of each
    /// full-screen canvas (HUD, menus). uGUI shares safeArea's bottom-left origin,
    /// so the rect maps onto anchors with no axis flip. Re-applies on rect change
    /// (rotation, Split View, stage changes on iPad).
    /// </summary>
    [RequireComponent(typeof(RectTransform))]
    [DisallowMultipleComponent]
    public sealed class SafeAreaFitter : MonoBehaviour
    {
        #region Private Fields

        private RectTransform _rectTransform;
        private Rect _appliedSafeArea = Rect.zero;
        private const float MinSizeEpsilon = 1f; // px; ignore sub-pixel safe-area noise

        #endregion

        #region Unity Lifecycle

        private void OnEnable()
        {
            _rectTransform = (RectTransform)transform;
            ApplySafeArea();
        }

        private void OnRectTransformDimensionsChange()
        {
            // Fires on orientation change / canvas resize; safeArea may lag one
            // frame, so apply defensively each time dimensions change.
            if (isActiveAndEnabled)
            {
                ApplySafeArea();
            }
        }

        private void Update()
        {
            // Cheap equality check only; no allocations. Catches Dynamic Island
            // inset changes on rotation that skip OnRectTransformDimensionsChange.
            if (Screen.safeArea != _appliedSafeArea)
            {
                ApplySafeArea();
            }
        }

        #endregion

        #region Private Methods

        private void ApplySafeArea()
        {
            Rect safe = Screen.safeArea;

            if (safe.width < MinSizeEpsilon || safe.height < MinSizeEpsilon)
            {
                return; // degenerate rect during transitions
            }

            _appliedSafeArea = safe;

            Vector2 anchorMin = safe.position;
            Vector2 anchorMax = safe.position + safe.size;
            _rectTransform.anchorMin = new Vector2(anchorMin.x / Screen.width, anchorMin.y / Screen.height);
            _rectTransform.anchorMax = new Vector2(anchorMax.x / Screen.width, anchorMax.y / Screen.height);
            _rectTransform.offsetMin = Vector2.zero;
            _rectTransform.offsetMax = Vector2.zero;
        }

        #endregion
    }
}
```

Usage rules: `SafeAreaFitter` sits on the **content root inside the scaled canvas**, above the Canvas Scaler node (18.14), so insets land in reference-resolution units. Full-bleed backgrounds (water gradient, §9) intentionally sit **outside** the fitted root. TV-overscan protection is inherited for free on Apple TV-class displays per the documented semantics; §9 adds a ~10% title-safe inset on top for critical HUD (industry convention).

### 18.8 iOS device matrix, performance targets, and Instruments

**Device matrix [ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (research captured no Apple device-distribution data; tiers are engineering classes, not market claims):

| Tier | Class (SoC-era proxy) | Representative devices | Target | Quality tier (§9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iOS-min | Oldest iOS-15-capable class (2015–2017 phones, 6th-gen-class iPads) | A9–A10 era | 60 fps gameplay, 30 fps tolerated under Critical thermal | Mobile Low: render scale 0.75, no postFX, shadows off |
| iOS-mid | A12–A14 era (2018–2020) | iPhone XR–12 class | 60 fps | Mobile Base: render scale 1.0, minimal postFX |
| iOS-high | A15+ (2021+) incl. ProMotion hw | iPhone 13+ / iPad M-class | 60 fps (120 future-gated, 18.2) | Mobile High: full postFX, water refraction on |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: map tier proxies to concrete currently-sold models + a TestFlight device pool at P5; Apple hardware matrix was outside research scope. -->

**Performance targets [ORIGINAL DESIGN]:** the binding budgets are §14.2's — §14's intro makes §14's numbers the budgets this section must hit. Frame split per §14.2.1's mobile rows (Android upper-mid / iOS A15-class): 16.67 ms at 60 fps = 3.0 ms sim (240 Hz physics substepping per §6 — the accumulator loop is fixed-cost dominant), 1.2 ms game logic, 1.8 ms render CPU, 5.5 ms GPU, 1.5 ms UGUI, 0.8 ms audio, headroom ≥ 2.2 ms. Ceilings per §14.2.2: ≤ 900 MB resident sustained (iOS jetsam margin), cold boot → main menu ≤ 5 s, level load ≤ 1.5 s warm / ≤ 3 s cold. Beneath those ceilings, the iOS-min tier target is < 600 MB resident — comfortably inside the §14.2.2 jetsam ceiling for the asset budget in §9 — with level-in ≤ 3 s from SSD-class storage.

**Thermal:** rely on the documented Player-Settings governor (Serious → 30 FPS, Critical → 15 FPS defaults, on by default, [class-PlayerSettingsiOS](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html), accessed 2026-09-24) rather than custom thermal polling; a §14 telemetry hook logs governor activations during soak tests.

**Instruments hookup (documented + standard):** build Development configuration to device; attach Instruments (Time Profiler / Core Animation FPS / Energy Log / Metal System Trace) to the running process. Apple's Metal API Validation is enabled by setting the Xcode Run scheme to Debug ([class-PlayerSettingsiOS](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettingsiOS.html), accessed 2026-09-24); Unity's editor-side Metal validation setting is a separate editor-only debugging aid. Device smoke tests via `xcodebuild test -destination "platform=iOS,id=<id>" -scheme Unity-iPhone` (18.5).

### 18.10 Gradle layer and manifest

**Toolchain pins (documented):** "Unity uses Gradle for all Android builds." 6000.6.3f1+ ships **Gradle 9.3.1 + Android Gradle Plugin 9.1.1** (6000.6.1f1–6000.6.2f1: Gradle 9.3.1 + AGP 9.0.0) ([android-gradle-version-compatibility](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-gradle-version-compatibility.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Android-side tools ship via Hub "Android Build Support" (18.13).

**Template map — what each file controls** ([gradle-templates](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/gradle-templates.html), accessed 2026-09-24):

| Template (in `Assets/Plugins/Android/` after enabling) | Becomes | Controls | Our customization |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseProjectTemplate.gradle` | root `build.gradle` | **AGP version**, repositories, plugin locations | none (pin AGP via Unity version, not the template) |
| `launcherTemplate.gradle` | `launcher/build.gradle` | bundling, **signing**, APK splitting, APK/AAB output | none — signing injected via Publishing Settings + `IPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject` |
| `mainTemplate.gradle` | `unityLibrary/build.gradle` | Unity-as-a-Library `.aar` build | none v1 |
| `settingsTemplate.gradle` | `settings.gradle` | module inclusion | none |
| `gradleTemplate.properties` | `gradle.properties` | **JVM heap**, build props | `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4G` for CI determinism **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| `libTemplate.gradle` | plug-in build.gradle | AARs lacking one | n/a |

**Minify/R8 [ORIGINAL DESIGN]:** v1 ships with Gradle minification **off**. IL2CPP + managed stripping already shrink the C# surface, and R8 keep-rule maintenance against AGP 9.x churn buys little for an offline puzzle game. Revisit only if the AAB threatens the 500 MB base cap (18.12). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact template keys to enable R8 with Unity 6.6 templates (minifyEnabled/keep rule file placement) were not captured in research notes. -->

**C# hook (documented interface):** implement `IPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject.OnPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject(string path)` — receives the **unityLibrary module path** after assembly, for manifest/resource edits from code:

```csharp
#if UNITY_ANDROID || UNITY_EDITOR
using System.IO;
using UnityEditor.Build;

namespace Aob.Platform.Android
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Post-assembly Gradle-project hook. Runs on every Android build (APK, AAB,
    /// and Export Project alike). Receives the unityLibrary module path.
    /// </summary>
    public sealed class GradlePostProcessor : IPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject
    {
        public int callbackOrder => 0;

        public void OnPostGenerateGradleAndroidProject(string path)
        {
            // v1: intentionally a no-op audit point. Candidate future work:
            // strip debuggable overlays, inject network security config, or
            // patch manifest resource strings for store variants.
            _ = path;
        }
    }
}
#endif
```

**Manifest layer (documented):** the final `AndroidManifest.xml` is Gradle's merge of the Unity **Library** manifest (Player activities), the Unity **Launcher** manifest (app wrapper), and any plug-in manifests; override via `Assets/Plugins/Android/AndroidManifest.xml`. A manifest inside a built APK/AAB **cannot be edited** ([android-manifest](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-manifest.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Unity auto-adds permissions from settings and API usage: INTERNET (Internet Access = Require in dev builds; `UnityWebRequest`; `Ping`; `System.Net.Sockets`; Analytics/Crash), VIBRATE (`Handheld.Vibrate`), ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE (reachability checks), ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (LocationService), CAMERA (WebCamTexture), RECORD_AUDIO (Microphone).

**Our permission budget:** v1 target = **zero permissions**. Concretely: Internet Access = Auto and no `UnityWebRequest` in shipped code paths (no ads/analytics/accounts, 18.1) → no INTERNET in release; no location/camera/mic anywhere; the only candidate is **VIBRATE** if we adopt `Handheld.Vibrate` for haptics — we don't (18.14 uses Input System rumble on 6000.6+) → release manifest ships empty of dangerous/normal permissions **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**. A permission-less manifest also simplifies the Data-safety form (18.12) and is a mild install-conversion win. Verify the merged manifest of each release candidate with Android Studio's APK/AAB Analyzer (18.13) — documented inspection path.

### 18.11 Keystore workflow and CI secret storage

Documented mechanics ([android-keystore-manager](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/android-keystore-manager.html), accessed 2026-09-24): Keystore Manager opens from Player Settings > Publishing Settings (Android); create keystore → add key → fields are keystore path, ASCII-only passwords, key alias, key password, **validity default 50 years** (must outlive the app so every update signs with the same key — Play enforces upgrade-key compatibility). Signing config is stored (optionally encrypted) per-project/machine in Publishing Settings.

**Operational rules (DevSecOps lens):**

1. One release keystore, created once in P4, stored in the password manager + an offline backup. **Losing it ends the app's update lineage** (new package name or Play key-reset escalation only).
2. CI: keystore + passwords live as GitHub Actions secrets (base64-encoded keystore decoded to a temp file in the job, never echoed, file deleted post-build; passwords via env vars consumed by the Gradle launcher template — never on the command line). This mirrors §16's secret-handling standard.
3. The Play **App Signing** key (Play's re-signing key) is separate from the upload key; enroll at first AAB upload so upload-key loss is recoverable. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: Play App Signing enrollment flow specifics were not captured in the 2026-09 sweep. -->
4. Dev builds: debug keystore (auto-generated); never release-sign on dev machines.

### 18.12 AAB build, Play Console submission, size and data-safety compliance

**Build:** Build Profiles (§4) → Android → **Build App Bundle (Google Play)** checkbox switches Gradle output APK → AAB via the launcher template (documented, [gradle-templates](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/gradle-templates.html)). AAB is Google-Play-only; the legacy APK path (100 MB cap) exists for other stores — v1 ships Play-only, sideload APK for QA (18.13). AAB as the required format for new Play apps is a long-standing Play policy that the 2026-09 sweep did **not** re-verify on-page <!-- TODO-VERIFY -->.

**Size compliance — the corrected numbers** ([Play size limits](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859372), accessed 2026-09-24) **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** *(sweep flagged Unity's "200 MB" figure as suspect; verify confirmed 200 MB is only the mobile-data install-dialog threshold — quote these instead)*: compressed-download caps are base module **500 MB**, per feature module 500 MB, per asset pack 1.5 GB, 4 GB cumulative (modules + install-time packs), 30 GB cumulative on-demand/fast-follow, **34 GB app total**; >1 GB requires minSdk 21+ (we are 24). Our content budget (§5/§9: ~200 levels as ScriptableObjects + ≤ 400 MB art/audio target) fits the base module with room — **Play Asset Delivery is out of scope for v1**, which removes the entire asset-pack runtime API surface (documented PAD Unity page exists if ever needed: [play-asset-delivery](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/play-asset-delivery.html), accessed 2026-09-24; delivery-mode enum names on the Unity side remain uncaptured in research).

**Target-API compliance:** Target API Level = 36 (18.9) satisfies "new apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher" effective 2026-08-31 ([Play Console Help](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878), accessed 2026-09-24). Watch item: the next annual bump (historically each Aug 31) becomes a §21 risk row with a P7-window trigger.

**Data safety form mapping — our actual data:**

| Play Data-safety question | Our answer | Ground truth |
|---|---|---|
| Does your app collect or share user data? | **No** | Local-only leaderboards/save (§6); no network permission (18.10); no SDKs |
| Permissions declared | none (18.10) | Merged-manifest audit per release |
| Encryption in transit | n/a (no network) | — |
| Data deletion | App uninstall deletes `persistentDataPath` | No cloud copies exist |

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** decision embedded here: had v1 adopted Play Games Services leaderboards, every row above would flip and add an SDK privacy-manifest surface on iOS too (18.4). Deferred to post-v1 with a §21 trigger.

**Upload flow:** Play Console → Create app → **internal testing track** → upload AAB → add testers → roll out; promote through closed → production. This is the standard console flow the research notes recorded as "not re-verified on-page this run" — treat step labels as approximate <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact console step names + the personal-account closed-testing requirement (20 testers / 14 days, reported 2025) — explicitly uncaptured in the sweep; fetch support.google.com before first submission -->. Store listing assets, IARC-style content rating questionnaire, and the privacy-policy URL (a static page suffices — "no data collected" still requires the URL) complete the checklist.

### 18.14 Touch controls integration (mobile UGUI + haptics)

Full provider architecture lives in §7; this is the mobile-execution summary with the platform-specific exacts.

**Touch input path (verified recipe, [Input System develop docs](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/InputSystem/tree/develop/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem/Documentation~) + [package root](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest), accessed 2026-09-24):** call `EnhancedTouchSupport.Enable()` once in `Awake`; read `Touch.activeTouches`/`activeFingers` (zero-GC); never poll the `Touchscreen` device directly in `Update` (state changes get missed — documented warning). `TouchDragInputProvider` (§7) maps drag deltas to cursor movement, `screenPosition - startScreenPosition` + `history` velocity for swipe-fling piece nudges, `tapCount`/`isTap` for double-tap rotate. UI pointer input flows natively: the `InputSystemUIInputModule`'s default Pointer Behavior ("Single Mouse or Pen But Multi Touch And Track") already gives multi-touch UI plus a unified cursor.

**On-screen controls (documented exacts):** `OnScreenButton` writes 1/0 on pointer down/up to a `ButtonControl` path; `OnScreenStick` drives a `Vector2Control` with `Movement Range` 50 (±25 px box). Because on-screen controls **synthesize a Gamepad**, the same gameplay bindings serve desktop and mobile — the touch layer adds zero new action-map surface (§7's key result). Our overlay **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Control | Component | controlPath | Placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rotate CW / CCW | 2 × `OnScreenButton` | `<Gamepad>/rightShoulder`, `<Gamepad>/leftShoulder` | bottom-right cluster, above safe-area inset |
| Drop | `OnScreenButton` | `<Gamepad>/buttonSouth` | bottom-right, largest hit target (≥ 88 px) |
| Pause | `OnScreenButton` | `<Gamepad>/startButton` | top-right inside safe area |

Enable **Use Isolated Input Actions** on the buttons (isolated defaults `<Touchscreen>/touch*/press` etc.) to stop paired-device scheme-switch jitter — documented setting. Buttons live on a canvas layer above the SafeAreaFitter root (18.7).

**Canvas Scaler (documented):** UI Scale Mode **Scale With Screen Size**; Screen Match Mode **Match Width or Height**; **Match = 0.5** — the official demo shows Match 0.5 holding element size across a 640×960 ↔ 960×640 orientation swap where width-only (Match 0) inflates by 1.5×; the scaler deliberately deviates from the reference resolution to respect the screen's aspect ([script-CanvasScaler](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@2.0/manual/script-CanvasScaler.html), accessed 2026-09-24). Reference resolution 1920×1080 shared with §9's UI spec.

**Haptics — version-gated matrix (documented):** `Gamepad.SetMotorSpeeds(low, high)` (left motor = low frequency); global `InputSystem.PauseHaptics()/ResumeHaptics()/ResetHaptics()`. **Android rumble requires Unity 6000.6+** (we qualify): Android 12+ gives per-motor control on most BT pads; Android ≤ 11 collapses to a single motor (max of L/R); rumble auto-stops ~10 s after the last call. **iOS/tvOS/visionOS rumble requires Unity 6000.7+ — we are on 6.6, so iOS rumble is OFF the table for v1** (first rumble call allocates resources with latency; 2-min idle release makes burst patterns viable only when we get there). No rumble on Web ([gamepad-haptics docs](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/InputSystem/tree/develop/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem/Documentation~/gamepad-haptics.md), accessed 2026-09-24). Our design defers to the canonical §13.4 haptic event map (piece settle = 60 ms at (0.15, 0.30); stack collapse = 250 ms at (0.90, 0.90); full table there) on every rumble-capable target — desktop Xbox/PS pads included per §7's documented matrix; within mobile that means Android BT pads in v1, because iOS rumble is version-gated off (above). The `Handheld.Vibrate` fallback would drag in the VIBRATE permission (18.10) and is rejected **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

### 18.15 Mobile performance budgets, frame pacing, thermal

**Frame pacing rules (documented, [Application-targetFrameRate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application-targetFrameRate.html), accessed 2026-09-24):** if `QualitySettings.vSyncCount != 0`, `targetFrameRate` is ignored; docs recommend vSync for smooth pacing, yet mobile pacing in practice is `vSyncCount = 0` + `Application.targetFrameRate = 60` (Android "Optimized Frame Pacing" on, 18.9); `targetFrameRate = -1` with vSync 0 renders a **fixed 30 fps battery mode** on mobile — our user-facing "Battery saver" toggle **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**; non-divisor rates round down to the largest refresh divisor (25 → 20 on 60 Hz — never ship odd rates); iOS 120 Hz requires the ProMotion toggle (off for v1, 18.2).

**Budget table [ORIGINAL DESIGN] (60 fps = 16.67 ms; frame-slice values restate the single binding §14.2.1 mobile rows — Android upper-mid / iOS A15-class, which per §14's intro are the budgets this section must hit; measured on tier-representative devices in P5):**

| Slice | iOS-mid / Android-mid budget | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Physics sim | 3.0 ms | 240 Hz substep loop per §6; ~100 active bodies trivial; worst case = collapse cascades |
| Game logic + events | 1.2 ms | LevelManager/ScoreController event-driven; zero-allocation rule (skill standard) |
| UI | 1.5 ms | Single HUD canvas; queue strip rebuilt only on advance |
| culling + render submit | 1.8 ms | URP Forward+; SRP-batcher-compatible shaders (§9) |
| Audio | 0.8 ms | §14.2.1 mobile-row slice |
| GPU | 5.5 ms | Mobile Base tier: render scale 1.0, water refraction via Opaque Texture with 2× downsampling (§9/§10 research: MSAA is ignored at runtime on mobile lacking StoreAndResolve when Opaque Texture is on — documented URP caveat) |
| Headroom | ≥ 2.2 ms | — |
| Memory resident | ≤ 900 MB sustained (binding ceiling, §14.2.2); < 600 MB iOS-mid/Android-mid tier target beneath it | Texture streaming: 512 MB is the documented Unity default (T10: "Texture Memory Budget default 512 MB"; §4 research), which §14.2.2 lowers to 128 MB on mobile |

**Thermal:** iOS relies on the governor ladder (18.8). Android has no Unity-side governor — our own 3-step fallback [ORIGINAL DESIGN]: watch `OnApplicationPause`/thermal hints if exposed, else degrade by sustained-frame-time EWMA crossing 18 ms for 5 s → drop render scale one step (§9 tiers) → 30 fps cap. Soak protocol (30-min Endurance runs on tier-min devices) lives in §14.

**Quality-tier switching:** per-platform URP asset assignment in Quality Settings (levels × platforms matrix with one default per platform — documented, [class-QualitySettings](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/class-QualitySettings.html), accessed 2026-09-24); mobile ships two tiers (Low/Base) with High reachable on flagship-class devices only.

### 18.16 Mobile test matrix

| Axis | Coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| iOS versions | **iOS 15 (floor)**, one mid version, **current major (iOS 26-generation)** on TestFlight devices | Floor pinned by Unity 6.6 (18.0); Apple's upload floor (target iOS 13+) is looser |
| iOS devices | 1 × iOS-min tier, 2 × mid, 1 × high + 1 iPad | Dynamic Island + home-indicator insets via SafeAreaFitter; iPad runs portrait+landscape matrix |
| Android APIs | **36 (target)** on primary matrix; **24 (min)** on one legacy device; one in-between | API 36 is the compliance target ([Play Console Help](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878), accessed 2026-09-24) |
| Android GPUs | Adreno (6xx + 7xx), Mali (G-series), one PowerVR-class | ASTC support verification; Vulkan-first with GLES3 fallback exercised on at least one device of each family |
| Form factors | 16:9 phone, 19.5:9+ tall phone, 4:3-class tablet, one foldable outer display | Canvas Scaler Match 0.5 math + orientation flips; foldable hinge via `Screen.safeArea` refresh |
| Input | Touch, one BT gamepad (Android), one BT gamepad (iOS — input yes, rumble no, 18.14) | Gamepad path = same synthesized-Gamepad bindings |
| Soak | 30-min Endurance on tier-min devices; battery-drain sanity | 18.15 thermal fallback validation |

**Exit criteria for the P5 "Multiplatform hardening" phase (§10):** all matrix cells green on the perf budgets; release AAB + archive buildable from clean CI checkouts (§16); merged-manifest audit shows the exact intended permission set (18.10); safe-area screenshots reviewed on every notch class; store compliance fields (privacy manifest on iOS, Data-safety on Android) filled and screenshot-archived. Task-level breakdown is §20's P5 epics; unresolved watch-items (bitcode remnant, upload-tool naming, Play console step labels, personal-account testing requirement, API-24 distribution re-check) are registered in §21 with the TODO-VERIFY flags placed throughout this section.

## 19. Multiplatform Master Reference — PC, macOS, Steam & Xbox

This section is the master reference for everything platform-specific outside mobile: the Windows player, the macOS player, the Steam integration that carries both, the Xbox path that follows, and the cross-platform unification layer that keeps them one game. It implements the release order decided at plan level: **Windows + macOS via Steam first, Android second, iOS third, Xbox last (explicitly gated on ID@Xbox onboarding)** — the original's Switch, PS4 and Wii U editions are treated as historical reference only (§11–§13) and are not build targets.

Engine baseline for every table in this section: **Unity 6.6 (6000.6)**, whose 6000.6.0f1 release shipped 2026-08-31 and which is officially the final Supported/Update release of the Unity 6 family, with 6.7 as the next LTS [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.6 availability announcement, accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/unity-6-6-is-now-available/1735357). Two 6.6-specific facts shape desktop planning: the Intel macOS Editor is deprecated in 6.6 and disappears after 6.7 LTS [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6000.6.0f1 release notes, accessed 2026-09-24](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), and from 6.6 the Input System ships as a built-in engine module rather than the com.unity.inputsystem package [DOCUMENTED — Unity staff post "Planned breaking changes in Unity 6.7", accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/planned-breaking-changes-in-unity-6-7/1723293). All external facts below were captured 2026-09-24; anything not source-backed is marked **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** or `<!-- TODO-VERIFY: ... -->`.

### 19.1 Platform and Release Matrix

| Target | Engine target | Store / distribution | Scripting | Graphics | Signing / cert gate | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Windows (primary desktop) | Standalone Windows x64 | Steam | IL2CPP, C++ config **Master** | D3D11 → D3D12 → Vulkan (pinned order, §19.2.2) | Azure Artifact Signing (OV-class reputation) | 1 — launch |
| macOS | Standalone macOS Universal (arm64 + x64) | Steam | IL2CPP (built on Mac only, §19.3.1) | Metal only | Developer ID + Hardened Runtime + notarization | 1 — launch |
| Steam client layer | — (wraps both depots) | Steamworks | Steamworks.NET 2025.164.1 | — | Steam Direct $100/app; store review | 1 — launch |
| Linux (optional) | Standalone Linux x64 | Steam depot (or Proton for the Windows depot) | IL2CPP | Vulkan | none extra | 1.x — post-launch **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Android / iOS | mobile targets | Google Play / App Store | IL2CPP | Vulkan / Metal | mobile store gates (owned by the mobile sections) | 2–3 |
| Xbox Series X\|S (+ One decision, §19.5.6) | Xbox build targets via Unity Xbox module + GDK | Xbox store / Game Pass | IL2CPP | GDK graphics (NDA surface) | XR certification + IARC | 4 — gated on ID@Xbox |

Floor versions that anchor every profile: the Windows player requires Windows 10 21H1 (build 19043)+ and supports x86, x64 (SSE2) and Arm64 target architectures [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.3 system requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/system-requirements.html); the macOS player floor is macOS 12 Monterey while the Mac **editor** itself needs macOS 13 Ventura [DOCUMENTED — Unity macOS requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html) — two different numbers that must never be conflated in marketing copy or support docs.

### 19.2 Windows

#### 19.2.1 Player Settings — shipping configuration

All settings live in Edit > Project Settings > Player (Windows tab); the **target architecture is not chosen here** — it is chosen per Build Profile in the Build Profiles window (§19.6.4), a deliberate Unity 6 reorganization in which Player Settings carry per-platform configuration and Build Profiles own platform/architecture/scene selection [DOCUMENTED — Unity Player project settings reference, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettings.html).

| Setting (group) | Ship value | Rationale / source |
|---|---|---|
| Scripting Backend | **IL2CPP** | Shipping standard; also mandatory for the Xbox and mobile phases, keeping one backend across the whole matrix |
| IL2CPP Code Generation | Optimize for runtime speed (default) | Puzzle sim is latency-sensitive; build time is a CI concern, not a player concern |
| C++ Compiler Configuration | **Master** | Unity's documented best practice for shipping builds (MSVC LTCG); slowest build, fastest runtime [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html) |
| IL2CPP Stacktrace Information | Method Name (release) / +File:Line (dev builds) | File/line info inflates and slows builds — dev-profile-only |
| Strip Engine Code | On | IL2CPP-only flag; managed stripping level tuned in §16 CI so reflection surfaces (Input System, serialization) survive |
| API Compatibility Level | .NET Standard 2.1 | Smaller closure than .NET Framework; all needed APIs available |
| Active Input Handling | **Both** (§4.8) | Defines `ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` + `ENABLE_LEGACY_INPUT_MANAGER`; all first-party input is Input System only (§7); Both is the §4.8 transitional setting — flip to Input System only after the §14 supply-chain audit confirms no legacy Input consumers (§20 P2.E9-automation-ci.10) [DOCUMENTED — Unity staff post, accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/planned-breaking-changes-in-unity-6-7/1723293) |
| Allow downloads over HTTP | Not allowed (default) | No plaintext network path in the game |
| Enable DirectStorage | Off for v1 | A 200-level 2D-physics puzzle game is not asset-I/O-bound; revisit only if load profiling says otherwise **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Fullscreen Mode | **Fullscreen Window** | Borderless default; see §19.2.3 |
| Resizable Window / Allow Fullscreen Switch | On / On | Desktop UX expectation |
| Run In Background | On | Pause-menu music + Steam overlay friendliness |
| Visible In Background | Off | Documented to break Alt+Tab/Win+M minimization when on [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html) |
| Capture Single Screen | On | Multi-monitor default |
| Use Player Log | On (default) | Basis of the crash/diagnostic policy (§19.2.7) |
| Force Single Instance | On | Prevents double-launch fighting over the same save root **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** |
| Icon | "Override for Windows, Mac, Linux" per-size slots filled from one master 1024 icon | Legacy .ico set; store logos are Steam-side (§19.4.11) |

The `x64`-only decision for the Windows depot (x86 and Arm64 remain supported engine targets per the system-requirements page above) is **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: 2026 Steam hardware is effectively all x64, and a single architecture halves the sign/QA/SmartScreen-reputation surface. The optional Linux depot decision is likewise **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (§19.4.9).

#### 19.2.2 Graphics API selection and ordering

Auto Graphics API for Windows lets the engine pick the recommended API per machine; disabling it pins an explicit ordered list that acts as a **fallback order — the first supported API wins at runtime** [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html). The docs do not hardcode what Auto chooses on a given machine.

Ship configuration **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — pin, in this order: **D3D11 → D3D12 → Vulkan**:

1. **D3D11 first.** The game is a stylized 2D-physics puzzler; URP forward rendering at puzzle workloads is trivially fast on D3D11, which remains the widest-validated driver surface on the Steam population. "Use DXGI flip model swap chain for D3D11" stays **On** (default; documented best performance; `PlayerSettings.useFlipModelSwapchain`) [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html).
2. **D3D12 second.** Kept in the list so modern machines that would otherwise prefer it can still land on a first-class path if D3D11 is unavailable; if the D3D12 path is ever promoted to first, the same page's **D3D12 Device Filtering Asset** (allow/block device lists) and **Graphics Jobs** modes (Native/Legacy/Split — only applicable with Graphics Jobs enabled and DX12/Vulkan) become the tuning levers [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html). Graphics Jobs stays off for v1 — a CPU-light 2D sim gains nothing from jobified render submission.
3. **Vulkan last.** Safety net; its "Number of swapchain buffers" stays at the default 3, and "Get swapchain image late as possible" left at default [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html).

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: the engine's actual Auto-mode preference order per GPU/driver (not stated on the Player settings page) — confirm on the Unity 6.6 rendering docs or by machine survey before locking the pinned list, in case Auto on the Steam population broadly prefers D3D12. -->

The pinned order itself is a project decision, not a documented engine default — hence the TODO above. macOS needs no equivalent decision: **Metal is the only supported API on supported Macs** [DOCUMENTED — Unity macOS requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html).

#### 19.2.3 Fullscreen, resolution and windowing UX

The four documented modes are Fullscreen Window (borderless; the cross-platform default), Exclusive Fullscreen (Windows-only; changes the OS display resolution), Maximized Window (Windows and Mac only), and Windowed [DOCUMENTED — Windows Player settings, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/playersettings-windows.html).

UX policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

- Boot into **Fullscreen Window** at the desktop resolution (no mode switch, no flicker, instant Alt+Tab — matches the calm lounge tone of the game; a jarring exclusive-mode change on launch is off-brand).
- Offer Windowed and (Windows) Exclusive Fullscreen in the video options; Exclusive Fullscreen matters mainly for high-refresh displays where borderless composition adds latency, so expose a refresh-rate readout beside it.
- The resolution picker lists only modes the current monitor reports; default is the desktop resolution; the choice persists into the shared settings file (§19.6.2).
- 16:9, 16:10, 21:9 and 4:3 are all supported: the play field is a fixed-logic-width column (as in the original's tower framing), so wider aspects gain water and ambient side art rather than gameplay width, and 4:3 letterboxes the sides gracefully.

#### 19.2.4 DPI awareness and display scaling

The captured Windows Player Settings reference does not document a per-project DPI-awareness toggle, so the plan treats Windows scaling as a **QA guarantee rather than a settings knob**. Policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

- Visually correct and interactively pixel-accurate at 100%, 125%, 150% and 200% display scaling on Windows 10 21H1+ and Windows 11, with cursor hotspot and UI hit areas tracking the OS scaling — a §19.6.5 release-candidate gate.
- UI sizing rides the shared canvas scale-with-screen-size approach, so the logical layout is identical across DPI; only the backing resolution changes.
- Minimum-legibility gate: text legible in a 1280×720 window at 150% scaling — deliberately mirroring the Steam Deck display criterion (§19.4.10); if it is legible there, it is legible everywhere.

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact Unity 6.6 DPI-awareness behavior/field for the Windows player (per-monitor-v2 awareness is expected but is not stated on the captured Player settings page) — confirm on the shipping exe during the Windows RC pass. -->

#### 19.2.5 Code signing — Azure Artifact Signing

Windows builds are signed with **Azure Artifact Signing** (the 2026 rename of Trusted Signing; old /azure/trusted-signing/* URLs redirect to the /azure/artifact-signing/* canonical set) [DOCUMENTED — Microsoft Learn, "What is the Artifact Signing service?", accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/overview).

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| SKUs | Basic and Premium only | [DOCUMENTED — overview, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/overview) |
| Basic tier | **$9.99/mo**, 5,000 signatures/mo, 1 of each certificate profile type | [DOCUMENTED — Artifact Signing pricing, accessed 2026-09-24](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/artifact-signing/) |
| Premium tier | **$99.99/mo**, 100,000 signatures/mo, 10 of each certificate profile type | same |
| Overage | **$0.005 per signature** beyond quota, both tiers | same |
| Subscription | Paid Azure subscription required — no free/trial/sponsored subscriptions | [DOCUMENTED — Artifact Signing FAQ, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/trusted-signing/faq) |
| Billing | Full SKU amount at account creation, **not pro-rated** | same |
| Identity validation (individual) | Microsoft Authenticator Verified ID + FaceCheck; first/last name and address must match documents; adequate lighting required | same |
| Identity validation (organization) | Email verification, link expires in 7 days; validations can expire — renew or signing stops, reminders begin 60 days out | same |
| Quota scope | Shared across **all certificate profiles in the account** | same |
| Key protection | FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs | [DOCUMENTED — overview, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/overview) |

Plan of record **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: Basic tier, one certificate profile, activated at the start of the Windows RC phase (not earlier — billing is not pro-rated and identity validation has a nonzero retry tail). One exe plus installer per monthly release sits far inside 5,000 signatures/month; the tier is revisited only if signing every CI artifact becomes policy. Integration is SignTool with the Azure signing dlib using the documented /dlib /dmdf pattern, invoked from the §16 pipeline after the IL2CPP build and before installer wrapping. <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact signtool invocation for Artifact Signing (/dlib /dmdf flag values and the "Artifact Signing Certificate Profile Signer" role assignment) — the how-to-sign page moved and was not captured; pin the command line once the Azure account exists. -->

#### 19.2.6 SmartScreen reputation strategy

Microsoft's current policy doc is unambiguous: **"EV certificates no longer bypass SmartScreen"** — OV and EV both show an unrecognized-app warning until reputation accumulates, so an EV premium is explicitly not justified for SmartScreen; reputation accrues per publisher identity and per file hash, unsigned re-releases restart from zero reputation every version, and Microsoft-Store-distributed apps never warn [DOCUMENTED — "SmartScreen reputation for Windows app developers", accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation).

Consequences baked into the plan **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

1. **Expect the warning on day one.** Every v1 direct download shows "Windows protected your PC" until reputation builds. The Steam launch FAQ says so up front with a one-line "Run anyway" walkthrough — turning an inevitable support ticket into a documented non-event.
2. **One stable signing identity forever.** Publisher reputation carries across versions only under a stable identity; never ship an unsigned or differently-signed build, and never rotate the certificate profile casually.
3. **Route the majority through Steam.** The Steam client is the primary distribution surface precisely so most players never execute a browser-downloaded binary; direct exe download is the exception path.
4. **No EV purchase.** Zero SmartScreen benefit per the doc above; Artifact Signing Basic is the entire signing budget.

#### 19.2.7 Crash handling, logging and diagnostics

Policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**, built on the documented Use Player Log setting (default on, §19.2.1):

- An early-load diagnostics hook subscribes to `Application.logMessageReceived` and `logMessageReceivedThreaded`, mirroring exceptions into a bounded in-memory ring buffer; on a fatal exception it flushes the ring plus context (level id, mode, `GameStateMachine` state, physics tick rate) to a crash-report file beside the player log before the process dies. No screenshots, no PII.
- A support-report button in the options menu packages player log + crash report + hardware survey into a zip the player can attach to a forum thread — the entire v1 telemetry story is opt-in and manual; there is no automatic upload path, keeping the privacy surface trivially explainable.
- CI archives IL2CPP release symbols per build id in §16 so a method-name-level player-log stack can be mapped to source when needed.
- Diagnostics are strictly machine-local; Steam Cloud never syncs them (§19.4.6).

### 19.3 macOS

#### 19.3.1 Build-host constraint and toolchain

The load-bearing constraint for the whole macOS phase: **IL2CPP players must be built from an Editor running on the same platform — "to build a macOS Player with IL2CPP, you must build on macOS"**, with Linux the only cross-compile exception (via the Linux IL2CPP cross-compiler) [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.3 "Introduction to IL2CPP", accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/il2cpp-introduction.html). The restriction exists because IL2CPP compiles generated C++ with the target platform's native toolchain — "you can't compile C++ code for macOS on Windows" [DOCUMENTED — Unity Discussions thread 700278, accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/il2cpp-for-mac-only-available-in-mac-editor/700278). IL2CPP for macOS additionally requires Xcode [DOCUMENTED — Unity macOS requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html). A Windows editor can still produce a macOS player, but only with the Mono backend — not shippable-grade for this project, which is IL2CPP everywhere.

Operational consequences **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

- The §16 CI matrix runs the macOS+IL2CPP build job on Apple hardware (a hosted Mac runner or a Mac Studio/mini agent) with current Xcode; the Windows editor never produces macOS artifacts.
- Because the Intel macOS Editor is deprecated in 6.6 and disappears after 6.7 LTS [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6000.6.0f1 release notes, accessed 2026-09-24](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1), all Mac build agents are Apple Silicon from day one; targeting Intel is a player-architecture question (§19.3.2), never an editor question.
- Editor floor on the agents: macOS 13 Ventura or newer (the editor requirement — distinct from the player floor of macOS 12, §19.1).

#### 19.3.2 Universal binary and architecture decision

Ship a **Universal (arm64 + x64) build**. Unity supports Apple Silicon and x64-with-SSE2 as macOS target architectures and explicitly warns that Apple is deprecating Rosetta, directing developers to build Apple Silicon or Universal instead of Intel-64-only [DOCUMENTED — Unity macOS requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html). The 6.7 Beta requirements page goes further and marks x64 "(Deprecated)" — Intel support for macOS standalone players "will be removed in a future version of Unity", with Apple Silicon the recommended target for new builds [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.7 Beta macOS requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.7/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html).

Decision matrix **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: Universal at launch (the 2026 Steam Mac population still includes Intel machines, and the added download size is acceptable for a puzzle game), with a planned drop to Apple-Silicon-only the moment engine support or player telemetry justifies it — never the reverse. The Steamworks native library is already ahead of this curve: `libsteam_api.dylib` ships as a genuine two-slice universal (x86_64 + arm64) Mach-O — verified at the binary level in the copy Steamworks.NET redistributes, matching Valve's documentation [DOCUMENTED — Valve Steamworks API overview, accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api).

#### 19.3.3 Signing identity, Hardened Runtime and entitlements

Direct distribution (Steam) uses the **Developer ID Application** certificate with **Hardened Runtime** enabled — both mandatory for notarization [DOCUMENTED — Apple, "Notarizing macOS software before distribution", accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution); [DOCUMENTED — Apple, "Hardened Runtime", accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/hardened-runtime). The Mac App Store route (Mac Distribution cert, sandbox entitlements, App Review) is explicitly rejected — Steam is the distribution plan, and MAS-submitted software is exempt from notarization only because its submission process carries equivalent checks [DOCUMENTED — Apple, notarization doc, accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution).

Runtime-exception entitlement keys, exact identifiers [DOCUMENTED — Apple, "Hardened Runtime", accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/hardened-runtime):

| Entitlement key | Grants | AOB need | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` | Execution of JIT-compiled code | **No** — IL2CPP is AOT | Omit |
| `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` | Writable+executable memory | **No** — AOT player; historically a Mono-backend need | Omit |
| `com.apple.security.cs.allow-dyld-environment-variables` | DYLD_* env vars at launch | No | Omit |
| `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` | Loading third-party libraries not signed by the same team | Only if a native plugin signed by another team is ever added | **Omit at v1**; documented as the single knob to turn if the Steamworks bundle ever fails library validation |

Two structural rules govern the entitlements file: entitlements attach **only to executables** (frameworks and plugins inherit the host's), and only what is needed should be granted [DOCUMENTED — Apple, "Hardened Runtime", accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/hardened-runtime). Start-empty policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: ship v1 with zero runtime-exception entitlements — a pure-IL2CPP Unity game with a self-signed plugin set does not need them, and adding `disable-library-validation` later is a one-line change with a documented trigger. The community precedent (enabling hardened runtime via the generated Xcode project or post-build codesign when the editor exposed no toggle) is the fallback path if the 6.6 Build window lacks a sign/notarize field [DOCUMENTED — Unity Discussions thread 841323, accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/enable-hardened-runtime-when-building-a-macos-app/841323).

#### 19.3.4 Notarization end-to-end

The Apple-side contract [DOCUMENTED — Apple, "Notarizing macOS software before distribution", accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution): Developer ID Application signature + Hardened Runtime, submit via **notarytool** (the notary service has rejected altool and Xcode 13-or-earlier uploads since 2023-11-01), wait for the ticket, **staple** it to the artifact, then distribute as dmg/pkg/zip — the stapled ticket lets Gatekeeper validate offline, while the online notary database covers unstapled copies. Unity's own "Code sign and notarize your macOS application" section still carries a stale altool child page [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.x notarization section, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.0/Documentation/Manual/macos-building-notarization.html); Apple's doc governs — the pipeline below is notarytool-only.

Release script `notarize-macos.sh` (CI step after the §16 macOS build; commands per Apple's doc above, assembled here as project design **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: notarize-macos.sh <path-to-AoB.app> <keychain-profile> <team-name>
set -euo pipefail
APP="$1"; PROFILE="$2"; TEAM="$3"

# 1) Sign every bundle inside-out, then the .app itself, with Hardened Runtime.
#    Entitlements apply to the main executable only; plugins inherit (§19.3.3).
ENTITLEMENTS="Build/MacOS/aob.entitlements"   # empty exemptions at v1
find "$APP/Contents" -type f \( -name '*.dylib' -o -name '*.so' \) -exec \
  codesign --force --timestamp --options runtime \
    --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" --sign "$TEAM" {} \;
codesign --force --timestamp --options runtime \
  --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" --sign "$TEAM" "$APP"

# 2) Wrap a read-only UDZO dmg (staple targets the artifact players download).
DMG="Build/ArtOfBalance-macOS.dmg"
hdiutil create -volname "Art of Balance" -srcfolder "$APP" \
  -ov -format UDZO "$DMG"
codesign --timestamp --sign "$TEAM" "$DMG"

# 3) Submit and wait (notarytool only — altool rejected since 2023-11-01).
xcrun notarytool submit "$DMG" --keychain-profile "$PROFILE" --wait

# 4) Staple the ticket and verify Gatekeeper acceptance.
xcrun notarytool staple "$DMG"
xcrun stapler validate "$DMG"
spctl --assess -vv "$DMG"
```

#### 19.3.5 Gatekeeper first-run UX

Since macOS 10.15, all Developer ID–distributed software must be notarized to run; a notarized+stapled build presents the clean first-run dialog with verified-developer information, and since macOS 10.14.5 new Developer ID certificates require notarization [DOCUMENTED — Apple, notarization doc, accessed 2026-09-24](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution). Notarization is not App Review — it is an automated malware scan, and passing it says nothing about product decisions. UX copy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: the Steam launch FAQ includes the expected first-launch dialog screenshot ("Art of Balance" verified developer, Open button) so Mac players do not mistake the normal Gatekeeper confirmation for an error; the dmg mounts a drag-to-Applications layout with an Applications symlink.

Player floor: **macOS 12 Monterey and later** — unchanged in the 6.7 Beta requirements page as of 2026-09-24 [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.7 Beta macOS requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.7/Documentation/Manual/macos-requirements-and-compatibility.html). Store-page copy and the support matrix state "macOS 12+" with the Universal badge; the deprecation horizon (x64 architecture deprecated heading into 6.7, Intel editor gone after 6.7 LTS — §19.3.1/§19.3.2) is tracked in §20 as the trigger for the Apple-Silicon-only transition decision.
