### 19.4 Steam

#### 19.4.1 C# wrapper choice

There is **no official Valve C# binding**; two MIT-licensed wrappers dominate and both are actively maintained in 2026 [DOCUMENTED — Steamworks.NET repository, accessed 2026-09-24](https://github.com/rlabrecque/Steamworks.NET); [DOCUMENTED — Facepunch.Steamworks repository, accessed 2026-09-24](https://github.com/Facepunch/Facepunch.Steamworks).

| Criterion | Steamworks.NET | Facepunch.Steamworks |
|---|---|---|
| License | MIT | MIT |
| Current release | 2025.164.1 (2026-08-02), building against Steamworks SDK 1.65 | 2.5.2 (2026-04-23) |
| Community traction | 3,617 stars; docs at steamworks.github.io | 3,764 stars |
| API shape | Near-1:1 mapping to the C++ Steamworks API (`ISteamUserStats`, `ISteamInput`, callback structs) | Friendlier, idiomatic C# surface (SteamClient.Init, async friends) |
| Native redistribution | Ships per-platform steam_api redistributables (universal dylib verified, §19.3.2) | Single managed dll wrapping the natives |
| Unity/IL2CPP | Unity-first wrapper (UPM/asset store install, SteamManager reference pattern) | Explicit "Unity IL2CPP Support" in the readme |

**Decision: Steamworks.NET [ORIGINAL DESIGN].** Rationale: this plan's Steam surface (achievements, leaderboards, cloud, Steam Input) is specified below as exact `ISteam*` call sequences taken from Valve's own interface documentation, and Steamworks.NET's near-1:1 parity means every one of those names compiles verbatim — no translation layer between spec and code, and community answers for ISteamUserStats/ISteamInput apply directly. The bundled per-platform redistributables (including the binary-verified universal dylib) remove the riskiest manual step of macOS linking, and its SteamManager pattern matches the bootstrap design in §19.4.2. Facepunch.Steamworks remains the documented fallback if Steamworks.NET maintenance stalls mid-project (swap cost is contained behind the service interfaces defined in §4).

#### 19.4.2 Lifecycle contract and init skeleton

Valve's documented initialization contract [DOCUMENTED — Valve Steamworks API overview, accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api):

1. `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary` — "should be the first Steamworks function call you make, right before `SteamAPI_Init`"; if it returns true, relaunch through Steam and exit.
2. `SteamAPI_Init` must succeed before any interface is touched (it fails without an App ID context).
3. `SteamAPI_RunCallbacks` every frame — at minimum once per second — to dispatch callbacks and call results.
4. `SteamAPI_Shutdown` at process exit. The overlay is hooked automatically once the API initializes and **shutdown does not unhook it**.

Bootstrap implementation (Steamworks.NET surface; attached once in the Boot scene per §4) **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

```csharp
using Steamworks;
using UnityEngine;

/// <summary>
/// Owns the documented Steamworks lifecycle: relaunch guard, init, per-frame
/// callback pump, and shutdown. One instance, created by the Boot scene (§4).
/// </summary>
public sealed class SteamworksBootstrap : MonoBehaviour
{
    #region Serialized Fields
    [Header("Configuration")]
    [Tooltip("Steam App ID; the real value is injected by CI (§16).")]
    [SerializeField] private uint steamAppId = 0;
    #endregion

    #region Public Properties
    /// <summary>True once SteamAPI.Init() has succeeded this session.</summary>
    public bool IsInitialized { get; private set; }
    #endregion

    #region Private Fields
    private const string AppIdFileName = "steam_appid.txt";
    #endregion

    #region Unity Lifecycle
    private void Awake()
    {
        // 1) Relaunch-through-Steam guard — must be the FIRST Steamworks call.
        if (SteamAPI.RestartAppIfNecessary(new AppId_t(steamAppId)))
        {
            Application.Quit();
            return;
        }

        // 2) Init before any interface access; degrade, never crash, without Steam.
        IsInitialized = SteamAPI.Init();
        if (!IsInitialized)
        {
            Debug.LogWarning($"{nameof(SteamworksBootstrap)}: SteamAPI.Init failed — running without Steam services.");
        }
    }

    private void Update()
    {
        // 3) Dispatch callbacks + call results every frame (minimum 1x/second).
        if (!IsInitialized)
        {
            return;
        }
        SteamAPI.RunCallbacks();
    }

    private void OnDestroy()
    {
        if (!IsInitialized)
        {
            return;
        }
        // 4) Shutdown at exit. Note: does NOT unhook the overlay.
        SteamAPI.Shutdown();
        IsInitialized = false;
    }
    #endregion
}
```

Degradation contract **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: the game is fully playable with Steam absent (dev machines, CI smoke tests) — achievements/leaderboards/cloud become inert services behind the §4 service interfaces; no code path outside this bootstrap touches Steamworks types directly.

#### 19.4.3 steam_appid.txt handling

The file contains **just the App ID and nothing else**, sits next to the executable at development time, overrides the App ID context Steam provides, makes `RestartAppIfNecessary` return false for convenience — and **"You should not ship this with your builds"** [DOCUMENTED — Valve Steamworks API overview, accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api). Handling **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: the §16 build pipeline writes `steam_appid.txt` into the dev-build output directory for local and QA runs, and a post-build step asserts its **absence** from every depot payload (§19.4.9) so the relaunch guard behaves correctly for players.

#### 19.4.4 Achievements implementation map

API surface [DOCUMENTED — Valve "Stats and Achievements", accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/achievements):

| Game moment | ISteamUserStats sequence | Callbacks |
|---|---|---|
| Session start | `RequestCurrentStats()` | `UserStatsReceived_t` gates every later call |
| Achievement unlock (via `ScoreController`/`LevelManager` events) | `SetAchievement(apiName)` then **immediate** `StoreStats()` | `UserStatsStored_t` + per-achievement `UserAchievementStored_t` (overlay toast fires automatically) |
| Progress toward cumulative achievements | `IndicateAchievementProgress(apiName, cur, max)` | none (progress bar in overlay UI) |
| Rarity display | `RequestGlobalAchievementPercentages()` → `GetMostAchievedAchievementInfo` / `GetNextMostAchievedAchievementInfo` | call results |
| Icon/label lookup | `GetAchievementIcon`, `GetAchievementDisplayAttribute` | none |

Achievements are configured in Steamworks App Admin (API name, display name, icon). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: achievement icon pixel size (the guide references 64x64 icons — confirm on the App Admin config page once the partner account exists). -->

The v1 achievement set **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — 20 achievements, sized against the original's 13 on 3DS (§1) plus the modern platform's tolerance for progression noise: one first-tower tutorial cheevo; 8 world-completion cheevos; "complete 50 levels" / "complete 100 levels" / "complete all 200" (the 3DS set documented 50/100 and a sub-30-second-puzzle award — §1); speed family ("finish any later puzzle in under 30 seconds", "under 20 seconds"); Endurance family (survive N waves on all 3 lives); Infinity height family; Swift Stacker round-sweep; Tower Tumble party win; one "all achievements" capstone. Exact names/icons live in the App Admin export checked into the project.

#### 19.4.5 Leaderboards implementation map

API surface [DOCUMENTED — Valve "Steam Leaderboards", accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/leaderboards):

- Create or fetch: `FindOrCreateLeaderboard(name, sortMethod, displayType)` / `FindLeaderboard` → `LeaderboardFindResult_t`; sort via `k_ELeaderboardSortMethod` (Ascending/Descending), display via `ELeaderboardDisplayType` (numeric/time).
- Upload: `UploadLeaderboardScore` with keep-best vs force-replace semantics → `LeaderboardScoreUploaded_t` (carries old and new global rank — the "you placed 3rd" UI reads it from this struct).
- Read: `DownloadLeaderboardEntries` (global / around-user / friends ranges) → `LeaderboardScoresDownloaded_t` → `GetDownloadedLeaderboardEntry` (entries are freed after the read — copy what the UI needs).
- Ghosts/replays: `AttachLeaderboardUGC` attaches Steam UGC to a score entry — the ghost-replay hook.

The v1 board set **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Board | Sort | Display | Upload | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Endurance score | Descending | Numeric | keep-best | Score = speed + lives + difficulty per the Endurance definition (§1) |
| Infinity height | Descending | Numeric | keep-best | Highest-stack metric |
| Swift Stacker best race time | Ascending | Time | force | One board; per-track variants post-launch if demand |
| Per-level best time | Ascending | Time | keep-best | Created lazily via `FindOrCreateLeaderboard("lvl_<id>_time", …)` on first completion — avoids hand-managing 200 boards in App Admin |

Ghost replays for per-level boards ride `AttachLeaderboardUGC` and the deterministic same-device replay rules established by the physics/simulation section — UGC ghosts are presentation-only and never authoritative.

#### 19.4.6 Steam Cloud implementation map

Two documented mechanisms [DOCUMENTED — Valve "Steam Cloud", accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud):

- **Steam Auto-Cloud** (zero-code, configured in App Admin): one root path + **Root Overrides** for the other OSes. The doc's warning is the design driver: default per-OS roots produce **per-OS sync with no cross-platform saves** — so the project defines exactly **one root** (the Windows save location) with Root Overrides mapping macOS (and the optional Linux depot) onto it, which is the documented recipe for cross-platform saves.
- **Steam Cloud API** (`ISteamRemoteStorage`): `FileWrite`/`FileReadStream`, `BeginFileWriteBatch`/`EndFileWriteBatch`, `SetSyncPlatforms` for per-file platform control, and local-change queries (`GetLocalFileChangeCount`/`GetLocalFileChange`) for conflict handling.

Hard limits and behaviors from the same page: **100 MB maximum single `FileWrite`/write-chunk call** (files above 256 MB may route to non-optimal storage endpoints); per-user-per-game byte and file-count quotas are set on the Steam Cloud Settings page in App Admin; sync runs before/after each session, so saves should be small and split frequently-changed from rarely-changed data; **Dynamic Cloud Sync** covers Steam Deck suspend/resume (upload at suspend, remote-change notification at wake).

Layout and policy **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — Auto-Cloud with an API escape hatch:

| File | Written | Sync platform |
|---|---|---|
| `settings.json` (video/input/audio prefs) | on change, debounced | all (SetSyncPlatforms default) |
| `progress.json` (world/level unlocks, per-level bests, achievement mirrors) | on level complete / unlock | all |
| `ghosts/lvl_<id>.bin` | on new personal best | all |
| save root | `…/SaveData/<accountid>/…` — per-Steam-user folder from `ISteamUser::GetSteamID` → `GetAccountID` | multiple local accounts on one machine never collide (documented pattern) |

Quota setting: 2 MB / 64 files per user — three orders of magnitude above the ~200 KB worst case (200 level ghosts × ≤1 KB). Conflict policy (§19.6.2): monotonic schema version field, newest-write-wins, losing file preserved one generation as `<name>.bak`.

#### 19.4.7 Steam Input: action-based config, glyphs, Deck

Steam Input is Valve's action-based input layer: games define an **Action Manifest** with an **In-Game Actions (IGA) file** describing actions, action sets, and action set layers; players get per-device glyph-correct prompts, remapping, activators, mode-shifting, radial/touch menus, and Steam Deck controls out of the box; legacy-mode bindings and gamepad emulation are documented fallbacks [DOCUMENTED — Valve "Steam Input", accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/steam_controller).

v1 IGA design **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

- Action set **Menu**: Navigate (Vector2), Submit, Cancel, Point.
- Action set **Gameplay**: MoveCursor, Grab, RotateCW, RotateCCW, Drop, Pause — mirroring the §7 action map one-to-one, so the desktop-native path and the Steam path share names and rebinding UI.
- Action set **SwiftStacker**: team-left/team-right variants of Gameplay via action set layers.
- Ship default configs generated from the official IGA templates; the per-device glyph text comes from Steam Input's origin data on Steam builds (§19.6.1).

#### 19.4.8 Overlay compatibility

The overlay hooks the running process automatically once Steamworks initializes and remains hooked even after `SteamAPI_Shutdown` [DOCUMENTED — Valve Steamworks API overview, accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api). Project obligations **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: the game pauses simulation and mutes gameplay audio when the overlay activates (listened for via the overlay-activation callback), the options menu and all HUD screens assume the overlay can appear at any frame (no modal state corrupts), and QA runs a dedicated overlay-on pass (§19.6.5). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: the overlay activation callback name in the current SDK (expected GameOverlayActivated_t on the friends interface) — confirm against the callback reference during integration. -->

#### 19.4.9 SteamPipe: depots, branches, builds and review

Concepts per Valve's application build docs [DOCUMENTED — Valve "Builds" (SteamPipe app configuration), accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/builds): the Steamworks SDK is required **only to upload content** — everything else it ships is optional; an upload happens via the SDK command line (`steamcmd` / `tools/ContentBuilder`; `SteamPipeGUI` wraps the simple cases); a build is a snapshot of one or more **depots** and emits a text manifest (file list, sizes, SHA-1, flags); builds are managed on the Builds page in App Admin; **Default is the only branch initially**, and setting a build live on Default pushes it to all owners; **depots** are logical file groupings identified by Depot ID where later-listed depots **override** earlier ones (first depot = lowest priority), with OS-specific depots the standard multi-platform pattern. Branches support private/password-protected beta and review branches.

Release pipeline **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Element | Plan |
|---|---|
| Depot 1 | Windows x64 payload (IL2CPP/Master exe, signed §19.2.5) |
| Depot 2 | macOS Universal payload (.app in dmg-mounted layout, notarized+stapled §19.3.4) |
| Depot 3 (optional, post-launch) | Linux x64 payload — otherwise Linux players run Depot 1 through Proton |
| Launch config | One launch per OS depot; no launcher executable (Deck criterion, §19.4.10) |
| Branch flow | `beta` (internal QA) → `review` (Valve review build) → `default` (owners) |
| Cadence | steamcmd run from §16 on tagged commits; manifest archived per build |

#### 19.4.10 Steam Deck Verified checklist

Categories: **Verified / Playable / Unsupported / Unknown**; Verified requires four criteria [DOCUMENTED — Valve Steam Deck Verified program page, accessed 2026-09-24](https://www.steamdeck.com/en/verified): Input (full controller support, correct controller input icons/glyphs, on-screen keyboard auto-appears when needed); Display (supports the default 1280×800 or 1280×720 resolution, good default settings, legible text); Seamlessness (no compatibility warnings; any launcher must be controller-navigable); System Support (game and all middleware Proton-compatible — the criterion that surfaces anti-cheat incompatibilities). Ratings are re-evaluated over time.

Project checklist **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — target **Verified**:

- [ ] Input: gameplay fully playable on Deck controls via the §19.4.7 IGA config; glyphs match Deck; OSK auto-invokes for any text field (profile name entry is the only v1 text field).
- [ ] Display: 1280×720 windowed and 1280×800 fullscreen both render the full play field with legible text (the §19.2.4 legibility gate doubles as this check).
- [ ] Seamlessness: no launcher, no compat warning, no mouse-only corner.
- [ ] System: no middleware outside Unity + Steamworks (both long Proton-proven); verify suspend/resume preserves a live level via Dynamic Cloud Sync (§19.4.6).
- [ ] Default settings sane at first boot on a clean Deck profile (720p-class, defaults silent-modality).

#### 19.4.11 Store page assets, review and the Steam Direct fee

Store presence spans capsule images (standard store, library, community, event assets plus overrides), description, tags, pricing (regional pricing with VAT handled by Steam), coming-soon page, demos/Next Fest adjacency, and achievements display [DOCUMENTED — Valve store application documentation surface, accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/builds). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: exact capsule image pixel dimensions and formats (partner store-asset page not captured), and the commonly cited ~30-day store review window (review-process page not captured) — pin both when App Admin access exists. -->

The Steam Direct fee: **$100 USD (or equivalent) per app**, paid during onboarding by a Steamworks partner Admin, not payable from Steam wallet funds, **non-refundable** but "recoupable in the payment made after your product has at least $1,000.00 Adjusted Gross Revenue" (shown as a line item in the monthly report); VAT/GST may apply and the invoice goes to the paying individual [DOCUMENTED — Valve "Steam Direct Fee", accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/appfee).

Asset production plan **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: one key art master (tower mid-collapse over water, lounge palette) generating all capsule sizes; six screenshots (calm stack, countdown lights, load-break special, Swift Stacker split-screen, Tower Tumble 4-player, Endurance HUD) plus one 30-second gameplay trailer capturing the 3-second-lights tension (§1); coming-soon page live at the start of the public build phase to accumulate wishlists ahead of the review window.

### 19.5 Xbox

#### 19.5.1 Public knowledge vs NDA-gated reality

Xbox planning has a hard information boundary; everything below states which side of it each fact lives on.

| Topic | Publicly documented | NDA-gated (design must reserve, not assume) |
|---|---|---|
| Access | ID@Xbox entry requirements (§19.5.2) | Concept-approval flow detail, onboarding timeline |
| SDK | GDK exists as one kit for console + PC + cloud; public GitHub subset (§19.5.3) | Secure console docs/samples, console-specific graphics APIs, the console-secure kit traditionally called GDKX |
| Engine | Unity lists Xbox Series X\|S and Xbox One as build targets (§19.5.3) | Unity Xbox platform-module install mechanics |
| Certification | XRs exist, are identical across devices with device-specific test cases (§19.5.5) | XR deep test cases, FMA scoring detail, cert tooling walkthroughs |
| Services | Xbox services surface (§19.5.6) | Partner Center configuration flows in detail |
| Ratings | IARC exists as the rating pathway (§19.5.8) | Partner Center IARC submission steps |
| Hardware | Dev kits exist and are provisioned via onboarding (§19.5.4) | Kit pricing/availability |

#### 19.5.2 ID@Xbox access path and timeline expectations

The three hard requirements from the ID@Xbox FAQ: **be at least 18 years old, sign an NDA, and reside in a country with which Microsoft can do business**; the program pitches self-publishing with platform support, and the page lists Unity among the engines ("Build with Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot, and supported middleware") [DOCUMENTED — xbox.com ID@Xbox developers page, accessed 2026-09-24](https://www.xbox.com/en-US/Developers/id). Microsoft's "500M MAU" and "$5B+ paid to independent developers" figures on that page are vendor marketing, recorded here as positioning, not as verified fact.

Timeline expectations **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (the honest part of the plan): the classic two-step concept approval and typical onboarding durations are not publicly documented, so the schedule reserves a **multi-month, non-binding buffer** for application → agreement → Partner Center provisioning → dev-kit acquisition before any Xbox milestone is even scheduled. Concretely: apply at Steam v1 launch; do not commit an Xbox ship date until kits and GDK access are in hand; treat every interim estimate as internal fiction. This matches the release order decision (Xbox last, explicitly gated).

#### 19.5.3 GDK, GDKX and the Unity Xbox module

The Microsoft GDK is the single kit covering Xbox consoles, Windows PC, and cloud: the **public GDK on GitHub** "contains the common tools, libraries, and documentation needed to build games for Xbox Game Pass for PC on Windows 10/11, Xbox consoles (Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One), and cloud gaming" [DOCUMENTED — Microsoft Learn GDK landing, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/). **Secure** console resources — secure downloads, NDA samples, and "Microsoft GDK NDA topics" including console-specific graphics APIs — unlock only after: the organization is onboarded as an Xbox development partner, a valid Microsoft GDK Agreement is signed, and a Partner Center account is provisioned at onboarding with permissions managed through a Microsoft Entra ID tenant [DOCUMENTED — Microsoft Learn, "Access Microsoft GDK development resources", accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/gdk-dev/development-downloads/access-resources).

The console-secure variant historically called **GDKX** is exactly the NDA territory the table above reserves: current naming, contents, and its relationship to the public GitHub GDK are not publicly documented. <!-- TODO-VERIFY (NDA): current GDKX naming/scope and the Unity Xbox platform-module install procedure — confirm after onboarding; the plan's only pre-onboarding commitment is that Xbox builds use Unity's Xbox support riding the GDK, not a hand-rolled wrapper. -->

Unity side: the Unity 6.3 system-requirements target table lists **Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One** as build targets, with a Windows 10 64-bit (1709+) Home/Pro/Enterprise development host [DOCUMENTED — Unity 6.3 system requirements, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/system-requirements.html). The Series+One generation decision is deferred until the phase starts: One is a 2013-era performance envelope, and a 2D physics puzzler fits it easily, but carrying two cert targets has cost — decide with real GDK timing data **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

#### 19.5.4 Development hardware

Dev kits and partner-centered Series X|S development-mode enablement are part of partner onboarding — not purchasable retail-side for GDKX certification work [DOCUMENTED — Microsoft Learn GDK access model, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/gdk-dev/development-downloads/access-resources). Budget line **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: at least one Series X dev kit and one Series S-class kit (the S is the tighter memory/performance envelope and the right minimum-spec target); retail hardware may serve early input/UX prototyping but never certification claims.

#### 19.5.5 Xbox Requirements (XR) certification overview

"XBOX Requirements (XRs) consist of the policies, technical requirements, and product component-related requirements to which all developers and publishers of XBOX titles must conform", and — the planning-critical property — **"the policies and requirements are the same on every device although there are device-specific test cases"**; XR sections cover games, Beta/Game Preview titles, XR change history, and Certification Failure Mode Analysis (FMA) scoring [DOCUMENTED — Microsoft Learn, "Policies and Xbox Requirements", accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/store/policies/gc-policies-nav).

Schedule posture **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: reserve **at least one full cert-submission cycle plus one failure-retry cycle** in the Xbox phase plan (FMA scoring means failures are graded, not binary — partial passes still cost time); pre-check continuously with the GDK's certification tooling rather than discovering XR gaps at submission; run the §19.6.5 shared QA checklist on dev-kit hardware every release candidate, since a desktop-green build is not an Xbox-green build (different sign-in, suspend/resume, and input-UX realities).

#### 19.5.6 Xbox services: sign-in, identity, achievements

"Xbox services are a collection of micro-services that expose features such as profile, friends and presence, stats, leaderboards, achievements, multiplayer, and matchmaking" — the same services usable from Windows PC GDK titles and console titles, configured in **Partner Center**, consumed through the **Xbox services API (XSAPI)** that ships with the GDK; the services area also includes identity (sign-in), the real-time-activity (RTA) service, and a PlayFab integration path [DOCUMENTED — Microsoft Learn, "Xbox services overview", accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/services/fundamentals/live-xbl-overview).

Mapping **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (behind the same §4 service interfaces as Steam, so `ScoreController` and the modes never know the store):

| Feature | Steam (§19.4) | Xbox |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in | implicit (Steam client) | XSAPI identity — explicit user sign-in UX, guest handling required |
| Achievements | ISteamUserStats | Xbox achievements configured in Partner Center, unlocked via the services API; platform-policy governed |
| Leaderboards | ISteamUserStats boards | Xbox services leaderboards (stats-based) |
| Cloud saves | Steam Auto-Cloud | The platform's title-storage/sync story — verified during onboarding (NDA) |

The achievement/leaderboard **content** (the 20-cheevo set, the four board families from §19.4.4/§19.4.5) is store-agnostic and mirrors 1:1 onto Xbox services configuration; only unlock plumbing differs.

#### 19.5.7 Input certification requirements

Controller support is the mandatory-class input reality on console, with mouse/keyboard optional and XR-governed; the specific XR clauses are public but deep and were not captured — so the plan treats them as verify-at-phase-start, not as assumptions [DOCUMENTED — XR policies surface, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/store/policies/gc-policies-nav). <!-- TODO-VERIFY (public-but-deep): exact mouse/keyboard XR clause references and their test cases, plus controller-glyph XR expectations — pull the XR text when the Xbox phase opens. --> Design-side the game is already aligned: gamepad-first via the Input System (§7), the full action surface identical to Steam's IGA set (§19.4.7), and no mouse-only interaction anywhere in the UI (§19.6.1's glyph system renders Xbox prompts natively).

#### 19.5.8 IARC ratings

Age ratings flow through **IARC** as the rating pathway in the Microsoft store pipeline, with regional rating hooks (USK and peers) — the same international survey mechanism Steam's parallel content-survey documentation mirrors for its store [DOCUMENTED — store/policies surface, accessed 2026-09-24](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/store/policies/gc-policies-nav). The content survey answers are a project asset **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: one canonical filled-in IARC questionnaire (no violence, no gambling, no user-generated-text exposure beyond leaderboards, mild physics-failure imagery) stored in the release wiki and reused verbatim across Xbox, and any other store that accepts IARC, so ratings never diverge between storefronts. <!-- TODO-VERIFY (public-but-deep): the exact Partner Center IARC submission steps and per-rating-board fee implications. -->

#### 19.5.9 Game Pass

Game Pass consideration comes with the ID@Xbox relationship — the program's pitch includes platform promotion and Game Pass [DOCUMENTED — xbox.com ID@Xbox page, accessed 2026-09-24](https://www.xbox.com/en-US/Developers/id). Decision posture **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: evaluate a Game Pass offer if/when approached post-Xbox-launch; the game's structure (200 levels, endless modes, party modes for couch co-op) fits subscription play patterns well, and no plan milestone depends on it.

### 19.6 Cross-Platform Unification

#### 19.6.1 Input glyph and prompt unification (ties to §7)

The prompt pipeline is device-driven, not platform-driven, so a player who swaps controllers sees correct glyphs without a settings change. Mechanism, per the Input System documentation [DOCUMENTED — Input System package docs, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest): rebinding display strings come from `GetBindingDisplayString(bindingIndex, out deviceLayout, out controlPath)`, and a device is classified as gamepad-class via `InputSystem.IsFirstLayoutBasedOnSecond(deviceLayout, "Gamepad")`. The documentable desktop device classes for glyph selection: `XInputController` (Windows/UWP), `DualShock4GamepadHID` (mac/win/uwp/linux), `DualSenseGamepadHID` (mac/win), `SwitchProControllerHID` (Bluetooth-only on desktop) — with rumble via `Gamepad.SetMotorSpeeds(low, high)` where supported.

Resolution order **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** — `InputGlyphProvider` resolves once per device-change event:

| Context | Glyph source |
|---|---|
| Steam build (Windows/macOS), Steam Input active | Steam Input origin glyphs (§19.4.7) — authoritative, covers Deck/Steam Controller/generic pads |
| Desktop, non-Steam context | Native atlas keyed by device layout: Xbox family, PlayStation family, Switch Pro, generic |
| Xbox build | Xbox controller atlas (Xbox glyph conventions per platform expectation, §19.5.7) |
| Touch platforms | On-screen control skins, no physical glyphs |

The atlas is keyed by `(deviceLayout, controlPath)` pairs, never by button names, so a rotated or rebound action automatically re-resolves its prompt — the same property §7's rebinding UI relies on.

#### 19.6.2 Cloud save parity across stores

One save schema everywhere, written by one persistence layer: monotonic `schemaVersion`, the three-file split of §19.4.6 (settings / progress / ghosts), per-account subfolder, and a shared conflict rule (newest-write-wins by session timestamp, loser preserved one generation). Store adapters only differ in transport: Steam Auto-Cloud (§19.4.6), the Xbox services sync story (verified at onboarding, §19.5.6), and the mobile store mechanisms owned by the mobile phases. Parity gate in §19.6.5: a save created on any platform loads on every platform — the cross-platform-saves recipe (one root + Root Overrides) is what makes this true on Steam specifically [DOCUMENTED — Valve Steam Cloud, accessed 2026-09-24](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud). **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** for the conflict/backup/battery-pull matrix beyond the schema rule above.

#### 19.6.3 Platform `#if` directive map

Compilation symbols available and their sanctioned uses; platform code paths stay thin enough to review in one screen each **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**:

| Define | Meaning / origin | Sanctioned use in this project |
|---|---|---|
| `UNITY_STANDALONE_WIN` | Unity built-in (Windows standalone) | Signing/diagnostics glue, exe metadata, DPI workarounds if needed |
| `UNITY_STANDALONE_OSX` | Unity built-in (macOS standalone) | Notarization post-build hooks, Metal-specific render tweaks |
| `UNITY_STANDALONE_LINUX` | Unity built-in (Linux standalone) | Optional depot build only |
| `UNITY_ANDROID` / `UNITY_IOS` | Unity built-ins | Mobile phases (not this section's scope) |
| `UNITY_GAMECORE` | Xbox platform define | Xbox service adapters — **verify exact symbol at phase start** (console defines are NDA-adjacent) |
| `ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` | Set by Active Input Handling — defined under Both and under Input System only [DOCUMENTED — Unity staff post, accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/planned-breaking-changes-in-unity-6-7/1723293) | Guard around input-version-sensitive API; asserts at boot that `ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` is defined (pre-transition, under Active Input Handling = Both per §4.8); assert `ENABLE_LEGACY_INPUT_MANAGER` absent only after the post-transition flip to Input System only (§20 P2.E9-automation-ci.10) |
| `UNITY_64`, `DEVELOPMENT_BUILD` | Legacy defines — deprecated in Unity 6.6 as part of the .NET migration prep | Do not add new uses; prefer explicit platform + custom defines |
| `AOB_STEAM` | Project-defined (§16 sets it on Steam Build Profiles) | All Steamworks-facing service implementations |
| `AOB_XBOX` | Project-defined | All XSAPI-facing service implementations |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY (NDA-adjacent): UNITY_GAMECORE as the current Xbox define in Unity 6.x — confirm symbol spelling in the Xbox module docs at onboarding. -->

`AOB_STEAM`/`AOB_XBOX` rather than raw platform defines is deliberate: the same Windows binary could theoretically ship outside Steam, and store identity (which achievements/cloud implementation is compiled in) is a distribution fact, not a platform fact **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**.

#### 19.6.4 Per-platform Build Profiles

Unity 6 replaced Build Settings with the Build Profiles window: classic platform profiles share Development flags and scene data across platforms, while build profiles are version-controllable Assets with independent settings and per-profile scene lists; architecture selection happens in the build window, not Player Settings [DOCUMENTED — Unity build profiles documentation surface via the Player settings reference, accessed 2026-09-24](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-PlayerSettings.html). <!-- TODO-VERIFY: the Unity 6 build-profiles documentation page URL (introduction slug unconfirmed) — pin the citation during the §16 pipeline build. -->

The profile set **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** (all checked into the project, driven by the §16 CI matrix):

| Profile | Platform / arch | Defines | C++ config | Scenes | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AoB-Win64-Steam-Ship` | Windows x64 | AOB_STEAM | Master | Boot → MainMenu → Game | signs §19.2.5, steam_appid.txt stripped §19.4.3 |
| `AoB-Win64-Steam-Dev` | Windows x64 | AOB_STEAM | Debug | same + Diagnostics | stacktraces w/ file:line |
| `AoB-MacOS-Universal-Steam-Ship` | macOS Universal | AOB_STEAM | Master | same as ship | built on Mac agent only (§19.3.1), notarize step §19.3.4 |
| `AoB-Linux-Steam-Ship` (optional) | Linux x64 | AOB_STEAM | Master | same | post-launch decision |
| `AoB-Android-Ship` / `AoB-iOS-Ship` | mobile | (mobile phase) | Master | mobile scene list | owned by the mobile sections |
| `AoB-Xbox-Ship` / `AoB-Xbox-Dev` | Xbox targets | AOB_XBOX | Master | same as ship | created at Xbox phase start on the dev host (§19.5.3) |

`DEVELOPMENT_BUILD` is deliberately absent from every Defines column above: it is implied by the Development Build flag on the profile, not authored as a scripting define — Unity 6.6 deprecated the `UNITY_64` and `DEVELOPMENT_BUILD` symbols as breaking-change prep for the .NET/CoreCLR migration [DOCUMENTED — Unity "Path to CoreCLR, 2026: Upgrade Guide", accessed 2026-09-24](https://discussions.unity.com/t/path-to-coreclr-2026-upgrade-guide/1714279), and §19.6.3 forbids new uses.

Rule **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]**: no per-profile scene drift — ship profiles differ from dev only in defines, C++ config, and diagnostics scenes, so a bug reproduced on dev is reproducible on ship.

#### 19.6.5 Shared QA checklist (release candidate gates)

Run per platform before any branch push beyond `beta`; every row is pass/fail with an owning role in §20.

**Shared gates (all platforms):**

| # | Gate |
|---|---|
| 1 | Clean install → first boot → options reachable without any input device beyond the platform default |
| 2 | Store sign-in (or graceful degradation when store absent) — no hang, no crash |
| 3 | Achievement unlock fires store toast; unlock persists across restart |
| 4 | Leaderboard upload + download round-trip displays the player's own entry |
| 5 | Save round-trip: create save → close → reopen → verify; cross-platform file load per §19.6.2 where applicable |
| 6 | Glyph correctness for every attached controller class (§19.6.1) including hot-swap mid-level |
| 7 | Pause behavior on overlay/system UI activation — simulation frozen, audio ducked, no state corruption |
| 8 | Fullscreen/window/resolution changes persist; DPI scaling matrix passes (§19.2.4) on desktop |
| 9 | Crash-log capture verified by forcing a scripted exception in a debug build |
| 10 | Uninstall → reinstall → cloud restore returns progress |

**Platform additions:**

| Platform | Additional gates |
|---|---|
| Windows | Artifact-Signing signature validates (signtool verify); SmartScreen copy present in support page; exclusive fullscreen on a high-refresh monitor; x64-only payload check |
| macOS | Notarization + staple validate on a clean VM (`spctl --assess`); first-run Gatekeeper dialog matches FAQ screenshot; Universal slice check (arm64 + x64 both launch); Rosetta absence tolerated |
| Steam (both depots) | steam_appid.txt absent from depot payload; relaunch guard works when launched outside Steam; Deck checklist §19.4.10; Dynamic Cloud Sync suspend/resume mid-level; overlay pass §19.4.8 |
| Xbox (phase start) | XR pre-check suite green on dev kit; sign-in + guest flows; suspend/resume (energy-saving) mid-level; controller-only navigation of every screen; cert submission package builds |

## 20. Master Task List

This section decomposes the §10 roadmap into the tracker-ready work breakdown: 8 phases, 44 epics, 231 tasks, 357 estimated dev-days. Every §4–§9 system, §18–§19 platform track, and §15–§17 automation workflow has a task; §20.10's coverage matrix proves it. Task IDs are stable keys that survive tracker import (§20.11).

### 20.1 How to read this list

**ID grammar.** Every task ID follows `P<phase>.<E#>-<epic-slug>.<task>` — e.g. `P1.E3-physics-core.6` is task 6 of epic 3 ("physics-core") in phase 1. Phase numbers and names match §10 exactly (P0 Pre-production through P7 Post-launch; full names in §10). IDs are **immutable and append-only**: cancelled tasks are marked `skipped` with a reason, never renumbered; epics are never renamed or merged.

**Columns.** Six fields per task:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ID** | Immutable key per the grammar above |
| **Task** | Description of the work (what exists when it is done) |
| **Deps** | IDs that must reach `done` first; `—` means none |
| **Est** | Estimate in dev-days for one senior engineer |
| **Acceptance** | Testable acceptance criterion — objectively checkable |
| **Ver / Plat** | Verification method code(s) and platform flag(s) |

**Verification legend (Ver).** `T` automated test (EditMode/PlayMode/CI), `R` design or code review against the relevant §, `M` manual checklist or playtest, `P` profiler/measurement evidence, `B` build-artifact inspection.

**Platform flags (Plat).** `ALL` every target; `Win`, `Mac`, `And`, `iOS`, `Xbx` the single platform; `Ed` editor/tooling only (never ships); `CI` build infrastructure only. P5–P6 tasks carry their flag; engine-side work defaults to `ALL`.

**Estimate basis.** All 357 dev-days are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** planning estimates at roughly 50% confidence — each task is as likely to overrun as underrun, so §20.10 quotes ±20% ranges per phase. Estimates cover engineering time only; store/account fees, identity validation, review windows, and certification queues are flagged as lead-time items and excluded from the day counts. Any task slipping past 2× its estimate triggers a re-plan of its dependent chain rather than silent absorption.

**Marker conventions** follow the document standard: `[DOCUMENTED — source, accessed 2026-09-24]` for externally verified facts, `[DOCUMENTED via §1]` for franchise facts, `[ORIGINAL DESIGN]` for this plan's inventions, and `<!-- TODO-VERIFY: ... -->` where the notes could not confirm a fact.

### 20.10 Summary, ranges, and critical path

**Counts and estimates per phase:**

| Phase | Name | Epics | Tasks | Est (d) | Range ±20% (d) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Pre-production | 4 | 18 | 21 | 17–25 |
| P1 | Vertical slice | 7 | 38 | 54 | 43–65 |
| P2 | Core systems | 10 | 61 | 88.5 | 71–106 |
| P3 | Content I | 4 | 15 | 43 | 34–52 |
| P4 | Content II | 4 | 13 | 41 | 33–49 |

| P7 | Post-launch | 3 | 11 | 14 | 11–17 |
| **Total** | | **44** | **231** | **357** | **286–428** |

At one engineer shipping 5 dev-days/week, 357 dev-days is roughly 14–20 months inside the band — before review windows, cert queues, and the gated Xbox track add calendar. A second engineer compresses the engineering chain, not the lead-time chains.

**Per-epic totals** sit in each epic header; the largest are P3.E2 and P4.E1 (18 d each), P5.E5 (17 d), P3.E1 (15 d), and P4.E2 (14 d), followed by a four-way 12 d tie (P2.E1, P2.E4, P2.E9, P5.E1) — check these first when re-planning.

**Critical path (engineering chain).** P0.E1.1 → P0.E1.2 → P1.E1.1 → P1.E1.5 → P1.E3.1 → P1.E3.6 → P1.E4.2 → P1.E4.5 → P2.E1.1 → P2.E8.1 → P3.E2.1 → P4.E1.1 → P5.E5.1 → P6.E1.5 — physics-first, with Steam integration landing last of the platform epics. **Parallel lead-time chain (calendar, not effort):** P0.E4 storefront accounts start day one; Artifact Signing identity validation (P5.E4.3) cannot be expedited and should overlap P4; Apple/Google/Valve review windows (P6.E1.2, P6.E2, P6.E3.4) are queue time excluded from estimates. **Gated track:** Xbox work (P5.E7, P6.E4, P7.E2) hangs off ID@Xbox approval and never blocks the other stores. Overlapping P3.E2 authoring with platform hardening on a second engineer **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** is the recommended fast lane — roughly 2–3 months of calendar for review bandwidth.

**Coverage matrix — spec section to epics** (proof every system/track has tasks): §2→P0.E2; §3→P0.E2/P1.E4/P2.E2/P4.E2; §4→P1.E1; §5→P1.E2, P2.E8, P3.E2, P4.E1; §6→P1.E3, P2.E3, P2.E7; §7→P1.E5, P2.E4; §8→P2.E1; §9→P2.E5–P2.E7, P3.E1; §11–§13 (historical deep-dives) inform P4.E2 mode designs but carry no build tasks; §14→P2.E3, P2.E10, P5.E4.2, P5.E6; §15→P0.E1, P2.E9; §16→P2.E9.4–P2.E9.6; §17→P2.E9.7, P2.E9.9, P6.E5.5; §18→P5.E1, P5.E2; §19→P5.E3–P5.E5, P5.E7, P6; §21→P0.E2.5, P5.E6.7.

### 20.11 Tracker CSV layout

The canonical tracker is a CSV with exactly these columns, in this order:

```csv
id,phase,epic_slug,task_no,title,description,depends_on,estimate_devdays,acceptance_criteria,verification,platforms,status
```

Example row:

```csv
P1.E3-physics-core.6,P1,E3-physics-core,6,"StabilityMonitor 3s window","Velocity/angular/height predicate with hysteresis driving countdown","P1.E3-physics-core.5",3.0,"Table-driven tests across 12 stability scenarios match designer expectations","T;R","ALL","todo"
```

Field rules: `id` matches §20.1 grammar and is the primary key — never edited. `depends_on` is a semicolon-separated ID list, empty if none. `verification` uses the §20.1 legend letters, semicolon-separated when a task needs more than one method. `platforms` uses the §20.1 flags with `ALL` as the default. `status` is one of `todo`, `doing`, `blocked`, `review`, `done`, `skipped` — `skipped` and `blocked` require a `blocked_reason`/`skip_reason` note column added on import (Jira: map phase→Epic, task→Story, epic_slug→Component; GitHub Projects: phase→iteration field, epic→milestone; Linear: phase→cycle, epic→label). Within an epic, task numbers are never reused — deleted tasks keep their ID with status `skipped`.

## 21. Risk Register & Open Questions

This section consolidates every risk and unresolved question surfaced by the eleven research tracks (T01–T11) and the adversarial verification pass, then converts them into a working register: scored rows with mitigations and watch triggers (owned by the system areas of §4–§9, §14–§19), and open questions with concrete resolution paths and phase-gate deadlines keyed to the §10 roadmap. Facts are cited from the track notes/digest/verify extract only; the register's scoring model, mitigations, triggers, and deadlines are ours.

### 21.1 Register method

**[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** The register format, scoring scale, exposure bands, review cadence, and all mitigations/triggers below are our design, built on top of [DOCUMENTED] facts cited inline and the verify-pass corrections. Scores are re-assessed at every §10 phase-gate review (P0–P7); any risk whose exposure rises a band triggers a §20 re-plan of the affected epic.

| Field | Convention |
|---|---|
| Likelihood (L) | 1 = very unlikely … 5 = near-certain, within the plan's horizon (through P7) |
| Impact (I) | 1 = cosmetic … 5 = project-ending (missed launch, unshippable platform, legal action) |
| Exposure | `L × I`; bands: **≥16 critical** (re-plan now), **9–15 high** (active mitigation), **5–8 medium** (monitor), **≤4 low** (accept) |
| Trigger to watch | A measurable condition; most are CI metrics, store-policy URLs, or release announcements re-checked on the cadence in §21.7.5 |
| Owner area | The section that owns mitigation (e.g. §6 Simulation/Physics, §7 Input, §16 CI, §19 PC/Console/Steam) |

Cross-cutting provenance note: where the verification pass corrected the sweep, the correction wins and is marked **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** inline. No verification verdict was left UNRESOLVED; the corrections themselves spawned follow-up verifications, carried as open questions in §21.7.

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: BuoyancyEffector2D's exact submerged-fraction force formula was not captured from a primary source (T11 gap) — prototype and measure before freezing ENG-03 thresholds -->

Prose rationale for the three load-bearing rows. ENG-01 is the plan's deepest technical commitment: the whole replay/ghost and determinism-testing strategy of §6/§14 is built on the 2D physics line precisely because upstream Box2D v3 was designed for cross-thread and cross-64-bit-platform determinism while Unity's 3D PhysX explicitly is not (conditions listed in ENG-01; sources per T11). Unity is also building a new 2D core ("PhysicsCore2D", Unity.U2D.Physics on Box2D v3; the Unity-Technologies/PhysicsExamples2D repo was active 2026-09-22) — a future convergence point, but its shipping status is unresolved (OQ-E04). ENG-04 is not an argument against 6.6 — Unity staff themselves recommend 6.6 for new projects (per T02) — it is a scheduling risk: one planned, branch-isolated, test-gated upgrade to 6.7 LTS, not rolling churn. ENG-02's numbers are T11's replication math for the documented-but-unresolved "240 fps physics" Wii U claim (see OQ-G01): the claim's original primary source was never located, so we engineer to the feel (substepping) rather than to an unverifiable figure.

### 21.5 Security & legal risks (DevSecOps lens)

| ID | Risk | L | I | Exp | Mitigation | Trigger to watch | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-01 | MCP arbitrary-code surfaces: every Unity MCP option grants effectively arbitrary C# execution in the Editor process (per T05); mcp-for-blender's `execute_blender_code` is arbitrary Python by design and port 9876 is RCE for anyone who can reach it ([addon.py / safe_mode.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/addon.py), accessed 2026-09-24); its AST sandbox is opt-in only (`BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=1`; unset = unvalidated execution) ([safe_mode.py](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender/blob/main/src/blender_mcp/safe_mode.py), accessed 2026-09-24). The official Blender Lab MCP states it "will execute LLM generated code in Blender without any guards" ([blender.org/lab/mcp-server](https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/), accessed 2026-09-24) | 2 | 4 | 8 | MCP binds localhost-only, never exposed; safe-mode env set in all wrapper scripts; no secrets in scenes/projects the agents read; IvanMurzak runtime mode (compiled player) exposes only developer-authored pre-compiled `[AiTool]`s — Roslyn eval is Editor-only **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** (the sweep's "executes arbitrary C# in the player" claim was refuted) — so keep runtime mode out of release builds | Port-scan of dev machine; unexpected outbound connections from Blender/Unity | §17 |
| SEC-02 | Prompt injection through agent-read data: console logs and scene-graph contents ingested by MCP-driven workflows are untrusted input that can carry instructions (per T05/T06 security analysis) | 2 | 3 | 6 | Human approval for destructive ops; the official server's client-approval dialog stays on; review diffs after agent sessions; keep CI (§16) — which never ingests external text — as the authority for what ships | An agent applying changes it was not asked to make | §17 |
| SEC-03 | CI secret exposure: Unity license serials/`.ulf`, Apple certs + profiles, Android keystore, Steam partner credentials all pass through CI | 2 | 5 | 10 | Secrets as GitHub Actions secrets/env vars, never CLI args; Android keystore validity 50 years + bundle version code <100000 (Unity offsets +100000/+200000 per ABI) per T07; rotate on any runner compromise; self-hosted runners for signing steps | Secret-scanner alerts; leaked-license invalidations | §16, §18, §19 |
| SEC-04 | Leaderboard cheating and save tampering: our leaderboards and star ratings are **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** and client-authoritative if unguarded | 3 | 3 | 9 | Sign save files (HMAC over serialized state) per §14; submit scores with a compact determinism replay attestation the server can re-simulate (ties to ENG-01); rate-limit uploads | Impossible scores appearing; tampered saves in support tickets | §14, §3 |
| SEC-05 | Supply chain: UPM git packages, PyPI MCP servers, and GitHub Actions are all in the build path; mcp-for-blender ships telemetry on-by-default (minimal anonymous; kill switch `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true`) (per T06) — a policy concern on corporate machines | 2 | 3 | 6 | Pin git-package commits and action SHAs; review transitive deps at pin bumps; both Steamworks wrappers are alive MIT (Steamworks.NET 2025.164.1 2026-08-02; Facepunch.Steamworks 2.5.2 2026-04-23) (per T08) — pick one (§19) and pin; disable telemetry in corporate policy | Dependency-audit failures; abandoned-dependency alarms | §16, §19 |
| SEC-06 | Privacy compliance drift: Unity auto-includes its required-reason declarations in PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy (UserDefaults CA92.1, file timestamps 0A2A.1+C617.1, boot time 35F9.1, disk space E174.1) but we must declare our own collected data or risk rejection (per T07); Google Play Data safety form must match actual data (leaderboards = the deciding feature) | 2 | 4 | 8 | Decide the leaderboard/telemetry data set once in §14 and generate both the xcprivacy entries and the Play Data safety answers from that single inventory; re-check at every store submission | Store rejection for undeclared data; new Unity auto-declarations | §14, §18 |

### 22.2 Glossary

**Art of Balance domain**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Stack loop | The core micro-loop: piece offered from queue → carried (move/rotate) → released → falling → settling → 3-second stability window → cleared or failed (§3.2). |
| Stability window | The documented ~3-second quiet period after the stack settles; if the stack holds, the level (or stage) is cleared (§3.2, §6.4). |
| Waterline / basin | The water surface in each level's container; any resting piece dropping to it fails the level (§3.4). |
| Piece queue | The fixed, level-defined order of pieces the player must place (§3.2, §5.3). |
| Load-break block | Documented special block (breakable): shatters when the stack presses on it beyond a threshold (§8.3). |
| Timer block | Documented special block (disappearing): vanishes after a lifetime, mid-stack removal destabilizes (§8.4). |
| Fire block | Documented special block: ignites and applies a blast that clears/scorches neighbors (§8.5). |
| Gravity inverter | Documented special block: flips gravity direction while active (§8.6). |
| Linked pair / seesaw | **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** extension: two blocks coupled so torque on one tilts the other (§8.7). |
| Arcade / Endurance / Infinity / Swift Stacker / Tower Tumble | The five documented game modes (§1.4, §5.4); Endurance scoring (speed + lives + difficulty) is partially documented, the rest of the mode math is [ORIGINAL DESIGN]. |
| 240 fps physics claim | Wii U edition marketing claim about simulation rate; modern analog is Physics2D substepping (§6.5, §11.2). |

**Unity 6.6 engineering**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Unity 6.6 / 6000.6 | Final Unity 6-family Tech Stream release (6000.6.0f1 Aug 31 2026; 6000.6.2f1 Sep 18 2026); Unity 6.7 is the next LTS (§1.7). |
| The new Unity CLI (`unity`) | Unity's official command-line tool (1.0.0-beta.11) for project/package/build management from the terminal, distinct from editor batch mode (§15). |
| Batch mode (`-batchmode -executeMethod`) | The traditional headless editor invocation used by CI since pre-CLI days (§16.1). |
| UBA | Unity Build Automation, the cloud build service (§16.3). |
| com.unity.pipeline | Package that provides the pipeline engine the new CLI drives for builds/tests (§15.3). |
| Build Profiles | Unity 6's per-platform build configuration replacing the single build-target scene list (§4.10). |
| URP | Universal Render Pipeline — the render pipeline this plan targets, with per-platform quality tiers (§9.2). |
| SRP Batcher | URP's draw-call batching path; block shaders are written to stay compatible (§9.3). |
| Input System | The package-based input layer; Active Input Handling = **Both** during migration (§4.8, §7.2). |
| `IPieceInputProvider` | This plan's input abstraction: one implementation per device class (pointer, gamepad, touch, motion) (§7.1). |
| InputActionAsset | The bindable action map asset (Gameplay / UI / Menus) all providers feed (§7.2). |
| asmdef | Assembly Definition — compile-scope boundaries for the plan's Core/Gameplay/UI/Input/Platform/Editor/Tests split (§4.4). |
| ScriptableObject (SO) | Data-asset class backing `PieceDefinition`, `LevelDefinition`, `GameModeDefinition`, config and event channels (§5, §4.6). |
| Addressables | Content packaging/loading system used for worlds and mode content (§5.6). |
| IL2CPP | The AOT scripting backend mandatory on iOS/Android/console targets (§18, §19). |
| Physics2D substepping | `useSubStepping` / `maxSubStepCount` / `minSubStepFPS` — the Unity 6.6 path to ≥240 Hz effective simulation (§6.5). |
| Fixed Timestep | ProjectSettings/Time deterministic step; anchor of the simulation contract (§4.9). |
| Play/Edit mode tests | Unity Test Framework's two phases; the plan splits physics/scoring math tests from loop integration tests (§14.4). |
| `persistentDataPath` | Per-platform writable root where saves live (§6.8). |

**Multiplatform shipping**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| AAB | Android App Bundle, Play Store upload format (§18.4). |
| Play API 36 | Google Play target-API level effective Aug 31 2026 — the compliance floor for new submissions (§18.4). |
| NDK r27c / JDK 17 / AGP 9.1.1 / Gradle 9.3.1 | The Android toolchain pins Unity 6.6 embeds (§18.4). |
| Xcode 26+ | Minimum Xcode for App Store uploads since 2026-04-28; iOS 15 deployment floor; Metal-only graphics (§18.1). |
| `PBXProject` post-processing | C# API for editing the generated Xcode project from Unity build callbacks (§18.1). |
| `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` | Apple privacy manifest Unity 6 generates and this plan extends (§18.1). |
| Hardened runtime / entitlements / notarytool | The macOS signing/notarization chain for Gatekeeper acceptance (§19.2). |
| Steamworks.NET | The chosen Steamworks binding (vs Facepunch/official) (§19.3). |
| SteamPipe / depots / steamcmd | Valve's content distribution: upload tooling and per-platform content buckets (§19.3). |
| Steam Input / Deck Verified | Valve's action-based controller layer and handheld certification checklist (§19.3, §7.6). |
| AutoCloud | Steam's file-based cloud save; the plan maps its save layout to it (§14.1). |
| GDK / GDKX | Xbox development kits; Unity's Xbox module targets them (§19.4). |
| ID@Xbox | Microsoft's self-publishing program — the realistic access path, with NDA-gated specifics (§19.4). |
| XR / TRC / lotcheck | Nintendo/Sony/Microsoft certification requirement families (context for §19.4). |
| IARC | The rating-body questionnaire flow used for console/store age ratings (§19.4). |

**Automation & MCP**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| MCP (Model Context Protocol) | Anthropic's open protocol connecting AI clients (Claude Code) to tool servers (§17.1). |
| Unity MCP server | The official Unity-side MCP support (built into Unity 6.6 via `unity mcp` / the AI assistant package) exposing editor/scene operations (§17.2). |
| blender-mcp / mcp-for-blender | The community Blender MCP server (renamed 2026); browser-driven PolyHaven access included (§17.3). |
| Editor bridge | The Unity-side component relaying MCP tool calls into editor script execution (§17.2). |
| bpy | Blender's Python module — both the in-app API and the pip-installable headless module (§16.5). |
| `--background --python` | Blender's headless script invocation pattern for asset generation (§16.5). |
| Prompt injection via scene data | The MCP risk class where fetched scene/console content carries instructions; mitigations in §17.4. |

**Provenance markers**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[DOCUMENTED]** | Externally verified against a cited source in §22.1. |
| **[ORIGINAL DESIGN]** | Designed for this clone because the original's internals are undocumented. |
| **[VERIFIED-REFUTED]** | An adversarial verification pass corrected the initial research; the correction stands. |
| `<!-- TODO-VERIFY -->` | A specific fact flagged for confirmation against current docs before reliance. |

### 22.3 Reproducibility

Every external fact in this plan traces to the research corpus produced on **2026-09-24** by a four-stage agentic pipeline (research sweep → authoring → adversarial review/fix round 1 → round 2). All web access happened that day through a local research-toolkit (per-search engine cascade over DDG / Bing / Google / Brave / keyless Tavily, page fetches via a supervised headed browser — human-solved CAPTCHAs, never automated).

**Corpus.** Research folder: `independent_research/research-aob-unity-clone-2026-09/` — 11 track notes (2,128 lines total) + 5 adversarial verification notes, with inline source URLs preserved; full page dumps under `scratch/pages/`. The 253-entry citation index in §22.1 is the deduplicated union of those notes' source lists.

**Orchestration run IDs** (this session's workflow journal, in order):
1. `wf_1a72be17-d9e` — research sweep: 16 agents (11 tracks + 5 verifies), ~2.0M subagent tokens, 994 tool calls, ~105 min. 30 claims adversarially adjudicated: 21 CONFIRMED, 9 REFUTED → corrections applied before authoring.
2. `wf_820de049-73c` — section authoring: 21 senior-author agents in parallel, ~135k words (recovered §10/§11 after API rate-limit failures via journal-cached resume).
3. `wf_59bbdb47-bf6` — review/fix round 1: 12 reviewers (3 completeness vs user requirements, 8 accuracy vs notes, 1 cross-section consistency) → adversarial verification (60-claim cap) → 19 per-file fixers: 89 findings raised, 60 confirmed, 78 edits applied, 7 skipped. One accuracy reviewer (§14/§18) was lost to a rate limit — covered by round 2.
4. `wf_42483300-40b` — review/fix round 2: 50 agents, ~21 min: re-ran the §14/§18 accuracy review (6 findings), adversarially verified the 34-finding pool (33 confirmed, 1 refuted), applied 39 edits across 15 files — every round-1 deferred and low-severity item now resolved, zero deferred remaining.

**Search-engine counters** (folder `scratch/quota.json`, final): DDG 13 · Bing (browser) 66 · Google (browser) 27 · Tavily keyless 8 · Tavily free-allowance 10 — 124 SERP queries total.

**Cost.** **$0 billed.** The only metered engine used (Tavily, 10 queries) drew from the monthly included allowance; pay-as-you-go was never enabled at any point in the run.

**Methodology inputs.** Research agents ran under the `browser-deep-wide-research-prompt-v4.md` system prompt with the `rdw-deep-wide-research` workflow (breadth angles + depth threads + pre-synthesis verification). Authoring and review agents applied the `unity-game-dev-expert`, `game-ultra-master-developer`, and `game-designer-developer-pro` standards for code, planning, and design-math quality respectively.
